examples.japanese: ここは夏は暑いし、冬は寒い・寒いです。
examples.english: Here it's hot in the summer, and what's more, it's cold in the winter.

examples.japanese: このアパートは奇麗だし、安い・安いです。
examples.english: This apartment is clean, and what's more, it's inexpensive.

examples.japanese: 遊びたいんです・だが明日は試験だし遊べない・遊べません。
examples.english: I would like to play, but there is an exam tomorrow, and I can't fool around.

examples.japanese: 仕事もあったし、結婚も出来たし、とても嬉しいです。
examples.english: Not only did I find a job, but I was also able to get married, so I'm very happy.

examples.japanese: 今日は天気もいいし、どこへ行きましょうか。
examples.english: It's a nice day, so shall we go out somewhere?

examples.japanese: あの人は美人だし、頭もいい。
examples.english: She's beautiful and what's more she's bright.

examples.japanese: 切符は買ってあるし、是非見に行きましょう。
examples.english: I've bought a ticket for you, so let's go see it, by all means.

meaning_en: Intend to ~; be convinced that ~; believe; feel sure that ~; be going to; mean
formation:
(i) Vinformal | つもりだ | | 
 | {話す /話した} つもりだ | Intend to talk/someone is convinced he talked | 
(ii) Adjective い informal nonpast | つもりだ | | 
 | 強いつもりだ | Someone is convinced that he is strong | 
(iii) Adjective な stem | なつもりだ | | 
 | 元気なつもりだ | Someone is convinced that he is healthy | 
(iv) Noun | のつもりだ | | 
 | 先生のつもりだ | Someone is convinced that he is a teacher |
explanation: An intention or conviction of a speaker (or a person with whom the speaker can empathise) about his future or past actions or current state.

examples.japanese: 私は来年結婚するつもりだ・です。
examples.english: I intend to get married next year.

examples.japanese: 父はまだ若いつもりだ・です。
examples.english: My father is convinced that he is still young.

examples.japanese: 私はよく読んだつもりだ・です。
examples.english: I'm convinced that I read it carefully.

examples.japanese: これはお礼のつもりだ・です。
examples.english: This is my intention of appreciation.

examples.japanese: 休みには何をするつもりですか。
examples.english: What do you intend to do during the vacation?

examples.japanese: 僕は大学に行くつもりはない。
examples.english: I have no intention of going to college.

examples.japanese: あんな人にはもう会わないつもりです。
examples.english: I do not intend to see that kind of person.

examples.japanese: 私はまだ元気なつもりだ。
examples.english: I'm convinced that I'm still healthy.

meaning_en: I expect that ~; it is expected that ~; ~ is expected to; I am fairly certain that ~; should; ought to; it is natural that ~; no wonder ~
formation:
(1) {V/Adjectiveい} informal | はずだ | | 
 | {話す /話した} はずだ | It is expected that someone will talk/talked. | 
 | {高い /高かった} はずだ | It is expected that something is/was expensive. | 
(2) Adjective な stem | [な / だった] はずだ | | 
 | {静かな/静かだった} はずだ | It is expected that something is/was quiet. | 
(3) Noun | {の/だった} はずだ | | 
 | {先生の /先生だった} はずだ | It is expected that s.o. is/was a teacher |
explanation: A dependant noun which expresses the speaker’s expectation that something will take place or took place or that someone/something is or was in some state.

examples.japanese: クラークさんはパーティーに行くはずだ・です。
examples.english: I expect that Mr. Clark will go to the party.

examples.japanese: 大野先生はサンドラを知っているはずです。
examples.english: I expect that Professor Ono knows Sandra.

examples.japanese: あの本は高かったはずだ。
examples.english: I expect that book was expensive.

examples.japanese: そのアパートは奇麗なはずです。
examples.english: I expect that apartment is clean.

examples.japanese: カールソンさんは昔先生だったはずだ。
examples.english: I'm fairly sure that Ms. Carlson was a teacher before.

meaning_en: Even if ~
formation:
(i) Vinformal past | って | | 
 | 話しって | Even if someone talks/talked | 
 | 食べだって | Even if someone eats/ate | 
(ii) Adjective い stem | くたって | | 
 | 高くたって | Even if something is/were expensive | 
(iii) {Adjective な stem/ N} | だっ(たっ)て | | 
 | 静かだっ(たっ)て | Even if something is/were quiet | 
 | 先生だっ(たっ)て | Even if someone is/were a teacher |
explanation: Even if someone did something or something were in some state (the desired result would not come about) or even if someone or something is in some state.

examples.japanese: あの人には話したって分からない・分かりません。
examples.english: Even if I tell him that, he won't understand it.

examples.japanese: 僕はその切符を高くたって買う・買います。
examples.english: I will buy the ticket even if it is expensive.

examples.japanese: お金があったって車は買いたくない。
examples.english: Even if I had money, I wouldn't want to buy a car.

examples.japanese: 本を買ったって、忙しくて読めない。
examples.english: Even if I buy books, I'm too busy to read them.

examples.japanese: 汚くたって構いません。
examples.english: I don't care even if it is dirty.

examples.japanese: 遠くて不便だってマイ・ホームなら構いません。
examples.english: Even if it is far away and inconvenient, it doesn't matter if it is 'my home'.

examples.japanese: どんなにいい先生だって時々間違います。
examples.english: No matter how good a teacher may be, he sometimes makes mistakes.

examples.japanese: 一人で旅行に行ったって面白くない。
examples.english: It's not fun traveling (literally: if I travel) alone.

examples.japanese: 私は少しくらい高く(っ)たって、質のいいものを買うことにしている。
examples.english: I make it a rule to buy good quality things even if they are a little more expensive.

examples.japanese: いくら日本語が上手だって専門知識がなかったらこの翻訳はできないよ。
examples.english: No matter how good someone's Japanese is, he/she cannot do this translation without technical knowledge (in this ﬁeld).

meaning_en: Do not do something and ~; is not ~ and ~; because ~ do not do something
formation:
(i) Vinformal negative | なくて | Where V is often a potential verb | 
 | {話さ /話せ} なくて | Someone doesn’t/can’t talk and ~ | 
 | {食べ /食べられ} なくて | Someone doesn’t/can’t eat and ~ | 
(ii) Adjective い stem | くなくて | | 
 | 高くなくて | Something isn’t expensive and ~ | 
(iii) {Adjective な stem/ N} | {では/じゃ} なくて | | 
 | {静かでは/静かじゃ} なくて | Something isn’t quiet and ~ | 
 | {先生では/先生じゃ} なくて | Someone isn’t a teacher and ~ |
explanation: A て form of the negative ない, which indicates a cause/reason for a state or action.

examples.japanese: 朝七時に起きられなくて会社に遅れた・遅れました。
examples.english: I couldn't get up at seven and was late for work (at my company).

examples.japanese: 先生の説明が分からなくて困りました。
examples.english: I didn't understand the teacher's explanation and had a difficult time.

examples.japanese: 日本では日本語が話せなくて残念でした。
examples.english: It's regrettable that I couldn't speak Japanese in Japan.

examples.japanese: 試験は難しくなくてよかったですね。
examples.english: The exam wasn't difficult and it was good, wasn't it?

examples.japanese: 字が上手じゃなくて恥ずかしいんです。
examples.english: My handwriting is so poor that I feel ashamed.

examples.japanese: 厳しい先生じゃなくてよかった。
examples.english: He wasn't a strict teacher and it was good.

formation:
(1) {Adjective な stem/ N} | だい | | 
 | 静かだい | Something is quiet? | 
 | 先生だい | Someone is a teacher? | 
(2) {V/Adjective い} informal | んだい | | 
 | {話す/話した} んだい | Someone talks/talked? | 
 | {高い/高かった} んだい | Something is/was expensive? | 
(3) {Adjective な stem/ N} | {な/だった} んだい | | 
 | {静かな/ 静かだった} んだい | Something is/was quiet? | 
 | {先生な/先生だった} んだい | Someone is/was a teacher? |
explanation: A sentence final particle which indicates an interrogative word question in informal male speech.

examples.japanese: どこが静かだい。
examples.english: What place is quiet?

examples.japanese: 誰が行くんだい。
examples.english: Who is going?

examples.japanese: 新しい仕事はどうだい。
examples.english: How's your new job

examples.japanese: あの人は誰だい。
examples.english: Who is that person?

examples.japanese: 何が可笑しいんだい。
examples.english: What's funny?

examples.japanese: どの人は佐藤先生なんだい。
examples.english: Which person is Professor Sato?

meaning_en: Show signs of ~
formation:
Adjective い/な stem | がる | | 
 | うれしがる | Someone shows signs of being glad | 
 | めんどうがる | Someone shows signs of being bothered |
explanation: An auxiliary verb attached to a psychological/physiological adjective meaning a person other than the speaker shows signs of ~

examples.japanese: 一男はスポーツカーを欲しがった・がりました。
examples.english: Kazuo showed signs of wanting a sports car.

examples.japanese: 上田さんはアイスクリームを食べたがった・がりました。
examples.english: Mr Uedo showed signs of wanting to eat ice cream.

examples.japanese: スーザンは一人で淋しがっています。
examples.english: Susan feels lonely by herself.

examples.japanese: 子供が眠たがっている。
examples.english: My child wants to go to sleep.

meaning_en: Cannot do something; must not do something; don’t do something; should not do something
formation:
Vて | はいけない | | 
 | 話してはいけない | Must not talk | 
 | 食べてはいけない | Must not eat |
explanation: A phrase which indicates prohibition.

examples.japanese: この部屋に入ってはいけない・いけません。
examples.english: You must not enter this room.

examples.japanese: 教室でものを食べてはいけません。
examples.english: You must not eat (food) in the classroom.

examples.japanese: 花子はまだ酒を飲んではいけない。
examples.english: Hanako must/can not drink alcohol yet.

meaning_en: Don't do ~
formation:
Vinformal nonpast | な | | 
 | 話すな | Don’t talk! | 
 | 食べるな | Don’t eat! |
explanation: A negative imperative marker used by a male speaker in very informal speech

examples.japanese: 煙草を吸うな！
examples.english: Don't smoke!

examples.japanese: 酒をあまり飲むな！
examples.english: Don't drink too much sake!

examples.japanese: そんな所にもう行くな！
examples.english: Don't go to such a place any more!

examples.japanese: あんな男とは結婚するな！
examples.english: Don't marry that kind of man!

examples.japanese: もう帰って来るな！
examples.english: Don't come home any more!

meaning_en: May; It is all right if
formation:
{V/Adjective(い/な)/Noun+copula} て | もいい | | 
 | 話してもいい | May talk; it is all right if someone talks | 
 | 高くてもいい | It is all right if something is expensive | 
 | 静かでもいい | It is all right if something is quiet | 
 | 先生でもいい | It is all right is someone is a teacher |
explanation: A phrase which expresses persmission or concession.

examples.japanese: A:ここで煙草を吸ってもいいですか。  B:はい、いいです。
examples.english: A: May I smoke here?  B: Yes, you may.

examples.japanese: 高くてもいい・いいです。
examples.english: It is all right if it's expensive.

examples.japanese: 学生でもいい・いいです。
examples.english: It is all right if you are a student.

examples.japanese: この椅子を使ってもいいですか。
examples.english: May I used this chair?

examples.japanese: 今日の宿題は作文です。短くてもいいですが面白いのを書いて下さい。
examples.english: Today's homework assignment is a composition. It is all right if it's short, but please write an interesting one.

examples.japanese: A:テニスをしませんか。  B:下手でもいいですか。
examples.english: A: Wouldn't you like to play tennis?  B: Is it alright if I'm poor at it?

examples.japanese: A:何か冷たいものを飲みたいんですが。  B:ビールでもいいですか。
examples.english: A: I want to drink something cold.  B: Will beer do?

meaning_en: Do something and see; try to do something
formation:
Vて | みる | | 
 | 話してみる | Try to talk | 
 | 食べてみる | Try to eat |
explanation: Do something to see what it’s like or what will happen.

examples.japanese: 私は日本の小説を読んでみる・みます。
examples.english: I will read Japanese novels (to see what they are like).

examples.japanese: 面白そうなコンサートだったので行ってみました。
examples.english: Since it seemed interesting, I went to the concert (to see what it was like).

examples.japanese: ここの刺身は美味しいですよ。食べてみますか。
examples.english: Sashimi here is good. Will you try it?

meaning_en: Have dome something; finish doing something; finish something up
formation:
Vて | しまう | | 
 | 話してしまう | Have talked | 
 | 食べてしまう | Have eaten |
explanation: An auxiliary verb which indicates the completion of an action.

examples.japanese: 池田君は三日でその本を読んでしまった・しまいました。
examples.english: Mr. Ikeda finished reading the book in three days.

examples.japanese: 私はルームメートのミルクを飲んでしまった・しまいました。
examples.english: I (mistakenly) drank my roommate's milk.

examples.japanese: もう宿題をしてしまいましたか。
examples.english: Have you done your homework yet?

examples.japanese: 私は今日中にそのレポートを書いてしまおうと思っている。
examples.english: I think that I will finish (writing) the report today.

examples.japanese: 早くご飯を食べてしまいなさい。
examples.english: Finish (eating) your meal quickly.

examples.japanese: シチューを作り過ぎてしまいました。
examples.english: I made too much stew (to my regret).

meaning_en: Do something in advance; go ahead and do something; let someone/something remain as he/it is
formation:
Vて | おく | | 
 | 話しておく | Talk in advance | 
 | 食べておく | Eat something in advance |
explanation: Do something in advance for future convenience.

examples.japanese: 明日パーティーをするのでビールを買っておいた・おきました。
examples.english: Since we are having a party tomorrow, I bought some beer for it.

examples.japanese: 今日は昼に客が来るので昼ご飯を早目に食べておいた。
examples.english: Since I'm having a guest at noon today, I had my lunch earlier.

examples.japanese: 来年日本へ行くから少し日本語を勉強しておきます。
examples.english: Since I'm going to Japan next year, I will study a little Japanese ahead of time.

meaning_en: Give
explanation: あげる (1) Someone gives something to a person who is not a member of the giver’s in group but whose status is about equal to that of the giver.

examples.japanese: 私は良子に花をあげた・あげました。
examples.english: I gave Yoshiko flowers.

examples.japanese: 大野さんは山本さんに本をあげた。
examples.english: Ms. Ono gave Mr. Yamamoto a book.

examples.japanese: 君はアンに何をあげましたか。
examples.english: What did you give to Ann?

meaning_en: Get; receive; be given
explanation: もらう (2) The first person or someone the speaker empathizes with receives some benefit from an action by someone whose status is not as high as the receiver’s.

examples.japanese: （私は）山本さんに本をもらった・もらいました。
examples.english: I got a book from Mr. Yamamoto.

examples.japanese: 山川さんは橋本さんにウイスキーをもらった。
examples.english: Mr. Yamakawa got whiskey from Mr. Hashimoto.

examples.japanese: （あなたは）モリスさんに何をもらったの？
examples.english: What did you get from Mr. Morris?

examples.japanese: （私は）父にカメラを買ってもらった・もらいました。
examples.english: My father bought a camera for me.

examples.japanese: （私は）友達に来てもらった・もらいました。
examples.english: I had my friend come (for my benefit).

examples.japanese: 木村さんは大野さんに車を貸してもらった。
examples.english: Mr. Kimura had Mr. Ono lend him his car.

examples.japanese: （君は）ベックさんに何をしてもらいましたか。
examples.english: What did you have Mr. Beck do for you? / What did Mr. Beck do for you?

examples.japanese: ジョンソンさんは鈴木さんに日本語を教えてもらっている。
examples.english: Mr. Johnson has Mr. Suzuki teaching him Japanese.

meaning_en: And; because of that; that is why; therefore; so
explanation: A conjunction to indicate that what is stated in the preceding sentence is the reason or cause for what is stated in the following sentence.

examples.japanese: 昨日は風邪を引きました。それで学校を休んだんです。
examples.english: I had a cold yesterday. That's why I took a day off from school.

examples.japanese: ちょっと大阪で用事がありました。それで昨日いなかったんです。
examples.english: I had some business in Osaka. That's why I wasn't here yesterday.

examples.japanese: A:昨日はちょっと大阪で用事がありました。  B:ああ、それでいらっしゃらなかったんですね。
examples.english: A: Yesterday I had to run an errand in Osaka.  B: Oh, that why you weren't here.

examples.japanese: A:昨日小川君とピンポンの試合をしたんだ。  B:それで、先週新しいラケットを買ったんですね。
examples.english: A: Yesterday I played ping pong with Mr. Ogawa.  B: That's why he bought a new paddle last week.

meaning_en: -ness; -ly
formation:
Adjective (い/な) stem | さ | | 
 | 高さ | Height | 
 | 静かさ | quietness |
explanation: A sentence final particle used in highly informal speech by male speakers to express different degrees of assertion ranging from a light touch comment up to opposition or imposition.

examples.japanese: このうちの広さはちょうどいい・いいです。
examples.english: This size of this house is just right.

examples.japanese: 富士山の高さはどのぐらいですか。
examples.english: What is the approximate height of Mt. Fuji?

examples.japanese: 日本語の難しさがよく分かりました。
examples.english: I'm now well aware of the difficulty of Japanese.

examples.japanese: アメリカのよさはパイオニア・スピリットでしょう。
examples.english: One of America's good qualities is perhaps its pioneering spirit.

examples.japanese: Ａ：就職出来るかな。Ｂ：出来るさ。
examples.english: A: I wonder if I can get a job. B: Sure you can.

examples.japanese: Ａ：君は日本語、読めないよね。Ｂ：いや、読めるさ。
examples.english: A: You cannot read Japanese, right? B: Yeah, sure I can.

examples.japanese: 人生は長い旅のようなものさ。
examples.english: Life is something like a long journey.

examples.japanese: どうして酒を飲んじゃいけないのさ。
examples.english: How come I can't drink sake?

examples.japanese: A: 今日の日本語のテストは難しいかな。B: いや、難しくないさ。
examples.english: A: I wonder if today's Japanese test is difficult. B: No, it's not difficult, I tell you.

examples.japanese: A: このスーツケース、持てるかな。B: 持てるさ。
examples.english: A: I wonder if I can carry this suitcase. B: I'm sure you can.

meaning_en: And so on; and the like; for example; things like ~
explanation: A marker that indicates exemplification.

examples.japanese: 日本の食べ物の中では寿司や天ぷらなどが好きだ・好きです。
examples.english: Among Japanese foods I like things like sushi and tempura.

examples.japanese: A:冬休みはどこに行きましょうか。  B:ハワイなどどうですか。
examples.english: A: Where shall we go during the winter vacation?  B: How about Hawaii, for example?

examples.japanese: 大学ではフランス語やドイツ語などを勉強した。
examples.english: In college I studied French and German and the like.

examples.japanese: この大学には中国や韓国などから学生が大勢来ます。
examples.english: A lot of students from China, Korea and so on come to this college.

examples.japanese: A:経済学を専攻するつもりですか。  B:いいえ、経済学など専攻するつもりはありません。
examples.english: A: Are you going to major in economics?  B: No, I have no intention of majoring in things like economics.

examples.japanese: A:この翻訳をして下さいませんか。  B:こんな難しいもの、私などには出来ません。
examples.english: A: Could you kindly translate this for me?  B: A person like me cannot translate such a difficult thing.

meaning_en: About; around
formation:
Noun (time) | ごろ(に) | | 
 | 三時ごろ(に) | At about 3 o'clock |
explanation: Approximately (with a specific point of time).

examples.japanese: 鈴木さんは朝七時ごろうちを出る・出ます。
examples.english: Mr. Suzuki leaves home at about 7:00 o'clock in the morning.

examples.japanese: A:いつごろ北京に行きますか。  B:来年の六月ごろ行きます。
examples.english: A: About when are you going to Beijing?  B: I'm going there around June of next year.

examples.japanese: A:今朝は何時ごろまで寝ていましたか。  B:十時ごろまで寝ていました。
examples.english: A: Until about what time were you asleep this morning?  B: I was asleep until about 10 o'clock.

examples.japanese: 去年の今ごろは大雪でしたね。
examples.english: About this time last year it snowed heavily, didn't it?

meaning_en: Then; in that case
explanation: If that is the case,

examples.japanese: A:頭が痛いんです。  B:それなら直ぐ寝なさい。
examples.english: A: I have a headache.  B: In that case, go to sleep right away.

examples.japanese: A:映画を見に行きませんか。  B:明日試験があるんです。  A:それなら、明後日はどうですか。
examples.english: A: Wouldn't you like to go see a movie?  B: I have an exam tomorrow.  A: Then, how about the day after tomorrow?

examples.japanese: A:日本にはどのぐらいいましたか。  B:三年です。  A:それなら、日本のことはよく知っているでしょうね。
examples.english: A: How long did you stay in Japan?  B: Three years. A: Then, you must know a lot about Japan.

meaning_en: Still; also; after all; as expected; you know
explanation: An adverb indicating that the actual situation expectedly/anticipatively conforms to a standard based on past experience, comparison with other people, or common sense.

examples.japanese: ベイリーさんはやはり来なかった・来ませんでしたね。
examples.english: As expected, Mr. Bailey hasn't come, has he?

examples.japanese: 雪子さんは今でもやはり奇麗です。
examples.english: Yukiko is still pretty.

examples.japanese: お兄さんはテニスが上手ですが、弟さんもやっぱり上手ですよ。
examples.english: The other brother is good at tennis, and the younger brother is also good at it.

examples.japanese: やはり日本のビールは美味しいですね。
examples.english: As expected, Japanese beer is good.

examples.japanese: 僕はやはり結婚することにしました。
examples.english: I've decided to get married, after all.

meaning_en: And
explanation: A coordinate conjunction that is used to list two or more items (nouns or noun phrases) in an inexhaustive fashion.

examples.japanese: 山田さんや小川さんが来た・来ました。
examples.english: Mr. Yamada and Mr. Ogawa (and others) came.

examples.japanese: 山本さんやスミスさんがテニスをしている。
examples.english: Mr. Yamamoto, Mr. Smith and others are playing tennis.

examples.japanese: 僕はビールやワインを飲んだ。
examples.english: I drank beer, wine and other things like that.

examples.japanese: 土田さんは大川さんや鈴木さんに手紙を書いた。
examples.english: Mr. Tsuchida wrote a letter to Mr. Okawa and Mr. Suzuki (and others).

meaning_en: Although; though
formation:
Sinformal | けれども | | 
 | {話す /話した} けれども | Although someone (will) talk/talked | 
 | {高い /高かった} けれども | Although something is/was expensive | 
 | {静かだ /静かだった} けれども | Although something is/was quiet | 
 | {先生だ /先生だった} けれども | Although someone is/was a teacher |
explanation: A disjunctive subordinate conjunction that combines two sentences.

examples.japanese: 私は言わなかったけれどもトムは知っていた・いました。
examples.english: Although I didn't tell him, Tom knew (about it).

examples.japanese: この本は高いけれどもいい本ですよ。
examples.english: Although it is expensive, this book is a good book.

examples.japanese: 僕はドイツ語があまり好きじゃないけれども勉強しなければならない。
examples.english: Although I don't like German very much, I have to study it.

examples.japanese: 大野さんは九十歳だけれどもとても元気だ。
examples.english: Although Mr. Ono is ninety years old, he is very healthy.

meaning_en: And; and then
explanation: A coordinate conjunction that connects two sentences.

examples.japanese: 今日は東京に行った・行きました。そして友達に会った・会いました。
examples.english: I went to Tokyo today. And I met my friend there.

examples.japanese: 昨日は朝ゴルフをしました。そして午後はテニスをしました。
examples.english: Yesterday I played golf in the morning. And I played tennis in the afternoon.

examples.japanese: この映画はつまらない。そして長過ぎる。
examples.english: This movie is uninteresting. And it's too long.

examples.japanese: この花は奇麗です。そして安いです。
examples.english: This flower is pretty. And it is inexpensive.

meaning_en: After that; and then; in addition to that
formation:
(i) {Vて/Vます} | それから | | 
 | {話して /話し}, それから | Someone talks, and then ~ | 
 | {食べて /食べ}, それから | Someone eats, and then ~ | 
(ii) Adjective い stem | く(て)、それから | | 
 | 高く(て)、それから | Something is not only expensive but ~ | 
(iii) Adjective な stem | で、それから | | 
 | 静かで、それから | Something is not only quiet but ~ | 
(iv) Noun1 (と) Noun 2 (と) | それからNoun3 | | 
 | 英語(と)日本語(と)、それから中国語 | English, Japanese and Chinese |
explanation: A conjunction that indicates (1) temporally contiguous actions or states, or (2) a cumulative listing of objects, actions or states.

examples.japanese: 昨日は二時間ぐらい友達と飲んでそれからうちに帰った・帰りました。
examples.english: Yesterday I drank with my friend for about two hours and then went home.

examples.japanese: 昨日は二時間ぐらい友達と飲んだ。それから本屋に寄ってうちに帰った。
examples.english: Yesterday I drank with my friend for about two hours. Then I dropped by a bookstore and went home.

examples.japanese: 十時まで宿題をしました。それから映画に行きました。
examples.english: I did my homework until 10 o'clock. And then, I went to the movie.

examples.japanese: 昨日は朝銀座に行って、それから映画を見に行った。
examples.english: Yesterday morning I went to Ginza and then went to see a movie.

examples.japanese: レストランではステーキとサラダとそれからチーズケーキを食べました。
examples.english: At the restaurant I ate steak, salad, and cheesecake.

examples.japanese: 湖の色は初めは青く、それから緑になりました。
examples.english: The colour of the lake was blue in the beginning and then turned green.

examples.japanese: 月曜、火曜、それから木曜もとても忙しいです。
examples.english: I am very busy on Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday, too.

meaning_en: Indeed one does something alright, (but ~); indeed ~ (but ~); do ~ (but ~)
formation:
(i) {V1/Adjective い1} informal | ことは{V2/Adjective い2} | Where {V1/Adjective い1}={V1/Adjective い2} | 
 | 話すことは{話す/話します} | Someone does talk | 
 | 話したことは{話した/話しました} | Someone did talk | 
 | 高いことは高い(です} | Something is expensive | 
 | 高かったことは高かった(です} | Something was expensive | 
(ii) {Adjective な stem1 なこと/Noun1} | は{Adjective な stem2/Noun2} {だ /です} | Where {Adjective な stem1 / Noun1}={Adjective な stem2/Noun2} | 
 | 静かなことは静か{だ/です} | Something is quiet | 
 | いい人はいい人{だ/です} | Someone is a good person | 
(iii) {Adjective な stem1/ Noun1} | だったことは {Adjective な stem2/ Noun2} {だった/でした} | Where {Adjective な stem1/Noun1}={Adjective な stem2/ Noun2} | 
 | 静かだったことは静か{だった/でした} | Something was quiet | 
 | いい人だったことは人{だった/でした} | Someone was a good person |
explanation: Speaking of proposition X, X is certainly true.

examples.japanese: 私はテニスをすることはする・しますが上手じゃない・上手じゃありません。
examples.english: I do play tennis, but I am not good at it.

examples.japanese: ジョーンズさんは日本語を話すことは話しますが、簡単なことしか言えません。
examples.english: Mr. Jones does speak Japanese, but he can say only simply things.

examples.japanese: ボストンシンフォニーの切符は買えたことは買えましたが、大変悪い席でした。
examples.english: I could buy a ticket for the Boston Symphony alright, but it was a very bad seat.

examples.japanese: この店は安いことは安いですが、ものが良くありません。
examples.english: This store is inexpensive alright, but its goods are of poor quality.

examples.japanese: 今日の試験は難しかったことは難しかったが、よく出来た。
examples.english: Today's test was indeed difficult, but I did well on it.

examples.japanese: 私のアパートは駅に近くて便利なことは便利ですが、家賃がとても高いです。
examples.english: My apartment is close to the station and convenient alright, but the rent is very high.

examples.japanese: その女の子が好きだったことは好きでしたが、結婚はしなかったんです。
examples.english: I did like the girl, but I didn’t marry her.

examples.japanese: あの人はいい人はいいだったけれど頑固だったね。
examples.english: He was indeed a good person, but he was stubborn, wasn’t he?

meaning_en: If so; then; well then
explanation: If that is the case

examples.japanese: A:このオレンジは甘くないです。  B:それではこれはどう（ですか）。
examples.english: A: This orange is not sweet.  B: How about this one, then?

examples.japanese: A:僕は魚も肉も嫌いです。  B:それでは何を食べるんですか。
examples.english: A: I hate both fish and meat.  B: Then, what do you eat.

examples.japanese: A:今日の午後テニスをしませんか。  B:今日の午後はちょっと都合が悪いんですが。 A:それでは明日の午後はどうですか。
examples.english: A: Wouldn't you like to play tennis this afternoon?  B: This afternoon is not convenient for me, but...  A: Then, how about tomorrow afternoon?

examples.japanese: それでは二十分ぐらい休みましょう。
examples.english: Well then, let's take a break for about twenty minutes.

examples.japanese: それではまた来週の金曜日に来ます。
examples.english: Well then, I'll come again next Friday.

meaning_en: I wish ~ had done something
formation:
(i) Group 1 verbs | Vconditionalばよかった | | 
 | 話せばよかった | I wish someone had talked | 
(ii) Group 2 verbs | Vstemればよかった | | 
 | 食べればよかった | I wish someone had eaten | 
(iii) Irregular verbs | 来る→来ればよかった | I wish someone had come | 
 | する→すればよかった | I wish someone had done |
explanation: A phrase which expresses the speaker’s regret.

examples.japanese: 先生に聞けばよかった・ばよかったです。
examples.english: I wish I had asked my teacher.

examples.japanese: あの本を読めばよかった。
examples.english: I wish I had read that book.

examples.japanese: ウェルズさんは日本へ行けばよかったね。
examples.english: I wish Mr. Wells had gone to Japan, don't you?

examples.japanese: ああ、もっと英語を勉強しておけばよかったなあ。
examples.english: Oh, I wish I had studied English harder!

meaning_en: For
formation:
Noun | としては | | 
 | 先生としては | For a teacher |
explanation: A compound particle which indicates a standard for comparisons.

examples.japanese: このステーキは日本のステーキとしては安い・安いです。
examples.english: This steak is inexpensive for Japanese steak.

examples.japanese: ジョンソンさんは日本語の一年生としては日本語が上手だ。
examples.english: Mr. Johnson is good at Japanese for a first-year student (of Japanese).

examples.japanese: これは日本のアパートとしては大きい方です。
examples.english: For a Japanese apartment, this is one of the bigger ones.

meaning_en: Be –ed; get –ed
formation:
(i) Group 1 verbs | Vnegれる | | 
 | 話される | Be told | 
(ii) Group 2 verbs | Vstemられる | | 
 | 食べられる | Be eaten | 
(iii) Irregular verbs | 来る→来られる | Someone (X) comes to someone (Y) and Y is unhappy | 
 | する→される | Be done |
explanation: られる (1)A state or an action cannot be controlled by someone or something.

examples.japanese: 一郎は花子に騙された・騙されました。
examples.english: Ichiro was deceived by Hanako.

examples.japanese: ジェーンはフレッドに夜遅くアパートに来られた・来られました。
examples.english: Fred came to Jane's apartment late at night (and Jane was unhappy).

examples.japanese: 私は弟にケーキを食べられた・食べられました。
examples.english: I got my cake eaten by my younger brother. / My younger brother ate my cake (and I was unhappy).

examples.japanese: 田中先生は日本へ帰られた・帰られました。
examples.english: Professor Tanaka went back to Japan (honorific).

examples.japanese: このビルは二年前に建てられた。
examples.english: This building was built two years ago.

examples.japanese: この本は１９６５年にアメリカで出版された。
examples.english: This book was published in America in 1965.

examples.japanese: 私は二年前妻に死なれた。
examples.english: My wife died two years ago (and gave me sorrow).

examples.japanese: 原田さんは奥さんに高いコートを買われた。
examples.english: Mr. Harada's wife bought an expensive coat (and he is unhappy).

examples.japanese: 私は日本語が読める・読めます。
examples.english: I can read Japanese.

examples.japanese: この水は飲めない・飲めません。
examples.english: This water is not drinkable.

meaning_en: Nothing/nobody/no ~ but; only
formation:
(i) Noun | しか | | 
先生が(subject)→ | 先生しか | No one but the teacher | 
先生を(direct object)→ | 先生しか | No one but the teacher | 
(ii) Noun+(Particle) | しか | | 
東京へ・に(direction)→ | 東京(へ・に)しか | To nowhere but Tokyo | 
先生に(indirect object, agent)→ | 先生(に)しか | No one but the teacher | 
日曜日に(time)→ | 日曜日(に)しか | Only on Sunday | 
東京に(location)→ | 東京(に)しか | Only in Tokyo | 
(iii) Noun+Particle | しか | | 
東京で(location)→ | 東京でしか | Only in Tokyo | 
車で(means)→ | 車でしか | Only by car | 
山田さんと(reciprocal)→ | 山田さんとしか | Only with Mr. Yamada | 
東京から(starting point/source)→ | 東京からしか | Only from Tokyo | 
五時まで(ending point)→ | 五時までしか | Only till five o’clock | 
(iv) Quantifier | しか | | 
 | 少ししか | Only a little |
explanation: A particle which marks an element X when nothing but X makes the expressed proposition true.

examples.japanese: 戸田さんしか煙草を吸わない・吸いません。
examples.english: No one but Mr. Toda smokes.

examples.japanese: 私は日本語しか知らない・知りません。
examples.english: I know nothing but Japanese.

examples.japanese: それは江口さんにしか話していない・いません。
examples.english: I haven't told it to anybody but Mr. Eguchi.

examples.japanese: 私はご飯を一杯しか食べなかった・食べませんでした。
examples.english: I had only one bowl of rice.

examples.japanese: パーティーには学生しか来なかった。
examples.english: Only students came to the party.

examples.japanese: 田村さんはサラダしか食べなかった。
examples.english: Mr. Tamura ate only salad.

examples.japanese: 私は日曜日（に）しか来られません。
examples.english: I can come only on Sunday.

examples.japanese: この本はこの図書館（に）しかありません。
examples.english: Only this library has this book.

meaning_en: In ~ of; inside; outside; before; after
explanation: An adverb which forms the comparative of an adjective or an adverb to mean 'more ~ than now or than otherwise'.

examples.japanese: メキシコは赤道より北にある・あります。
examples.english: Mexico is located north of the equator.

examples.japanese: この線より内側に入ってはいけません。
examples.english: You must not get inside this line.

examples.japanese: 三時より前に来て下さい。
examples.english: Please come before three o'clock.

examples.japanese: これより先はバスがありません。
examples.english: There's no bus service from here (beyond this point).

examples.japanese: 私達はいつも、よりよいサービスの提供に努めています。
examples.english: We are always trying to offer better services.

examples.japanese: 外国語は新しい技術を利用すればより効果的に教えることが出来る。
examples.english: We can teach foreign languages more effectively if we utilize new technology.

examples.japanese: 子供達に自分で考えさせる方がより教育的だ。
examples.english: It is more educational to have children think for themselves.

examples.japanese: 今後もより速い、より大容量の記憶装置の開発が続くだろう。
examples.english: The development of faster and larger (literally: of a larger capacity) storage devices will continue from now on, too.

examples.japanese: 私達はより多くの人々にこの施設を利用してもらいたいと思っています。
examples.english: We would like more people to use this facility.

examples.japanese: この車は車体をより軽くするためにアルミの合金を使っている。
examples.english: In order to make the body lighter, aluminium alloy is used for this car.

meaning_en: Speaking of ~
explanation: An expression which presents as the topic of a following discourse a phrase which has just been uttered.

examples.japanese: A:この本は田中さんに借りたんです。  B:田中さんと言えばもう病気は治ったのかしら。
examples.english: A: I borrowed this book from Mr. Tanaka.  B: Speaking of Mr. Tanaka, I wonder if he's gotten over his illness yet.

examples.japanese: A:次の日曜日は京都へ行くつもりだ。  B:京都と言えば、春子が京都大学の入学試験に通ったそうだ。
examples.english: A: I'm going to Kyoto next Sunday.  B: Speaking of Kyoto, I heard that Haruko passed Kyoto University's entrance exam.

examples.japanese: A:小西君はよく休むね。  B:よく休むと言えば、山本君も最近見ませんね。
examples.english: A: Mr. Konishi is absent frequently, isn't he?  B: Talking about about (someone's) frequent absences, we don't see Mr. Yamamoto these days either, do we?

meaning_en: Not ~ any more
formation:
(i) Vinformal negative | なくなる | Where V is often a potential verb | 
 | {話さ /話せ} なくなる | Someone doesn’t talk/can’t talk anymore | 
 | {食べ /食べられ} なくなる | Someone doesn’t/can’t eat any more | 
(ii) Adjective い stem | くなくなる | | 
 | 高くなくなる | Something isn’t expensive any more | 
(iii) {Adjective な stem/ Noun} | {では/じゃ} なくなる | | 
 | {静かでは/静かじゃ} なくなる | Something isn’t quiet any more | 
 | {先生では/先生じゃ} なくなる | Someone isn’t a teacher any more |
explanation: It has reached the point where some state or action does not take place anymore.

examples.japanese: 易しい漢字も書けなくなった・なりました。
examples.english: I cannot even write easy kanji any more.

examples.japanese: 前は酒をよく飲んでいたが、この頃は飲まなくなりました。
examples.english: I used to drink sake a lot, but now I don't drink any more.

examples.japanese: 彼は前よく電話をかけて来ましたが、もうかけて来なくなりました。
examples.english: He used to call me frequently, but he doesn't call me any more.

examples.japanese: 日本語はもう難しくなくなりました。
examples.english: Japanese isn't difficult for me any more.

examples.japanese: この郊外も地下鉄が来て不便ではなくなった。
examples.english: This suburban area is no longer inconvenient because there is a subway now (literally: the subway has reached here).

examples.japanese: やっと大学を出て学生ではなくなりました。
examples.english: I finally graduated from college and am not a student any longer.

meaning_en: Make someone/something do something; cause someone/something to do something; let someone/something do something; allow someone/something to do something; have someone/something do something; get someone/something to do something.
formation:
(i) Group 1 verbs | Vnegative せる | | 
 | 話させる | Cause to talk | 
(ii) Group 2 verbs | Vstem させる | | 
 | 食べさせる | Cause to eat | 
(iii) Irregular verbs | 来る→来させる | Cause to come | 
 | する→させる | Cause to do |
explanation: Cause someone/something to do something or cause something to change its state.

examples.japanese: 鈴木さんは娘を・に大学へ行かせた・行かせました。
examples.english: Mr. Suzuki made/let his daughter go to college.

examples.japanese: 父は妹にピアノを習わせた・習わせました。
examples.english: My father made (or let) my younger sister learn to play the piano.

examples.japanese: 久子は私を困らせた。
examples.english: Hisako made me have trouble. / Hisako caused me trouble.

examples.japanese: このゲームはジムに勝たせようと思う。
examples.english: I think I'll let Jim win this game.

examples.japanese: 友達は私にチップを払わせた。
examples.english: My friend made me leave (lit pay) a tip.

examples.japanese: アンダーソンさんは子供達に好きなだけアイスクリームを食べさせた。
examples.english: Mr. Anderson let his children eat as much ice cream as they liked.

examples.japanese: 私は冷蔵庫でミルクを凍らせた。
examples.english: I made milk freeze (I froze milk) in the refrigerator.

examples.japanese: それは私にさせてください。
examples.english: As for that, let me do it.

meaning_en: Unbearably ~; extremely; be dying to do ~
formation:
Adjective い stem | くて堪らない | | 
 | 寒くて堪らない | Something is unbearable cold | 
Adjective な stem | で堪らない | | 
 | 不便で堪らない | Something is unbearable inconvenient |
explanation: The speaker or whomever he empathises with cannot cope with a situation expressed by the て phrase.

examples.japanese: 今日は暑くて堪らない・堪りません。
examples.english: It is unbearably hot today.

examples.japanese: 数学が嫌いで堪らない・堪りません。
examples.english: I really hate math.

examples.japanese: この本は面白くて堪りません。
examples.english: This book is extremely interesting.

examples.japanese: 父が死んで、悲しくて堪りません。
examples.english: My father died and I'm awfully sad.

examples.japanese: 美味しい魚が食べたくて堪りません。
examples.english: I'm dying to eat some good fish.

examples.japanese: 僕はあの子が好きで堪らない。
examples.english: I just love that girl.

examples.japanese: 兄は田中先生の授業が嫌で堪らなかった。
examples.english: My older brother really hated Mr. Tanaka's class.

meaning_en: With effort; at great pain; take the trouble to do ~
explanation: Some situation which seldom occurs has now occurred and one can either make use of it or, to one’s regret, cannot make use of it.

examples.japanese: せっかく会いに行ったのに友達はいなかった・いませんでした。
examples.english: I took the trouble to go see my friend, but he wasn't at home.

examples.japanese: せっかくいい大学に入ったのだからよく勉強するつもりだ・です。
examples.english: I entered a good college with great effort, so I intend to study hard.

examples.japanese: せっかくの日曜日なのに働いた・働きました。
examples.english: Although Sunday is precious (to me), I worked (all day long).

examples.japanese: せっかくアメリカまで行ったのにニューヨークに行けなくて残念だった。
examples.english: I went as far as America at great expense, but, to my regret, I couldn't make it to New York.

examples.japanese: せっかく日本語を三年間も勉強したのだから、是非一度日本へ行ってみたいと思います。
examples.english: Because I studied Japanese for (as many as) three years, I would love to go to Japan once.

examples.japanese: せっかくの旅行が病気で駄目になりました。
examples.english: My long awaited trip had to be canceled because of my illness.

examples.japanese: せっかくですが今日は忙しくて行けません。
examples.english: I appreciate your most kind offer, but I'm too busy to go there today.

examples.japanese: せっかくのチャンスだからデートしたらどうですか。
examples.english: It's a good chance, so why don't you date her?

meaning_en: Thereupon ~; then ~; and ~
explanation: A coordinate conjunction which connects two sentences (the second sentence either describes an event which takes place right after the event described in the first sentence or it expresses a logical guess related to the event in the first sentence.)

examples.japanese: ジョギングを始めました。するとご飯が美味しくなりました。
examples.english: I began jogging. Then, I began to have a good appetite.

examples.japanese: A:今日は月曜日ですよ。  B:するとあのデパートは休みですね。
examples.english: A: Today is Monday, you know.  B: Then, that department store is closed, isn't it?

examples.japanese: 私は自転車を買いました。すると弟も欲しがりました。
examples.english: I bought a bike. Then, my younger brother wanted one, too.

examples.japanese: 頭が痛かったのでアスピリンを飲みました。すると痛みがすぐ止まりました。
examples.english: I took an aspirin because I had a headache. Then, the headache disappeared right away.

examples.japanese: A:息子は今高校三年です。  B:すると、来年は大学受験ですね。
examples.english: A: My son is now a junior at high school.  B: Then, he is going to take a college entrance examination next year, isn't he?

meaning_en: Or; either ~ or ~
explanation: A coordinate conjunction which connects two alternatives expressed by sentences.

examples.japanese: この本が間違っているか（それとも）私が間違っているかどちらだ・です。
examples.english: It's either that this book is wrong or that I am wrong.

examples.japanese: 刺身を食べますか。それともすき焼きにしますか。
examples.english: Will you have sashimi, or will you have sukiyaki?

examples.japanese: 僕が来るか（それとも）村井さんが来るかどちらかです。
examples.english: Either I will come or Mr. Murai will come.

examples.japanese: あの人は先生ですか。それとも医者ですか。
examples.english: Is he a teacher or a doctor?

explanation: An infix attached to the stem of an adjective い to indicate something that one cannot objectively measure on any scale (e.g. human emotion).

examples.japanese: 悲しい  楽しい  らしい  美味しい  苦しい  頼もしい
examples.english: Sad  enjoyable  seem  delicious  painful  dependable

examples.japanese: 悔しい  厳しい  羨ましい  寂しい  惜しい 妬ましい
examples.english: Regrettable  strict  envious  lonely  regrettable  enviable

examples.japanese: 恐ろしい  難しい  恋しい  嬉しい  親しい  涼しい
examples.english: Scary  difficult  dear  happy  intimate  cool

meaning_en: By; at a time.
explanation: A particle that indicates equal distribution of quantity.

examples.japanese: 私は漢字を毎日五つずつ覚える・覚えます。
examples.english: I memorize five kanji every day.

examples.japanese: 毎月三冊ずつ本を買っています。
examples.english: I'm buying three books per month.

examples.japanese: ゴルフが少しずつ上手になって来た。
examples.english: I have become a better golfer bit by bit.

examples.japanese: 私は子供達に本を二冊ずつやった。
examples.english: I gave two books to each of the children.

examples.japanese: どのクラスにも女子学生が六人ずついた。
examples.english: There were six girl students in each class.

meaning_en: For ~; ~ worth; amount equivalent to ~; portion
formation:
(i) Number+Counter | 分 (のNoun) | | 
 | 五人分の食料 | Food for five people | 
(ii) Noun | 分 | | 
 | 減少分 | The amount by which something decreased |
explanation: A suffix which indicates the amount of something.

examples.japanese: ガソリンを十ドル分入れておきました。
examples.english: I put in ten dollars worth of gas.

examples.japanese: 私は今日三日分の仕事を片付けた。
examples.english: Today I did three days worth of work.

examples.japanese: 現金の不足分は小切手で払います。
examples.english: I'll pay the remaining amount (literally: the amount for which cash is short) by check.

examples.japanese: 会議の資料を六人分用意しておいて下さい。
examples.english: Please get six sets of materials ready for the meeting.

examples.japanese: ここは後でサインをしますので二行分あけておいて下さい。
examples.english: Please leave two lines (of space) here because someone will sign there later.

examples.japanese: 私達は四か月分のボーナスをまらった。
examples.english: We were paid a bonus equivalent to four months pay.

examples.japanese: トラック三台分のごみが出た。
examples.english: Three trucks-full of garbage came out.

examples.japanese: 政府は十万人分の食糧を被災地に送った。
examples.english: The government sent food for 100,000 people to the disaster-stricken area.

meaning_en: But; however; yet; nevertheless
formation:
S1 informal | だが、S2 informal | | 
 | あの人の話は面白い。だが、内容がない。 | His talk is interesting, but there is no content |
explanation: A conjunction that expresses something that is contrasted with what is expressed in the previous sentence.

examples.japanese: 日本の経済力は伸びている。だが、いつまで続くかは分からない。
examples.english: Japanese economic power is growing, but we can't tell how long it will last.

examples.japanese: 都会の生活は便利だ。だが、ストレスが多すぎる。
examples.english: Urban life is convenient. But there are too many stresses.

examples.japanese: 私は彼女とは初めて会った。だが、前から知っていたような親しみを感じた。
examples.english: I met her for the first time; but I felt close to her as if I had known her for a long time.

examples.japanese: 山本は医者に何度も煙草を辞めるように言われた。だが、辞める気はないらしい。
examples.english: Yamamoto was told by his doctor to quit smoking, but he doesn't seem to have any intention of quitting.

examples.japanese: あの人には才能がある。だが、その才能を使っていない。
examples.english: He is talented, but he is not using his talents.

examples.japanese: 今日の試験のために寝ないで勉強した。だが、さっぱり出来なかった。
examples.english: I studied hard for today's exam without sleeping, but I couldn't do it at all.

examples.japanese: 妹はよく勉強するし、頭もいい。だが、成績はなぜかよくない。
examples.english: My younger sister studies hard and she is intelligent, but somehow her grades are not good.

meaning_en: However, it doesn't follow from this that ~; but it doesn't mean that ~; because of that
formation:
S1 | (S2…) だからと言って Sn | Where Sn often ends with わけではない or とは限らない | 
 | 彼は若い。経験も浅い。だからと言って教えられない {わけではない/とは限らない}。 | He is young. He has little experience. But it doesn’t follow from this that he cannot teach |
explanation: A coordinate conjunction indicating that even if one accepts a premise expressed in the preceding sentence(s) one cannot jump to an expected conclusion from the premise.

examples.japanese: チェンさんは日本語が苦手だ。テストではいつも半分も出来ない。だからと言って、頭が悪いわけではない。
examples.english: Mr. Cheng is not good at Japanese. On a test he cannot even finish half of it. But it doesn't follow from this that he is not smart.

examples.japanese: 吉田さんは日本人だ。しかも、小説家だ。だからと言って、日本語が教えられるとは限らない。
examples.english: Ms. Yoshida is Japanese. And she is a novelist. But she may not be able to teach Japanese.

examples.japanese: ジョンは奥さんのことをちっとも褒めない。時々口をきかないこともある。だからと言って、奥さんを愛していないわけではない。
examples.english: John does not praise his wife at all. Sometimes he doesn't talk with her. But it doesn't mean that he doesn't love her.

examples.japanese: 僕は毎日運動をしている。食べ物にも注意している。しかし、だからと言って、長生きする保証はない。
examples.english: I am doing exercise every day. I am also paying attention to what I eat. But it doesn't guarantee that I will live long.

examples.japanese: 日本人は集団行動が好きだと言われる。何をするにも一緒にやる。しかし、だからと言って、個人行動が全くないわけではない。
examples.english: They say that Japanese like group activities. Whatever they do, they do together. But it is not the case that there are no individual activities.

examples.japanese: 魚は健康にいい。しかし、だからと言って、魚ばかり食べていたら、体に悪いはずだ。
examples.english: Fish is good for you. But if you ate nothing but fish, it would be bad for you.

examples.japanese: 日本語はよく難しい言語だと言われる。文法が複雑だし、漢字を覚えるのも大変だ。だからと言って、外国人が学べないわけではない。
examples.english: Japanese is often said to be difficult. The grammar is complex and kanji are hard to memorize. But that doesn't mean foreigners cannot learn it.

meaning_en: Just V-ing is enough; can just ~; just by V-ing
formation:
V informal | だけで | | 
 | {読む/読んだ} だけで | Just by reading |
explanation: A phrase which expresses the idea that just doing something is enough for something.

examples.japanese: 君はここに座っているだけでよい。
examples.english: You can just sit (literally: be sitting) here.

examples.japanese: 私は筆跡を見ただけで誰が書いたか分かった。
examples.english: I knew who wrote it just by looking at the handwriting.

examples.japanese: この植木は二週間に一度水をやるだけでよい。
examples.english: Watering just once every other week is enough for this plant.

examples.japanese: この用紙にサインしていただくだけで結構です。
examples.english: It will be enough if you just sign this form.

examples.japanese: 本当に来るだけでいいんですか。
examples.english: Are you sure that I don't have to do anything except attend?

examples.japanese: その会議では私はただ座っているだけでよかった。
examples.english: At that meeting all I had to do was sit there.

examples.japanese: 村上君は一週間勉強しただけであの試験に通ったそうだ。
examples.english: I heard that Murakami passed that exam just by studying for one week.

examples.japanese: お金を入れてボタンを押すだけで暖かいラーメンが出てくる自動販売機がある。
examples.english: There is a vending machine which serves hot ramen (literally: from which hot ramen comes out) just by inserting coins and pushing a button.

meaning_en: Probably
formation:
Sinformal | であろう | | 
 | {話す/話した} であろう | Will probably talk/probably talked | 
 | {高い/高かった} であろう | Is/was probably expensive | 
 | {静か/静かだった} であろう | Is/was probably quiet | 
 | {先生/先生だった } であろう | Is/was probably a teacher | 
Exception | {Adjective な stem/Noun}であろう | |
explanation: An auxiliary which indicates the writer's conjecture which is not based on any particular information or evidence.

examples.japanese: 日本経済は今後も成長を続けるであろう。
examples.english: The Japanese economy will probably still keep growing (literally: from now on, too).

examples.japanese: このようなブームはもう二度と起こらないであろう。
examples.english: Such a boom will probably not happen again.

examples.japanese: この次に起こる地震は非常に大きいであろうと予想される。
examples.english: It is expected that the next earthquake will (probably) be very strong.

examples.japanese: その交渉は極めて困難であろう。
examples.english: That negotiation will probably be very difficult.

examples.japanese: この辺りは昔、湖だったであろうと思われる。
examples.english: I think that this area was probably a lake a long time ago.

meaning_en: Be
formation:
(i) Noun | である | | 
 | 先生である | Be a teacher | 
(ii) Adjective な stem | である | | 
 | 静かである | Be quiet |
explanation: A copula which is used in formal writing and formal speech.

examples.japanese: 「坊っちゃん」は漱石の初期の代表作である。
examples.english: Botchan is representative of Soseki's early work.

examples.japanese: 今年の水不足は極めて深刻である。
examples.english: The water shortage this year is extremely serious.

examples.japanese: 人間は考える葦である。
examples.english: “Man is a thinking reed.”

examples.japanese: 日本語があいまいな言語であるというのは誤りである。
examples.english: (The idea) that Japanese is an ambiguous language is wrong.

examples.japanese: 大型車に一人で乗るのは不経済である。
examples.english: Using a big car for one person is uneconomical.

examples.japanese: 彼に何度も手紙を書いたが無駄であった。
examples.english: I wrote him many letters but it was useless.

examples.japanese: 日本語では文脈から分かることは原則として言わないのである。
examples.english: In principle, in Japanese we do not say what is understood from context.

examples.japanese: 彼らが出来ないのは練習していないからである。
examples.english: It is because they haven't practiced that they can't do it.

meaning_en: I don't know why but; I cannot manage to; just; from what I gather; seem; no matter how ~; I gather that ~; for some reason
formation:
(i) どうも~ | {V /Adjective (い/な)} negative | | 
 | どうも話せない | No matter how one tries, someone can’t talk | 
 | どうも食べられない | No matter how one tries, someone doesn’t eat | 
 | どうもよくない | I don’t know why but something isn’t good | 
 | どうも上手じゃない | I don’t know why, but someone is not good at something | 
(ii) どうも~ | {V /Adjective い} informal {らしい/ようだ} | | 
 | どうも話す{らしい/ようだ} | I gather that someone is going to talk | 
 | どうも食べる{らしい/ようだ} | I gather that someone is going to eat | 
 | どうも高い{らしい/ようだ} | I gather that something is expensive | 
(iii) どうも~ | Adjective な stem {らしい/ようだ} or Adjective な stem だった{らしい/ようだ} | | 
 | どうも静か{らしい/ようだ} | I gather that something is quiet |
explanation: An adverb to indicate that one cannot make a definite statement about something due to lack of hard evidence.

examples.japanese: この文の意昧がどうもよく分からない。
examples.english: I tried, but I cannot understand the meaning of this Japanese sentence very well.

examples.japanese: 鈴木さんはどうも京都大学に入りたいらしい。
examples.english: I gather that Mr. Suzuki wants to enter Kyoto University.

examples.japanese: あの先生の授業はどうも面白くない。
examples.english: I don't know why, but that instructor's class is uninteresting.

examples.japanese: このごろどうも体の詞子がよくないんです。
examples.english: I don't know why, but lately I don't feel very good.

examples.japanese: あの人の日本語はどうも聞きにくい。
examples.english: I don't know why, but his Japanese is hard to listen to.

examples.japanese: 先生、この間題の意味がどうもつかめないんです。
examples.english: Professor, I can't manage to grasp the intent of this problem.

examples.japanese: こんな田舎に住むのはどうも不便だ。
examples.english: It is just inconvenient to live in such countryside.

examples.japanese: うちの子はテレビばかり見て、どうも本を読まない。
examples.english: I don't know why, but our kids are always watching TV and do not read books.

meaning_en: How ~ (!)
formation:
(i) | どんなに～(こと)か | | 
 | どんなに難しいことか。 | How difficult something is! | 
(ii) | どんなに～か Predicate | | 
 | どんなに面白いか知らない。 | Someone doesn’t know how interesting something is |
explanation: どんなに~（こと）か - A structure that indicates an exclamation about the degree to which an action or state takes/took place.

examples.japanese: 兄は病気が治ってどんなに嬉しかったことか。
examples.english: How glad my elder brother was when he recovered from his illness!

examples.japanese: 父は母をどんなに愛していたことか。
examples.english: How dearly my father loved my mother!

examples.japanese: 日本へ行くまで日本がどんなに狭いか分からなかった。
examples.english: I didn't realise how small Japan was until I got to Japan.

examples.japanese: 英夫は由美子に結婚を断られた時にどんなに残念に思ったことか。
examples.english: How disappointed Hideo must have felt when Yumiko refused to marry him.

examples.japanese: 勉強が嫌いだった良夫には大学に入るのがどんなに難しかったか。
examples.english: For Yoshio, who didn't like to study, how hard it was to enter college!

examples.japanese: 圭子はどんなにフランスに留学したかったことか！
examples.english: How strongly Keiko wanted to go to France!

examples.japanese: 学生達はその厳しい先生をどんなに強く憎んだことか！
examples.english: How strongly the students hated their strict teacher!

examples.japanese: 駅前のアパートはどんなに便利だったことか！
examples.english: How convenient my apartment right in front of the station was!

meaning_en: In any case; anyway; at all events; after all; at all
explanation: An adverb that indicates the speaker/writer's feeling that no matter what s/he does or how s/he does it, the situation will not change.

examples.japanese: 受けても、どうせ、駄目だから、文部省の留学生試験を受けないことにしました。
examples.english: I decided not to try for the Education Ministry's Scholarship, because I'd be doomed to failure.

examples.japanese: どうせ外国旅行をするんなら、若いうちにした方がいい。
examples.english: If you make a trip abroad at all, it's better to do it when you are young.

examples.japanese: どうせこんな沢山の宿題、出来るわけがないから、遊ぶことにしたよ。
examples.english: I cannot do this much homework anyway, so I've decided to play.

examples.japanese: 人間はどうせ死ぬんだから、あくせく働いても仕方がない。
examples.english: Since we humans are bound to die, it is no use working hard.

examples.japanese: どうせ捨てられるのに、どうして彼の後を追うの?
examples.english: Why are you following him, when you are well aware that you are going to be dumped after all?

examples.japanese: どうせあの女性とは結婚出来ないよ。早くあきらめた方がいいよ。
examples.english: You cannot marry that woman anyway. You'd better give her up as soon as possible.

examples.japanese: Ａ：君はこんなことが分からないのかい? Ｂ：どうせ私は馬鹿ですよ。
examples.english: A: Don't you understand this simple matter? B: I'm stupid, as you know.

examples.japanese: どうせ来週日本へ行きますから、その辞書は日本で買います。
examples.english: I'm going to Japan next week anyway, so I'll buy that dictionary over there.

meaning_en: In ~ manner; after ~ style; a la ~; like
formation:
(i) {Noun/こんな/そんな/あんな/どんな} | 風に | Like {Noun/this/that/that ~ over there}, in what manner? | 
 | 西洋風に | In Western style | 
 | こんな風に | Like this | 
(ii) Sinformal | という風に | Like | 
 | 行かないという風に(聞いている) | (I hear) that someone doesn’t go there | 
 | 今日はデート、明日はコンサートという風に | Like a date one day and a concert the next |
explanation: With an appearance/style/tone/manner of ~.

examples.japanese: 私の家の庭は日本風に大きい石が置いてあります。
examples.english: The yard of my house has big rocks arranged in Japanese style.

examples.japanese: あんな風に勉強していたらいい成績は取れないだろう。
examples.english: If he studies like that, he won't get good grades.

examples.japanese: 私は先生に頭がいいんだからもっと勉強しろという風によく言われた。
examples.english: I was often told by my teacher that I have to study harder because I am smart.

examples.japanese: Ａ：これはどんな風に持ったらいいんですか。 Ｂ：こんな風に持って下さい。
examples.english: A: How should I hold this? B: Please hold it like this.

examples.japanese: あんな風に毎日飲んでいたら、きっと病気になるでしょう。
examples.english: If he keeps drinking like that every day, he will surely become ill.

examples.japanese: このカレーライスはインド風に、とても辛くしてあります。
examples.english: We have made this curried rice very spicy like an Indian version.

examples.japanese: ジェミーが日本風のお辞儀をした時にはびっくりした。
examples.english: I was surprised when Jemmy bowed in Japanese style.

examples.japanese: 京子は、今日はお花、あすはダンスという風に、毎日何かを習いに行っている。
examples.english: Kyoko goes out every day to take lessons, like flower arrangement one day and dance, the next.

meaning_en: Contrary to one's expectation; contrary to one's intention; conversely
explanation: An adverb to introduce an event which takes place contrary to one's expectation/intention, or an action or event which is converse to that stated in the preceding sentence or clause.

examples.japanese: 薬を飲んだら、逆に熱が出た。
examples.english: Contrary to expectations, when I took medicine, I got a fever.

examples.japanese: 叱られると思ったのに、逆にほめられた。
examples.english: I expected to be scolded but, contrary to my expectation, I was praised.

examples.japanese: 会話を強調すると文法が不正確になる。逆に文法を強調すると話せなくなる。
examples.english: 1. If we emphasize conversation, their grammar becomes inaccurate. 2. Conversely, if we emphasize grammar, they are (literally: become) unable to speak.

examples.japanese: しばらく練習をしなかったら、逆に成績が伸びた。
examples.english: I didn't practice for some time; then, contrary to expectations, my performance improved.

examples.japanese: 寝すぎると、元気にならないで、逆に疲れてしまう。
examples.english: If you sleep too much, you don't feel well; instead (literally: conversely), you feel tired.

examples.japanese: 文句を言ってやろうと思っていたら、逆に文句を言われてしまった。
examples.english: I was thinking of complaining; then, contrary to my intention, I had to listen to complaints.

examples.japanese: 一生懸命仕事をしたのに、逆に仲間に嫌われてしまった。
examples.english: I worked very hard, but, contrary to expectations, my peers hated me.

examples.japanese: ガールフレンドを喜ばせようとしたのに、逆に怒らせてしまった。
examples.english: I tried to please my girlfriend, but, contrary to my intention, I made her angry.

meaning_en: Other than; except (for); but; besides; as well as
formation:
(i) Noun | 以外(のNoun) | | 
 | コーヒー以外(の飲み物) | (drinks) other than coffee | 
(ii) Sinformal | 以外 | だ after Adjective な stem and Noun changes to である | 
 | 勉強する以外 | Besides studying | 
 | 高い以外 | Besides the fact that something is expensive | 
 | 便利である以外 | Besides the fact that something is convenient | 
 | 先生である以外 | Besides the fact that someone is a teacher |
explanation: A dependent noun which means "something/someone other than".

examples.japanese: 山田さん以外の人はみんなそのことを知っています。
examples.english: Everybody except Yamada knows it.

examples.japanese: 日本語以外に何か外国語が話せますか。
examples.english: Can you speak any foreign language besides Japanese?

examples.japanese: 私には酒を飲む以外に何も楽しみがない。
examples.english: I have nothing to enjoy other than drinking.

examples.japanese: 私は日本酒以外の酒は飲まない。
examples.english: I do not drink any alcohol but sake.

examples.japanese: 我々の会社では現在オーストラリア以外の国と取引はない。
examples.english: At present our company is not dealing with any countries but Australia.

examples.japanese: アメリカ以外の国からも沢山研究者が来た。
examples.english: Many researchers came from countries other than America, too.

examples.japanese: 原因はこれ以外に考えられない。
examples.english: I can't think of any causes other than this.

examples.japanese: 私は散歩以外にも毎日軽い運動をしている。
examples.english: I take (other) light exercise every day as well as taking a walk.

meaning_en: Really; truly; indeed
explanation: An adverb that indicates the speaker/writer's emotive conviction.

examples.japanese: アメリカ人の目から見ると、日本の社会はいかにも閉鎖的だ。
examples.english: From an American perspective, Japanese society is indeed closed.

examples.japanese: 外は雪が降っていて、いかにも寒そうだ。
examples.english: It is snowing outside, and it looks really cold.

examples.japanese: 彼の書斎の本棚には古今東西の本が詰まっていて、いかにも学者の部屋らしい。
examples.english: The bookshelves of his study room are packed with books of all ages and countries, and it surely looks like a scholar's room.

examples.japanese: 先生は最近いかにもお忙しいよう / 様子だ。
examples.english: These days the professor appears to be really busy.

examples.japanese: 日本人は集団行動がいかにも好きではあるが、個人行動をしないわけではない。
examples.english: The Japanese indeed like group behaviour, but it is not the case that they do not behave individually.

examples.japanese: 彼はいかにも紳士であるかのように振る舞っているが、なかなかの策士だ。
examples.english: He is behaving as if he were truly a gentleman, but he is quite calculated.

examples.japanese: 彼の発想はいかにも日本的だ。
examples.english: His manner of thinking is very Japanese.

examples.japanese: その教授の知識はいかにも百科全書的だ。
examples.english: The professor's knowledge is really encyclopaedic.

meaning_en: On the contrary; rather
explanation: Contrary to one's expectation an opposite result comes about.

examples.japanese: 薬を飲んだら、かえって病気がひどくなった。
examples.english: I took medicine, and the illness got worse (contrary to my expectation).

examples.japanese: Ａ：一時間も泳いで、疲れたでしょう。 Ｂ：いや、かえって元気になったよ。
examples.english: A: You must be tired after swimming as long as one hour. B: No, on the contrary, I feel fit now.

examples.japanese: 日本へ行ったら日本語が上手になるかと思って、日本へ行ったんですが、日本人と英語でばかり話していたので、かえって、下手になって帰って来ました。
examples.english: I went to Japan, believing that my Japanese will improve (if I go) there, but I spoke only in English with Japanese there, so (contrary to my expectation) my Japanese became worse when I came back here.

examples.japanese: 就職のことで三人の先生にアドバイスをしてもらったのですが、アドバイスが全然違うので、かえって、分からなくなってしまいました。
examples.english: I was given advice on job searching from three professors, but their advices are so different that I am rather at a loss.

examples.japanese: いわゆる一流大学で勉強するより小さな私立大学で勉強する方が、かえって、いい教育を受けることが出来る。
examples.english: (Contrary to your expectation) if you study at a small, private college, you can receive better education than to study at the so-called first-rate university.

examples.japanese: アルコールも適量飲めば、かえって、体にいいそうだ。
examples.english: Alcohol is said to be rather good for your health if you drink it in moderate quantity.

meaning_en: Not always; not necessarily
formation:
(i) 必ずしも{Vinformal/Adjectiveい} | とは{限ら /言え/思わ}ない | | 
 | 必ずしも{静か/先生}ではない | Something is not always quiet/someone is not always a teacher |
explanation: An adverb that indicates that the proposition expressed in the sentence is not always true.

examples.japanese: 頭のいい人が、必ずしも成功するとは限らない。
examples.english: A bright person does not always succeed.

examples.japanese: 高い料理が必ずしも美味しいわけではない。
examples.english: Expensive dishes are not always delicious.

examples.japanese: 記憶力のいい人が必ずしも外国語が上手だとは言えない。
examples.english: One cannot always say that people with good memories are good at foreign languages.

examples.japanese: 日本人が必ずしもいい日本語の先生だとは思わない。
examples.english: I don't think that a Japanese is always a good Japanese language teacher.

examples.japanese: 結婚しても必ずしも幸福になるとは言えない。
examples.english: One cannot always say that marriage brings happiness.

examples.japanese: 運動をよくする人が必ずしも長生きするとは限らない。
examples.english: People who exercise regularly do not always live long.

examples.japanese: 日本へ行った学生が日本語が上手になるかというと、必ずしもそうではない。
examples.english: Students who have been to Japan do not always become proficient in Japanese.

examples.japanese: お金は人を必ずしも幸福にはしない。
examples.english: Money does not always bring happiness to people.

meaning_en: Through ~ into ~; through ~ on to; from ~ till/to
formation:
Noun | からNounにかけて | | 
 | 一月から二月にかけて | From January through February |
explanation: から~にかけて A structure that expresses coverage from one time/location into the other.

examples.japanese: 今年の夏、七月から八月にかけて中国大陸を旅行した。
examples.english: This summer I travelled on the Chinese continent from July through August.

examples.japanese: 今週は木曜から金曜にかけて雪が降るでしょう。
examples.english: This week it will probably snow from Thursday through Friday.

examples.japanese: 日本は六月から七月にかけて梅雨が続く。
examples.english: In Japan the rainy season continues through June and July.

examples.japanese: 高気圧が朝鮮半島から九州にかけて張り出している。
examples.english: High atmospheric pressure extends from the Korean Peninsula up through Kyushu.

meaning_en: Just because; even if; even though
formation:
Sinformal | からと言って | | 
 | 高いからと言って | Because/even if/even though it is expensive |
explanation: A conjunction which introduces the reason for someone's action or for someone's having some idea, and conveys disapproval of the action or idea.

examples.japanese: 子供だからと言って許すわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I cannot forgive him just because he is a child.

examples.japanese: 何も不平を言わないからと言って現状に満足しているわけではない。
examples.english: Even though I don't complain, it doesn't mean that I'm satisfied with the present situation.

examples.japanese: 試験に受からなかったからと言ってそんなに悲観することはない。
examples.english: You don't have to be so pessimistic because you didn't pass the exam.

examples.japanese: 弁償したからと言って済む問題ではない。
examples.english: It is not a problem which will be solved because you have paid / will pay compensation.

examples.japanese: 上司の命令だからと言って黙って従うわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I cannot obey the order without asking questions even if it is from my boss.

examples.japanese: アメリカへ行ったからと言って勝手に英語が上手になるものではない。
examples.english: Your English will not improve (itself / automatically) even if you go to America.

examples.japanese: 毎日授業に出ているからと言って真面目に勉強していることにはならない。
examples.english: Even though he goes to class every day, it doesn't mean that he is studying seriously.

examples.japanese: こんなことを言うからと言って別に批判しているわけではない。
examples.english: Even though I tell you such a thing, it doesn't mean that I'm criticizing you.

meaning_en: Probably
formation:
(i) Adjective い stem | かろう | | 
 | 面白かろう | Someone/something is probably interesting | 
 | よかろう | Someone/something is probably good | 
 | なかろう | Someone/something does not probably exist | 
(ii) {Adjective い stem く (は)/Adjective な stem/Noun} | なかろう | | 
 | 面白く(は)なかろう | Someone/something is probably not interesting | 
 | 困難ではなかろう | Something is probably not hard | 
 | 学者ではなかろう | Someone is probably not a scholar |
explanation: An auxiliary indicating the writer's conjecture which is not based on any particular information or evidence.

examples.japanese: 十年後の自分を予想するのは難しかろう。
examples.english: It is probably difficult to predict what one's self will be like in ten years time.

examples.japanese: この研究を一年で完成するのは極めて難しかろう。
examples.english: It is probably extremely difficult to complete this research in one year.

examples.japanese: 日本人の中にも創造性のない教育に反対する人は多かろう。
examples.english: Even among the Japanese, there are probably a lot of people who oppose education without creativity.

examples.japanese: 私のように文化は宗教のようなものだと考えている人は少なかろう。
examples.english: Few people probably think, as I do, that culture is something like religion.

examples.japanese: アメリカの大学のように、日本の大学でも学生に教師の評価をさせるとよかろう。
examples.english: It would probably be good if Japanese universities allowed students to evaluate instructors as American universities do.

examples.japanese: 人種偏見ほど人間に根深いものはなかろう。
examples.english: Nothing is probably as deep-rooted in humans as racial prejudices.

examples.japanese: 近い将来に日米関係に大きな変化はなかろう。
examples.english: There will probably not be a big change in the US-Japan relationship in the near future.

examples.japanese: あの二人の間柄は親しくはなかろう。
examples.english: The relationship between the two is probably not close.

meaning_en: Do something in a ~ fashion/manner/way
formation:
(i) | {Adjective い informal/Adjective な stem な/Vinformal} + (Noun の) +Vます方をする | | 
 | ひどい負け方をする | Lose in a terrible way | 
 | ユニークなものも見方をする | View things in a unique fashion | 
 | よく分かる教え方をする | Teach clearly (literally: in a way one can understand well) | 
(ii) Noun | のような+(Nounの)+ Vます方をする | | 
 | 子供のようなものの言い方をする | Talk like a child (literally: talk in a child like manner) | 
(iii) Vinformal | ような+(Nounの)+ Vます方をする | Adjectives rarely occur before ような | 
 | 人が感動するような話し方をする | Speak in such a way that people are impressed |
explanation: A phrase to indicate a manner of doing something.

examples.japanese: 林田先生は厳しい教え方をする。
examples.english: Professor Hayashida teaches in a strict manner.

examples.japanese: 昭は変わったものの見方をする。
examples.english: Akira views things in a peculiar fashion.

examples.japanese: ブラウンさんは日本人のような考え方をする。
examples.english: Mr. Brown thinks like the Japanese.

examples.japanese: 誰にでも分かるような書き方をして下さい。
examples.english: Please write in such a way that anyone can understand it.

examples.japanese: あのピッチャーは面白い投げ方をする。
examples.english: That pitcher throws (a ball) in an interesting way.

examples.japanese: 吉田君は乱暴な運転のし方をするので乗せてもらうのが怖い。
examples.english: I'm afraid of getting a ride from Yoshida because he drives carelessly (literally: in a wild fashion).

examples.japanese: 正はほかの学生と違った勉強のし方をしているようだ。
examples.english: Tadashi seems to study in a different way from other students.

examples.japanese: 私には野村先生のような考え方は出来ない。
examples.english: I cannot think like Professor Nomura.

meaning_en: You would think that ~ but (that is not right)
formation:
(i) ~{V/Adjective い} informal | かと言うと、S | | 
 | {話す /話した} かと言うと | You would think that someone talks/talked but ~ | 
 | {高い /高かった} かと言うと | You would think that something is/was expensive but ~ | 
(ii) {Adjective な stem/ Noun} | {Ø/だった} かと言うと、S | | 
 | {静か /静かだった} かと言うと | You would think that something is/was quiet but ~ | 
 | {先生/先生だった} かと言うと | You would think that someone is/was a teacher but ~ |
explanation: A conjunction to indicate the speaker's assertion that a popular belief is not right.

examples.japanese: 日本人はみんな寿司が好きかと言うと、そうではない。嫌いな人もいる。
examples.english: You would think that all the Japanese like sushi, but that is not true. Some Japanese don't like it.

examples.japanese: がんは治らない病気かと言うと、そうではない。早期発見をすれば治ると言われている。
examples.english: You would think that cancer is not curable, but that is not true. If it is detected early it is said to be curable.

examples.japanese: 日本に行って、二、三年住めば日本語が上手になるかと言うと、そうでもないようだ。かえって下手になることもある。
examples.english: You'd think that if you went to Japan and lived there for a few years, your Japanese would become good, but that doesn't seem to be true. On the contrary, your Japanese may become worse than before.

examples.japanese: 大学の時にいい成績の学生が社会で成功するかと言うと、必ずしもそうではないようだ。
examples.english: You'd think that a college student with good grades would be successful in society, but that doesn't always seem to be the case.

examples.japanese: 毎日運動をすれば長生きをするかと言うと、そうでもなさそうだ。
examples.english: You'd think that if you did exercise every day, you would live long, but that does not seem to be true.

examples.japanese: 日本語は難しいかと言うと、話したり聞いたりすることはそんなに難しくない。
examples.english: You'd think that Japanese would be hard, but speaking and listening are not that hard.

examples.japanese: ボストンでの車なしの生活が不便だったかと言うと、全然そうではなかったんです。
examples.english: You'd think that my life without a car in Boston must have been inconvenient, but it wasn't at all.

meaning_en: Instead of; instead; but (to make up for ~); so (to make up for ~); in place of
formation:
(i) {V/Adjective い} informal | 代わりに | | 
 | 話す代わりに | Instead of talking | 
 | 高い代わりに | Instead of being expensive | 
(ii) Adjective な stem | {な/だった}代わりに | | 
 | 静か{な/だった}代わりに | Is/was quiet but (to make up for ~) | 
(iii) Noun | {の/だった}代わりに | | 
 | 先生の代わりに | In place of the teacher | 
 | いい先生だった代わりに | Someone was a good teacher, but (to make up for ~) |
explanation: （の）代わりに An action/state that is expressed in the subordinate clause is balanced by another action/state expressed in the main clause, or something/someone that is replaced by something/someone else.

examples.japanese: 昼間遊ぶ代わりに夜勉強するつもりだ。
examples.english: I am going to enjoy myself in the daytime, so /but (to make up for it) I will study at night.

examples.japanese: 山田さんにはちょっと余分に働いてもらった代わりに特別手当てを出した。
examples.english: Mr. Yamada worked for us a bit extra, so / but (to make up-for it) we paid him special compensation.

examples.japanese: 前のアパートは設備が悪かった代わりに家賃が安かった。
examples.english: The former apartment had bad facilities, so /but (to make up for it) the rent was cheap.

examples.japanese: 今朝は、コーヒーの代わりにココアを飲んだ。
examples.english: This morning I drank cocoa instead of coffee.

examples.japanese: 今日は図書館で勉強する代わりに寮の部屋で勉強した。
examples.english: Today I didn't study in the library. Instead, I studied in my dorm room.

examples.japanese: 私はトムに日本語を教えてあげた代わりに彼に英語を教えてもらった。
examples.english: I taught Tom Japanese, so (to make up for it) he taught me English.

examples.japanese: 高い長距離電話をかける代わりに、手紙をよく書いています。
examples.english: Instead of making expensive long distance calls I often write letters.

examples.japanese: 私のアパートは家賃が高い代わりに、駅に近くてとても便利です。
examples.english: My apartment is expensive, but it is close to the station and very convenient.

meaning_en: Quite; rather; pretty
explanation: An adverb that indicates that something exceeds the speaker's and/or hearer's expectation to a considerable degree.

examples.japanese: ここの寿司は、結構美味しいね。
examples.english: The sushi in this place is quite good, isn't it?

examples.japanese: この車は古いんだけど、結構よく走りますよ。
examples.english: This car is old, but it runs quite well, you know.

examples.japanese: あの人は間抜けに見えるでしょう。でも、結構頭がいいんです。
examples.english: He looks dumb, but he is quite sharp.

examples.japanese: 四月だというのに、結構寒いね。
examples.english: It is April, but it is rather cold, isn't it?

examples.japanese: 小さい町なのに、結構いいレストランがあるね。
examples.english: There are quite a few good restaurants in this small town, aren't there?

examples.japanese: この料理は量は少ないけど、結構胃にもたれるね。
examples.english: This dish is small in quantity, but it is pretty heavy on the stomach.

examples.japanese: 今日は日曜日なのに高速が結構混んでいるね。
examples.english: Today is Sunday, but the highway is rather crowded, isn't it?

examples.japanese: 父は楽天的な人でしたが、失職した時に結構悩んだようです。
examples.english: My father was an optimist, but when he lost his job, I think he suffered quite a bit.

meaning_en: The last; this past; this; this coming
formation:
(i) この | Noun | | 
 | この秋 | This autumn; this coming autumn | 
(ii) この | Number+Counter | | 
 | この一年 | This past year; this coming year |
explanation: A demonstrative adjective which indicates a time or time period around the moment of speech.

examples.japanese: 秋山さんはこの春結婚します。
examples.english: Miss Akiyama will marry (this spring / this coming spring).

examples.japanese: 山下君はこの一週間授業を休んでいます。
examples.english: Yamashita has been absent from class for the past (one) week.

examples.japanese: この間吉岡さんに会いました。
examples.english: I met Mr. Yoshioka the other day.

examples.japanese: このたびこの会の会員に加えていただきました。
examples.english: I became a member of this club at this time.

examples.japanese: この際車を買おうか。
examples.english: Shall we buy a car given this occasion?

examples.japanese: この辺で妥協したらどうですか。
examples.english: Why don't we compromise now (literally: around this time)?

examples.japanese: この夏は日本の女流作家の研究しています。
examples.english: This summer I'm doing research on Japanese female writers.

examples.japanese: この一週間は忙しくて何もできないだろう。
examples.english: I'll be busy this coming week and probably won't be able to do anything (else).

meaning_en: Such; like this
formation:
こうした | Noun | | 
 | こうした人々 | Such people |
explanation: A demonstrative which refers to someone or something mentioned as an example in previous discourse.

examples.japanese: こうした問題はこの国では聞かれないようである。
examples.english: We do not seem to hear about problems like this in this country.

examples.japanese: こうした行為がどのような結果を招くかは誰の目にも明らかだ。
examples.english: It is clear to anyone what kind of result such behaviour brings about.

examples.japanese: こうした経験は日本へ行ったことのある者なら誰にでもあるはずだ。
examples.english: Anyone who has been to Japan would have had such an experience.

examples.japanese: 私はこうした話には耳を貸さないことにしている。
examples.english: I make it a rule not to listen to such stories.

meaning_en: By V-ing; because; result in; cause
formation:
(i) Vinformal nonpast | ことで | Means | 
 | 行くことで | By going | 
(ii) Sinformal | ことで | Cause | 
 | {行く /行った} ことで | Because someone will go/went | 
 | {高い /高かった} ことで | Because something is/was high | 
(iii) Adjective な stem | なことで | Exception | 
 | 便利なことで | Because something is convenient | 
(iv) Noun | であることで | Exception | 
 | 女であることで | Because someone is a woman |
explanation: A compound particle which indicates a means or a cause.

examples.japanese: 私は週末にゴルフをすることで気分転換を図っています。
examples.english: I try to lift my spirits by playing golf on weekends.

examples.japanese: 彼が仲裁の場に出ていったことで事態は余計にこじれた。
examples.english: His appearance at the mediation scene complicated the situation even more. (literally: The situation got even more complicated because he appeared at the mediation scene.)

examples.japanese: 私が十万円出すことで問題は解決した。
examples.english: The problem was solved by my paying 100,000 yen.

examples.japanese: 彼女はものを言わないことで私へ精一杯の抵抗を示しているのです。
examples.english: She is demonstrating her utmost resistance to me by not talking.

examples.japanese: 朝晩簡単な体操をするだけのことで素晴らしい健康が保てます。
examples.english: You can maintain wonderful health just by taking simple exercise in the morning and evening.

examples.japanese: 私が参加することであなたに迷惑はかかりませんか。
examples.english: Wouldn't my participation cause you trouble?

examples.japanese: 彼のパーティーに行かなかったことで彼の気持ちを害したのでなければよいが。
examples.english: I hope I didn't hurt his feelings because I didn't go to his party (literally: by not having gone to his party).

examples.japanese: 私は英語が下手ことで時々損をしている。
examples.english: I am sometimes put at a disadvantage because I am poor at English.

meaning_en: Be due to the fact that; be caused by; be brought about by; be the result of; because
formation:
Sinformal | ことによる | Exceptions: Adjective な stem なことによる; Noun であることによる | 
 | 家賃が高いことによる | Because the rent is expensive | 
 | 表現が不正確なことによる | Because the expression is inaccurate | 
 | 母が日本人であることによる | Because one’s mother is Japanese |
explanation: A phrase which is used to present an event as the cause of something.

examples.japanese: 今回の失敗は事前の話し合いが不十分だったことによる。
examples.english: The failure this time is the result of insufficient discussion beforehand (literally: due to the fact that the preceding discussion was insufficient).

examples.japanese: 進が非行に走ったの両親の愛情が不足していたことによる。
examples.english: Susumu's delinquency was caused by his parents' lack of affection. (literally: The fact that Susumu ran to juvenile delinquency is because his parents were not affectionate enough with him.

examples.japanese: 彼の現在の成功は平生の努力を怠らなかったことによる。
examples.english: His present success is due to the fact that he worked hard every day (literally: did not neglect daily effort).

examples.japanese: 彼らの離婚は二人の価値観があまりに違っていたことによる。
examples.english: Their divorce was caused by the fact that their value systems were very different.

examples.japanese: 彼が負けたのは勝ちを焦りすぎたことによる。
examples.english: His loss is due to the fact that he tried to win quickly.

examples.japanese: 彼の才能がこれ程までに開発されたのは鈴木氏に師事したことによる。
examples.english: That his talent was developed to this degree is due to the fact that he studied with Mr. Suzuki.

meaning_en: And; so
explanation: A continuative form of an い-type adjective.

examples.japanese: 加奈子の性格は明るく、無邪気だった。
examples.english: Kanako's personality was cheerful and innocent.

examples.japanese: せっかく講演をしに行ったのに、聴衆が少なく、がっかりした。
examples.english: I went all the way to give a lecture, but the audience was so small that I felt discouraged.

examples.japanese: カルフォルニアの空は青く、美しかった。
examples.english: The Californian sky was blue and beautiful.

examples.japanese: トムの東京のアパートの部屋は暗く、狭い。
examples.english: Tom's apartment room in Tokyo is dark and small.

examples.japanese: バッハの音楽は歯切れがよく、幾何学的だ。
examples.english: Bach's music is very crisp and geometrical.

examples.japanese: ニューヨークタイムズは質が高く、購読者の数も多い。
examples.english: The New York Times is high in quality and has many subscribers.

examples.japanese: 世界の平和は得られにくく、維持しにくい。
examples.english: World peace is hard to achieve and hard to maintain.

examples.japanese: あの哲学者の思想は分かりやすく、文章も簡潔だ。
examples.english: That philosopher's ideas are easy to understand and his writing is simple, too.

meaning_en: Although; in spite of the fact that; and yet; but
formation:
(i) Noun | のくせに | | 
 | 子供のくせに | Although ~ is a child | 
(ii) {V/Adjective い} informal | くせに | | 
 | {出来る/出来た} くせに | Although ~ can/could | 
 | {弱い/弱かった} くせに | Although ~ is/was weak | 
(iii) Adjective な stem | {な / だった} くせに | | 
 | {下手な / 下手 だった} くせに | Although ~ is/was bad at something |
explanation: A conjunction which expresses the speaker's contempt, anger, or disagreement about someone's action, behaviour, or state.

examples.japanese: 山田さんは日本人のくせにあまり漢字を知らない。
examples.english: Although Mr. Yamada is Japanese, he doesn't know many kanji.

examples.japanese: 山内はよく知っているくせに何も教えてくれない。
examples.english: In spite of the fact that Yamauchi knows a lot about it, he doesn't tell me anything.

examples.japanese: 彼は大学生のくせに漫画ばかり読んでいる。
examples.english: Although he is a college student, all he does is read comics.

examples.japanese: 良子はまだ学生のくせに高いマンションに住んでいる。
examples.english: Although Yoshiko is still a student, she lives in an expensive condominium.

examples.japanese: 隆司は下手なくせに私とテニスをしたがる。
examples.english: Takashi is a bad (tennis) player, and yet he wants to play with me.

examples.japanese: 怖いくせに無理するなよ。
examples.english: You are afraid. Don't pretend to be strong.

examples.japanese: 孝男はお金もないくせに外車を欲しがっている。
examples.english: Takao doesn't have money, and yet he wants a foreign car.

examples.japanese: 吉田は前は私を見ても挨拶もしなかったくせに、私が部長になった途端に急に愛想がよくなった。
examples.english: Before (the time I became a division chief), Yoshida never greeted me when he saw me, but he suddenly became friendly when I became a division chief.

meaning_en: Incredible; never thought; never dreamed; surely not; impossible; don't tell me that ~; not at all likely; absolutely not.
formation:
(i) まさかSとは | {思わなかった/考えてもみなかった} | | 
 | まさか雪が降るとは{思わなかった/考えてもみなかった} | {I didn’t believe/I never though} that it would snow | 
(ii) まさかS | {んじゃ/のでは} ないだろうね | | 
 | まさか会社を辞める{んじゃ/のでは}ないだろうね | Don’t tell me that you are going to quit the company | 
(iii) まさかS | はずがない | | 
 | まさか四月に雪が降るはずがない | It is not at all likely that it will snow in April | 
(iv) まさかS | まい | | 
 | まさか雪は降るまい | Don’t tell me it’s going to snow |
explanation: An adverb that indicates the speaker's strong belief that something is not expected to (have) become a reality.

examples.japanese: まさか美智子があんな男と結婚するとは思わなかった。
examples.english: I never dreamed that Michiko would marry that kind of a guy.

examples.japanese: まさかあたしの誕生日を忘れたんじゃないでしょうね。
examples.english: Don't tell me that you forgot my birthday!

examples.japanese: まさか彼がこんな寒い日に来るはずはないですよ。
examples.english: Surely he won't show up on such a cold day!

examples.japanese: 最近父から手紙が来ないけれど、まさか具合が悪いのではあるまい。
examples.english: Lately I haven't heard from my father, but God forbid that he might be ill.

examples.japanese: Ａ：七十のおじいさんが高校に入ったんだって。 Ｂ：まさか。
examples.english: A: I heard that an old man of 70 entered a high school. B: Incredible!

examples.japanese: まさか自分が交通事故に巻き込まれるとは思いませんでしたよ。
