examples.english: I never thought that I would be involved in a traffic accident.

examples.japanese: まさか司法試験に一度でパス出来るとは考えてもいなかった。
examples.english: I never dreamed that I could pass the bar examination on my first attempt.

examples.japanese: 青い顔をしているけど、まさか病気じゃないでしょうね。
examples.english: You look pale. Are you sure you are not ill?

meaning_en: Better; less objectionable; preferable; might as well ~
explanation: A phrase indicating that although someone/something (or some situation) is not satisfactory it is better than someone/something else.

examples.japanese: こんな給料をもらう（くらい）なら辞めた方がましだ。
examples.english: If this is the salary, it would be better to quit.

examples.japanese: 今度の日本語の先生は前の先生よりずっとましだ。
examples.english: This new Japanese teacher is much better than the former teacher.

examples.japanese: もう少しましなコーヒーはありませんか。
examples.english: Isn't there coffee that's a bit better?

examples.japanese: こんな大学に入るくらいなら、仕事をした方がましだ。
examples.english: I might as well work as enter such a college.

examples.japanese: こんな苦しい生活をするくらいなら、死んだ方がましだ。
examples.english: It is better to die than to lead such a life.

examples.japanese: 学校へ行くくらいなら家でテレビでも見ていた方がましだ。
examples.english: It's better to watch TV at home rather than going to school.

examples.japanese: こんな不味いご飯を食べるくらいなら何も食べない方がいい。
examples.english: It's better not to eat anything rather than eating such an untasteful meal.

examples.japanese: あのレストランよりこのレストランの方がましだ。
examples.english: This restaurant is better than that restaurant over there.

meaning_en: Or; either ~ or ~
formation:
(i) Noun (か)、 | またはNoun | | 
 | 日本語(か)、または語英語 | Either Japanese or English | 
(ii) Sinformal か | またはSinformal | | 
 | 手紙を書くか、または電話をする | Either write a letter or make a phone call |
explanation: A conjunction which connects two choices or possibilities expressed by noun phrases or sentences.

examples.japanese: 現金（か）、または小切手でお払い下さい。
examples.english: Please pay either in cash or by check.

examples.japanese: Ａ（か）、またはＢのどちらかを選びなさい。
examples.english: Select either A or B.

examples.japanese: 電話番号を聞き違えたか、またはもうこの電話は使われていないのだろう。
examples.english: I guess that either I misheard the phone number or this number (literally: phone) is no longer in use.

examples.japanese: 黒（か）、または青のボールペンを使って下さい。
examples.english: Please use a black or blue ballpoint pen.

examples.japanese: 三年以下の懲役（か）、または百万円以下の罰金。
examples.english: Imprisonment up to three years or a penalty up to one million yen.

examples.japanese: 昼は仕事があるから、夜間コースを取るか、または家庭教師を探すしかない。
examples.english: I have to work during the day, so I have no choice but to take a night course or look for a tutor.

examples.japanese: 二週間前に出したはずの手紙がまだ先方に着いていない。私の秘書が出し忘れたか、または郵便局が間違えたのだろう。
examples.english: A letter that I assumed was mailed two weeks ago has not reached the addressee yet. It is probably that my secretary forgot to mail it or that the post office made a mistake.

meaning_en: (on) the side of; (from) the aspect of; (from) the standpoint/viewpoint of; in terms of
formation:
Noun | 面 | | 
 | 運営面 | The aspect of operation; the standpoint of operation |
explanation: A suffix which forms a compound that means a side of X, or an aspect of X.

examples.japanese: 彼か学業面では優秀だが、精神面に少し弱さがあるようだ。
examples.english: He is excellent in terms of his academic performance (literally: on the side of his academic performance) but he seems to have some psychological weakness (literally: have some weakness on the side of his psychology).

examples.japanese: この食堂は衛生面によく気を配っている。
examples.english: This restaurant pays close attention to hygiene (literally: the hygienic aspect).

examples.japanese: 藤田さんは技術面からのみものを見る傾向がある。
examples.english: Mr. Fujita tends to view things from the technical standpoint alone.

examples.japanese: ここの土地所有者は税金面で優遇措置を受けている。
examples.english: The land owners here receive favourable treatment in terms of tax.

examples.japanese: あの候補者の演説は政策面での説得力に欠ける。
examples.english: That candidate's speech is not convincing (literally: lacks persuasive power) from the standpoint of policy.

examples.japanese: 彼女は日本へ行っても語学面は心配しなくてもいい。
examples.english: She does not need to worry about language (literally: the aspect of language) when she goes to Japan

examples.japanese: この車は性能面を高く評価された。
examples.english: This car was highly regarded in terms of performance.

meaning_en: Can manage to; will definitely do; am determined to
formation:
Vて | みせる | (Group 2) | 
 | 読んでみせる | I will definitely read it/I will show you how to read it |
explanation: The speaker's strong determination to achieve something for others to see.

examples.japanese: 僕は小説を書いて、芥川賞を取ってみせる。
examples.english: I will definitely write a novel and get the Akutagawa Prize.

examples.japanese: 僕はこの会社の社長になってみせる。
examples.english: I am determined to become the president of this company.

examples.japanese: 私はあのハンサムな男の子と結婚してみせるわ。
examples.english: I can manage to marry that handsome guy.

examples.japanese: 三百ページの本を一時間で読んでみせるぞ。
examples.english: I will definitely read a 300-page book in one hour.

examples.japanese: 今年こそは修士論文を書き上げてみせる。
examples.english: This year I will definitely finish writing my M.A. thesis.

examples.japanese: 一男は百メートルを十一秒で走ってみせた。
examples.english: Kazuo managed to run 100 meters in 11 seconds.

meaning_en: (things) like ~; ~ or something like
formation:
(i) {V/Adjective い}informal | などと | | 
 | 話すなどと | (say) something like someone talks | 
 | つまらないなどと | (say) something like something is uninteresting | 
(ii) {Adjectiveな stem/Noun} | {だ/だった}などと | | 
 | 便利{だ/だった}などと | (say) something like something is/was convenient | 
 | 学生{だ/だった}などと | (say) something like someone is/was a student |
explanation: A compound particle that indicates an approximate quote of words or ideas.

examples.japanese: 日本の文化はユニークだなどと言う人がいるが、私はそうは思わない。
examples.english: There are people who say things like Japanese culture is unique, but I don't think so.

examples.japanese: お金がないから、日本へ行くなどということは夢です。
examples.english: I don't have money, so ideas like going to Japan are just dreams.

examples.japanese: 毎日運動しろなどとは言いませんから、週に二、三度運動したらどうですか。
examples.english: I'm not saying you should exercise every day, but why don't you do it 2 or 3 times a week.

examples.japanese: ジョンソンさんは日本語で何でも話せるなどと言っている。
examples.english: Mr. Johnson says things like he can say anything in Japanese.

examples.japanese: 困った時は助けてくれるだろうなどと甘く考えてはいけない。
examples.english: Don't think indulgently things like people will help you when you are in trouble.

examples.japanese: 日本へ留学しようとしているケントさんは、うまく日本の生活に適応出来るかなどと心配している。
examples.english: Mr. Kent, who is about to go to Japan to study, is worried about things like whether he will be able to adjust to Japanese life.

examples.japanese: みんなが君のことをクラブのホープだなどと言っているよ。
examples.english: Everybody is saying something like you are the hope of our club.

examples.japanese: 尊敬しています、などと言われると照れくさい。
examples.english: When I am told that they respect me, I feel embarrassed.

meaning_en: It isn't the case that ~ not ~; it is not that ~ not ~
formation:
{V/Adjectiveい/な/Copula}negative | ないこと{も/は}ない | | 
 | 話さないこと{も/は}ない | I do speak, but ~ | 
 | 高くないこと{も/は}ない | Something is expensive/high, but ~ | 
 | 不便{で/じゃ}ないこと{も/は}ない | Something is frequent, but ~ | 
 | 学者{で/じゃ}ないこと{も/は}ない | Someone is a scholar, but ~ |
explanation: ないことも / はないA double negative phrase used to make a conditional affirmative statement.

examples.japanese: Ａ：日本語の新聞は読まないんですか。Ｂ：いいえ、読まないこと{も/は}ないんですが、時たまですね。
examples.english: A: Don't you read Japanese newspapers? B: I do read them, but very rarely. (literally: It isn't the case that I don't read them, but very rarely.)

examples.japanese: A: この辺は夏涼しくないんですか。B: いや、涼しくないこともないんですが、時々ひどく暑くなります。
examples.english: A: Isn't it cool around here during the summer? B: Yes, it is cool, but sometimes it gets terribly hot.

examples.japanese: A: お父さんはお元気じゃないんですか。B: いや、元気じゃないことはないんですが、血圧が少し高いようです。
examples.english: A: Isn't your father in good health? B: Yes, he is healthy, but his blood pressure is a bit high.

examples.japanese: A：日本語は難しくありませんか。B: いえ、難しくないこともないんですが、日本語の難しさは強調されすぎていると思いますよ。
examples.english: A: Isn't Japanese difficult? B: Yes, it is difficult, but it seems that the difficulty of Japanese is overemphasized.

examples.japanese: A：山田さんは政治学者じゃないんですね。B: いや、政治学者じゃないこともないんですが、どちらかというと政治家です。
examples.english: A: Mr. Yamada isn't a political scientist, is he? B: Yes, he is a political scientist, but he is more of a politician.

examples.japanese: 日本人は集団行動が好きだとよく言われている。確かに、集団行動をしないことはないのだが、個人行動をとる日本人も結構いる。
examples.english: Japanese are said to like group behaviour. Certainly, they do behave as a group, but there are quite a few Japanese who behave individually.

meaning_en: It isn't the case that ~ not ~; it is not that ~ not ~
formation:
{V/Adjectiveい/な/Copula}negative | ないこと{も/は}ない | | 
 | 話さないこと{も/は}ない | I do speak, but ~ | 
 | 高くないこと{も/は}ない | Something is expensive/high, but ~ | 
 | 不便{で/じゃ}ないこと{も/は}ない | Something is frequent, but ~ | 
 | 学者{で/じゃ}ないこと{も/は}ない | Someone is a scholar, but ~ |
explanation: ないことも / はないA double negative phrase used to make a conditional affirmative statement.

examples.japanese: Ａ：日本語の新聞は読まないんですか。Ｂ：いいえ、読まないこと{も/は}ないんですが、時たまですね。
examples.english: A: Don't you read Japanese newspapers? B: I do read them, but very rarely. (literally: It isn't the case that I don't read them, but very rarely.)

examples.japanese: A: この辺は夏涼しくないんですか。B: いや、涼しくないこともないんですが、時々ひどく暑くなります。
examples.english: A: Isn't it cool around here during the summer? B: Yes, it is cool, but sometimes it gets terribly hot.

examples.japanese: A: お父さんはお元気じゃないんですか。B: いや、元気じゃないことはないんですが、血圧が少し高いようです。
examples.english: A: Isn't your father in good health? B: Yes, he is healthy, but his blood pressure is a bit high.

examples.japanese: A：日本語は難しくありませんか。B: いえ、難しくないこともないんですが、日本語の難しさは強調されすぎていると思いますよ。
examples.english: A: Isn't Japanese difficult? B: Yes, it is difficult, but it seems that the difficulty of Japanese is overemphasized.

examples.japanese: A：山田さんは政治学者じゃないんですね。B: いや、政治学者じゃないこともないんですが、どちらかというと政治家です。
examples.english: A: Mr. Yamada isn't a political scientist, is he? B: Yes, he is a political scientist, but he is more of a politician.

examples.japanese: 日本人は集団行動が好きだとよく言われている。確かに、集団行動をしないことはないのだが、個人行動をとる日本人も結構いる。
examples.english: Japanese are said to like group behaviour. Certainly, they do behave as a group, but there are quite a few Japanese who behave individually.

meaning_en: Quite; fairly; considerably; (not) easily; pretty; (not) readily
formation:
(i) なかなか | Adjective(い/な)affirmative | | 
 | なかなか面白い | Quite interesting | 
 | なかなか便利だ | Quiet convenient | 
(ii) なかなか | Vaffirmative | | 
 | なかなかやる | Someone performs something quite well | 
(iii) なかなか | Vnegative | | 
 | なかなか分からない | Cannot understand something easily | 
(iv) なかなか | Adverb | | 
 | なかなか上手に話す | Someone speaks quite well | 
(v) なかなか(の) | Noun | | 
 | なかなか(の)学者 | Quite a scholar |
explanation: An adverb used to indicate the speaker's feelings that something is impressive or his annoyance at slowness or difficulty in achieving something.

examples.japanese: ブラウンさんは日本語がなかなか上手ですね。
examples.english: {Mr. Brown is / Mr. Brown, you are} remarkably good at Japanese.

examples.japanese: この生け花はなかなか見事に生けてある。
examples.english: This flower arrangement is done quite nicely.

examples.japanese: 今年は桜の花がなかなか咲きません。
examples.english: It will be a long time before the cherry blossoms are out this year. (literally: This year the cherry blossoms do not bloom easily.)

examples.japanese: あの男は仕事がなかなか出来るねえ。
examples.english: That guy does his job quite well, doesn't he?

examples.japanese: 山田部長の奥さんはなかなか（の）美人だ。
examples.english: The wife of our departmental chief Yamada is quite a beauty.

examples.japanese: この庭園はなかなか綺麗ですね。
examples.english: This garden is quite beautiful, isn't it?

examples.japanese: この数学の問題はなかなか難しそうだ。
examples.english: This math problem looks quite difficult, doesn't it?

examples.japanese: 君はなかなかコンピュータに強いそうじゃないか。
examples.english: I heard that you are quite good with computers.

meaning_en: Not ~ and; not ~ but
formation:
(i) Adjective い stem | くなく | | 
 | 大きくなく | Something/someone is not big and ~ | 
(ii) {Adjective な stem/Noun} | ではなく | | 
 | 静かではなく | Something/someone is not quiet and ~ | 
 | 先生ではなく | Someone is not a teacher but ~ |
explanation: a continuative form of ない used in written Japanese (to indicate a reason/cause for what follows if ない is attached to Adjective (い/な) and contrast if it is attached to a Noun+Copula).

examples.japanese: 日本語の期末試験はあまり難しくなく、ほっとした。
examples.english: The Japanese final examination was not very hard, and I felt relieved.

examples.japanese: 私の研究対象は現代史ではなく、古代史だ。
examples.english: My research area is not modern history, but ancient history.

examples.japanese: 今年の冬はあまり寒くなく、オーバーも二、三度しか着なかった。
examples.english: It wasn't very cold this winter and we wore our overcoats only two or three times.

examples.japanese: 昨日見た映画は実に面白くなく、途中で寝てしまった。
examples.english: The movie I saw yesterday was so boring that I went to sleep during it.

examples.japanese: 私には日本語を聞くのが容易ではなく、大分苦労した。
examples.english: To listen to Japanese was not easy, and I had quite a difficult time.

examples.japanese: 彼女と別れた時はそれほど悲しくなく、自分でも驚いた。
examples.english: I was surprised that I did not feel so sad when I parted with her.

examples.japanese: 私には日本語を教えてくれたのは日本人ではなく、アメリカ人だった。
examples.english: The person who taught me Japanese was not a Japanese but an American.

examples.japanese: 僕が好きなのは日本料理ではなくタイ料理だ。
examples.english: What I like is not Japanese cuisine, but Thai cuisine.

meaning_en: I don't know for sure, but
explanation: A phrase that indicates the speaker's uncertainty about something.

examples.japanese: 何でも山本さんは奥さんと別れて、一人で暮らしているそうですよ。
examples.english: I don't know for sure, but they say that Mr. Yamamoto has separated from his wife and lives alone.

examples.japanese: 何でもこの辺は物価が非常に高いそうですよ。
examples.english: I don't know for sure, but they say things are expensive in this neighbourhood.

examples.japanese: 何でもあの人は株で大分もうけたようですよ。
examples.english: I don't know for sure, but he appeared to have earned a lot of money through stocks.

examples.japanese: 何でも戸田さんの息子さんはシカゴ大学で経営学修士を取ったらしいですよ。
examples.english: I don't know for sure, but it seems that Mr. Toda's son received an MBA at the University of Chicago.

examples.japanese: 何でも日本とアメリカの西海岸を五時間ぐらいで飛ぶ飛行機を開発しているという話ですよ。
examples.english: I don't know for sure, but there's some talk that they are developing an airplane that flies between Japan and the west coast of the States in about five hours.

meaning_en: As a matter of fact; no matter what; believe it or not; you may be surprised, but ~; in fact; unbelievably
explanation: An adverb that indicates the speaker's emotive feeling about some extreme state of affairs.

examples.japanese: うちの父は頑固なんだ。何しろ一度言い出したら絶対に引き下がらないんだから。
examples.english: My father is obstinate. As a matter of fact, once he says he will do something, he never changes his mind.

examples.japanese: Ａ：この大学の教育はいいらしいね。Ｂ：うん、何しろ学生六人に先生一人だからね。
examples.english: A: I heard that education at this college is good. B: Yeah, you may be surprised, but the student-instructor ratio is 6 to 1.

examples.japanese: 一日中ボスにがなり立てられるんで、何しろ、ストレスが多いんだ。
examples.english: Because my boss hollers at me all day long, I'm unbelievably stressed.

examples.japanese: あの人は金持ちですよ。何しろベンツを三台も持っているんですからね。
examples.english: He is rich, you know. Believe it or not, he has three Mercedes Benz.

examples.japanese: 今年の冬は本当に雪が多かったです。何しろ、雪の降らない日の方が少ないくらいでしたからね。
examples.english: It snowed a lot this winter. In fact, there were less snow-free days than snowy days, you know.

examples.japanese: あの人はよく煙草を吸いますよ。何しろ一日に六十本ぐらい吸うんですから。
examples.english: He is a heavy smoker. In fact, he smokes about 60 cigarettes a day.

examples.japanese: A: 日本は人が多いねえ。B: うん、何しろ、面積はアメリカの二十五分の一なのに、人口は二分一だからね。
examples.english: A: Japan is crowded, isn't it? B: Yeah, as a matter of fact, the size is one twenty fifth of America but the population is one half, you know.

examples.japanese: 何しろ、忙しいんだ。寝る時間もないんですよ。
examples.english: I'm unbelievably busy. I don't have any sleeping time, you know.

meaning_en: Cannot help -ing; irresistibly; unbearably
formation:
(i) Adjective (い/な)て | ならない | | 
 | 嬉しくてならない | I cannot help feeling happy | 
 | 残念でならない | I cannot help feeling sorry | 
(ii) Vて | ならない | | 
 | 気がせいてならない | I cannot help feeling pressed |
explanation: A phrase that is used to express insurmountable psychological or physical feelings.

examples.japanese: 病気の母のことが心配でならない。
examples.english: I'm very much worried about my sick mother. (Literally: I cannot help worrying about my sick mother).

examples.japanese: 日本の歴史をもっと深く知りたくてならない。
examples.english: I'm dying to know Japanese history more deeply.

examples.japanese: 一人で住んでいる母親のことが気になってならない。
examples.english: I cannot help worrying about my mother who is living alone.

examples.japanese: 夫が単身赴任しているので、寂しくてなりません。
examples.english: My husband has gone alone for work and I cannot help feeling lonely.

examples.japanese: 二人の婚約が決まって、嬉しくてならないようだ。
examples.english: The couple have decided to get engaged and they look overjoyed.

examples.japanese: 松本清張の推理小説は面白くてならない。
examples.english: The mystery novels by Seicho Matsumoto are irresistibly interesting.

examples.japanese: 隣の家のステレオがやかましくてならない。
examples.english: Our neighbour’s stereo is unbearably noisy.

examples.japanese: 山田先生がこの大学をお辞めになるので、残念でならない。
examples.english: Since Professor Yamada is going to quit this university, I cannot help feeling disappointed.

meaning_en: Without
formation:
Noun | なしでは | | 
 | 先生なしでは | Without a teacher |
explanation: If something/someone is missing.

examples.japanese: 実力なしでは世の中は渡れない。
examples.english: Without real talents one cannot get along in the society.

examples.japanese: あなたなしでは生きていけない。
examples.english: Without you I cannot keep on living.

examples.japanese: お金なしではいい教育は受けられない。
examples.english: Without money we cannot receive good education.

examples.japanese: 暇なしでは人生はつまらなくなってしまう。
examples.english: Without leisure time life will become dull.

examples.japanese: 仕事なしでは生活が出来ない。
examples.english: Without a job one cannot live a life.

examples.japanese: 基礎研究なしでは科学は発展しない。
examples.english: Without basic research science would not develop.

examples.japanese: 車なしではちょっと不便だ。
examples.english: Without a car it is a bit inconvenient.

meaning_en: On the occasion of; at; in; before; prior to
formation:
(i) Noun | に{当たって/当たり} | | 
 | 結婚に{当たって/当たり} | On the occasion of the marriage | 
(ii) Vinformal nonpast | に{当たって/当たり} | | 
 | 話すに{当たって/当たり} | On the occasion of talking |
explanation: に当たって/当たり A compound particle that indicates occasion of doing something or of having done something in formal Japanese.

examples.japanese: 新入社員の入社に{当たって/当たり}社長はホテルでパーティーを開いた。
examples.english: On the occasion of new employees' entering the company, the president threw a party at a hotel.

examples.japanese: 和也は大学を卒業するに{当たって/当たり}、指導教官に今後の進路について相談した。
examples.english: On the occasion of graduating from college, Kazuya consulted with his academic adviser on his future direction.

examples.japanese: 私の留学に当たり、父は自分の経験を話してくれた。
examples.english: On the occasion of my study abroad, my father told me about his own experience.

examples.japanese: 日本の経済を研究するに当たって、国会図書館で資料集めをした。
examples.english: Before I did research on the Japanese economy, I collected materials at the National Diet Library.

examples.japanese: 総理はサミット出席に当たり、閣僚と会議をした。
examples.english: The Premier had a conference with cabinet members before attending the summit.

examples.japanese: 小説家は時代小説を書くに当たり、その時代の歴史を詳しく調べた。
examples.english: Before writing a historical novel, the novelist did an in-depth survey of the history of the period he dealt with.

meaning_en: Against; contrary to; in contrast to; in violation of; while; whereas
formation:
(i) Noun | に反して | | 
 | 予想に反して | Contrary to expectation | 
(ii) Sinformal | のに反して | Connection rules: the same as のだ | 
 | よく勉強するのに反して | In contrast to the fact that someone studies hard | 
(iii) Demonstrative Pronoun | に反して | | 
 | これに反して | In contrast to this | 
(iv) Noun | に反するNoun | | 
 | 予想に反する結果 | A result which is contrary to someone’s expectation |
explanation: に反して/反する Contrary to or in contrast to.

examples.japanese: 今年の東京国際マラソンは大方の予想に反して無名の選手が優勝した。
examples.english: Contrary to the majority's expectations, an unknown runner won the Tokyo International Marathon this year.

examples.japanese: 我が社はテレビの売れ行きが伸びているのに反してオーディオ製品の売れ行きが下がっている。
examples.english: In our company, in contrast to the increase in sales of TV sets, the sales in audio products are decreasing.

examples.japanese: Ｓ１：日本ではいい大学に入るのは難しいが卒業するのは易しいと言われている。Ｓ２：これに反して、アメリカではいい大学でも入学が比較的易しいが卒業するには相当勉強しなければならない。
examples.english: S1: It is said that to enter good universities in Japan is difficult but to graduate from them is easy. S2: In contrast to this, in America even good universities are relatively easy to enter, but students must study quite hard to graduate from them.

examples.japanese: 妙子は意に反する結婚を押しつけられた。
examples.english: Taeko was forced to marry. (literally: A marriage which was against Taeko's will was forced upon her.)

examples.japanese: 浩は両親の期待に反して高校を出てからコックになった。
examples.english: Contrary to his parents' wishes, Hiroshi became a chef after finishing high school.

examples.japanese: 彼は自分の意思に反して賄賂を受け取ってしまった。
examples.english: He was forced to accept a bribe. (literally: He received a bribe against his will.)

examples.japanese: この規則に反して従業員を働かせた場合は一か月の営業停止になる。
examples.english: Your business will be suspended for one month if you work your employees in violation of these rules.

examples.japanese: 奥村さんのうちはご主人が無口なのに反して奥さんが人一倍のおしゃべりだ。
examples.english: In Okumura's family, whereas the husband is quite, the wife is very talkative.

meaning_en: Compared with/to; when compared with/to; in comparison to
formation:
Noun | に比べると/比べて | | 
 | 去年に比べると/比べて | Compared with last year |
explanation: に比べると/比べて If we compare (it) with/to; comparing (it) with.

examples.japanese: 欧米に比べて日本の住宅事情は極めて貧困だ。
examples.english: Compared to (the situations) in Europe and the U.S., the housing situation in Japan is extremely poor.

examples.japanese: 日本に来る前に比べると今は大分日本語でものが言えるようになった。
examples.english: I can speak Japanese fairly well now (literally: I have become able to say things in Japanese fairly well) compared to my level before I came to Japan.

examples.japanese: 今年は去年に比べて雨の日が多いようだ。
examples.english: In comparison to last year, we seem to have more rainy days this year.

examples.japanese: 十年前の暮らしに比べると今の暮らしは天国です。
examples.english: Compared with our life ten years ago, our present life is heavenly (literally: is heaven).

examples.japanese: この新しい（コンピュータ）モデルは、古いモデルと比べて演算が三倍速くなっている。
examples.english: When compared with the older (computer) model, the operation speed of this new model is three times as fast.

meaning_en: When it becomes; when it comes to; when; if
formation:
(i) Noun (time) | になると | | 
 | 八になると | When it becomes 8 o’clock; at 8 o’clock | 
(ii) Noun (non-time) | になると | | 
 | 雨になると | When it becomes rain |
explanation: A phrase that expresses the time when an uncontrollable state or a habitual action occurs.

examples.japanese: 夏になると、摂氏三十度を越す日が多いです。
examples.english: In summer (literally: When it becomes summer), there are many days that exceed 30 degrees Celsius.

examples.japanese: 父は食べ物のことになると、とてもやかましかった。
examples.english: When it comes to the matter of food, my father was very particular.

examples.japanese: 四月半ばになると、この辺は桜が綺麗に咲きます。
examples.english: In this area, in the middle of April, the cherry trees bloom beautifully.

examples.japanese: ニューイングランドと言われるアメリカの東北地方は、秋になると、紅葉がとても綺麗です。
examples.english: In the north-east area of the U.S. called New England, tinted autumn leaves are very beautiful.

examples.japanese: 私は夜十一時になると、頭が働かなくなる。
examples.english: At about 11 p.m., my brain stops working.

examples.japanese: 子供の頃、夏になると、両親は僕を海に連れて行ってくれた。
examples.english: When I was a child, in summer, my parents took me to the ocean.

examples.japanese: 大学生の時は、休みになると、よく旅行をした。
examples.english: When I was a college student, I travelled a lot during vacations.

examples.japanese: 彼はフットボールの話になると夢中だ。
examples.english: When the topic of the conversation is football, he is totally absorbed in it.

meaning_en: At; on; in; during
formation:
(i) Noun | において | | 
 | アメリカにおいて | In America | 
(ii) Noun | におけるNoun | | 
 | アメリカにおける学生生活 | Student life in America |
explanation: において/おける A compound particle which indicates the place of an action/event, a state or time.

examples.japanese: 来年の総会はシカゴのヒルトン・ホテルにおいて行われる。
examples.english: Next year's general meeting will be held at the Hilton Hotel in Chicago.

examples.japanese: コンピュータは近い将来においてほとんどの家庭に行き渡るだろう。
examples.english: Computers will probably spread to almost every household in the near future.

examples.japanese: 先月の東京における環境保護国際会議には全世界から大勢の学者が参加した。
examples.english: Many scholars from all over the world took part in last month's international conference in Tokyo on environmental protection.

examples.japanese: １９９２年のオリンピックはバルセロナにおいて開催された。
examples.english: The 1992 Olympiad was held in Barcelona.

examples.japanese: 過去においてはこのようなことはあまり問題にならなかった。
examples.english: Such things were hardly considered to be problems before (literally: in the past).

examples.japanese: この作文は文法においてはあまり問題はない。
examples.english: This composition doesn't have many problems in terms of grammar.

examples.japanese: 本校における男女学生の比率は二対一である。
examples.english: The ratio of male students to female students at this school is 2 to 1.

examples.japanese: 木村博士は遺伝学における権威者として知られている。
examples.english: Dr. Kimura is known as an authority in (the field of) genetics.

meaning_en: As, accordingly; in proportion to; in accordance with; following
formation:
(i) Vinformal nonpast | に{従って/従い} | | 
 | その本を読むに{従って/従い} | As someone reads the book | 
(ii) Noun | に{従って/従い} | | 
 | 指示に{従って/従い} | In accordance with the instructions |
explanation: に従って/従い Something spontaneously and gradually occurs in accordance with some change.

examples.japanese: 日本の経済力が強くなるに{従って/従い}、日本語学習者が増えてきた。
examples.english: As Japan's economic power has become stronger, Japanese language learners have increased, accordingly.

examples.japanese: 契約に{従って/従い}雇用期間を三年とする。
examples.english: In accordance with the contract, your tenure shall be three years.

examples.japanese: 収入が増えるに従って、支出も増える。
examples.english: As our income increases, our expenditure, too, increases.

examples.japanese: 年を取るに従い、体力が衰える。
examples.english: As you grow older, your physical strength declines.

examples.japanese: 文明が進むに従い、人間のストレスが多くなる。
examples.english: As civilization progresses, human stresses increase.

examples.japanese: 日がたつに従って、父の病気は回復してきた。
examples.english: As the days went by, my father recovered from his illness.

examples.japanese: 太陽が沈んで行くに従って、温度がどんどん下がった。
examples.english: As the sun went down, the temperature went down rapidly.

examples.japanese: 約束に従い、借金を一か月後に返した。
examples.english: In accordance with the promise I returned the loaned money after a month.

meaning_en: Nothing more than; not more than; mere; merely; only; just; as little/few as; that's all
formation:
(i) Noun | に過ぎない | | 
 | 学生に過ぎない | Just a student | 
(ii) Number+Counter | に過ぎない | | 
 | 五人に過ぎない | As a few as five people | 
(iii) Vinformal(だけ) | に過ぎない | | 
 | 話している(だけ) に過ぎない | Someone is doing nothing but talking | 
 | 話した(だけ) に過ぎない | Someone did nothing more than talk |
explanation: Something or someone is nothing more than what is stated in terms of amount, degree, status, significance, etc.

examples.japanese: これは私の私見に過ぎない。
examples.english: This is nothing more than my personal opinion.

examples.japanese: 今期の売り上げの伸びは三パーセントに過ぎない。
examples.english: The sales increase this term is as little as three percent.

examples.japanese: あの男は（ただ）言われたことをしている（だけ）に過ぎない。
examples.english: That man is not doing more than what he was told to do.

examples.japanese: 彼は私のボーイフレンドの一人に過ぎない。
examples.english: He is nothing more than one of my boyfriends.

examples.japanese: これは数ある中のほんの一例に過ぎない。
examples.english: This is only one example among many.

examples.japanese: 今言ったことは私の希望に過ぎませんので、あまり深刻に考えないで下さい。
examples.english: What I've just told you is nothing more than my hope, so please don't take it too seriously.

examples.japanese: 私の収入はアルバイトを入れても年二万ドルに過ぎない。
examples.english: My income is only $20,000 even if I include my side job (income).

examples.japanese: 私を支持してくれる人は身内を入れても五十人程度に過ぎない。
examples.english: There are no more than about 50 people who support me (literally: The people who support me are no more than about fifty), even if I include my relatives.

meaning_en: Toward; to; in contrast to; whereas; in regard to; in; per
formation:
(i) Noun | に対して | | 
 | 先生に対して | Towards one’s teacher | 
(ii) {V/Adjective い} informal | のに対して | | 
 | {話す/話した}のに対して | Someone talks/talked, whereas ~ | 
 | {若い/若かった}のに対して | Someone is/was young, whereas ~ | 
(iii) {Adjective な stem/Noun} {な/である/だった/であった} | のに対して | | 
 | 元気{な/である/だった/であった}のに対して | Someone is/was healthy, whereas ~ | 
 | 学生{な/である/だった/であった}のに対して | Someone is/was a student, whereas ~ | 
(iv) Noun | に{対する/対しての}Noun | | 
 | 結婚に{対する/対しての}考え方 | One’s view of marriage |
explanation: に対して/対する Regarding something/someone one opposes, compares, or shows interest in regarding something/someone one opposes, compares or shows interest in.

examples.japanese: これまで日本は外国に対して閉鎖的な政策を取ってきた。
examples.english: Up until now Japan has taken a closed policy toward foreign countries.

examples.japanese: 日本の大学は入学するのが難しいのに対して、アメリカの大学は卒業するのが難しい。
examples.english: Japanese colleges are hard to enter; whereas American colleges are hard to graduate from.

examples.japanese: アメリカでは離婚に{対する/対しての}考え方が大分変わってきた。
examples.english: In America, attitudes toward divorce have greatly changed.

examples.japanese: 鈴木さんは誰に対しても丁寧だ。
examples.english: Mr. Suzuki is polite towards everybody.

examples.japanese: 日本は外国に対して市場をもっと開放すべきた。
examples.english: Japan should open its market more widely towards foreign countries.

examples.japanese: 私は政治に対して強い関心がある。
examples.english: I have a strong interest in politics.

examples.japanese: 手数料は一万円に対して五百円です。
examples.english: The commission charge will be 500 yen per 10,000 yen.

examples.japanese: 市民は増税に対して強く反対している。
examples.english: The citizens are strongly opposed to the tax hike.

meaning_en: According to; due to; owing to; because of; depending on; from ~ to; by means of; on the basis of; with; by
formation:
(i) Noun | によって | | 
 | 政府によって | By the government | 
(ii) {V/Adjective い}informal | かどうかに{よって/より} | | 
 | {来る/来た}かどうかに{よって/より} | Depending on whether someone comes/came or not | 
 | {面白い/面白かった}かどうかに{よって/より} | Depending on whether something is/was interesting or not | 
(iii) {Adjective な stem/Noun} | {Ø/だった}かどうかに{よって/より} | | 
 | {静か/静かだった}かどうかに{よって/より} | Depending on whether something is/was quiet or not | 
(iv) Embedded Wh-Question | に{よって/より} | | 
 | 何を食べたかに{よって/より} | Depending on what someone ate | 
 | 誰が来るかに{よって/より} | Depending on who comes |
explanation: によって/より A particle that indicates means, cause, agent of passive sentence, or dependency on a situation.

examples.japanese: 漢和辞典によって知らない漢字を調べる。
examples.english: We examine unknown kanji with a Chinese character dictionary.

examples.japanese: 先生によって、勿論、教え方が違います。
examples.english: Teaching methods are, of course, different, depending on the teacher.

examples.japanese: 戦争によって父を亡くした。
examples.english: We lost our father, owing to the war.

examples.japanese: この研究所は文部省によって設立された。
examples.english: This research institute was established by the Ministry of Education.

examples.japanese: 奨学金がもらえるかどうかによって大学入学を決めます。
examples.english: I will decide my entrance to college, depending on whether I can get a scholarship or not.

examples.japanese: 何を食べるかによって健康状態は変わる。
examples.english: Our health condition changes according to what we eat.

examples.japanese: 我々は本を読むことによって視野を広げることが出来る。
examples.english: We can expand our horizons by reading books.

examples.japanese: この頃は宇宙中継によって世界のニュースをテレビで見ることが出来る。
examples.english: These days we can watch world news on TV via satellite live broadcasting.

meaning_en: Because of
formation:
Noun | の関係で | | 
 | 会社の関係で | Because of the company | 
 | 天気の関係で | Because of the weather |
explanation: A phrase indicating that something takes place or does not take place because of something.

examples.japanese: ホールさんは今仕事の関係で東京に行っています。
examples.english: Mr. Hall has gone to Tokyo on a business-related matter.

examples.japanese: 鈴木は単位の関係で今年は卒業出来ないそうだ。
examples.english: I heard that Suzuki cannot graduate this year because of insufficient credits / units.

examples.japanese: 時間の関係で、残念ですが、詳しくお話し出来ません。
examples.english: Because of the time limit, I am sorry I cannot go into detail.

examples.japanese: 部屋の広さの関係で、四十人以上はお呼び出来ません。
examples.english: Because of the size of the room we cannot invite more than 40 people.

examples.japanese: 桃子は年齢の関係で、採用されなかったようだ。
examples.english: It seems that Momoko was not hired because of her age.

examples.japanese: レズリーは会社の関係でよく海外に出張するらしい。
examples.english: I was told that Leslie makes frequent company-related business trips abroad (literally: makes frequent trips abroad because of his company).

examples.japanese: みゆきは御主人の仕事の関係でロンドンに三年住むそうだ。
examples.english: I heard that because of her husband's work Miyuki is going to live in London for 3 years.

examples.japanese: 予算の関係で、そのプロジェクトは中止になった。
examples.english: Because of the budgetary situation, the project has been cancelled.

meaning_en: About; in terms of; related to
formation:
Noun | のこと | | 
 | 試験のこと | About an/the exam |
explanation: Things of/about.

examples.japanese: 私は明日の講義で日本文化のことを話すつもりだ。
examples.english: I'm going to talk about Japanese culture in my lecture tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼女のことはもう忘れた方がいいよ。
examples.english: You'd better forget about her now.

examples.japanese: 日本留学のことでちょっとご相談があるんですが。
examples.english: I'd like to talk to you about studying in Japan.

examples.japanese: 実は、明日の会議のことなんですが。
examples.english: Actually, it's (=the reason I'm calling is /the reason I came to see you is) about tomorrow's meeting.

examples.japanese: 昨日荒井さんが君のことを色々聞いていたよ。
examples.english: Miss Arai asked various questions about you yesterday.

examples.japanese: レポートは日本の大学生活のことを書こうと思っている。
examples.english: For my term paper I'm thinking of writing about college life in Japan.

examples.japanese: 子供のことは私が責任を持ちます。
examples.english: I'll take the responsibility for our children (literally: for things related to our children).

examples.japanese: 今回の実習のことでは大変お世話になりました。
examples.english: I owe you a lot in terms of my internship this time.

meaning_en: Only; just; alone
formation:
(i) Noun | のみ(Particle) | | 
 | 学生のみ(が)来た | Only students came | 
 | 学生のみ(を)呼ぶ | Invite students only | 
(ii) Noun | {Particle のみ/のみ Particle} | | 
 | 学生{にのみ/のみに}話す | Talk only to students/talk to students only | 
(iii) Vinformal | のみだ | | 
 | {行く/行った}のみだ | Only go/went |
explanation: A particle which expresses a limit imposed upon an action, event, or a state.

examples.japanese: 要点のみ（を）話して下さい。
examples.english: Please tell me just the main point.

examples.japanese: これは吉田先生にのみ話してあります。
examples.english: I have told this only to Professor Yoshida.

examples.japanese: 勝てるかどうか分からないが、ベストを尽くすのみだ。
examples.english: I don't know whether I can win or not, but I will just do my best.

examples.japanese: この答えは私のみ（が）知っている。
examples.english: Only I know the answer to this.

examples.japanese: 姓のみ記入のこと。
examples.english: Write your surname only.

examples.japanese: 私はただ言われたことをするのみだ。
examples.english: I will just do what I was told to do.

examples.japanese: ただ実行あるのみ（だ）。
examples.english: The only thing we have to do is to put it into practice.

examples.japanese: 外装が終わったのみでまだほかは何も手が着いていない。
examples.english: We've just finished the exterior and haven't started anything else yet.

meaning_en: Under; in; with
formation:
Noun | の下で | | 
 | 学部長の指揮の下で | Under the direction of the dean |
explanation: Under some object; under the control or influence of someone or something.

examples.japanese: 私は鈴木先生の指導の下で修士論文を書き上げた。
examples.english: I finished my master's thesis under Professor Suzuki's guidance.

examples.japanese: さんさんたる太陽の下で開会式が行われた。
examples.english: The opening ceremony was held in (literally: under) the brilliant sun.

examples.japanese: 彼はカラヤンの下で指導法を学んだ。
examples.english: He studied conducting under (Herbert von) Karajan.

examples.japanese: 弁護士（の）立ち会いの下で私達の離婚が成立した。
examples.english: Our divorce was agreed upon in (literally: under) the presence of attorneys.

examples.japanese: 囚人達は厳しい監視の下で強制労働をさせられた。
examples.english: The prisoners were forced to work under strict supervision.

examples.japanese: このインフレの下では金を貯めても意味がない。
examples.english: With this inflation there's no point in saving money.

meaning_en: As far as ~ is concerned; as far as ~ goes; from the viewpoint/standpoint of; according to; in terms of
formation:
Noun | の上では | | 
 | 理論の上では | In theory; on paper; as far as the theory goes |
explanation: As far as ~ is concerned.

examples.japanese: この計画は書類の上では問題なさそうだ。
examples.english: There seems to be no problem with this plan as far as the documents are concerned.

examples.japanese: 計算の上では二百万円ぐらい儲かることになっている。
examples.english: According to the calculations, we are supposed to make a profit of (about) two million yen.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは話しの上ではうまく行きそうだが、何となく不安だ。
examples.english: Although in theory (literally: As far as the story is concerned,) it looks like this project will work out, I feel somewhat uneasy

examples.japanese: 数字の上では川野の方が倉田より強そうだ。
examples.english: Statistically, (literally: As far as the figures are concerned,) Kawano looks stronger than Kurata.

examples.japanese: 大野は仕事の上では完全主義者だが、私生活はだらしがない。
examples.english: Ohno is a perfectionist at work (literally: as far as his business is concerned) but messy in his private life.

examples.japanese: 彼の行為は法律の上では罰しようがない。
examples.english: There's no way to punish his conduct legally (literally: from the legal point of view).

meaning_en: It will be/was ~ when/that ~
formation:
Sinformal | のはNounのことだ | (the same formation as のだ) | 
 | 話したのは去年のことだ | It was last year when someone talked… |
explanation: のは~のことだ A structure which focuses on a time when something takes place.

examples.japanese: 吉田さんと最後に会ったのは１９８５年の五月のことだ。
examples.english: It was in May 1985 that I last met Mr. Yamada.

examples.japanese: 日本語の面白さが分かり始めたのはごく最近のことだ。
examples.english: It was only recently that I began to understand how interesting Japanese is.

examples.japanese: 本格的なロボットが現れたのは１９６０年代後半のことである。
examples.english: It was in the late sixties when genuine robots came out.

examples.japanese: ゲラ刷りが出来るのは来月の終わりのことになるだろう。
examples.english: It will be around the end of next month when we get galley proofs.

examples.japanese: 父が公務員だったのは私がまだ学校へ行く前のことだ。
examples.english: It was before I went to school that my father was a government worker.

examples.japanese: 日本製品の評判が悪かったのは戦後二十年くらいの間のことだ。
examples.english: It was for a period of about twenty years after World War II that the reputation of Japanese products was bad.

examples.japanese: 健一と利子が仲良く歩いているところを見たのはつい一か月ほど前のことなのに彼らはもう別れたという話だ。
examples.english: Although it was only (about) a month ago when I saw Ken'ichi and Toshiko walking together intimately, I heard they've already split up.

meaning_en: Seem; appear; apparently
formation:
(i) {V/Adjective い}informal | ように思われる | | 
 | {来る/来た}ように思われる | It appears that someone is coming/came | 
 | {面白い/面白かった}ように思われる | It appears that someone is/was interesting | 
(ii) Adjective な stem | {な/だった}ように思われる | | 
 | 元気{な/だった}ように思われる | It seems that someone/something is/was healthy/sturdy | 
(iii) Noun | {の/だった}ように思われる | | 
 | 学生{の/だった}ように思われる | Someone seems to be/have been a student | 
(iv) Sinformal | と思われる | | 
 | 正しくないと思われる | It appears that something is not right |
explanation: A verb that indicates what the speaker/writer feels spontaneously or his/her hesitation about asserting himself/herself.

examples.japanese: 来年の景気は今年よりもいいように思われる。
examples.english: It seems that the business conditions of the coming year will be better than those of this year.

examples.japanese: この病気の治療は約一か月かかると思われる。
examples.english: It appears that the treatment of this disease will take approximately one month.

examples.japanese: 日本の輸出は今後あまり伸びないように思われる。
examples.english: It seems that Japanese exports are not going to grow so much in the future.

examples.japanese: 子供の非行を犯罪映画に結び付けるのは短絡的なように思われる。
examples.english: It appears too simplistic to relate children's delinquency to crime movies.

examples.japanese: この大学の教育は理工系が特にいいように思われる。
examples.english: Education at this university seems to be particularly good in science and engineering.

examples.japanese: 二十一世紀は情報化がもっと進んで、世界が一つの共同体になるだろうと思われる。
examples.english: It seems to me that in the 21st century society will become more information oriented, and the world will become one community.

examples.japanese: 日本語を習う時はローマ字を使わない方がよいと思われる。
examples.english: When you learn Japanese it seems better not to use romanization.

examples.japanese: 健康管理には毎日三十分ぐらいの運動をするのが効果的だと思われる。
examples.english: To look after your health, it is apparently effective to exercise for about 30 minutes every day.

meaning_en: Be ~ and
formation:
Vて | おり | | 
 | 話しており | Be speaking and |
explanation: Vます of the auxiliary verb おる.

examples.japanese: この入口は従業員専用になっており、一般の人はここからは入れない。
examples.english: This entrance is for employees only and other people (literally: general people) cannot enter from here.

examples.japanese: 彼は最近プラモデルに凝っており、暇さえあれば模型の飛行機に組み立てている。
examples.english: He is crazy about plastic models these days and is assembling model planes whenever he has free time.

examples.japanese: 日本では義務教育がよく行き届いており、識字率はほとんど１００パーセントに近い。
examples.english: In Japan compulsory education is very thorough (literally: prevails thoroughly) and the literacy rate is almost 100 percent.

examples.japanese: この高校は全寮制になっており、全学生が三つの寮で生活している。
examples.english: This high school is a boarding school (literally: total dormitory system) and all the students live in three dormitories

meaning_en: Through; by the medium of; via; throughout
formation:
Noun | を通して | | 
 | 先生を通して | Through my teacher |
explanation: A compound particle that is used to indicate a medium through which something is done or time through which something takes place.

examples.japanese: 私は親しい友達を通してそのピアニストと知り合いになった。
examples.english: I became acquainted with the pianist through a close friend of mine.

examples.japanese: 私は一年を通して五回ぐらい海外に行っている。
examples.english: I go abroad about 5 times a year (literally: throughout the year).

examples.japanese: お書きになった御本を通して、先生のことは存じ上げておりました。
examples.english: I knew of you through the books you wrote.

examples.japanese: その事件のことは新聞の記事を通して知っていた。
examples.english: I knew about the incident from newspaper articles.

examples.japanese: その政治家は、首相の側近を通して、首相に接近した。
examples.english: That politician approached the Prime Minister through his entourage.

examples.japanese: 二人は手紙のやり取りを通して親しくなっていった。
examples.english: Through an exchange of letters, the two became close.

examples.japanese: ラジオもテレビも全国の放送網を通して放送される。
examples.english: Both radio and television programs are broadcast through the nationwide network.

examples.japanese: 海外生活の経験を通して色々なことを学んだ。
examples.english: I have learned all sorts of things through my life in foreign countries.

meaning_en: For; in; since
formation:
(i) Noun (duration) | 来 | | 
 | 三十年来 | For the past 30 years | 
(ii) Noun (duration) | 来 | | 
 | 六十年来の大地震 | The strongest earthquake in 60 years |
explanation: During a certain amount of time (something has continued up until the moment of speech or something has never been like the current state).

examples.japanese: トムは二十年来日本語の勉強を続けている。
examples.english: Tom has been studying Japanese for the past 20 years.

examples.japanese: 今年の冬は五十年来の寒さだ。
examples.english: This winter is the coldest one in 50 years.

examples.japanese: 父は三十年来、同じ会社に勤めています。
examples.english: My father has been employed in the same company for the past 30 years.

examples.japanese: 私はこの研究を十年来続けてきました。
examples.english: I've been continuing this research for the past 10 years.

examples.japanese: 夜半来の雨が、ようやく上がったようだ。
examples.english: The rain which started after midnight appeared to have finally stopped.

examples.japanese: 僕と岡田とは四十年来の友人だ。
examples.english: Okada and I have been friends for the past 40 years.

examples.japanese: 今年の夏は六十年来の暑さだそうだ。
examples.english: They say that this summer is the warmest in 60 years.

examples.japanese: これは三十年来の大雪です。
examples.english: This is the heaviest snow we have had in 30 years.

meaning_en: The ~ (in question); that (same); the usual
formation:
例の | Noun | | 
 | 例の問題 | The problem (in question) |
explanation: A phrase which signals that the referent of the following noun phrase is definite and that the speaker expects the hearer to understand what the referent is.

examples.japanese: 例のプロジェクトはどうなりましたか。
examples.english: What happened to the project (in question)?

examples.japanese: 今年の忘年会はまた例の中華料理屋だそうだ。
examples.english: I heard that this year's year-end party is going to be at that Chinese restaurant again.

examples.japanese: 例のレポートは出来ましたか。
examples.english: Have you finished the report (I requested, you mentioned, etc.)?

examples.japanese: 例のコピーが出来ましたよ。
examples.english: The copy (you asked for) is ready.

examples.japanese: 例のダイアナ妃の本、さっそく買って読んだよ。
examples.english: I bought the book about Princess Diana (everybody is talking about, you recommended, etc.) right away and read it.

examples.japanese: A：一時に学生が来るんですよ。B: ああ、例のドイツから来た学生ですね。
examples.english: A: student is coming at one. B: Oh, that student from Germany (you mentioned), right?

examples.japanese: 今晩、会える？B:ええ、いいわよ。A: じゃ、六時に例の喫茶店で。
examples.english: A: Can we meet this evening? B: sure. A: Then, (let's meet) at the usual coffee house at six.

examples.japanese: 吉田さんがまた例の冗談を言ったが誰も笑わなかった。
examples.english: Mr. Yoshida told us that (same) joke again, but no one laughed.

meaning_en: Even; if ~ only; if ~ just; as long as; the only thing ~ need is
formation:
(i) Noun | さえ | | 
 | 鹿さえ出る | Even deer appear | 
 | 刺身さえ食べる | Eat even sashimi | 
(ii) Noun(Particle) | さえ | | 
 | アフリカ(へ/に) さえ行った | Went even to Africa | 
(iii) Noun Particle | さえ | | 
 | こんな街にさえある | Exist even in such a town | 
 | 私にさえ分かる | Understandable even to me | 
 | 学校でさえ教える | Teach even at school | 
 | 犬とさえ遊ぶ | Play even with a dog | 
 | 中国からさえ来る | Come even from China | 
(iv) Noun (Particle) | でさえ | | 
 | 専門家でさえ分からない | Even professionals don’t understand (literally: one doesn’t understand something even if he is a professional) | 
 | 果物でさえ食べない | Don’t eat even fruit (literally: don’t eat something even if it is fruit) | 
 | 私からでさえもらわない | Don’t accept (something) even from me (literally: don’t receive something even if it is from me) | 
(v) Vて | さえ (いる/もらう/etc.) | | 
 | 読んでさえいない | Have not even read | 
 | 見てさえ分からない | Don’t understand even by looking at | 
(vi) Vます | さえする | | 
 | 書きさえする | Even write | 
(vii) Adjective い stem | くさえある | | 
 | 安くさえある | Be even inexpensive | 
(viii) {Adjective な stem/Noun} | でさえある | | 
 | 便利でさえある | Be even convenient | 
 | 学者でさえある | Be even a scholar |
explanation: An emphatic particle which expresses the idea of "even" in non-conditional clauses (or sentences) or the idea of "only" in conditional clauses.

examples.japanese: 彼女は現代日本語は勿論古典さえ読める。
examples.english: She can read even classical Japanese, not to mention modern Japanese.

examples.japanese: この研究所にはアメリカからさえ研究者が来る。
examples.english: Researchers even from America visit this lab.

examples.japanese: その歌は子供でさえ知っている。
examples.english: Even children know this song.

examples.japanese: ここに置いておきさえすれば後はここの人が全部やってくれます。
examples.english: If you just leave it here, the people in this place will take care of the rest.

examples.japanese: この仕事さえ片付いたら後は楽なんです。
examples.english: If we can only finish (literally: If we only finish) this work, the rest will be easy.

examples.japanese: 彼はもうおかゆさえ喉を通らなかった。
examples.english: He was no longer able to eat even porridge.

examples.japanese: 私はその写真を大人には勿論子供にさえ見せた。
examples.english: I showed the picture even to kids, not to mention adults.

examples.japanese: 彼は私の言うことを聞こうとさえしない。
examples.english: He doesn't even try to listen to me.

meaning_en: As might be expected; after all; it is only natural that ~; naturally; truly; really; indeed; impressive
formation:
(i) さすが | にSentence | | 
 | さすがに、疲れた | It is only natural that I got tired | 
(ii) さすが | (は)Nounだ | | 
 | さすが(は)日本の車だ | After all, it is a Japanese car | 
(iii) さすが | {V/Adjective い}informalだけ{あって/に} | | 
 | さすがよく{勉強する/勉強した}だけ{あって/に} | As might be expected from the fact that someone studies/has studied hard | 
 | さすが{面白い/面白かった}だけ{あって/に} | As might be expected from the fact that something is/was interesting | 
(iv) さすが | {Noun (Ø/だった)/Adjective な(な/だった)} だけ{あって/に} | | 
 | さすが{若い人/若い人だった} だけ{あって/に} | as might be expected from the fact that someone is/was a young person | 
 | さすが{綺麗/綺麗だった} だけ{あって/に} | As might be expected from the fact that something/someone {is/was} beautiful | 
(v) さすが | のNounも | | 
 | さすがの天才も | Even a genius |
explanation: An adverb that expresses the speaker's/writer's strong feeling that something has turned out as s/he expected.

examples.japanese: ネルソンさんは日本に三年留学していたので、さすがに日本語が上手です。
examples.english: Because Mr. Nelson has studied in Japan for three years, naturally he speaks Japanese well.

examples.japanese: さすが（は）広島のかきだ。実に美味しい。
examples.english: After all, they are Hiroshima oysters. They are really good.

examples.japanese: さすが元ボートの選手だけ{あって/に}、体格がいい。
examples.english: After all, he is a former boating man. He has a fine physique.

examples.japanese: さすが、パリで十年暮らしただけ{あって/に}、彼は大変フランス通だ。
examples.english: It is only natural that he is well versed in things French, because he lived in Paris for 10 years.

examples.japanese: 難しい質問に、さすがの大先生も、困ってしまった。
examples.english: The great teacher that he was, even he had a hard time answering the difficult question.

examples.japanese: 昨日は十時間も運転をしたので、さすがに疲れました。
examples.english: Yesterday I drove a car for 10 hours, so I got tired, as might be expected.

examples.japanese: 運動を何もしないで、食べてばかりいたから、さすがに太ってしまった。
examples.english: It is only natural that I gained weight, because I was just eating without doing any exercise.

examples.japanese: いつも、CDで音楽を聞いているんですが、生のコンサートはさすがにいいですね。
examples.english: I'm always listening to music on CDs, but concerts are good, after all.

meaning_en: Because; due to
formation:
(i) Nounの | せい (で/か/etc.) | | 
 | 過労のせいで | Because of overworking | 
(ii) Sinformal | せい (で/か/etc.) | The same as the relative clause formation | 
 | 働きすぎたせいで | Because someone worked too hard |
explanation: A dependent noun expressing a cause which brings about an undesirable result.

examples.japanese: 今年は不況のせいで車があまり売れない。
examples.english: Because of the depression, cars are not selling well this year.

examples.japanese: 寝不足のせいか体に力が入らない。
examples.english: Because of lack of sleep, I suppose, I feel weak (literally: the body has no power).

examples.japanese: 私が失敗したのは彼のせいだ。
examples.english: It is because of him that I failed.

examples.japanese: 昨夜飲みすぎたせいで今日は頭がふらふらする。
examples.english: I am dizzy today because I drank too much last night.

examples.japanese: 最近運動不足のせいで体重が増えた。
examples.english: I've gained weight because of lack of exercise these days.

examples.japanese: 雨が少なかったせいで今年は米が不作だそうだ。
examples.english: It is reported that because there was little rain, we are going to have a bad crop of rice this year.

examples.japanese: 年のせいか最近耳が聞こえにくくなった。
examples.english: Due to my age, I suppose, I cannot hear well these days.

examples.japanese: 新しい土地に来て水が変わったせいか近頃お腹の調子がよくない。
examples.english: Maybe because I have moved to a new place and the water is different, my stomach is uncomfortable these days.

meaning_en: At least
formation:
(i) せめて | Number+Counter (ぐらい)~ | | 
 | せめて二時間ぐらい | At least two hours | 
(ii) せめて | Noun{ぐらい/(だけ)でも} | | 
 | せめて新聞{ぐらい/(だけ)でも} | At least a newspaper | 
(iii) せめて | Noun Particle | | 
 | せめて妻に | At least to my wife |
explanation: An adverb that indicates the speaker/writer's minimally satisfactory level.

examples.japanese: 百点とは言いませんが、せめて八十点ぐらいは取りたいです。
examples.english: I am not saying that I want to get 100 points, but I would like to get at least 80 points.

examples.japanese: せめて鍋（だけ）でもあれば、ご飯が炊けるんですが。
examples.english: If we had a pan, at least, we would be able to cook rice.

examples.japanese: せめて両親には分かってもらいたいんですが。
examples.english: I wanted at least my parents to understand me.

examples.japanese: せめて一年に十日ぐらい、休暇が取れるといいんですが。
examples.english: I wish I could take at least 10-day's leave each year.

examples.japanese: 日本にいる間に、せめて一度ぐらいは会いに来て下さい。
examples.english: Please come and see me at least once while you are in Japan.

examples.japanese: 美人でなくてもいいけど、せめて、可愛らしい女の子と結婚したい。
examples.english: It's alright if she is not a real beauty. But I would like to marry at least a cute girl.

examples.japanese: 日本に行くんだから、せめて、日本語だけは勉強して来ようと思っています。
examples.english: I am going to Japan, so, I'm thinking of learning at least Japanese.

examples.japanese: せめてもう後一日生きていたら、父の死に目に会えたのに。
examples.english: If my father lived at least one day longer I could have been with him when he died.

meaning_en: Moreover; furthermore; besides; on top of that; what's more; what's worse; more surprisingly; at that; nevertheless; and yet; even so
formation:
(i) {V/Adjective/Noun+Copula}て | しかも | | 
 | 結婚していて、しかも子供までいる | Someone is married, and what’s more, s/he even has a child | 
 | 面白くて、しかも只だ | Something is interesting, and what’s more, it is free of charge | 
 | ハンサムで、しかもお金持ちだ | Someone is handsome, and what’s more, he is rich | 
 | 失業中で、しかも病気だ | Someone is out of work, and what’s worse, s/he is ill | 
(ii) Vます | しかも | | 
 | よく働き、しかも不平を言わない | Someone works hard, and yet (or nevertheless), s/he does not complain | 
(iii) Adjectiveい/く | しかも | | 
 | 値段が安く、しかも丈夫だ | Something is cheap; furthermore, it’s durable | 
(iv) Sentence1 | しかもSentence2 | | 
 | この仕事は面白い。しかも給料がいい | This job is interesting. On top of that, the pay is good |
explanation: A conjunction which is used to provide additional important information.

examples.japanese: 最近のテープレコーダーは小さくて軽く、しかも音が素晴らしくよくなった。
examples.english: The tape recorders available these days are compact and light, and on top of that, their sound has improved greatly.

examples.japanese: 彼は家を買った。しかも大きい庭付きのを（だ）。
examples.english: He bought a house, and more surprisingly, a house with a large yard.

examples.japanese: 彼はいつも夜遅くまで勉強し、しかも朝は誰よりも早く起きる。
examples.english: He studies till late every night; nevertheless, he gets up earlier than anyone else.

examples.japanese: 彼女は美人でしかも頭がいい。男子学生が夢中になるのも無理はない。
examples.english: She is pretty, and what's more, (she is) smart. It is natural that boys (literally: male students) should be crazy about her.

examples.japanese: 日本語は語彙が英語と全然違うし文法も難しい。しかも、日本語には漢字がある。
examples.english: Japanese has entirely different vocabulary from English, and the grammar is also difficult. On top of that, Japanese has kanji.

examples.japanese: あのレストランの定食は美味しくて安い。しかも、ボリュームがあるから学生や若いサラリーマンに人気がある。
examples.english: That restaurant's teishoku (set meal) is good and reasonable. On top of that, it is substantial (literally: it has volume), so it is popular among students and young white-collar workers.

examples.japanese: 彼はこの大雨の中を出かけて行った。しかも、傘も持たずに。
examples.english: He went out in this heavy rain, and more surprisingly, without an umbrella.

examples.japanese: 彼は試験に遅刻してしまった。しかも、三十分も。
examples.english: He was late for the exam, and what's worse, as much as thirty minutes late.

meaning_en: Therefore; accordingly; consequently
formation:
Sentence1 | したがってSentence2 | | 
 | 雨がよく降る。したがって緑が多い | It rains a lot. Therefore there is a lot of greenery |
explanation: A conjunction that is used to indicate that a result/situation follows necessarily from the foregoing situation.

examples.japanese: 予算が不足している。したがってこの計画は実行できない。
examples.english: The budget is insufficient. Therefore this plan cannot be implemented.

examples.japanese: 今週は重役達は朝から晩まで会議で忙しい。したがって好きなゴルフをする暇もない。
examples.english: This week the executives are busy attending meetings from morning till night. Therefore they don't even have time to play their favourite golf.

examples.japanese: 運動をすると、エネルギーを使う。したがって太らない。
examples.english: If you do exercise, you use energy. Accordingly you don't gain weight.

examples.japanese: 日本の車は故障が少ない。したがってよく売れる。
examples.english: Japanese cars have fewer troubles. Therefore they sell well.

examples.japanese: 彼女は日本に五年も住んでいた。したがって日本のことをよく知っている。
examples.english: She lived in Japan for five years. Therefore she knows a lot about Japan.

examples.japanese: 日本では父親はあまり家にいない。したがって母親が子供の教育をすることになる。
examples.english: In Japan fathers are seldom at home. Therefore mothers are in charge of their children's education.

meaning_en: But; yet; even so
formation:
(i) A: | Sentence1 | | 
B: | そうかと言って、Sentence2 | | 
A: | 漫画は面白いですね | Comic books are fun | 
B: | そうかと言って、漫画ばかり読んでいるわけにもいきませんよ | But you can’t read just comic books, you know | 
(ii) Sentence1が | そうかと言って、Sentence2 | | 
 | 漫画は面白いですが、そうかと言って、漫画ばかり読んでいるわけにもいきませんよ | Comic books are fun , but you can’t read just comic books, you know |
explanation: A structure which expresses that the speaker/writer cannot easily accept the corollary from the preceding statement owing to some circumstances, although he feels like accepting it

examples.japanese: Ａ：魚が体にいいそうですよ。Ｂ：そうかと言って、毎日魚ばかりを食べているわけにもいかないでしょう。
examples.english: A: I hear that fish is good for your health. B: But we couldn't eat just fish every day, you know.

examples.japanese: アメリカの方が土地も家も安いが、そうかと言って、簡単に移住するわけにもいかない。
examples.english: Land and housing are less expensive in America, but we cannot easily immigrate.

examples.japanese: A: 手ぶらで来て下さいと言っていましたよ。B: そうかと言って、何も持って行かないわけにもいかないでしょうね。
examples.english: A: He told me not to bring anything. B: But, we cannot go there empty handed, you know.

examples.japanese: A: 明日の試験はとても易しいそうですよ。B: そうかと言って、何も勉強しないわけにもいかないでしょう。
examples.english: A: They say that tomorrow's examination is very easy. B: But still, it can't mean that we don't need to study at all.

examples.japanese: A: 来週は連休だから、遊べますね。B: そうかと言って、ゴルフばかりしているわけにもいかないね。
examples.english: A: There are consecutive holidays next week, so we can have fun. B: But, I cannot just play golf, you know.

examples.japanese: A: 煙草は体に悪いですよ。B: そうかと言って、煙草に代わる物が見つからないし。
examples.english: A: Cigarettes are bad for your health, you know. B: Even so, I cannot find a substitute for cigarettes.

examples.japanese: A：毎日三十分くらい運動するといいそうですよ。B: そうかと言って、それだけの時間は作れないしね。
examples.english: A: They say that it's good to exercise for about 30 minutes every day. B: But it is next to impossible to make that amount of free time, you know.

examples.japanese: 漢字をもっと覚えなければならないのは分かっているが、そうかと言って、漢字ばかり覚えているわけにもいかない。
examples.english: I know I have to memorize more kanji, but even so, I cannot memorize just kanji.

meaning_en: So; because of that; therefore
formation:
Sentence1 | そこで、Sentence2 | | 
 | 会議室が使えなくなった。そこで、食堂で打ち合わせをすることにした。 | The conference room has become unavailable. So, we’ve decided to have the meeting in the cafeteria |
explanation: A conjunction which connects a situation presented as a reason and an action taken because of that situation

examples.japanese: 友達が夕食は簡単なものでいいと言った。そこで、ピザを注文した。
examples.english: My friend told me that something simple would be fine for supper. So, I ordered a pizza.

examples.japanese: 荷物が沢山あるのに雨が降り出した。そこで、タクシーで行くことにした。
examples.english: I had a lot of baggage and it began to rain. Therefore, I decided to go by taxi.

examples.japanese: リーダーの山田さんが来られなくなった。そこで、ミーティングは延期せざるをえなくなった。
examples.english: It has turned out that our leader Mr. Yamada can't come, so we have no choice but to postpone the meeting.

examples.japanese: 試験の日に怪我をして学校へ行けなくなった。そこで、先生に電話して別の日に受けられるか聞いてみた。
examples.english: I got injured and couldn't go to school on the day of an exam. So, I called my teacher to ask if I could take it another day.

examples.japanese: 彼はすべて私が悪かったような言い方をした。そこで、私も黙っていられなくなって、言い返した。
examples.english: He talked as if it were all my fault. Therefore, I couldn't hold my tongue and I talked back.

examples.japanese: 息子が来年大学なんですが英語が苦手で困っているんです。そこで、お願いがあるんですが、息子に英語を教えてやっていただけませんか。
examples.english: My son is going to college next year but he is not good at English (literally: and has trouble with it). Therefore, I'd like to ask a favour of you. Could you teach him English?

examples.japanese: 私が手を振ったら、そこで拍手をして下さい。
examples.english: When I wave my hand, (literally: then,) please clap your hands.

examples.japanese: 彼は飲み物を勧めるかもしれません。そこで、遠慮をしてはいけません。
examples.english: He might offer you a drink. At that time you mustn't hesitate.

examples.japanese: 一時間たったら私が「やめ！」と言いますから、そこで書くのをやめて鉛筆を置いて下さい。
examples.english: In an hour I will say, "Stop!" Then, stop writing and put your pencils down.

examples.japanese: 私が合図をしたら、そこで皆さんお立ち願います。
examples.english: When I give you a signal, (literally: then,) you will all stand up, please.

meaning_en: But; in spite of that
explanation: A conjunction used to indicate that in spite of the negative situation mentioned in the previous part of the sentence/discourse some positive effort is made.

examples.japanese: トムはフットボールの選手としては小さいが、そこを脚力で補っている。
examples.english: Tom is small for a football player, but he makes up for it with his swift legs.

examples.japanese: Ａ：これ以上金を貸すわけにはいかないよ。Ｂ：そこを何とかして下さいませんか。
examples.english: A: I cannot loan you more money than this. B: But, could you do something about it?

examples.japanese: 彼は頭はそれほどよくないが、そこを努力で何とかやっている。
examples.english: He is not that bright, but he manages to get along on his efforts.

examples.japanese: その女優はもう年齢を隠すことは出来ないが、そこを芸で何とか持たせている。
examples.english: The actress cannot hide her age any longer, but she is somehow preserving herself with her arts.

examples.japanese: お忙しいとは存じますが、そこを何とか出席していただけないでしょうか。
examples.english: I know that you are busy, but I wonder if you could possibly attend it.

examples.japanese: A: こんな成績じゃ、君、卒業できないよ。B: そこを、先生、どうにかしていただけないでしょうか。
examples.english: A: With such poor grades, you cannot graduate, you know. B: But, could you do something about it, Professor?

examples.japanese: A: こんな企画に予算を付けるわけにはいかないな。B: 部長、そこを何とか一つお願いします。
examples.english: A: I cannot allocate a budget for such a project. B: But, chief, could you give me a chance?

meaning_en: Almost
formation:
Vます | そうになる | | 
 | 忘れそうになる | Someone almost forgets something | 
 | わかりそうになる | Someone almost understands something | 
 | 失職しそうになる | Someone almost loses his/her job |
explanation: A phrase expressing that something almost happens.

examples.japanese: 冷たい雨の中を傘もささないで歩いていたら、風邪を引きそうになった。
examples.english: While walking in the cold rain without using an umbrella, I almost caught a cold.

examples.japanese: 私は子供の時、プールで危うく溺れそうになったことがある。
examples.english: When I was a child I almost drowned in a swimming pool.

examples.japanese: 昨日もうちょっとで車にひかれそうになった。
examples.english: Yesterday I almost got run over by a car.

examples.japanese: 地震で僕の家は潰れそうになった。
examples.english: My house almost got destroyed by an earthquake.

examples.japanese: 庭の古い松の木が台風で倒れそうになった。
examples.english: An old pine tree in the yard almost fell down in the typhoon.

examples.japanese: 今日混んだ電車の中で、財布をすられそうになった。
examples.english: Today in a crowded train I almost got my purse pickpocketed.

examples.japanese: 数学の試験で最後の問題がもう少しで解けそうになった時に、時間切れになってしまった。
examples.english: In the math exam, I was almost able to solve the last problem when the time was up.

examples.japanese: やっと日本へ行けそうになった時に、母が病気になってしまった。
examples.english: When I was almost able to go to Japan my mother got ill.

meaning_en: On top of that; besides; moreover; furthermore; what's more; what's worse; not only ~ but also
formation:
(i) {V/Adjective/Noun+Copula}て | その上 | | 
 | いつでも使えて、その上、無料だ | You can use it any time, and on top of that, it’s free | 
 | おいしくて、その上、栄養がある | It’s delicious and what’s more， nutritious | 
 | 不便で、その上、家賃が高い | It’s inconvenient, and moreover，the rent is expensive. | 
 | 純金製で、その上、ダイヤがはまっている | It’s made of pure gold, and besides, it has a diamond (literally: a diamond is embedded) | 
(ii) Vます | その上 | | 
 | ほめられ、その上、ほうびまでもらった | I was praised，and what’s more, I was given an award | 
(iii) Adjective い | くその上 | | 
 | 話が面白く、その上、読みやすい | The story is interesting, and on top of that, it’s easy to read | 
(iv) Sentence し | その上 | | 
 | その仕事はつまらないし、その上、給料が悪い | The job is boring, and what’s worse, the pay is bad | 
(v) Sentence | その上 | | 
 | その老人は体が不自由。その上、耳が遠い | The old man is disabled. Furthermore, he is hard of hearing |
explanation: A conjunction which introduces an additional, emphatic statement.

examples.japanese: 彼は一緒にアパートを探してくれて、その上、引っ越しまで手伝ってくれた。
examples.english: He looked for an apartment with me, and moreover, he even helped me move.

examples.japanese: この仕事は給料がいいし、その上、時々外国に行く機会もある。
examples.english: This job pays a good salary, and what's more, it offers opportunities to go abroad from time to time.

examples.japanese: バナナは安い。その上、栄養も豊富だ。
examples.english: Bananas are cheap. On top of that, they are nutritious.

examples.japanese: 彼女は美人で、その上、気立てがいいから、みんなに好かれている。
examples.english: Everybody loves her because she is not only pretty but also good-natured (literally: because she is pretty, and what's more, she is good-natured).

examples.japanese: 先生のうちに就職の相談に行ったら、色々アドバイスを頂いて、その上、夕食までごちそうになった。
examples.english: When I went to my professor's house to consult him about my job, he gave me all kinds of advice, and on top of that, he even served me dinner.

examples.japanese: ジョンのうちに遊びに行ったら、家のペンキ塗りを手伝わされ、その上、芝刈りまでさせられた。
examples.english: When I went to see John at his place, he got me to help him paint his house, and what's more, he even got me to mow the lawn.

examples.japanese: このアパートは通勤に便利で家賃も安く、その上、駐車場まである。
examples.english: This apartment is convenient for commuting and the rent is reasonable. Moreover, it even has a parking space.

examples.japanese: 日本語は構造が英語とかなり違うし、その上、漢字があるから、アメリカ人に習得が難しい。
examples.english: The structure of Japanese is considerably different from that of English, and on top of that, it has kanji; therefore, it is difficult for Americans to learn.

meaning_en: Nevertheless; yet; but in spite of that; even so
formation:
(i) Sentence1(しかし) | それでもSentence2 | | 
 | 悪い天気だった。(しかし) それでも私達は出かけた | The weather was bad. Nevertheless we went out | 
(ii) Sentence2{が/けれど(も)/のに}、 | それでもSentence2 | | 
 | 悪い天気だった{が/けれど(も)/のに}、それでも私達は出かけた | The weather was bad. Nevertheless we went out |
explanation: In spite of the circumstance expressed in the preceding sentence.

examples.japanese: 両親は二人の結婚に反対している。それでも二人は結婚するつもりらしい。
examples.english: The parents are opposed to the couple's marriage. Nevertheless, they seem intent to marrying.

examples.japanese: 暑いので扇風機をつけたが、それでもまだ暑かった。
examples.english: It was so hot that we turned on an electric fan, but it was still hot.

examples.japanese: 父はひどい風邪を引いていた。しかしそれでも旅行に出かけた。
examples.english: My father was suffering from a bad cold. Nevertheless, he went on a trip.

examples.japanese: この本はとても高いのに、それでもいい本だから、よく売れている。
examples.english: This book is very expensive, yet it is selling well, because it is a good book.

examples.japanese: 彼はとても忙しいのに、それでもジョギングを一日も欠かさない。
examples.english: He is very busy, yet he does not miss jogging even a day.

examples.japanese: A: そのオーバー、高いねえ。 B: それでも買うつもり？
examples.english: A: This overcoat is expensive, isn't it? B: But do you intend to buy it?

meaning_en: On the contrary; far from that; as a matter of fact
formation:
(i) Sentence1 | それどころかSentence2 | | 
 | 暑くない。それどころか寒い | It’s not hot. On the contrary, it’s cold | 
(ii) A: Sentence | | | 
B: | それどころか{が、/ではない。/じゃない。}Sentence | | 
A: | 疲れたね。 | Tired, aren’t we? | 
B: | それどころか{が、/じゃない。}死にそうなんだよ | Far from it. I’m almost dead |
explanation: A conjunction that is used to indicate that the level/degree of a fact or a situation expressed in the second sentence is far above or below the level/degree of a fact or a situation expressed in the first sentence.

examples.japanese: スミスさんは漢字が書けない。それどころか、平仮名も満足に書けない。
examples.english: Mr. Smith cannot write kanji. As a matter of fact, he cannot write even hiragana satisfactorily.

examples.japanese: Ａ：今晩パーティーに行かない？ Ｂ：それどころ{か、/じゃないよ。}親父が入院したんだ。
examples.english: A: Shall we go to the party tonight? B: No way (literally: Far from it). Dad got hospitalized.

examples.japanese: あの人は若くはありませんよ。それどころか、お孫さんが三人もいるんですよ。
examples.english: She is not young. On the contrary, she has as many as three grandchildren.

examples.japanese: お金は一銭もありません。それどころか、借金で苦しんでいるんです。
examples.english: I don't have a penny. As a matter of fact, I'm suffering from debts.

examples.japanese: ジムは日本語の会話が出来ない。それどころか、簡単な挨拶も日本語で出来ない。
examples.english: Jim cannot speak Japanese. In fact, he cannot even make simple greetings in Japanese.

examples.japanese: A: 風邪を引いたんだって？B:それどころか、肺炎になって、入院していたんだ。
examples.english: A: Did you have a cold? (literally: I heard that you had a cold, but is it true?) B: On the contrary, I had pneumonia and got hospitalized.

examples.japanese: A：映画を見に行こうか？B:それどころじゃないよ。今晩が徹夜しなければならないほど忙しいんだ。
examples.english: A: Shall we go see a movie? B; Are you kidding? (literally: Far from it) Tonight I'm so busy that I have to stay up all night.

examples.japanese: A:和子、手伝ってくれる？B:それどころじゃないのよ、今宿題で忙しくて。
examples.english: A: Kazuko, can you help me? B; No way, I'm busy doing my homework, you know.

meaning_en: Well (contrary to your expectation; I'm afraid to say this, but)
explanation: An interjection which signals that the speaker is going to provide an unexpected response to a question.

examples.japanese: Ａ：奨学金がもらえそうですか。Ｂ：（いえ）それが難しそうなんです。
examples.english: A: Does it look like you can get a scholarship? B: Well, (no,) it looks difficult.

examples.japanese: A: 試験、どうだった？B:それが、駄目だったんだ。
examples.english: A: How was the exam? B: Well, (I'm sorry to say this, but) it was no good.

examples.japanese: A: 来年は日本で働くんですね。B: いや、それが行けなくなってしまったんです。
examples.english: A: You're going to work in Japan next year, aren't you? B: Well, no, it's turned out that I can't go.

examples.japanese: A：彼女に会って話したんだろう。B: それが、合ったことは合ったんだけど、顔を見たら何も言えなくなってしまって。
examples.english: A: You met her and talked to her, right? B: Well, I did meet her, but when I saw her face, I couldn't say anything.

meaning_en: What's more; what's worse; at that; furthermore; moreover; on top of that
formation:
(i) AdverbPhrase1 | それもAdverbPhrase2(Verbal) | | 
 | 日本語で、それもくずし字で書いてある | It is written in Japanese, and what’s worse, in flowing style | 
(ii) AP1 | それもAP2(Noun) | | 
 | ダイヤ(の)、それも二カラットのダイヤの指輪だ | It is a diamond ring, and a 2-karat diamond ring at that | 
(iii) Clause1 | それもClause2 | | 
 | 新築で、それも駅から五分という便利な所にある | It is newly built, and on top of that, it is conveniently located five minutes from the station |
explanation: A conjunction which is used to add more specific information to information about a rather uncommon action or state.

examples.japanese: 英語で、それも早口で話されたので全然分からなかった。
examples.english: Because he spoke (literally: I was talked to) in English, and what's worse, rapidly, I didn't understand anything.

examples.japanese: 彼女は銀座の、それも一流の店でばかり買い物をする。
examples.english: She always does her shopping at shops in Ginza, and moreover, at first-class ones.

examples.japanese: 子供が五人もいて、それもいたずら盛りの男の子ばかりなので、野口さんの奥さんは毎日大変忙しいです。
examples.english: Because she has as many as five children, and moreover, they are all very mischievous boys, Mrs. Noguchi is extremely busy every day.

examples.japanese: 彼はその場で、それも現金で払ってくれた。
examples.english: He paid on the spot, and what's more, in cash.

examples.japanese: 真冬に、それも裸足で走った。
examples.english: I ran in midwinter, and what's more, barefooted.

examples.japanese: その銀行は都心の、それも東京駅前の一当地に本社ビルを建てた。
examples.english: The bank built their headquarters building in central Tokyo, and moreover, on the best spot, in front of Tokyo Station.

examples.japanese: 彼女は雑誌記者、それもゴシップ雑誌の記者に見つかってしまった。
examples.english: She was seen by a magazine reporter, and what's worse, a reporter from a gossip magazine.

examples.japanese: 忙しい学期末に、それも論文の締め切り直前に手紙を訳してくれと頼まれた。
examples.english: I was asked to translate a letter when I was busy at the end of the semester, and what's worse, just before the deadline for my term paper.

meaning_en: (and) in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that
formation:
(i) Noun1{と/に/、}Noun2{と/に/、} | …それにNoun | | 
 | テレビ、ステレオ、それにビデオカメラ | A TV set, a stereo, and, in addition a videocamera | 
(ii) Sentence1し | それにSentence2 | | 
 | その仕事はうまらないし、それに給料が悪い | The job is boring, and what’s worse, the pay is bad | 
(iii) Sentence1 | それに、Sentence2 | | 
 | その老人は体が不自由だ。それに、耳が遠い | The old man is disabled. Furthermore, he is hard of hearing |
explanation: A conjunction which introduces an additional item or statement.

examples.japanese: ここのモーニングセットはコーヒーにトースト、それにゆで卵が付いている。
examples.english: The "morning set" here includes coffee and some toast; in addition, there is a boiled egg (literally: it is accompanied by a boiled egg).

examples.japanese: 車を買っても置く所がないし、それにあまり乗る機会もない。
examples.english: Even if we bought a car, there would be no place to park it, and moreover, there would be few occasions to use it

examples.japanese: 私は家では仕事の話はしないことにしているんです。それに、今晩はとても疲れているので、その話は明日にしてもらえませんか。
examples.english: I make it a rule not to discuss business at home. In addition, I'm very tired this evening, so could we discuss it tomorrow?

examples.japanese: 私のうちには私達夫婦と子供が二人、それに猫と犬が一匹ずついる。
examples.english: My family consists of my wife and me, and two children, and in addition, (there are) a cat and a dog.

examples.japanese: いい仕事がないし、それに子供も日本の学校へ行きたがっているので、日本へ帰ろうと思っている。
examples.english: We are thinking of going back to Japan because there are no good jobs here, and what's more, my child wants to go to a Japanese school.

examples.japanese: ピアノなんか買っても誰も弾く者はないし、それにうちは狭いので置く所がありません。
examples.english: Even if we bought a piano, no one would play it, and moreover, there would be no place to put it because our place is small.

examples.japanese: このアパートは明るくて清潔だ。それに家賃が安い。
examples.english: This apartment is light and clean. Furthermore, the rent is reasonable.

examples.japanese: 昔と違って今は相手がどこにいても電話で簡単に話が出来る。それに、テレビ電話を使うと相手の顔を見ながら話すことも出来る。
examples.english: Unlike the old days, we can easily talk with people over the phone these days no matter where they are. Moreover, if we use a TV telephone, we can talk with someone while watching his or her face.

meaning_en: And; also; in addition; as well
formation:
(i) Noun1{と/に/、}Noun2{と/に/、} | …それと、Noun | | 
 | ビールとチーズ、それと、ポテトチップ | Beer and cheese, and potato chips as well | 
(ii) Sentence1 | それと、Sentence2 | | 
 | 音楽はコーラスをしています。それと、学生の頃フルートを少しやりました | Speaking of music, I am a member of a chorus. In addition, I played flute a little when I was a student |
explanation: A conjunction which introduces an additional item or statement.

examples.japanese: 林檎三つとオレンジ二つ、それと、バナナを三本下さい。
examples.english: Give me three apples and two oranges, and three bananas, as well.

examples.japanese: スポーツはテニスとゴルフをします。それと、学生時代はアイスホッケーをしていました。
examples.english: S1: Speaking of sports, I play tennis and golf. S2: In addition, I played ice hockey at school (literally: in my school days).

examples.japanese: 山田さん、木下さん、上野さん、それと、高橋さんもお見えになります。
examples.english: Mr. Yamada, Mr. Kinoshita, and Mr. Ueno are coming. And Mr. Takahashi, too.

examples.japanese: 外国語はドイツ語にフランス語、それと、日本語が少しが話せます。
examples.english: Talking about foreign languages, I can speak German and French, and a little Japanese.

examples.japanese: 留守中に山村さんと浜田さんからお電話がありました。それと、吉田さんからお手紙が来ております。
examples.english: There were calls from Mr. Yamamura and Mr. Hamada while you were out. Also, a letter came from Mr. Yoshida.

examples.japanese: 緊急の問題は先生をどうするかということです。それと、もう一つ、教室の問題も考えなければなりません。
examples.english: How to get a teacher is the urgent problem. And, for another thing, we have to think about the classroom problem.

examples.japanese: この手紙を昼までにタイプしておいてくれる？あ、それと、昨日頼んでおいた飛行機の切符、取れた？
examples.english: Could you type this letter by noon? Oh, and did (literally: could) you get the air tickets I asked for yesterday?

meaning_en: (yes,) naturally; (yes,) of course; oh, surely
explanation: An interjection which is used when the speaker emphatically provides an expected response to a question.

examples.japanese: Ａ：勝ちたいでしょうね。Ｂ：（ええ）それは勝ちたいですよ。
examples.english: A: I bet you want to win (the game). B: (Yes,) of course, I do.

examples.japanese: A: 国へ帰りたいと思うことがありますか。B: （ええ、）それはありますよ。
examples.english: A: Are there times when you want to go back to your country? B: (Yes,) Of course.

examples.japanese: A: この値段だったらみんな買うでしょうか。B: それは買いますよ。そんな値段では絶対買えませんから。
examples.english: A: I wonder if they would buy (them) for this price. B: They surely would. They could never buy them (anywhere else) for that price.

examples.japanese: A: もっと給料が高い方がいいでしょう？B:そりゃ（あ）そうですが…。
examples.english: A: You would prefer a higher salary, right? B: Naturally, I would, but. . .

meaning_en: Each; respectively
explanation: Each of two or more things/persons.

examples.japanese: 山田さんと鈴木さんは、果物とお菓子をそれぞれ買った。
examples.english: Yamada and Suzuki bought fruits and cakes, respectively.

examples.japanese: 読んだ小説はそれぞれ面白かった。
examples.english: Each of the novels I read was interesting (in its own way).

examples.japanese: 好子、美保子、信夫はそれぞれ十五歳、十三歳、九歳です。
examples.english: Yoshiko, Mihoko, and Nobuo are 15, 13, and 9 years old, respectively.

examples.japanese: 父は私と妹に、それぞれ、一万円のお小遣いをくれた。
examples.english: Father gave me and my younger sister a 10,000 yen allowance each.

examples.japanese: トムは寮の部屋で、僕は図書館で、それぞれ勉強する。
examples.english: Tom and I study in the dorm room and at the library, respectively.

examples.japanese: ボブはベスと、一雄はジェミーと、それぞれ出かけた。
examples.english: Bob and Kazuo went out with Beth and Jemmy, respectively.

examples.japanese: 私達は兄弟だが、趣味がぞれぞれ違う。
examples.english: We are brothers, but each of us has different interests.

examples.japanese: 誰でもそれぞれ長所と短所がある。
examples.english: Each of us has our strengths and weaknesses.

meaning_en: At once; soon; right away; immediately; readily; instantly; easily; right
explanation: Without having much temporal or physical distance.

examples.japanese: 家に帰ったらすぐ、寝てしまいました。
examples.english: I went to sleep as soon as I got home.

examples.japanese: 銀行は駅のすぐ前です。
examples.english: The bank is right in front of the station.

examples.japanese: 部長は会社に着くとすぐ、仕事を始めた。
examples.english: The departmental head started to work as soon as he arrived at the company.

examples.japanese: 日本に来たらすぐ、電話して下さい。
examples.english: Please call me as soon as you come to Japan.

examples.japanese: 話したいから、すぐ来て下さい。
examples.english: I want to talk with you, so please come right away.

examples.japanese: 安いテレビを買ったらすぐ、壊れてしまいました。
examples.english: I bought a cheap TV and it broke right away.

examples.japanese: あの人はすぐ怒るから、嫌いだ。
examples.english: He easily gets angry so I don't like him.

examples.japanese: その数学の問題はすぐ解けた。
examples.english: I could solve that math problem easily.

meaning_en: Only; just; simply; that's all
formation:
(i) ただ | One+Counter (のNoun) | | 
 | ただ一人の息子 | The only son | 
 | ただ一発で | With only one shot | 
(ii) ただ | One+CounterもVerbal(negative) | | 
 | ただ一日も休んだことがない | Have not taken even one day off | 
(iii) ただ | Nounだけ(Particle) | | 
 | Nounだけ(Particle) 単語だけ(を)覚える | Remember only words | 
 | Nounだけ(Particle) 力だけで解決する | Solve something only with force | 
(iv) ただ | Verbal(という)だけ(だ) | | 
 | ただ読んだ(という)だけ(だ) | Someone just read it; that’s all | 
 | ただ安い(という)だけ(だ) | Something is just cheap; that’s all | 
 | ただ{静かな/静かだという}だけ(だ) | Something is just quiet; that’s all | 
 | ただ大学教授(だ)(という)だけ(だ) | Someone is just a college professor; that’s all |
explanation: A conjunction that introduces a supplementary remark.

examples.japanese: 彼のただ一つの欠点は時間にルーズだということだ。
examples.english: His only (one) defect is that he is not punctual (literally: he is slack about time).

examples.japanese: 彼女はただの一度も手紙をくれなかった。
examples.english: She didn't write me even once (literally: only once).

examples.japanese: 彼はただ弁護士だけが頼りだ。
examples.english: He has no one else to rely on but his lawyer.

examples.japanese: 彼女とはただお茶を飲んで話をした（という）だけだ。
