examples.english: I just talked with her over a cup of tea; that's all.

examples.japanese: 彼はただ一人でやってきた。
examples.english: He came over alone.

examples.japanese: 私達が困っていた時、助けてくれた者はただの一人もいなかった。
examples.english: Not a single person helped us when we were in trouble.

examples.japanese: ただそれだけのことで彼を首にしたんでか。
examples.english: Did you fire him only for that reason?

examples.japanese: ただ言われたことだけをやっていても進歩はない。
examples.english: There will be no progress if you do only what you are told to do.

examples.japanese: この辺りは駅にもスーパーにも近くて便利だ。ただ環境があまりよくない。
examples.english: This area is close to both the station and a supermarket, so it's convenient, but the environment is not very good.

examples.japanese: とてもいいコンピュータだと思います。ただ値段が問題ですね。
examples.english: I think this is a very good computer. But, the price is a problem.

meaning_en: Usual; ordinary; plain; common; rank and file
formation:
ただの | Noun | | 
 | ただの先生 | An ordinary teacher |
explanation: Not deserving to be mentioned.

examples.japanese: 私はただの平社員ですから、そんなことは知りません。
examples.english: I'm only an ordinary employee, so I'm not aware of that.

examples.japanese: ただの風邪だと思っていたら、肺炎だった。
examples.english: I thought it was an ordinary cold, but it was pneumonia.

examples.japanese: あの人はただの学者ではないようですね。
examples.english: He doesn't appear to be an ordinary scholar, does he?

examples.japanese: ただの集まりだと思って、顔を出したら、偉い人達が出席していたのでびっくりした。
examples.english: I put in an appearance because I thought it was an ordinary gathering, but to my surprise there were big shots attending.

examples.japanese: A: お父様はお偉い方だったそうですね。B: いいえ、とんでもありません。ただの大学教師でした。
examples.english: A: I heard that your father was a great man. B: No, not at all. He was an ordinary college professor.

examples.japanese: ただの冗談ですよ。
examples.english: I'm just kidding, you know.

meaning_en: Not until; only after; for the first time
formation:
Vて | 初めて | | 
 | 読んで初めて | Only after you read |
explanation: A phrase which expresses the idea that someone does something or something happens only after something else happens or something else is done.

examples.japanese: アメリカへ来て初めて竜巻を見た。
examples.english: It was not until I came to America that I saw a tornado.

examples.japanese: 日本で生活して初めて日本人のものの考え方が分かってきた。
examples.english: It was not until I lived in Japan that I started to understand how Japanese people think.

examples.japanese: 日本語を勉強して初めて外国語を学ぶ面白さを知った。
examples.english: I didn't realise how interesting learning a foreign language was until I studied Japanese.

examples.japanese: 考えは文字にしてみて初めてはっきりすることが多い。
examples.english: It is often not until you write down your idea that it becomes clear.

examples.japanese: 病気になって初めて健康の有り難さが分かる。
examples.english: It is only after you become ill that you realise the value of health.

examples.japanese: 生まれて初めて刺身を食べた。
examples.english: I ate sashimi for the first time in my life.

meaning_en: If; when; because
formation:
(i) Verb | ては | | 
 | 食べては | When/if one eats; to eat | 
(ii) Adjective(い/な) | ては | | 
 | 大きくては | When/if something/someone is big | 
 | 不便では | When/if something is inconvenient | 
(iii) Noun | では | | 
 | 病気では(頼めない) | If someone is ill (I can’t ask him to do something) | 
 | あの先生では(話にならない) | That teacher (would be out of the question) |
explanation: A conjunction which presents an action/state as a topic about which a negative comment is given.

examples.japanese: そんなに勉強しては、体を壊しますよ。
examples.english: If you study that hard, you will ruin your health.

examples.japanese: こんなに寒くては外出できません。
examples.english: We cannot go out in this cold weather (literally: when it is this cold).

examples.japanese: 仕事がそんなに嫌いでは困りますね。
examples.english: It's too bad that you hate your work that much.

examples.japanese: そんなに遊んでいては、試験に失敗しますよ。
examples.english: If you are fooling around like that, you will fail the examination.

examples.japanese: あの男が来ては邪魔になる。
examples.english: If he comes he will get in our way.

examples.japanese: こんなに働かされては、病気になってしまうよ。
examples.english: If I'm forced to work like this, I will end up by becoming ill.

examples.japanese: こんなに部屋が汚くては、お客さんが見えた時に恥ずかしい。
examples.english: Because the room is messy like this, I feel ashamed when I have a guest.

examples.japanese: 人が皆個人主義的では、国はやっていけない。
examples.english: If everybody is individualistic, a country cannot get along well.

meaning_en: At the same time (as); at the time; when; as; while; as well as ~
formation:
(i) Noun | と同時に | | 
 | 到着と同時に | At the same time as someone’s arrival | 
(ii) Vinformal nonpast | と同時に | | 
 | 着くと同時に | At the same time as someone arrives | 
(iii) {Adjective な stem/Noun}である | と同時に{Adjective な stem/Noun}である | | 
 | 便利であると同時に経済的である | Something is economical as well as convenient | 
 | フットボールの選手であると同時に野球の選手である | Someone is a baseball player as well as a football player |
explanation: A phrase which is used to express the idea that someone does something or something takes place at the same time as another action or event, or that someone or something is in two states simultaneously.

examples.japanese: 彼は大学卒業と同時に銀行に就職した。
examples.english: He got a job at a bank at the time of (literally: at the same time as) his graduation from college.

examples.japanese: 部屋に入ると同時に電話が鳴った。
examples.english: The telephone rang (literally: at the same time) as I entered the room.

examples.japanese: 彼はこの会社の社長であると同時に大株主でもある。
examples.english: He is the president of this company and, at the same time, a big stockholder.

examples.japanese: 彼女は結婚と同時に会社を辞めた。
examples.english: She quit her company at the time of (literally: at the same time as) her marriage.

examples.japanese: 銃声と同時に警官の一人が倒れた。
examples.english: We heard the shot and saw one of the policemen fall. (literally: One of the policemen fell at the same time as the sound of a gun.)

examples.japanese: 新しい単語の学習と同時に文法の復習も忘れてはならない。
examples.english: You mustn't forget grammar review as well as new vocabulary study.

examples.japanese: 私はルースと同時に日本語の勉強を始めた。
examples.english: I started my Japanese study when (literally: at the same time as) Ruth did.

examples.japanese: 電車が止まってドアが開くと同時に客がなだれ込んだ。
examples.english: The train came to a halt and as the doors opened the passengers rushed into the train (literally: the passengers rushed into the train at the same time as the doors opened).

meaning_en: Although ~ say/said that ~; even though ~ say/said that ~
formation:
(i) Noun | と言っても | | 
 | 先生と言っても | Although (I) say, “teacher” | 
(ii) {V/Adjective(い/な)/Noun+Copula}informal | と言っても | | 
 | {行く/行った}と言っても | Although (I) say that someone {will go/went} | 
 | {安い/安かった}と言っても | Although (I) say that it is/was cheap | 
 | {静か/静かだった}と言っても | Although (I) say that it is/was quiet | 
 | {病気だ/病気だった}と言っても | Although (I) say that someone is/was ill |
explanation: A phrase which is used to clarify a statement in the preceding discourse which might be misleading.

examples.japanese: 私には子供がいます。子供と言ってももう大学生ですが。
examples.english: I have a child. Well, although I said, "child," he is already a college student (literally: he is already a college student, though).

examples.japanese: Ａ：毎日お忙しいんでしょうね。Ｂ：いえ、忙しいと言っても週末は休んでいますから。
examples.english: A: You are busy every day, aren't you? B: No, although people may say that I'm busy, I do not work on weekends, so . . .

examples.japanese: もう三月だ。しかし、三月と言ってもこの辺はまだ寒い。
examples.english: It's already March. But even though I say, "March," it is still cold around here.

examples.japanese: 山崎先生はまだお若いです。勿論、若いと言っても五十代ですが。
examples.english: Professor Yamazaki is still young. Of course, even though I said, "young," he is in his fifties (literally: he is in his fifties, though)

examples.japanese: 仕事が見つかりました。と言ってもパートなんですが。
examples.english: I've found a job. Well, although I said, "job", it is part-time (literally: it is a part-time job, though).

examples.japanese: A: 韓国語をご存知なんでしょう？B:いや、知っていると言っても二年勉強しただけですから大したことはありません。
examples.english: A: You know Korean, right? B: No, even though people say that I know it, my knowledge is limited because I studied it only two years.

examples.japanese: A：辻村さんが手伝ってくれるそうですよ。B: でも、手伝ってくれると言ってもせいぜい二、三時間でしょう。
examples.english: A: I heard that Mr. Tsujimura will help us. B: But, even though he says that he will help us, it will probably be for a couple of hours at most.

examples.japanese: A: あの子は強いですよ。B: いや、強いと言ってもたかが小学生ですよ。
examples.english: A: That boy is strong, you know. B: Well, even though you say he is strong, he is only an elementary school kid.

meaning_en: In such a way that; in such a fashion to suggest/show (etc.) that; as if to say/show (etc.) that
formation:
(i) Sinformal | という風に | | 
 | 困ったという風に頭を抱えた | Someone held his head in such a fashion as to suggest that he didn’t know what to do | 
(ii) XはA; YはB | という風に | | 
 | 月曜日はピアノ、火曜日はダンスという風に良子は毎日レッスンがある | Yoshiko has a lesson every day –piano on Monday, dance on Tuesday, and so on |
explanation: A phrase which expresses a manner or a way in which someone does something.

examples.japanese: 彼はどうしようもないという風に首を振った。
examples.english: He shook his head as if to say that there was no way out.

examples.japanese: 私は河村さんは来られないという風に聞いている。
examples.english: I have been informed that Mr. Kawamura cannot come. (literally: I have been informed in such a way that I understand that Mr. Kawamura cannot come.)

examples.japanese: 浩司は鰻、友子は天ぷら、という風にめいめいが自分の好きなものを注文した。
examples.english: Each of them ordered the (different) things they liked- Hiroshi, eel, Tomoko, tempura, and so on.

examples.japanese: 彼はもう我慢が出来ないという風に荒々しく立ち上がった。
examples.english: He stood up in a violent manner showing that he could no longer bear it.

examples.japanese: 彼女はもうこれ以上聞きたくないという風に両手で耳を被った。
examples.english: She covered her ears as if to say that she didn't want to listen to it any more.

examples.japanese: 社長には、特に問題はなかったという風に言っておいて下さい。
examples.english: Please tell the president that (literally: tell it to the president in such a way to convey that) there were no particular problems with it.

examples.japanese: この物語は今の社会を風刺しているという風には考えられませんか。
examples.english: Can't we think that (literally: think in such a way that) this story mocks contemporary society?

examples.japanese: そういうことは規則に反するから出来ないという風に説明しておけばいい。
examples.english: You can explain that (literally: explain it in a way to mean that) we cannot do things like that because they are against the rules.

meaning_en: That; the fact that
formation:
Sinformal | ということは | | 
 | 返事がないということは | The fact that there is no reply |
explanation: A phrase which changes a sentence into a topic noun clause.

examples.japanese: 彼がこの集まりに来ないということは考えられない。
examples.english: It is unthinkable that he won't come to this meeting.

examples.japanese: 手紙が戻って来たということは彼女はもうこの住所にはいないということだ。
examples.english: The fact that the letter came back means that she no longer lives at this address.

examples.japanese: 彼が真面目に日本語を勉強していないということは本気で日本で仕事をする気がないのだ。
examples.english: The fact that he is not studying Japanese seriously means that he is not serious about working in Japan.

examples.japanese: これだけ丁寧に説明すれば、分からないということはあり得ない。
examples.english: If we explain it this thoroughly, it is impossible that they won't understand it.

examples.japanese: 空がこんなに赤いということは何かよくないことが起こる前兆かもしれない。
examples.english: This red sky (literally: That the sky is this red) might be an omen that something bad will happen.

examples.japanese: 彼が金を貸してくれたということは私は彼に信用されているということだ。
examples.english: The fact that he lent me money means that I am trusted by him.

examples.japanese: 言うことを聞かないということは体罰を与えるしかないということだ。
examples.english: The fact that he doesn't listen to us means that there is no alternative but to punish him physically.

examples.japanese: 私がこれだけ言っても分からないということはどういうことなんでしょう。
examples.english: What does it mean that he doesn't understand me even though I have talked to him such a lot?

meaning_en: But; although; in spite of the fact that ~
formation:
Sinformal | というのに | | 
 | いい天気だというのに | Although it is a fine day | 
 | 人が来るというのに | Although someone is coming | 
 | 無駄だというのに | Although it is a waste | 
 | 危ないというのに | Although it is dangerous |
explanation: A conjunction to indicate that an action/state takes place quite contrary to one's expectation.

examples.japanese: 四月だというのに、まだ肌寒い。
examples.english: It is April, but still chilly (literally: cold on the skin).

examples.japanese: 明後日はロンドンへ行かなければならないといのに、まだ何も準備していないんですよ。
examples.english: Although I have to go to London the day after tomorrow, I haven't prepared anything yet, you know.

examples.japanese: 彼は母親が危篤だというのに、映画を見に行った。
examples.english: He went to see a movie in spite of the fact that his mother is in a critical condition.

examples.japanese: 年末でとても忙しいというのに、うちの人は一体どこへ行ったのだろう。
examples.english: It's the end of the year, and we are very busy, but where in the world did my husband go?

examples.japanese: 小学四年生だというのに、あの子はもう中学の数学をやっている。
examples.english: The child is a fourth grader, but he is already studying junior high school math.

examples.japanese: 先生がわざわざ本を貸して下さったというのに、読んでいないの？
examples.english: Your teacher kindly loaned a book to you, but you haven't read it?

examples.japanese: 学生は貧乏だというのに、結構いい車を乗り回しているね。
examples.english: Students are said to be poor, but they are driving around in pretty good cars, aren't they?

meaning_en: Mean; the meaning of ~ is; what ~ means is
formation:
(i) Noun/Adjective な stem | というのは | | 
 | マンションというのは | What manshon means is ~ | 
 | 独創的というのは | Dokusouteki means ~ | 
(ii) {VP/AP/Sentence}informal | というのは | | 
 | 「首を切る」というのは | What kubi wo kiru (literally to cut one’s head off) means is ~ | 
 | 「溺れる者はわらをもつかむ」というのは | What oboreru mono wa wara wo mo tsukamu (literally a drowning person cluthes even at a straw) means is ~ | 
(iii) のことだ | | | 
 | 買取のアパートのことだ | ~ means an apartment for purchase | 
(iv) Verb/Adjective | ことだ | The same as the relative clause formation rules | 
 | (何かをするのが)易しいことだ | ~ means ‘easy to do something’ | 
 | (何かが)大好きなことだ | ~ means ‘to like someone a lot’ | 
 | (何かが上手に)なることだ | ~ mean ‘to become skilful in something’ | 
(v) {VP/AP/Sentence}informal | ということだ | | 
 | 細かい所ばかりを見て全体を見ないということだ | ~ means that one sees only details and does not see the whole |
explanation: というのは~ことだ A structure which is used in interpreting, explaining, or defining a word, a phrase, or a sentence.

examples.japanese: パソコンというのはパーソナル・コンピュータのことだ。
examples.english: Pasokon means personal computer.

examples.japanese: 過労死というのは働き過ぎがもとで死ぬ（という）ことだ。
examples.english: Karoushi means to die from overwork.

examples.japanese: 「足が出る」というのは出費が予定していたより多くなる（という）ことだ。
examples.english: Ashi ga deru (literally: a foot sticks out) means that an expense exceeds the amount budgeted.

examples.japanese: 「猿も木から落ちる」というのは上手な人でも時には失敗することがあるということだ。
examples.english: Saru mo ki kara ochiru (literally: even monkeys fall from trees) means that even a skilful person sometimes makes a mistake.

examples.japanese: マイカーというのは個人が持っている車のことだ。
examples.english: Maikaa (literally: my car) means a car owned by an individual.

examples.japanese: 裏口入学というのは試験を受けないで学校に入ることだ。
examples.english: Uraguchi-nyuugaku (literally: entering school through the back door) means to enter a school without taking an entrance exam.

examples.japanese: 「口が軽い」というのは人に言ってはいけないことをすぐ言ってしまう（という）ことだ。
examples.english: Kuchi ga karui (literally: one's mouth is light) means easily telling others things one shouldn't.

examples.japanese: 「頭を絞る」というのはいいアイディアを出そうとして一生懸命考える（という）ことだ。
examples.english: Atama wo shiboru (literally: squeeze one's head) means to think hard to get good ideas.

meaning_en: When ~ mention; if ~ say that ~; when ~ say that ~; when it comes to
formation:
(i) Noun | と言うと | | 
 | 長崎と言うと | When it comes to Nagasaki | 
(ii) Sinformal | と言うと | | 
 | 家を買ったと言うと | If I say that I’ve bought a house |
explanation: A phrase which is used when something which someone has mentioned causes an involuntary response.

examples.japanese: サンフランシスコと言うと、あのケーブルカーを思い出す。
examples.english: When you mention San Francisco, I remember those cable cars.

examples.japanese: 日本語を話すと言うと聞こえはいいんですが、実は簡単な挨拶が出来るだけなんです。
examples.english: It sounds impressive when I say that I can speak Japanese, but the fact is that all I can do is exchange simple greetings.

examples.japanese: パリと言うと、誰でも真っ先にあのエッフェル塔を思い浮かべるだろう。
examples.english: When someone mentions Paris, the (literally: that) Eiffel Tower is the first thing likely to come to everyone's mind.

examples.japanese: 柔道と言うと、毎日練習した学生時代を思い出す。
examples.english: When it comes to judo, I remember my school days when I used to practice it every day.

examples.japanese: 漫画と言うと馬鹿にする人もあるが、あれはあれで面白いのだ。
examples.english: Some people ridicule comics (literally: Some people despise you when you mention comics), but comics are interesting in their own way.

examples.japanese: 東大卒と言うと偉そうに聞こえるが、私は勉強なんか全然しない劣等生だったんです。
examples.english: It sounds great when I say that I am a graduate of the University of Tokyo, but I was (in fact) a poor student who didn't study at all.

examples.japanese: 会社を辞めたと言うと体裁がいいんですが、彼は本当は辞めさせられたんですよ。
examples.english: It sounds good when he says that he quit his company, but the truth of the matter is that he was fired (literally: was made to quit).

meaning_en: Rather than; more ~ than ~
formation:
(i) Adjective い informal | というより(は)、(むしろ)Adjective い/な | | 
 | 涼しいというより(は)、(むしろ)寒い | Cold rather than cool | 
(ii) Adjective な stem | というより(は)、(むしろ)Adjective い/な | | 
 | 奇麗というより(は)、(むしろ)可愛い | Cute rather than pretty | 
(iii) Noun | というより(は)、(むしろ)Noun | | 
 | 青いというより(は)、(むしろ)紫 | Purple rather than blue | 
(iv) Vinformal | というより(は)、(むしろ)Verb | | 
 | 食べるというより(は)、(むしろ)飲み込んでいる | Someone is swallowing rather than eating |
explanation: というより（は）A phrase that is used to indicate more accurate characterisation of someone or something.

examples.japanese: 今年の夏は涼しいというよりは寒かった。
examples.english: This summer was cold rather than cool.

examples.japanese: カーラは臆病というより（は）むしろ用心深い。
examples.english: Kara is cautious rather than timid.

examples.japanese: 本田さんは教育者というより（は）むしろ学者に近い。
examples.english: Mr. Honda is more of a scholar than an educator.

examples.japanese: あの人は酒を飲むというより（は）むしろ酒に飲まれていると言った方がいい。
examples.english: One should say that sake drinks him rather than he drinks sake.

examples.japanese: 私にはこの音楽は楽しいというよりは、むしろやかましい。
examples.english: To me this music is noisy rather than enjoyable.

examples.japanese: あの人は丁寧というよりは、慇懃無礼だ。
examples.english: He is politely insolent rather than polite.

examples.japanese: 彼の説明は簡潔というよりは、むしろ不十分だと言うべきだ。
examples.english: We should say that his explanation is insufficient rather than concise.

examples.japanese: 父は、父親というよりは、むしろいい友達という感じでした。
examples.english: I felt that my father was a good friend rather than a father.

meaning_en: When; then
formation:
Vinformal past | ところ | | 
 | 使ったところ | When someone used (it) |
explanation: A dependent noun which is used to express the idea that when someone did something, something took place as the result.

examples.japanese: 先生に相談したところ、ぜひ大学院に行くよう進められた。
examples.english: When I consulted with my teacher, he strongly advised me to go to graduate school.

examples.japanese: 部長に頼んでみたところ、喜んで引き受けてくれた。
examples.english: When I asked my boss (literally: department chief), he was glad to do it.

examples.japanese: 友達に話したところ、しばらく考えさせて欲しいと言った。
examples.english: When I told one of my friends (about that), he said he would like to think (literally: would like me to let him think) (about it) for a while.

examples.japanese: これまでに書いた論文を本にしたとろこ、意外によく売れた。
examples.english: When I published a book of the papers that I had written (literally: till this time), it sold unexpectedly well.

examples.japanese: 人に勧められてヨガを始めたところ、非常に効果があることが分かった。
examples.english: I started yoga because someone recommended it; then, I realised it had a great effect.

examples.japanese: 冗談のつもりで言ったところ、思わぬ結果になって驚いている。
examples.english: I'm surprised that what I said as a joke had unexpected consequences' (literally: that when I said it as a joke, it brought about an unexpected result).

examples.japanese: その仕事に興味のある旨、手紙を出したところ、すぐに面接をしたいとの返事があった。
examples.english: When I wrote to them saying that I was interested in the job, I got a letter immediately saying they wanted to interview me.

meaning_en: However; but
explanation: A conjunction which is used to present what in fact happened or what is in fact the case when something else was/is expected.

examples.japanese: 日本式の部屋に泊まりたいと思って旅館を予約した。ところが、通された部屋は洋式だった。
examples.english: I wanted to stay in a Japanese-style room and made a reservation at an inn. However, the room I was shown to was a Western-style one.

examples.japanese: Ａ：彼女にプロポーズしたんだろう？どうだった？Ｂ：ところが、駄目だったんだ。
examples.english: A: You proposed to her, right? What happened? B: It didn't work out. (literally: It was no good.)

examples.japanese: 私の娘はアメリカにいる時綺麗な英語を話していた。ところが、日本へ帰って一年もたたないうちにきれいに忘れてしまった。
examples.english: My daughter was speaking beautiful English when she was in America. However, she forgot it completely within a year (literally: even before one year elapsed) after we came back to Japan.

examples.japanese: 日本から来た有名な先生の講演があるというので行ってみた。ところが、その先生は英語が下手で何を言っているのか全然分からなかった。
examples.english: Because I heard that there was going to be a lecture by a famous professor from Japan, I went (to listen to it). However, his English was so bad that I didn't understand what he was saying at all.

examples.japanese: 先生は私達に遅刻してはいけないと何度も言った。ところが、次の日、時間通りに行ってみると先生はまだ来ていなかった。
examples.english: Our teacher repeatedly told us that we mustn't be late for his class. However, when I went to his class on time the next day, he was not yet there.

examples.japanese: アメリカへ来ればいくらでも仕事はあると言われた。ところが、来てみるとアメリカは不況でどこにも仕事はなかった。
examples.english: I was told that if I came to America, there would be a lot of jobs. However, when I came, there were no jobs anywhere because of the depression.

examples.japanese: アメリカでは鋸は押して切る。ところが、日本では引いて切る。
examples.english: In America you push a saw in order to cut; however, in Japan you pull one to cut.

examples.japanese: A: 今晩のパーティー、君も来てくれるね。B: ところが、あいにく行けないの。
examples.english: A: [male speech] You can come to tonight's party, too, can't you? B: [female speech] No, I'm afraid I can't.

meaning_en: No matter ~ may be; even if; at ~ -est
formation:
(i) Wh-word+Vvol | とも | | 
 | どこへ行こうとも | No matter where someone may go | 
 | 何を食べようとも | No matter what someone may eat | 
 | 何があるうとも | No matter what may happen | 
(ii) Wh-word+Adjective い stem | {く/かろう}とも | | 
 | {いかに/どんなに}難し{く/かろう}とも | No matter how difficult something may be | 
(iii) Wh-word+Adjective な stem | であろうとも | | 
 | {いかに/どんなに}好きであろうとも | No matter how much someone likes something | 
(iv) Adjective い stem | くとも | | 
 | 早くとも | At the earliest |
explanation: A conjunction in written Japanese that is used to express a concession.

examples.japanese: よく勉強したから、試験にどんな問題が出ようとも大丈夫だ。
examples.english: Since I studied hard I feel confident no matter what problem shows up on the test.

examples.japanese: いかに家事が忙し{く/かろう}とも母は文句一つ言わなかった。
examples.english: No matter how busy she was with housekeeping, my mother never uttered a single complaint.

examples.japanese: どんなに健康であろうとも、一年に一回は健康診断を受けるべきだ。
examples.english: No matter how healthy you are, you should have a check-up once a year.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは遅くとも来年の四月には完了するだろう。
examples.english: At the latest, this project will be complete in April of next year.

examples.japanese: 父は何が起きようともいつも平然としている。
examples.english: My father is always very calm no matter what is impending.

examples.japanese: 私は世界のどこに住もうとも一向に構わない。
examples.english: I do not care at all where in the world I live.

examples.japanese: 万一失敗しようとも、簡単に諦めてはいけない。
examples.english: Even if by any chance you fail you shouldn't give up easily.

examples.japanese: いかに頭がよ{く/かろう}とも、努力しなければいい仕事は出来ない。
examples.english: No matter how bright you may be, you cannot do a good job unless you make an effort.

meaning_en: Become
formation:
Noun | となる | | 
 | 必修科目となる | Become a compulsory subject |
explanation: A phrase which expresses the idea that someone or something becomes something.

examples.japanese: 吉田さんが初代の委員長となった。
examples.english: Mr. Yoshida has become the first committee chairman.

examples.japanese: その土地は結局国の所有物となった。
examples.english: That land eventually become state property.

examples.japanese: 戦後義務教育は九年間となった。
examples.english: After the war, (the period of) compulsory education was changed to (literally: became) nine years.

examples.japanese: 彼らの結婚は悲劇的な結果となった。
examples.english: Their marriage ended in tragedy (literally: became a tragic result).

examples.japanese: 彼は証拠不十分で無罪となった。
examples.english: For lack of evidence, he was found (literally: became) innocent.

examples.japanese: その試合は雨のため中止となった。
examples.english: The game was cancelled (literally: became a cancellation) due to rain.

meaning_en: When it comes to; if it is true that ~; if it is the case that ~; if it turns out that ~
formation:
(i) Noun | となると | | 
 | 映画となると | When it comes to movies | 
(ii) Sinformal | となると | Exception: XがNounとなると | 
 | 彼が来るとなると | If it is true that he is coming | 
 | 彼女が病気となると | If it is the case that she is ill |
explanation: A phrase which expresses the idea "when it comes to" or "if it is true that".

examples.japanese: 私は機械のこととなると何も分からない。
examples.english: When it comes to mechanical things, I don't understand anything.

examples.japanese: 彼が手伝ってくれないとなると誰かほかの人を頼むしかない。
examples.english: If it's true that he is not going to help us, we'll have no alternative but to ask someone else.

examples.japanese: 勉はギャンブルとなると人が変わってしまう。
examples.english: When it comes to gambling, Tsutomu becomes another person.

examples.japanese: 日本語が出来る科学者となると数がかなり限られてくる。
examples.english: When it comes to scientists who can speak Japanese, the number is quite limited.

examples.japanese: 何でも仕事となると楽なものはない。
examples.english: Nothing is easy (literally: There is nothing easy) when it comes to work.

examples.japanese: 彼が参加できないとなるとこのプロジェクトは考え直さなければならない。
examples.english: If it turns out that he cannot participate (in this project), we'll have to reconsider it.

examples.japanese: 秘密が漏れたとなるとこの計画は変更しなければならない。
examples.english: If it is true that the secret (of this plan) has leaked, we must change it.

examples.japanese: 彼が新しい社長になるとなると経営方針がかなり変わるだろう。
examples.english: If he turns out to be the new president, the management policy will probably be considerably different.

meaning_en: (in) the same way as; (in) the way; as
formation:
(i) Noun | の通り(に) | | 
 | 計画の通り(に) | The same way as the plan | 
(ii) Vinformal | 通り(に) | | 
 | 見た通り(に) | The way someone saw something | 
(iii) Demonstrative Adjective | 通り(に) | | 
 | この通り(に) | The same way as this; this way |
explanation: 通り（に）A dependent noun which expresses the idea that someone does something or something takes place in the same way as something else.

examples.japanese: 説明書の通り（に）やったが、うまくいかなかった。
examples.english: I did it as the manual shows (literally: in the same way as the manual), but it didn't work.

examples.japanese: 私の言う通り（に）体を動かして下さい。
examples.english: Please move your body as I tell you to (literally: in the same way as I tell you).

examples.japanese: 思った通り彼が一番先に来ていた。
examples.english: As I expected (literally: thought), he was the first to come.

examples.japanese: 結果はやはり予想した通りだった。
examples.english: The result was just as I expected, after all.

examples.japanese: この地図の通り（に）行けば間違いなく行けます。
examples.english: If you go as this map shows (literally: in the same way as this map), you can get there without fail.

examples.japanese: 私はただ言われた通り（に）やっているだけです。
examples.english: I'm just doing as I'm told (literally: in the way I'm told).

examples.japanese: ここに書いてある通り（に）すれば誰にでも出来ます。
examples.english: If you follow what is (literally: do it in the way) written here, anyone can do it.

examples.japanese: 予想した通り誰も宿題をやってこなかった。
examples.english: As I expected, no one did their homework.

meaning_en: Assume that; regard ~ as; let; suppose
formation:
(i) Noun1 は Noun2 | (だ) とする | | 
 | 一ドルは百三十円(だ) とする | We assume that one dollar is 130 yen | 
(ii) Sinformal nonpast | とする | | 
 | 山田さんが来られないとする(ちょっと困る) | If we assume that Mr. Yamada cannot come, (we are at a bit of a loss) | 
 | 日本へ行くとすれば(いつ行ったらいいだろう) | Assuming that we go to Japan, (I wonder what would be the best time) | 
(iii) Sinformal past | とする | | 
 | 百万円もらったとしよう | Suppose you received ￥1,000,000 | 
 | あと百日の命だと言われたとする | Let’s suppose that you were told you only had 100 days left to live |
explanation: とする (1) A phrase indicating that someone assumes something.

examples.japanese: 温度は一定（だ）とする。
examples.english: We assume that the temperature is constant.

examples.japanese: 一日に五百マイル運転できるとすれば・すると、何日で着きますか。
examples.english: Assuming that we can drive 500 miles a day, how many days will it take to get there?

examples.japanese: 温暖化現象がこのまま続いたとしよう。
examples.english: Suppose the greenhouse effect continued on like this.

examples.japanese: 今、空気抵抗は無視出来るものとする。
examples.english: Now let's assume that we can ignore air resistance.

examples.japanese: 男性の女性に対するこのような行為は性的いやがらせであるとする。
examples.english: Let's assume such behaviour by men towards women is regarded as a sexual harassment.

examples.japanese: 西洋では日本のいわゆる私小説は小説ではないとされる。
examples.english: In the West the Japanese so-called 'I' novels are not regarded as novels.

examples.japanese: 私はアメリカを第二の故郷とすることに違和感を覚えない。
examples.english: I don't feel uneasy regarding America as my second home country.

examples.japanese: 夏の九週間集中日本語講座の単位は六単位とする。
examples.english: We let the units of the 9-week intensive Japanese course in summer count for 6 units.

examples.japanese: あの人はちょっとしたことでかっとする。
examples.english: That person flares up at the slightest provocation.

examples.japanese: あの男の人は目がギョロリとしている。
examples.english: He has goggling eyes.

meaning_en: The moment; just as; as soon as; then
formation:
(i) Vinformal past | 途端(に) | | 
 | 座った途端(に) | The moment someone sat down | 
(ii) Vinformal pastら | 途端に | | 
 | 食べたら、途端に | The moment someone ate something |
explanation: 途端（に）A noun/adverb which expresses the idea that 'something occurred the moment someone did something or something took place'.

examples.japanese: 先生の顔を見た途端（に）宿題があったことを思い出した。
examples.english: The moment I saw my teacher, I remembered that there was a homework assignment.

examples.japanese: ドアを開けたら、途端にカレーの匂いがした。
examples.english: The moment I opened the door, I smelled curry.

examples.japanese: 部屋に入った途端（に）電話が鳴った。
examples.english: Just as I entered my room, the telephone rang.

examples.japanese: その日本の写真を見た途端（に）家族に会いたくなった。
examples.english: I wanted to see my family the moment I saw that Japanese photograph.

examples.japanese: 彼女は私の顔を見た途端（に）泣き出した。
examples.english: As soon as she saw me, she started to cry.

examples.japanese: コンセントを差し込んだら、途端に家中の電気が消えた。
examples.english: The moment I put the plug in, all the lights went out in the house.

examples.japanese: その牛乳を飲んだら、途端に腹が痛み出した。
examples.english: As soon as I drank the milk, my stomach started to ache.

examples.japanese: 助かったと思った。その途端（に）、力が抜けて気を失ってしまった。
examples.english: I thought I was saved; then (literally: at that moment), my strength was gone and I lost consciousness.

meaning_en: Finally; at (long) last; eventually; in the end; after all
explanation: An adverb that is used to express the eventual arrival of an expected situation.

examples.japanese: 朝から降りそうだった雨がとうとう降り出した。
examples.english: It's been threatening to rain since the morning and finally it started to rain. (literally: The rain which threatened to fall from the morning finally started to fall.)

examples.japanese: 弟は医者の忠告を聞かないで煙草を吸い続け、とうとう肺がんになってしまった。
examples.english: My younger brother didn't take his doctor's advice and kept smoking until he finally got lung cancer.

examples.japanese: 日本語の先生が余りにも厳しかったから、その学生はとうとう日本語が嫌いになってしまった。
examples.english: Because his Japanese instructor was so strict the student eventually came to hate the Japanese language.

examples.japanese: その数学の問題は何時間かけても解けなかったので、とうとう諦めてしまった。
examples.english: I wasn't able to solve the mathematical problem after spending many hours on it, so I finally gave up.

examples.japanese: ビルは妻との関係がだんだん悪化し、とうとう別れてしまった。
examples.english: Bill's relationship with his wife gradually deteriorated and they eventually separated.

examples.japanese: この会社で働くのもとうとう今日が最後となった。
examples.english: At long last this is the last day I work at this company.

examples.japanese: 十五年も飼っていた猫がとうとう老衰で死んでしまった。
examples.english: The cat we had kept for 15 years finally died of old age.

examples.japanese: とうとう博士論文を書いてしまった。
examples.english: At long last I finished writing a Ph.D. dissertation.

meaning_en: As well as; with; along with; at the same time; when, as; while
formation:
(i) Noun | と共に | | 
 | 山田先生と共に | As well as Mr. Yamada; with Mr. Yamada | 
 | 退職と共に | At the same time as one’s retirement | 
 | 気候の変化と共に | With the climate change; as the climate changes | 
(ii) Vinformal nonpast | と共に | | 
 | 景気が回復すると共に | As business recovers | 
(iii) {Noun/Adjective な stem} | であると共に | | 
 | 医者であると共に | As well as being a doctor | 
 | 経済的であると共に | As well as being economical | 
(iv) Adjective い informal nonpast | と共に | | 
 | 興味深いと共に | As well as being interested |
explanation: A phrase which is used to express the idea that A and B share a common property or do the same thing together, that two things take place at the same time, or that someone or something possesses two properties.

examples.japanese: スタインベックはへミングウィイと共にアメリカの代表的作家の一人だ。
examples.english: Steinbeck, as well as Hemingway, is a writer representative of American writers.

examples.japanese: 私は職場の同僚達と共にそのデモに参加した。
examples.english: I took part in the demonstration with my office colleagues.

examples.japanese: 病気が回復すると共に食欲も出てきた。
examples.english: As I'm recovering from my illness, my appetite is coming back.

examples.japanese: 彼は科学者であると共に哲学者でもあった。
examples.english: He was a philosopher as well as a scientist.

examples.japanese: 原子力は石油と共に重要なエネルギー源だ。
examples.english: Atomic energy, as well as petroleum, is an important energy source.

examples.japanese: 轟音と共にジェット機が飛び去った。
examples.english: A jet flew off with a roaring sound.

examples.japanese: 武士階級は封建制と共に滅びだ。
examples.english: The samurai class died with the feudal system.

examples.japanese: 終戦と共に激しいインフレが人々を襲った。
examples.english: Severe inflation hit people when the war ended (literally: with the end of the war).

meaning_en: That is (to say); namely; in short; to sum up; in other words; after all; that means
formation:
(i) Sentence 1 (Sentence2…) | つまり Sentence Noun | | 
 | 金がない。つまり、貧乏なんです。 | I don’t have money. In other words, I’m poor | 
(ii) Noun Phrase | つまり Noun/Noun Phrase | | 
 | 母の姉の子供、つまり、私のいとこ | The child of my mother’s older sister, my cousin, that is |
explanation: An adverb that is used to summarise or rephrase what has been mentioned/stated in the preceding context.

examples.japanese: ベルリンの壁が崩れた。これはつまり、民主化の嵐が始まったということだ。
examples.english: The Berlin Wall fell apart. This means that the storm of democratization has started.

examples.japanese: 私の母の弟、つまり、叔父が最近離婚した。
examples.english: My mother's younger brother, that is to say, my uncle, has recently divorced.

examples.japanese: アメリカに一年間一人で出張するんです。つまり、単身赴任ということですよ。
examples.english: I'm going without my family to work for the company in America for one year. In other words, I'm becoming a tanshin-funin worker.

examples.japanese: 運動をした後は気分がよくなりますね。つまり、運動でストレスがなくなるということなんですよ。
examples.english: You feel good after exercise, right? That means, stress is eliminated by exercise.

examples.japanese: A：部長、このプロジェクトは出来ますか。B: そうだね。いいプロジェクトだと思うけど、予算がどうもねえ。A：つまり、出来ないということですね。
examples.english: A: Chief, can we do this project? B: Well, I think it's a fine project, but you know how the budget is. A: In short, we cannot do it, right?

examples.japanese: 日本の父親は子供がまだ寝ている時に家を出て、子供達が寝てから家に帰って来る。つまり、父親不在ということだ。
examples.english: Japanese fathers leave home while their children are still asleep and come home after they have gone to sleep. This is, in short, an absence of fathers.

examples.japanese: A：彼女、僕が会いに行っても、あまり話してくれないんですよ。B: それは、つまり、君のことが嫌いなんだよ。
examples.english: A: I go to see her, but she doesn't talk much to me, you know. B: That means, she doesn't like you.

examples.japanese: 産業化のために自然が破壊されること、つまり、環境破壊は人類の問題だ。
examples.english: The destruction of nature by industrialization, that is to say, environmental destruction, is a problem of mankind.

meaning_en: Upon ~; after ~
formation:
(i) Vinformal past | 上で | | 
 | 読んだ上で | Upon reading | 
 | 研究した上で | Upon conducting research | 
(ii) Noun | の上で | | 
 | 調査の上で | After investigating | 
 | 討議の上で | After discussion |
explanation: （の）上で A compound particle that is used to express a preparatory action for a relatively important action.

examples.japanese: よく考えた上で御返事いたします。
examples.english: I will reply upon careful consideration.

examples.japanese: 話し合いの上で結論を出したいと思います。
examples.english: I would like to draw a conclusion after discussion.

examples.japanese: よく問題を話し合った上で決めたらどうでしょうか。
examples.english: Why don't we decide after discussing the matter?

examples.japanese: 実験をした上で、理論の正しさを証明しなければならない。
examples.english: We have to prove the correctness of the theory after conducting an experiment.

examples.japanese: 日本文学のスミス先生と相談した上で、修士論文の題目を決めました。
examples.english: I decided the topic of my M.A. thesis after consulting with Japanese literature Professor Smith.

examples.japanese: 彼女とはお見合いをして、一年間交際した上で、結婚に踏み切りました。
examples.english: I decided to get married after meeting her through an arranged match and dating her for one year.

examples.japanese: 日本の生活は高くつくと知った上で、日本へ留学した。
examples.english: I went to Japan to study, knowing that life is expensive there.

examples.japanese: 十冊ぐらい本を読んだ上で、学期末のレポートを書き上げた。
examples.english: I finished writing my term paper after having read about 10 books.

meaning_en: Can; possible; -able
formation:
Vます | うる/える | | 
 | 起こり{うる/える} | Can happen | 
 | あり{うる/える} | Can exist |
explanation: 得る　（うる・える）An auxiliary verb that expresses possibility.

examples.japanese: 二十一世紀に日本語は国際語になり得ると思う。
examples.english: I think it's possible for the Japanese language to become an international language in the 21st century.

examples.japanese: 株の変動はいつでも起こり得る。
examples.english: The fluctuation of stocks can happen any time.

examples.japanese: ほとんどの癌は予防し得る。
examples.english: The majority of cancers are preventable.

examples.japanese: 一度に記憶し得る単語の数は限られている。
examples.english: The number of vocabulary items one can memorize at one time is limited.

examples.japanese: 運動をすることによって健康を維持し得る。
examples.english: By doing exercise one can maintain one's health.

examples.japanese: 日本語の基礎はだいたい二年間で学び得る。
examples.english: One can learn the basics of Japanese in roughly two years.

examples.japanese: 日本の経済が不況になることだって十分にあり得る。
examples.english: It is quite possible that the Japanese economy will go into a slump.

meaning_en: Not to speak of; let alone; not to mention; to say nothing of
formation:
Noun | は言うまでもなく | | 
 | スポーツは言うまでもなく | Not to speak of sports |
explanation: An adverbial phrase that conveys the meaning of 'not to speak of something/someone'.

examples.japanese: 大統領の職務は頭脳は言うまでもなく、体力も要求される。
examples.english: The duty of the presidency requires physical strength, not to mention brains.

examples.japanese: 日本は土地は言うまでもなく、家も非常に高い。
examples.english: In Japan houses are very expensive, not to mention land.

examples.japanese: この大学は教育内容は言うまでもなく、設備も抜群に優れている。
examples.english: This university excels in facilities, to say nothing of educational programs.

examples.japanese: 彼は平日は言うまでもなく、週末や祭日も仕事をしている。
examples.english: He is working even on weekends and holidays, not to speak of weekdays.

examples.japanese: ジュリアンは菜食主義者なので、牛肉は言うまでもなく、魚も鶏肉も食べない。
examples.english: Julian is a vegetarian, so he doesn't eat fish or chicken, let alone beef.

examples.japanese: あの学生は漢字は言うまでもなく、平仮名、片仮名さえ知らない。
examples.english: That student doesn't know even hiragana and katakana, let alone kanji.

meaning_en: Send; give; do; play; operate; eat; drink
formation:
(i) someone が someone を place | にやる | | 
 | 私が息子を外国にやる。 | I will send my son to a foreign country | 
(ii) someone が someone に something | をやる | | 
 | 僕が妹に人形をやる。 | I will give my younger sister a doll | 
(iii) someone が something | をやる | | 
 | 友達が弁護士をやる。 | My friend is (literally doing) a lawyer |
explanation: やる (2) An auxiliary verb which expresses the idea that someone does something undesirable to someone else when he/she knows his/her action will cause hardship or trouble.

examples.japanese: 貧乏な家庭は子共を大学にやれない。
examples.english: Poor families cannot send their children to college.

examples.japanese: 僕は弟に自転車をやるつもりだ。
examples.english: I intend to give a bike to my younger brother.

examples.japanese: 午後、テニスをやりませんか。
examples.english: Won't you play tennis this afternoon?

examples.japanese: 今アメリカで日本語の教師をやっています。
examples.english: I'm now (literally: doing) a Japanese instructor in the U.S.

examples.japanese: 三船敏郎のやる役は正義感の強い男だ。
examples.english: The role played by Toshiro Mifune is a male with a strong sense of justice.

examples.japanese: 先月まで煙草をやっていました。
examples.english: I was smoking up until last month.

examples.japanese: 息子を郵便局にやって、切手を買って来させた。
examples.english: I sent my son to the post office and had him buy stamps.

examples.japanese: 猫にこのえさをやってね。
examples.english: Give this food to the cat, OK?

examples.japanese: 私は正をからかってやった。
examples.english: I teased Tadashi.

examples.japanese: ルームメートが部屋を全然掃除しないので、文句を言ってやった。
examples.english: Because my roommate never cleans our room, I complained (to her about it).

meaning_en: Finally; at last; barely
formation:
(i) やっと | Vinformal | | 
 | やっと {会える/会えた} | I am/was finally able to meet him | 
(ii) やっと | Vinformal | | 
 | やっと {乗れる/乗れた} | Can/could barely ride | 
(iii) Vinformal nonpast | のがやっと {だ/だった} | | 
 | そう言うのがやっと {だ/だった} | Somone can/could barely say so | 
(iv) | やっとのことでV | | 
 | やっとのことで {着く/着いた} | At long last, someone gets/got there |
explanation: An adverb to indicate that something desirable has been finally achieved or will be eventually achieved though with great difficulty.

examples.japanese: 日本史の期末レポートやっと書き終えた。
examples.english: I finally finished writing my Japanese history term paper.

examples.japanese: この道は車がやっと一台通れるくらいの狭さです。
examples.english: This street is so narrow that one car can barely go through.

examples.japanese: 私の日本語の力では挨拶をするのがやっとです。
examples.english: My Japanese language ability is barely enough to make greetings.

examples.japanese: やっとのことで、家が買えた。
examples.english: At long last, I could buy a house.

examples.japanese: 半年の長い冬が終わって、やっと暖かい春になった。
examples.english: The long winter that lasted for half a year has ended and finally the warm spring is here.

examples.japanese: 日本で一年間日本語を勉強したら、やっと、日本語が通じるようになった。
examples.english: After I studied Japanese for a year in Japan, I finally reached the point where I could make myself understood in Japanese.

examples.japanese: あの二人はずいぶん長い間付き合っていたが、やっと結婚したようだね。
examples.english: The couple have been together for a very long time, but it seems that they finally got married.

examples.japanese: 長い間の夢だった海外旅行にやっと行けそうだ。
examples.english: It seems that finally I can travel abroad which was a dream I cherished for a long time.

meaning_en: I tell you; I'm telling you; you know
formation:
{V/Adjective い} informal | ぞ | | 
 | 食べるぞ。 | Hey, someone is going to eat it | 
 | 食べたぞ。 | Hey, someone ate it | 
 | まずいぞ。 | Yuck! | 
 | まずかったぞ。 | It was yucky | 
{Adjective な/Noun} | {だ/だった} ぞ | | 
 | 元気だぞ。 | Someone is healthy | 
 | 元気だったぞ。 | Someone was healthy |
explanation: A sentence final particle that emphasises a male speaker's emotion about something in his monologue or his strong desire to draw someone else's attention.

examples.japanese: あれ、財布がどこかへ行ってしまったぞ。
examples.english: Hey, my purse has gone somewhere!

examples.japanese: 急がないとバスに乗り遅れるぞ。
examples.english: If you don't hurry, you'll be late for the bus, you know.

examples.japanese: 今日はあの子とデートが出来るぞ。
examples.english: Wow! I can date that girl today.

examples.japanese: 変だぞ。女房の顔が猫の顔に見える。
examples.english: Strange indeed! My wife's face looks like a cat's face.

examples.japanese: 今度こそ文部省の奨学金をもらってやるぞ。
examples.english: By God, this time I will get the Education Ministry's Scholarship.

examples.japanese: 今日の日本語の試験はうまくいったぞ。
examples.english: Thank God, today's Japanese exam went well!

examples.japanese: 今日は寒いから、オーバーを着て行った方がいいぞ。
examples.english: It's cold today, so you'd better go out with an overcoat on.

examples.japanese: このケーキ、食べないなら、俺が食べちゃうぞ。
examples.english: If you don't eat this cake, I will.

meaning_en: Daringly; boldly; dare to ~; venture to ~; force oneself to ~
formation:
あえて | Verb | | 
 | あえて反対する | Someone dares to disagree |
explanation: An adverb that expresses the speaker's/writer's desire or will to dare to do something in spite of difficulty, danger or opposition.

examples.japanese: 部長はあえて社長に反対意見を述べた。
examples.english: The department head boldly expressed his opposing view directly to the company president.

examples.japanese: 私はあえて大がかりな研究計画を立てたいと思う。
examples.english: I would like to take on a large-scale research proposal.

examples.japanese: あえて先生の理論に異議を唱えてみようと思う。
examples.english: I think I will try to oppose my professor's theory.

examples.japanese: あえて言えばあなたの考えは机上の空論だ。
examples.english: If I dare to say so, your idea is an unrealistic, ivory tower theory.

examples.japanese: 君の言うことにあえて反対はしないよ。
examples.english: I don't dare oppose what you're saying.

examples.japanese: アメリカでは黙っていると損をするので、私は日本人としてあえて自己主張をすることにしている。
examples.english: In the U.S., if I keep silent I lose out, so as a Japanese, I'm making a point of asserting myself.

examples.japanese: 委員会の賛同を得るのは難しいとは知りつつも、あえて新機軸の計画を提案した。
examples.english: Although I knew that it was hard to get approval from the committee, I dared to propose a brand new plan.

examples.japanese: 彼の両親があえて住居を変えたのは彼の教育を考えた上であった。
examples.english: It was after his parents thought about his education that they made the bold move to change their residence.

meaning_en: in the end; finally; eventually; after
formation:
(i) Vinformal past | あげく(に) | | 
 | 話したあげく(に) | After someone talked | 
(ii) Vinformal past | あげくのNoun | | 
 | 考えたあげくの決断 | A decision made after deliberation |
explanation: あげく（に）An adverb/conjunction indicating that one spends an extended period of time before reaching a result.

examples.japanese: さんざん考えたあげく（に）大学院へ進学することにした。
examples.english: After thinking for a long time, I decided to go on to graduate school.

examples.japanese: 彼女の離婚は数年悩んだあげくの決断だった。
examples.english: Her divorce was a decision she made after agonizing for several years.

examples.japanese: 私はさんざん悩んだあげくに最初に勤めていた会社を辞めた。
examples.english: I quit the company where I first worked after thinking very hard (about what to do).

examples.japanese: 彼はアジア、ヨーロッパ、北米などいろいろな国の女性とつき合ったあげくに、結局は生涯独身で過ごした
examples.english: He dated women from various countries in Asia, Europe and North America, but in the end he spent his entire life single.

examples.japanese: 妻はあの靴がいい、この靴がいいと、いろいろと履いてみたあげくに、どれも買わずに店を出た。
examples.english: Saying "I like this one" or "I like that one," my wife tried on all sorts of shoes, but after all that, she left the store without buying any of them.

examples.japanese: 山田は私の車を一か月も使ったあげく、返す時お礼の一言も言わなかった。
examples.english: After using my car for a whole month, Yamada didn't even say a word of thanks when he returned it.

examples.japanese: さんざん迷ったあげく、一年休職してアメリカに留学することにした。
examples.english: After weighing my options for a long time, I finally decided to take a one-year leave from my company to study abroad in the U.S.

examples.japanese: 彼女は既婚の男性との恋に溺れたあげくに、自分の人生を台無しにしてしまった。
examples.english: After falling in love with a married man, her own life was in ruins.

meaning_en: to the end; persistently; insist; strictly; just; under any circumstance; absolutely; never; completely; ultimately
explanation: An adverb that represents the idea of "to the utmost degree".

examples.japanese: 江本氏はあくまでも自説を変えなかった。
examples.english: Mr. Emoto persistently maintained (literally: didn't change) his opinion.

examples.japanese: これはあくまでも小説であって実話ではない。
examples.english: literally: This is strictly fiction and not a true story.

examples.japanese: 彼女はあくまでも自分に正直だった。
examples.english: She was true to herself to the end.

examples.japanese: 私はあくまでも彼の無実を信じる。
examples.english: I will believe in his innocence to the end.

examples.japanese: 彼はあくまでも日本の参戦に反対を唱え続けた。
examples.english: He kept opposing Japan's entry into the war up to the end.

examples.japanese: あくまで一人でやると言うのならあえて手助けはしない。
examples.english: If you insist on doing it by yourself, I won't venture to assist you.

examples.japanese: 反乱軍はあくまでも抵抗を続けた。
examples.english: The insurgent troops continued their resistance to the end.

examples.japanese: 君がそういう風にあくまでも話し合いを拒否するのならこちらにも考えがある。
examples.english: If you persistently refuse to have a discussion (with me) like that, I'll make another plan.

meaning_en: (not) necessarily; (not) always
formation:
あながち～ない | | 
あながち間違いではない | ~ isn’t necessarily wrong |
explanation: あながち～ない A structure that indicates that something is not necessarily the way the speaker/writer thought.

examples.japanese: 彼の推理もあながち間違っていないのかもしれない。
examples.english: His guess may not necessarily be wrong.

examples.japanese: バーチャル指揮者ソフトが売れているところを見ると、一度は指揮者になってみたいというのは、あながち僕だけの願望ではないらしい。
examples.english: Judging by how well virtual conducting software has been selling, apparently I'm not necessarily the only one who'd like to try orchestra conducting at least once in my life.

examples.japanese: 最後の一章はやや蛇足とも思えるが、そのエピソードは読んでいて気分がいい。ということはあながち蛇足とは言えないということか。
examples.english: I felt like the last chapter wasn't quite necessary, but it feels good to read it. So, I guess it's not so superﬂuous after all.

examples.japanese: 皮膚のpHが体調によっても変わるとすれば、「気分次第で色が変わる口紅」というのもあながち嘘ではない。
examples.english: If it's true that the pH of your skin changes depending on your health, then "the lipstick that changes its colour depending on your mood" isn't necessarily a lie.

examples.japanese: 完全に男女平等な社会が来るのは困るというのも、あながち偽った気持ちではない。
examples.english: It wouldn't be a total lie for me to say I would have difﬁculty with a society in which men and women are completely equal.

examples.japanese: この俳優の演技はうまいが、時々違和感を覚えるのは、あながち演出のせいとばかりは言えない。
examples.english: This actor is talented, but sometimes his performances come off a little strange, and I don't think it's necessarily always the fault of the producer.

examples.japanese: 生死の境をさまよっていた人が手術中の会話を鮮明に覚えていたりすることから、幽体離脱現象もあながち否定できない。
examples.english: Since some people who've come close to dying say that they can clearly recall what was being said around them while they were on the operating table, we can't simply deny the occurrence of out-of-body experiences.

meaning_en: or; either ~ or; perhaps
formation:
(i) Noun1 (か)、 | <あるいはNoun2 | | 
 | 父(か)、あるいは母 | Either my father or my mother | 
(ii) Vinformalか、 | あるいはV2 informalか | | 
 | 本を読むか、あるいはテニスをするか | Either reading books or playing tennis | 
(iii) {Adjective い informal/Adjectiveな stem}か、 | あるいは{Adjective い informal/Adjective な stem}か | | 
 | 面白いか、あるいはつまらないか | Interesting or boring | 
 | 民主的か、あるいは独裁的か | Democratic or dictorial | 
(iv) あるいは | {Verb/Adjective い} informal(の)かもしれない | | 
 | あるいは{行く/行った}(の)かもしれない | Someone perhaps will go/went there | 
 | あるいは{面白い/面白かった}(の)かもしれない | Something is/was perhaps interesting | 
(v) あるいは{Adjectiveな stem/Noun} | {Ø/だった(の)}かもしれ | | 
 | あるいは{元気/元気だった(の)}かもしれない | Someone is/was perhaps healthy | 
 | あるいは{先生/先生だった(の)}かもしれない | Someone is/was perhaps a teacher |
explanation: A conjunction that marks alternatives

examples.japanese: ボールペン(か)あるいは万年筆でお書き下さい。
examples.english: Please write either with a ballpoint pen or a fountain pen.

examples.japanese: 日本のような少子化社会では、大学の数を少なくするか、あるいは外国人の学生を増やすかしなければなるまい。
examples.english: In a society like Japan where the number of children is decreasing, we may have to either reduce the number of colleges or increase the number of foreign students.

examples.japanese: 性格が明るいか、あるいは暗いかによって、人生は非常に変わってくる。
examples.english: Depending on whether someone's personality is cheerful or gloomy, his or her life will change dramatically.

examples.japanese: すべての宗教は、あるいはアニミズムから来ている（の）かもしれない。
examples.english: Perhaps all religions originate from animism.

examples.japanese: 社長は朝ご飯にはトーストかあるいはオートミールを召し上がる。
examples.english: For breakfast, the company president has either toast or oatmeal.

examples.japanese: 政治学あるいは経済学を専攻した学生を採用します。
examples.english: We will hire a student who has majored in either political science or economics.

examples.japanese: ご注文は電話か、あるいはインターネットでお願いします。
examples.english: Please place your order either by phone or by Internet.

examples.japanese: この会社は大規模なリストラをするか、あるいは、倒産するかしかない。
examples.english: The only choice left for this company is to execute a large-scale restructuring or else go bankrupt.

meaning_en: (just) as if ~ were; (just) as if ~ did ~; just like; just; exactly
formation:
(i) あたかもNoun | の{ように/ようなNoun} | | 
 | あたかも上司の{ように/ような言い方} | As if someone were a supervisor; a way of talking as if someone were a supervisor | 
(ii) あたかも{V/Adjectiveい}informal | (かの){ように/ようなNoun} | | 
 | あたかもよく知って{いる/ いた}(かの){ように/ような言い方} | As if someone knew/had known something well; a way of talking if someone knew/had known something well | 
 | あたかも{安い/安かった}(かの){ように/ような言い方} | As if something were/had been cheap; a way of talking as if someone were/had been cheap | 
(iii) あたかも{Noun/Adjectiveな stem} | {である/であった}(かの){ように/ようなNoun} | | 
 | あたかも専門家{である/であった}(かの){ように/ような言い方} | If someone were/had been a specialist; a way of talking as if someone were/had been a specialist | 
 | あたかも上手{である/であった}(かの){ように/ような言い方} | If someone were/had been good at something; a way of talking as if someone were/had been good at something |
explanation: An adverb used to present a counter-factual statement emphatically

examples.japanese: 彼はあたかも責任者のように振る舞っている。
examples.english: He behaves as if he were the person in charge.

examples.japanese: リニアモーターカーはあたかも氷の上をすべる（かの）ように走る。
examples.english: The linear motor car runs as if it were gliding on ice.

examples.japanese: この装置を使って、あたかも現場にいる(かの)ような感覚で現場にいるロボットを操縦できる。
examples.english: Using this device you can operate a robot at the site as if you were actually there.

examples.japanese: この磁石はあたかも永久磁石のように動作する。
examples.english: This magnet acts as if it were a permanent magnet.

examples.japanese: リモートコントロールソフトは遠くのPCのデスクトップ画面をそのまま手元のPCに映し出し、あたかも自分のデスクトップのように操作することができる。
examples.english: A remote control software program displays the desktop of a remote personal computer on the computer in front of you and enables you to operate it as if it were your own computer's desktop.

examples.japanese: 彼女はあたかも自分のうちにいるように振る舞っている。
examples.english: She behaves as if she were in her own house.

examples.japanese: 上手な説明文は、あたかも目の前にその光景が広がっているように鮮明にイメージできるものです。
examples.english: With well-written explanatory sentences, the reader can get vivid images, as if the scenes were spread out in front of his eyes.

examples.japanese: 彼はあたかも自分が上司であるかのように私に仕事を言いつける。
examples.english: He gives me assignments as if he were my boss.

meaning_en: it is precisely because ~ that ~; only because ~; to the extent that ~
formation:
(i) {v/Adjective い} Conditional | ばこそ | | 
 | 読めばこそ | It is only because someone reads something | 
 | 面白ければこそ | It is only because something is interesting | 
(ii) {Adjective な stem/Noun} | であればこそ | | 
 | 元気であればこそ | It is only because someone is healthy | 
 | 先生であればこそ | It is only because someone is a teacher |
explanation: A conjunction that emphasizes a reason

examples.japanese: 環境保護を支持していればこそ植林に力を入れているのだ。
examples.english: It is only because I support environmental protection so much that I put my efforts into planting trees.

examples.japanese: 「愛」があればこそ生きる喜びがある。
examples.english: Only because there is love is there joy for living.

examples.japanese: 膨大な電力の需要があればこそ原子力発電を開発せざるを得ないのだ。
examples.english: It is precisely because of the enormous demand for electricity that we cannot help but develop atomic power plants.

examples.japanese: 中近東の和平を熱望すればこそ、国連の役割を強化しなければならないと思う。
examples.english: It is only because I hope for peace in the Middle East as much as I do that I think we have to strengthen the role of the UN.

examples.japanese: 親友であればこそ君にこんなにずけずけとものが言えるんだよ。
examples.english: It is precisely because I'm your close friend that I can talk straight to you like this.

examples.japanese: ビジョンを持った社長であればこそ社員は張り切って仕事をしているのだ。
examples.english: It is precisely because he is a president with vision that his employees are working with high spirits.

examples.japanese: 人は一人でいるのが寂しければこそペットを飼うのだ。
examples.english: To the extent a person feels lonely when he/she is alone, he/she will keep a pet.

examples.japanese: 言論が自由であればこそ民主主義は育っていくのである。
examples.english: To the extent that there is freedom of speech, democracy will keep growing.

examples.english: It is only because I hope for peace in the Middle East as much as I do that I think we have to strengthen the role of the UN.

examples.english: It is precisely because I'm your close friend that I can talk straight to you like this.

examples.japanese: ビジョンを持った社長であればこそ社員は張り切って仕事をしているのだ。
examples.english: It is precisely because he is a president with vision that his employees are working with high spirits.

examples.japanese: 人は一人でいるのが寂しければこそペットを飼うのだ。
examples.english: To the extent a person feels lonely when he/she is alone, he/she will keep a pet.

examples.japanese: 言論が自由であればこそ民主主義は育っていくのである。
examples.english: To the extent that there is freedom of speech, democracy will keep growing.

meaning_en: Shouldn’t; must not; ought not to ~; cannot; don’t ~
formation:
(i) Vinformal nonpast | べからず | Exception: する→{す/する}べからず | 
 | 読むべからず | You shouldn’t read it | 
 | 食べるべからず | Don’t eat (it) | 
 | 盗作をす(る) べからず | You shouldn’t plagiarize | 
(ii) Vinformal nonpast | べからざるNoun | Exception: する→すべからざる | 
 | あるべからざる状態 | A situation that shouldn’t exist | 
 | 必要欠くべからざるもの | An indispensable thing (literally: a thing that is necessary and that one cannot lack) | 
 | 否定べからざる事実 | An undeniable fact |
explanation: べからず・べからざる An auxiliary verb that indicates a strong prohibition.

examples.japanese: 芝生に入るべからず。
examples.english: Keep off the lawn. (literally: Don't enter the lawn.)

examples.japanese: 原子力はエネルギー源として欠くべからざるものとなっている。
examples.english: Atomic energy has become indispensable as a source of energy.

examples.japanese: 電車の中で携帯電話を使うべからず。
examples.english: You ought not to use your cell phone in the train.

examples.japanese: ここで犬に糞をさせるべからず。
examples.english: Don't let your dog go (to the bathroom) here.

examples.japanese: 授業中に隣の者と私語をするべからず。
examples.english: You shouldn't talk in class with your neighbours.

examples.japanese: 無用の者、入るべからず。
examples.english: No trespassing. (literally: Don't enter if you aren't on business.)

examples.japanese: 虚言を吐くべからず。
examples.english: Don't tell a lie.

examples.japanese: インターネットを使う時の「べからず集」からいくつか引用してみよう。プライバシーを公開するべからず。怪しげなファイルに触れるべからず。インターネットの向こうに人間がいることを忘れるべからず。
examples.english: Let me quote some of the Internet don'ts from this collection: Don't make private matters public. Don't touch suspicious-looking files. Don't forget that there are people on the other end of the Internet.

meaning_en: Incidentally; in this connection
formation: Sentence1。 (Sentence2。…。) | ちなみにSentence(n)。 |
explanation: A conjunction to indicate that what follows is additional information related to the previously stated main theme

examples.japanese: 彼の小説はポストモダン的で大変気に入ってる。解釈が読み手にゆだねられているところがよい。ちなみに、去年の作品はベストセラー第一位だった。
examples.english: I love his postmodern novels. I like the way he leaves the interpretation to the reader. Incidentally, his work published last year topped the bestseller list.

examples.japanese: 先週から上野の美術館で印象派の絵画展が開かれており、ルノアール、モネ、マネなどの代表作が出品されている。ちなみに、入場料は大人三千五百円、子供千円である。
examples.english: An exhibit of Impressionists' paintings opened last week at an art museum in Ueno and representative works of Renoir, Monet and Manet, among others, are displayed there. Incidentally, the admission fee is 3,500 yen for adults and 1,000 yen for children.

examples.japanese: 先月の26日と２７日に東京で国際建築学会が開かれた。建築の人間化というのがテーマだった。ちなみに参加者数は約千五百人だった。
examples.english: On the 26th and 27th of last month, there was an international conference on architecture in Tokyo. The theme of the conference was "The humanization of architecture." Incidentally, about 1,500 people attended.

examples.japanese: アメリカの大学教授は7年に一度、研究休暇をとることができる。その期間中に研究を集中的にやるわけである。ちなみにその間の給料は、休暇が一年間なら半額、半年ならば全額が支給される。
examples.english: A professor in the U.S. can take a sabbatical every seventh year. During that period the professor concentrates on research. Incidentally, professors are paid half their salary for a year's sabbatical or their full salary for half a year.

meaning_en: And as one would expect; so (naturally); for good reason
formation:
(i) Vinformal | だけあって | | 
 | {教えている/教えていた}だけあって | Someone is/was teaching something, and as one would expect | 
(ii) Adjective い informal | だけあって | | 
 | {若い/若かった}だけあって | Someone is/was young, and as one would expect | 
(iii) Adjective な stem {な/だった} | だけあって | | 
 | 上手{な/だった}だけあって | Someone is/was good at something, and as one would expect | 
(iv) Noun {Ø/だった} | だけあって | | 
 | 先生{Ø/だった}だけあって | Someone is/was a teacher, and as one would expect |
explanation: A phrase that means "and as one would expect" or "for good reason".

examples.japanese: 彼女は人気女優だけあってすごいうちに住んでいる。
examples.english: She is a popular actress and, as one would expect, she lives in a splendid house.

examples.japanese: 聡子は小さい時からバレエをしているだけあって体が柔らかい。
examples.english: Satoko has practiced ballet since she was a child, so naturally she is limber.

examples.japanese: 彼が自慢するだけあって、彼のオフィスからの眺めはちょっとほかでは見られないものだった。
examples.english: He is proud of his ofﬁce for good reason: the view is something you could never see from other ofﬁces.

examples.japanese: 日本は火山国だけあって年中地震が絶えない。
examples.english: Japan is a volcanic country, and, as one would expect, earthquakes occur constantly throughout the year.

examples.japanese: この壷はさすが名工の作品だけあって色や形に気品がある。
examples.english: This pot was made by a master craftsman, so naturally its colours and shape are graceful.

examples.japanese: オーストラリア南端の地だけあって八月のメルボルンは実に寒い。
examples.english: Melbourne, as one would expect from its location in the southern comer of Australia, is really cold in August.

examples.japanese: さすが日本一の花火大会と言われるだけあって、規模も芸術性も素晴らしいものだった。
examples.english: (i) As one would expect from what people call the best fireworks in Japan, the scale and artistry were both amazing. (ii) People call it the best ﬁreworks show in Japan for good reason: Its scale and artistic quality were both excellent.

examples.japanese: あのレストランは笠原さんのお薦めだけあって美味しかったです。
examples.english: (i) Ms. Kasahara recommended that restaurant, and, as one would expect, the food was delicious. (ii) Ms. Kasahara recommended that restaurant for good reason: The food was delicious. [Ms. Kasahara is known as a gourmet.]

meaning_en: Don’t do something for nothing; ~ explains it; no wonder; it’s no surprise
formation:
(i) {V/Adjective い}informal | だけのことはある | | 
 | {読む/読んだ}だけのことはある | Someone doesn’t/didn’t read something for nothing | 
 | {高い/高かった}だけのことはある | Something isn’t/wasn’t expensive for nothing | 
(ii) Adjective な {な/だった} | だけのことはある | | 
 | 好き{な/だった}だけのことはある | It’s no surprise someone likes/liked it | 
(iii) Noun {Ø/だった} | だけのことはある | | 
 | プロゴルファー{Ø/だった}だけのことはある | It’s no surprised someone is/was a professional golfer |
explanation: A phrase expressing an evaluative comment regarding how something is contributing to an expected, remarkable result.

examples.japanese: 明子は韓国語がとても上手だ。さすがに二年間ソウル大学に留学していただけのことはある。
examples.english: Akiko is very good at Korean. She didn't study at Seoul National University for two years for nothing.

examples.japanese: 毎日一キロ以上水泳をしてきただけのことはあって、彼は九十歳の今もかくしゃくとしている。
examples.english: He has been swimming more than 1 kilometre every day. No wonder he is still in such good shape at 90 (years old).

examples.japanese: 山田先生は日本語の教え方が上手だ。アメリカの大学で二十年近く日本語を教えていらしただけのことはある。
examples.english: Professor Yamada is good at teaching Japanese. She didn't teach it at a U.S. university for nearly 20 years for nothing.

examples.japanese: チャンさんは世界の経済状況をよくつかんでいる。経済コンサルタントとして世界を飛び回っているだけのことはある。
examples.english: Ms. Chang has a ﬁrm grip on the world economic situation. She doesn't ﬂy around the world as a ﬁnance consultant for nothing.

examples.japanese: 隣の家の子供達は実に行儀がいい。親のしつけが厳しいだけのことはある。
examples.english: The kids next door have very good manners. Strict parental discipline explains it.

examples.japanese: 田中はさして才能もないのに昇進が早い。上司への気配りが巧みなだけのことはある。
examples.english: Tanaka's rise has been quick, although he isn't that talented. His careful attention to his boss explains it.

examples.japanese: アインシュタインの理論は二十一世紀の現在でも死んでいない。さすがに二十世紀最大の物理学者と言われるだけのことはある。
examples.english: Einstein's theory is still alive, even in the 21st century. No wonder he is called the greatest physicist of the 20th century.

examples.japanese: 幸い日本で日本語を勉強して、かなり話せるようになりました。日本に行っただけのことはありました。
examples.english: Fortunately, I studied Japanese in Japan and now I can speak it fairly well. I didn't go to Japan for nothing.

meaning_en: And (~ and); or (~ or); and things like that
formation:
(i) Noun1 | だのNoun2だの(Noun3だの) | | 
 | そばだの、うどんだの、寿司だの | Soba and undon and sushi, and things like that | 
(ii) {V/Adjectiveい}1 informal | だの{V/Adjectiveい}2 informalだの | | 
 | 疲れるだのお腹が空くだのと | Saying that someone gets tired or hungry, and things like that | 
 | 疲れただのお腹が空いただのと | Saying that someone got tired or hungry, and things like that | 
 | 暑いだの、雨が多いだのと | Saying that it is hot or it rains too much, and things like that | 
 | 暑かっただの、雨が多かっただのと | Saying that it was hot or it rained too much, and things like that | 
(iii) {Adjective な stem/Noun}{∅/だった} | だの{Adjective な stem/Noun}{∅/だった}だのと | | 
 | 不健康{∅/だった}だの、非衛生的{∅/だった}だのと | Saying that something is/was unhealthy and unhygienic, and so on | 
 | バカ者{∅/だった}だの、腑抜け{∅/だった}だのと | Saying that someone is/was a fool or and idiot, among other things |
explanation: A conjunction that lists nouns/quotes inexhaustively.

examples.japanese: 庭にはすみれだのチューリップだのつつじだの、花がたくさん咲いていた。
examples.english: In the garden, many ﬂowers such as pansies, tulips, azaleas and others, were in bloom.

examples.japanese: 学生たちは食堂のご飯がまずいだの、授業がつまらないだのと、いつも不平を言っている。
examples.english: The students are always complaining that the food at the cafeteria isn't good, or their classes are boring and so on.

examples.japanese: 僕はそばだの、うどんだの、ラーメンだのといった麺類が大好きだ。
examples.english: I like noodles such as soba, udon and ramen.

examples.japanese: 今の高校生は携帯電話だのコンピュータゲームだのにはまっている。
examples.english: High school students now are addicted to things like cell phones and computer games.

examples.japanese: 彼は僕が飲みに行こうかと誘っても、いつも頭が痛いだの、約束があるだのと言い訳をする。
examples.english: Whenever I invite him to go out for a drink, he has an excuse: he's got a headache or another appointment or something.

examples.japanese: 彼女は仕事が好きだから結婚しても仕事を続けるだの、家庭生活と職業を両立できるだのと主張していた。
examples.english: She used to claim that she would keep working after she got married because she liked her work and could manage both family life and her career.

examples.japanese: 彼女は自分がテニスが上手だの、ピアノがうまいだのと自慢ばかりしている。
examples.english: She's always boasting that she's good at tennis and (also good at) piano, and things like that.

examples.japanese: 受験生たちは塾だのテストだのと忙しい毎日を送っている。
examples.english: Students preparing for the examination are spending busy days stuffed with cram school and tests.

meaning_en: Because
formation:
(i) だって{V/Adjective い} | Informal んだ({もの/もん}) | | 
だって{V/Adjective い} | Informal {もの/もん} | | 
 | だって{食べる/食べた}んだ({もの/もん}) | Because someone eats/ate something | 
 | だって{食べる/食べた}{もの/もん} | Because someone eats/ate something | 
 | だって{面白い/面白かった}んだ({もの/もん}) | Because something is/was interesting | 
 | だって{面白い/面白かった}{もの/もん} | Because something is/was interesting | 
(ii) だって{Noun/Adjective な stem} | {な/だった}んだ({もの/もん}) | | 
だって{Noun/Adjective な stem} | {な/だった}{もの/もん} | | 
 | だって学生{な/だった}んだ({もの/もん}) | Because someone is/was a student | 
 | だって学生{な/だった}{もの/もん} | Because someone is/was a student | 
 | だって変{な/だった}んだ({もの/もん}) | Because something/someone is/was strange | 
 | だって変{な/だった}{もの/もん} | Because something/someone is/was strange |
explanation: だって (1) A conjunction that indicates a reason.

examples.japanese: A:どうして会ってくれないの？B:だって、僕、今日忙しいんだ。
examples.english: A: Why won't you see me? B: 'Cause I'm busy today.

examples.japanese: A:母：さや、どうしてもっとご飯食べないの。B:さや：だっておなか、空いていないもん。
examples.english: Mother: Saya, how come you aren't eating more? Saya: 'Cause I'm not hungry.

examples.japanese: A:妻：健太さん、今日はどうしてゴルフに行かないの。B:夫：だって、今日は客と銀座で昼食をとらなきゃならないんだ。
examples.english: Wife: Kenta, how come you're not going golﬁng today? Husband: 'Cause I have to have lunch with a client in Ginza.

examples.japanese: A:路子、笑い事じゃないよ。B:だって二人の話しているのを聞いていると面白いんだもん。
examples.english: A: Michiko, it's no laughing matter! B: But it's so funny just listening to you guys talk.

examples.japanese: もう３５度じゃ驚かないね。だって連日気温は３５度、３６度、３７度が当たり前の状態なんだもの。
examples.english: 35°(C) isn't anything surprising, because the temperature is normally 35°(C), 36°(C), 37°(C) every day.

examples.japanese: A:なんで、僕だけ烏龍茶なんですか？ B:だって、お前はまだ未成年だろう？
examples.english: A: How come you put oolong tea only in my glass? B: Because you are not an adult yet, are you?

examples.japanese: 彼がいるはずの店にやってきたが、入るべきかどうか迷っていた。だって、ここに来るとろくなことがない。
examples.english: I came to the restaurant where I knew he'd be, but I wondered whether I should go in or not, because something bad always occurs there.

examples.japanese: この翻訳なら私にだってできます。
examples.english: (i) I could do this translation, too. (literally: If it's this translation, I can do it, too. (ii) Even I could do this translation. (literally: If it's this translation, even I can do it.

examples.japanese: 数多いお客さんの中には難しい人だっている。
examples.english: In a large group of customers, there will be difficult people(, too).

examples.japanese: 今からだって遅くないから、彼に電話してみたら?
examples.english: It's not too late now (literally: It is not late, even from now), so why don't you call him?

formation:
(i) Noun | であれ | | 
 | たとえ病気であれ | Even if someone is ill | 
 | 誰であれ | No matter who it may be | 
 | いかに弱いチームであれ | No matter how weak a team it may be |

 | たとえ可能であれ | Even if something is possible |

explanation: ～であれ～であれ A structure that means "no matter which one is the case"

examples.japanese: たとえ社長であれ、そのような行為は許されない。
examples.english: Even the (company) president shouldn't be allowed to do things like that. (literally: Even if it is the president, such conduct should not be allowed.

examples.japanese: どんな問題であれ、必ず私に報告して下さい。
examples.english: Whatever kind of problem it may be, please report it to me without fail.

examples.japanese: 通勤がいかに不便であれ、今の家を変わるつもりはない。

examples.japanese: いかに難しい問題であれ、彼ならきっと解決できるはずだ。
examples.english: No matter how difficult the problem may be, he certainly should be able to solve it.

examples.japanese: この練習は、たとえ数分間であれ、毎日することが大切です。
examples.english: It is important to practice this every day, even if it is only for a few minutes.

examples.japanese: 彼の提言は、たとえそれが実行不可能であれ、聞くに値する。
examples.english: His suggestions are worth listening to even if they cannot be carried out.

examples.japanese: 暗号技術については、たとえ短期間の使用であれ、その輸出入を規制している国があります。
examples.english: Some countries regulate the export and import of cryptographic technology, even when it is intended for short-term use.

examples.japanese: 何事であれ、その仕事で生活するとなれば楽なものはない。
examples.english: Whatever kind it may be, if you make a living from it, there is no such thing as easy work.

examples.japanese: 男性であれ、女性であれ、人間としての権利は同じはずだ。
examples.english: Whether one is a man or a woman, one's rights as a human being should be the same.

examples.japanese: 有名であれ、無名であれ、人生は短い。
examples.english: No matter if one is famous or nameless, life is short.

meaning_en: You are not ~, so; it isn’t ~, so
formation:
(i) Noun | {でも/じゃ}あるまいし | | 
 | 子供{でも/じゃ}あるまいし | You aren’t a child, so ~ (literally: you couldn’t possibly be a child, so ~) | 
(ii) Vinformal わけ | {でも/じゃ}あるまいし | | 
 | プロ野球の選手に{なる/なった}わけ{でも/じゃ}あるまいし | It isn’t the case that someone will/has become a professional baseball player, so ~ | 
(iii) Adjective い informal わけ | {でも/じゃ}あるまいし | | 
 | {面白い/面白かった}わけ{でも/じゃ}あるまいし | It isn’t the case that something is/was interesting, so ~ | 
(iv) Adjective な stem {な/だった}わけ | {でも/じゃ}あるまいし | | 
 | 有名{な/だった}わけ{でも/じゃ}あるまいし | It isn’t the case that someone is/was famous, so ~ | 
(v) Noun {である/だった}わけ | {でも/じゃ}あるまいし | | 
 | 社長{である/だった}わけ{でも/じゃ}あるまいし | It isn’t the case that someone is/was a company president, so ~ |
explanation: でも・じゃあるまいし A phrase expressing the speaker’s belief that someone’s action is based on mistaken identity of himself/herself and also expressing the speaker’s critical comments about someone’s behaviour.

examples.english: There's no way you can get to France. How come you're studying French so hard?

examples.japanese: 学生じゃあるまいし、仕事でも探したらどうだ。

examples.japanese: 政治家でもあるまいし、嘘をつかないで下さい。

examples.japanese: 犬じゃあるまいし、そんなに人にじゃれるようなことはやめなさい。
examples.english: You aren't a dog, you know. Stop being so playful with me.

examples.japanese: お葬式でもあるまいし、そんなにしゅんとしないで下さい。

examples.japanese: このうどん屋では注文してから、うどんがくるまで長く待たされ、いらいらする。フランス料理でもあるまいし…。
examples.english: At this noodle shop it takes so long from the time you order noodles to the time they bring them to the table that I get annoyed. It's not French cuisine, you know.

Noun (particle) | でも, (Noun (particle) でも,) でも、Wh-word (particle) でも | | 
 | 小学生(に) でも、誰(に) でも | (to) an elementary pupil or (to) anybody |

examples.english: That sort of thing is known even to a child or to anybody.

examples.japanese: 私って漫画でも何でも読み出すと止まらないタイプなの。
examples.english: I'm the type of person who cannot stop reading manga or whatever once I start.

examples.japanese: Tシャツの大きさはMでもLでも、どちらでもかまいません。
examples.english: It doesn't matter to me whether (the size of) the T-shirt is M or L (literally: or whichever).

examples.japanese: 欧米では、バスでも地下鉄でも、車椅子でどこへでも行ける。どうしても助けが必要な時は、誰かに頼めばたとえ日本人にでも誰にでも手を貸してくれる。
examples.english: In Europe and America you can go anywhere in a wheelchair by bus or by subway. When you ﬁnd you need help, just ask anyone. People there will lend a hand to anyone who asks, Japanese or otherwise.

examples.japanese: 最近のパーティーは留学生でも日本人でも誰でも参加自由で、来る人は飲み物、音楽、自分の作った料理を持ってくるというようにしています.
examples.english: At our recent parties we've made it so all students, whether Japanese or from abroad, can freely participate and ask everyone to bring drinks, music or food they've made.

examples.japanese: A:すみませんが、来週、検査の結果が出たら、もう一度来ていただけますか。B:分かりました。来週でもいつでも伺います。
examples.english: A: Can you come back next week when we get the result of the examination? B: Yes, I can come next week or whenever.

examples.japanese: 私はどちらかと言うと外向的というより（は）内向的だ。
examples.english: I'm more of an introvert than an extrovert.

examples.japanese: 母はどちらかと言うと、大人しい方です。
examples.english: My mother is rather on the quiet side.

examples.japanese: 洋食も悪くはないが、どちらかと言うと、和食の方がいい。
examples.english: It's not that Western-style food is bad, but I prefer Japanese-style food.

examples.japanese: 山本は決して呑気な男ではない。どちらかと言うと神経質な男だ.
examples.english: Yamamoto is far from easy-going. He's more of a nervous type of guy.

examples.japanese: あの政治家のやり方はどちらかと言うと賢いというよりはずる賢い。

examples.japanese: 君はどちらかと言うと楽観的というよりは悲観的だね。

examples.japanese: 彼女はどちらかと言うと、仕事に生きるタイプで、精神的にも強い人間だと思う。

examples.japanese: 向寒の折から、どうかお体にお気をつけ下さい。

examples.english: Although the way in which these two compositions are written is different, their claims are the same.

examples.japanese: 行けども行けども人家が見えてこない。

examples.english: Although I have (a good amount of) knowledge, I have no scholastic talent, so I don't think I can survive in academia (in the future).

examples.japanese: 汲めども尽きぬ泉のように、彼は次々と美しい曲を書き続けた。
examples.english: Just like a spring which never dries up no matter how much water is taken out, he kept writing beautiful songs, one after another.

examples.english: Regarding things you are used to seeing, even though you look at them, you don't really see them. So, you don't notice their problems even if you see them every day.

examples.japanese: 親といえども子供に対してそんな横暴は許されない。

examples.japanese: 老いたりといえども、伊藤先生はまだ動きも速く、この剣道場の人は誰も先生に勝つことができない。

examples.japanese: 走れども走れども雪原が続いているだけだった。

examples.japanese: この書類は印刷が悪くてどうにも読めない。

examples.japanese: 会社経営で破綻寸前まで来るとどうにも救いようがない。

examples.japanese: これだけストレスが溜まると、どうにも解消しようがない。

examples.japanese: 高校時代の友達同士で海外旅行に行くことになった。

examples.japanese: 決勝戦はアルゼンチン選手同士の対決になった。

examples.japanese: このケーブルを使うと、パソコン同士を直接つないで高速ファイル転送をすることができる。

examples.japanese: タバコを吸う者同士は、何となく相手に親しみを感じやすい。

examples.japanese: 茨城沖で貨物船同士が衝突、二人死亡四人行方不明。

examples.japanese: 人生は旅のごとし。
examples.english: Life is like a journey.

examples.japanese: その無謀な行為は火中に飛び込む｛が/かの｝ごとし。
examples.english: Acting recklessly like that is like jumping into the ﬁre.

examples.japanese: 彼女はモナリザのごとくいつも微笑んでいる。
examples.english: She is like Mona Lisa, always smiling.

examples.japanese: x氏は超人のごとき人だ。
examples.english: Mr. X is like a superman.

examples.japanese: 彼女は僕のことを全然覚えていないかのごとき様子だった。
examples.english: She looked as if she didn't remember me at all.

examples.japanese: 光陰矢のごとし。
examples.english: Time ﬂies like an arrow. (literally: Time is like an arrow.)

examples.japanese: 人生は航海のごとし。
examples.english: Life is like a voyage.

examples.japanese: 東京人は万人走っているかのごとし。
examples.english: Tokyoites all look as if they were always running.

examples.japanese: 今年の冬も暖冬だと言われていたが、はたして暖冬だった。
examples.english: They said this would be a warm winter, and indeed it has been.

examples.japanese: はたして日本の教育は改革される(の)だろうか。
examples.english: I wonder if Japanese education will really be reformed at all.

examples.japanese: はたして女性の地位が改憲されるとしても時間がかかるだろう。
examples.english: Even if women's status improves, as expected, it may take time.

examples.japanese: 東西ドイツ統一はいずれは起こると思っていたが、はたして予想通り起きた。
examples.english: I thought that sooner or later East and West Germany would be united, and, just as I expected, it happened.

examples.japanese: 二人の仲は周知の事実で、いつかはゴールインすると思っていたら、はたしてその通りになった。
examples.english: Everyone knew about their relationship, and, just as we expected, they got married.

examples.japanese: そこのレストランは魚料理で有名だったが、はたして思った通りの美味しい料理が出てきた。
examples.english: That restaurant was famous for its ﬁsh dishes, and the food really was as good as we had expected.

examples.japanese: イスラエルをパレスチナ両国の間にはたして真の平和が訪れるのだろうか。
examples.english: I wonder if real peace will indeed come to Israel and the Palestinian territories.

examples.japanese: はたして日本経済は近い将来に復興するだろうか。
examples.english: I wonder if the Japanese economy really will revive in the near future.

meaning_en: Eventually (lead to) ~; even

 | (see key sentence A) | |
