 | (see key sentence B) | |
explanation: An adverb indicating that something is perceived to eventually lead to a signiﬁcant result.

examples.japanese: イラクへの攻撃はアメリカの孤立を招き、ひいてはイスラム社会全体との戦争に発展していく恐れがある。
examples.english: There is fear that an attack against Iraq will bring about American isolation, and eventually will lead to a war with Muslim society as a whole.

examples.japanese: 彼は同僚にライバル意識、ひいては殺意すら抱いていた。
examples.english: He regarded his colleague as a rival, even to the point of considering murder.

examples.japanese: 東京の産業構造を適切に転換していくことが、東京の産業を活性化させ、ひいては日本の経済力の強化につながっていく。
examples.english: Addressing the appropriate restructuring of Tokyo's industrial structure will revitalize Tokyo's industry and eventually lead to the strengthening of the Japanese economy.

examples.japanese: 「誰もが自分自身の能力を最大限に活かして、自ら積極的に新しいことにチャレンジして、よりよく生きていく」という考えを、日本国内、ひいては世界に波及させたいと思っています。
examples.english: Life will improve when everyone uses their abilities to the greatest extent and actively takes on new challenges. I would like this idea to spread within Japan, and, eventually, in the world.

examples.japanese: 世間では、企業経営から、教育、ひいては犯罪まで、話題はインターネットが独占しているという感じです。
examples.english: Throughout society, in business management and education, and even crime, it seems like the Internet is the dominant topic of discussion.

examples.japanese: 道を歩いていて、奇妙な姿の人が向こうから歩いてくると、不安な気持ちになる。これは人間、ひいては動物の防衛機能の一つだろう。
examples.english: If a person with a strange ﬁgure walks towards you on the street, you might start to feel uneasy. This is a human defence mechanism, and is used even by animals.

examples.japanese: 栄養価が高い旬のものをおいしく食べることは、ひいては病気を予防する。
examples.english: Food eaten in season is richer in nutrition, and thus can help prevent disease.

examples.japanese: マスメディアが個人の名誉やプライバシーを不当に侵害する状況が続けば、ひいては報道に対して権力が介入する口実を与えることになる。
examples.english: If the media continues to violate people's reputations and privacy unjustly, some day it could provide an excuse for the government to intervene.

meaning_en: Give something a try

(ii) ひとつNounでも | {Vては/Vinformal pastら}どうですか。 | | 
 | ひとつ散歩でも{しては/したら}どうですか。 | How about taking a walk or something? |

explanation: An adverb used when the speaker intends to do something, or asks someone a favour, or makes a suggestion or gives advice to someone.

examples.japanese: ひとつ日本の小説の英訳をやってみょう。
examples.english: I will try to translate a Japanese novel into English.

examples.japanese: ひとつゴルフでもやったらどうですか。
examples.english: How about giving golf a try?

examples.japanese: ひとつ相談にのって下さい。
examples.english: Please give me your advice.

examples.japanese: ひとつインターネットでもやってみよう。
examples.english: I will try the Internet or something.

examples.japanese: ひとつ東大を受けてみたいと思います。
examples.english: I'd like to give the entrance exam for the University of Tokyo a try.

examples.japanese: 「Shall we ダンス？」という面白い映画を見たので、ひとつ社交ダンスでもやってみようかという気になった。
examples.english: Now that I've seen the (interesting) movie Shall We Dance?, I want to give social dancing a try.

examples.japanese: ひとつ映画でも見に行きませんか。
examples.english: Why don't we go see a movie?

examples.japanese: ひとつ株でもやってみませんか。
examples.english: Don't you want to try stocks?

 | 食べなかった{の/理由}は一つにはまずかった{から/ため}だ | One reason why someone didn’t eat something was because it didn’t taste good | 
 | 美味しい{の/理由}は一つには素材がいい{から/ため}だ | One reason why something is delicious is because the ingredients are good | 
 | 美味しかった{の/理由}は一つには素材がよかった{から/ため}だ | One reason why something was delicious was because the ingredients were good |

examples.japanese: 大学教育の目的は、一つには幅広い教養と専門的な知識・能力を授けること、一つには社会に貢献する指導者を育成することだ。
examples.english: The objective of college education is partly to provide broad schooling and professional knowledge and ability, and partly to train and produce leaders who will contribute to society.

examples.japanese: 彼が外国語を好んで勉強しているのは、一つには、異文化学習が好きだからだ。
examples.english: One reason he likes studying foreign languages is because he likes to learn about different cultures.

examples.japanese: 彼がよく家族と旅行に出かけるのは、一つには自分のため、一つには家族のためだ。
examples.english: He travels so frequently with his family, partly for himself and partly for his family.

examples.japanese: 日本人が大人まで漫画を読んでいるのは、一つには、大人が十分味わえるような漫画があるからだ。
examples.english: The reason even Japanese adults read comics is because there are comics that adults can fully enjoy.

examples.japanese: 彼がその子を好きな理由はいろいろとあるが、一つには彼女の話し方がいつも生き生きとしているためだ。
examples.english: He likes that girl for many reasons, but partly because her talk is always lively.

examples.japanese: 私がアメリカに来た理由は、一つには、そこに学問の自由があると思ったからだ。
examples.english: One reason I came to the U.S. was because I thought there was academic freedom here.

examples.japanese: 政治家が嫌われる理由は、一つには、選挙の時には魅力的な公約を言うのに、当選するとそれを実行しないからだ。
examples.english: Part of the reason politicians are disliked is because they make attractive promises when campaigning but don't put them into practice once they are elected.

examples.japanese: 日本に来た外国人が体験するカルチャーショックには色々あると思うが、一つには、日本人が彼らをガイジン、つまりソトの人と呼ぶということがある。
examples.english: Foreigners experience a variety of culture shocks when they come to Japan, one of which is being called gaijin, or "outside people," by the Japanese.

meaning_en: For the time being; for the present; for now; tentatively; for formality’s sake; nominally; kind of; sort of
explanation: An adverb indicating that an action or state is only temporary or tentative or is superﬁcially conceived.

examples.japanese: 会議の日取りを一応来週の水曜日と決めておきましょう。
examples.english: Let's tentatively set our meeting date for next Wednesday.

examples.japanese: 私は一応トムにその仕事を担当させることにした。
examples.english: I've put Tom in charge of the project for the time being.

examples.japanese: この問題についてはまだ議論の余地はあるとは思うが、一応ここでけりをつけたいと思う。
examples.english: I believe that on this issue there is still a lot to be discussed, but I'd like to bring it to a close for the time being.

examples.japanese: 一応大学を出ておいた方が都合がいいと思い、大学に進学したんです。
examples.english: I thought it would be better for me to graduate from college, to keep up appearances. That's why I went on to college.

examples.japanese: A:コンピュータを使っていらっしゃいますか。 B:はあ、まあ、一応は使っていますが。
examples.english: A: Are you using a computer? B: Well, I'm kind of using one, but . . .

examples.japanese: A:あなたは情報技術の研究者ですか。 B:まあ、一応そういうことです。
examples.english: A: Are you an IT researcher? B: Yes, sort of.

examples.japanese: A:このお金どうするの? B:俺が一応銀行に入れておくよ。
examples.english: A: What are you going to do with this money? B: I will put it in the bank for now.

examples.japanese: 二人は兄弟と言うだけに頭は、まあ、一応似ている。しかし気性はかなり違う。
examples.english: The two are brothers, so their faces do sort of resemble each other. But, their temperaments are quite different.

examples.japanese: 彼はいかなる忠告（に）も耳を貸さなかった。

examples.english: No matter what the theory is, it will have holes in it.

examples.japanese: 父はいかなる事態になっても常に沈着だった。
examples.english: My father was always calm no matter what situation he found himself in.

examples.japanese: 重要なことは、いかなる結果が出ようと（も）自分で決めたい。
examples.english: I would like to make my own decisions about important matters, no matter what happens as a result.

examples.japanese: 日本語運用能力はいかなる基準で測るべきか。
examples.english: By what kind of standards should we assess proﬁciency in Japanese?

examples.japanese: 厳しい父はいかなる口実も許してくれなかった。
examples.english: My strict father never allowed me to make any kind of excuse.

examples.japanese: いかなる文化にも宗教は存在する。
examples.english: There is religion in any culture.

examples.japanese: いかに日本語が難しいかは学習者の母語による。
examples.english: How difficult Japanese is (for someone) depends on the learner's mother tongue.

examples.japanese: いかに運動しても長生きできるとは限らない。
examples.english: No matter how hard one exercises, it doesn't guarantee a long life.

examples.japanese: いかに一生懸命働こうとも一戸建ての家は買えない。
examples.english: No matter how hard I work I cannot buy a single house.

examples.japanese: 人生はいかに短いことか。
examples.english: How short life is!

examples.japanese: いかに死ぬかはいかに生きるかと同じように大事だ。
examples.english: How one dies is as important as how one lives.

examples.japanese: ヒトゲノムの解読が病気の根本的な治療にいかに必要かが分かってきた。
examples.english: We began to understand how important decoding the human genome is for the basic treatment of illness.

examples.japanese: クローン人間がいかに創られるのかは私には理解できないが、その倫理性についての論争には強い興味を覚える。
examples.english: I cannot comprehend how human clones are created, but I have a strong interest in the debate over the ethics of cloning.

examples.japanese: 食べた物がいかにおいしかったかを言葉で適確に説明することは至難のわざだ。
examples.english: It is extremely difﬁcult for one to describe in words how delicious the food he/she ate was.

examples.japanese: A:寄付はいくらぐらいすればいいでしょうか。 B:いくらでも結構です。
examples.english: A: About how much money should I donate? B: Any amount would be ﬁne.

examples.japanese: いくら時間とお金をかけてもそのプロジェクトは終わるまい。
examples.english: No matter how much time and money we spend on this project, it probably won't end.

 | {今更何が/何が今更}言いたいのか。 | What do you want to say now (at this late date)? | 
(ii) 今更 | +Predicate(Negative)。 | | 
 | 今更行けない。 | It’s too late to go (there) |

 | 今更{見ても/見たところで}仕方がない。 | It is no use looking at it now |
explanation: 今更・いまさら An adverb indicating that someone feels that it is too late to do something.

examples.japanese: この話は二年も前に話し合ったじゃないか。なんで、今更同じ話を持ち出すんだ。
examples.english: Didn't we discuss this issue two years back? How come you are bringing it up after such a long time?

examples.japanese: 今更契約を解消するわけにはいかない。
examples.english: It is too late to cancel the contract.

examples.japanese: 今更後悔しても仕方がない。
examples.english: It is useless now to regret what you have done.

examples.japanese: この問題を今更議論したところで無意味でしょう。
examples.english: It would be meaningless to discuss this issue now.

examples.japanese: 卒業してから二十年だが今更ながら母校の教育の質のよさが分かってきた。
examples.english: It's been 20 years since I graduated, (literally: it is too late) but now l've ﬁnally come to appreciate the educational quality of my alma mater.

examples.japanese: あなたはあの男とはきっぱり別れたはずなのに、今更なんで会おうとしているの。
examples.english: I thought you had broken up with that guy. Why in the world are you still trying to see him?

examples.japanese: 今更ですが、「明けましておめでとうございます」。
examples.english: I'm afraid it is too late, but let me wish you a Happy New Year.

examples.japanese: 今日の講師は皆さんよくご存じの方ですから、今更ご紹介する必要はないとは思いますが…。
examples.english: All of you know today's lecturer very well, so I believe it is not necessary to introduce him now, but . . .

meaning_en: Only; always; continue to; keep ~ing; be steadily ~ing; become ~er and ~er
formation:
(i) Vinformal nonpast | 一方だ | | 
 | 悪くなる一方だ | Something only worsens | 
(ii) Vinformal nonpast | 一方のNoun | | 
 | 増える一方の財政赤字 | The fiscal deficit, which continues to increase |
explanation: 一方（だ）A phrase indicating that "something happens continuously" or "someone does something repeatedly".

examples.japanese: 物価は上げる一方だ。
examples.english: (Commodity) prices are rising steadily.

examples.japanese: 久子は私にものを頼む一方で、何もしてくれたことがない。
examples.english: Hisako is always requesting favours but has never done anything for me.

examples.japanese: 電話や電子メールを利用した詐欺は巧妙化する一方だ。
examples.english: Telephone and email fraud is becoming cleverer and cleverer.

examples.japanese: この市は急増した人口にインフラ整備が追いつかず、犯罪も増える一方だ。
examples.english: Improvements to the infrastructure in this city have not kept pace with the sudden population increase, and crime keeps increasing as well.

examples.japanese: ビジネスのグローバル化が進む今日、英語によるコミュニケーション能力の重要性は増す一方だ。
examples.english: English communication skills are becoming more and more important today as businesses continue to globalize.

examples.japanese: サッカー熱は高まる一方だが、少年サッカーでひざの故障を起こすケースも増えている。
examples.english: People's enthusiasm for soccer is growing steadily, but the number of (cases of) knee injuries in youth soccer is also growing.

examples.japanese: 深刻化する一方の医師不足に早急に何らかの対策が必要だ。
examples.english: We need some immediate countermeasures for the shortage of doctors, which is just getting worse.

examples.japanese: 昨日のホッケーでは我々のチームは攻められる一方だった。
examples.english: In yesterday's hockey match, our team was always on the defensive.

examples.japanese: 我々は化石燃料による環境汚染の問題に対応する一方（で）、新しいエネルギーの開発に力を入れなければならない。
examples.english: We have to make more effort in developing new energy (sources) while countering the problem of environmental pollution caused by fossil fuels.

examples.japanese: 企業はIT投資には熱心な一方（で）、セキュリティ意識はまだ低いところが多い。
examples.english: Many companies are still not very conscious about (information) security, even though they are eager to invest in information technology.

meaning_en: Not ~ at all; absolutely not; not ~ whatsoever
formation:
一切 | Vnegativeない | | 
 | 一切食べない | Someone doesn’t eat a thing | 
 | 一切読まない | Someone doesn’t read at all |
explanation: 一切～ない A structure that means "not at all".

examples.japanese: 飛行機事故の原因は一切分からない。
examples.english: We have no idea what caused the airplane accident.

examples.japanese: この製品には遺伝子組み換え大豆は一切使用していません。
examples.english: For this product we haven't used any genetically modiﬁed soybeans at all.

examples.japanese: 盗難に関しては当社は一切責任を負いません。
examples.english: Our company will not take any responsibility whatsoever for thefts.

examples.japanese: 私はその汚職事件とは一切関係ない。
examples.english: I have nothing whatsoever to do with the bribery scandal.

examples.japanese: 謝金は一切いただくわけにはまいりません。
examples.english: I couldn't possibly accept any honorarium at all.

examples.japanese: 私は有害物質を一切含んでいない洗剤を使うことにしている。
examples.english: I make it a rule to use detergents that contain no harmful ingredients.

meaning_en: Once; for a time; temporarily; for the moment; for the present; now
formation:
一旦 | Verb | | 
 | 一旦やめる | Stop something temporarily |
explanation: 一旦・いったん An adverb meaning "once" or "for a short time".

examples.japanese: このは小説一旦読み始めたらやめられない。
examples.english: Once you begin reading this novel, you won't be able to put it down (literally: stop reading it).

examples.japanese: 邦彦は一旦やめたタバコをまた吸い出した。
examples.english: Kunihiko resumed smoking, which he had quit for a time.

examples.japanese: 開演までまだだいぶ時間があるので、一旦ホテルに帰ってから出直そう。
examples.english: There's still a lot of time before the performance begins, so let's go back to the hotel (now) and come again later.

examples.japanese: この大学は、一旦入学してしまえば、そんなに勉強しなくても必ず卒業できる。
examples.english: Once you've entered this university, you will definitely be able to graduate, even if you don't study very hard.

examples.japanese: この電子掲示板は一旦書き込むと消せないので、自分のメッセージを書く時に注意しないといけない。
examples.english: Once you write a message on this electronic bulletin board, you cannot delete it, so you have to be careful (when you write a message).

examples.japanese: 石田は、一旦約束した以上は必ず守る男だ。
examples.english: Ishida is someone who keeps his promise (once he has made one), no matter what.

examples.japanese: 一旦こじれた我々の関係は、容易には元に戻らなかった。
examples.english: Our relationship, once it had become complicated, did not recover easily.

examples.japanese: 予算が厳しくなったので、無料健康相談サービスを一旦中止します。
examples.english: Because the budget has become tight, we are going to discontinue our free health consultation service temporarily.

meaning_en: Figuratively speaking; so to speak; metaphorically speaking; in a manner of saying
formation:
(i) 言ってみれば | Sentence。 | Where Sentence is a simile or a metaphor | 
 | 言ってみれば、彼は熊(のような男)だ。 | Figurately speaking, he is (like) a bear | 
(ii) 言ってみれば | Nounのように～。 | | 
 | 言ってみれば、彼は小説の神様のように見られていた。 | One could say that he was regarded as a god of novels |
explanation: A phrase signalling a comparison (including the use of simile and metaphor), a deﬁnition, or an explanation.

examples.japanese: 言ってみれば、人生は航海（のようなもの）だ。
examples.english: Figuratively speaking, life is (like) a voyage.

examples.japanese: 彼女の家は、言ってみれば、お城のように作られている。
examples.english: You could say her house is built like a castle.

examples.japanese: 日本の文化には厳しいしきたりがあって、言ってみれば、それは宗教のようなものだ。
examples.english: Japanese culture has a set of strict conventions; you could almost call it a religion.

examples.japanese: 結婚は言ってみれば人生の墓場だ。
examples.english: Marriage is, in a manner of speaking, the graveyard of life.

examples.japanese: 医者と弁護士は、言ってみれば、神様のように振る舞う。
examples.english: One could say medical doctors and lawyers act like God.

examples.japanese: 学生たちが学んだ多くの知識は、頭の中に放置されたままで、言ってみれば、死んだ状態になっているのである。
examples.english: A lot of the knowledge that students have learned remains piled up in their brains, and ﬁguratively speaking, it is dead to them.

examples.japanese: シリコンバレーも、結局は日本の、言ってみれば商店街なり地域作りの話と本質的には同じなんだと思いました。
examples.english: I would say Silicon Valley is, after all, essentially the same story as commercial district or community development in Japan.

examples.japanese: 著作権とは、言ってみれば、創造者の権利を守る法律だ。
examples.english: Copyright can be thought of as a law to protect the rights of creators.

meaning_en: It is needless to say that ~; needless to say; it goes without saying
formation:
(i) {V/Adjectiveい} informal+Nominalは | 言うまでもない。 | | 
 | {買う/買った}{の/こと}は言うまでもない。 | Needless to say, someone will buy/bought something | 
 | つまらない{の/こと}は言うまでもない。 | It goes without saying that something is boring | 
 | つまらなかった{の/こと}は言うまでもない。 | It goes without saying that something was boring | 
(ii) Adjective な stem{な/である/だった/であった} | +Nominalは言うまでもない。 | | 
 | 立派{な/である/だった/であった}{の/こと}は言うまでもない。 | It goes without saying that something is/was magnificent | 
(iii) Noun{な/である/だった/であった} | のは言うまでもない。 | | 
 | 教授{な/である/だった/であった}のは言うまでもない。 | It goes without saying that someone is/was a professor | 
(iv) Noun{である/だった} | ことは言うまでもない。 | | 
 | 天才{である/だった}ことは言うまでもない。 | Needless ot say, he is/was a genius | 
(v) 言うまで | {なく/ない(ことだ)が}、Sentence。 | | 
 | 言うまで{なく/ない(ことだ)が}、日本は島国だ。 | Needless to say, Japan is an island country |
explanation: A phrase indicating that what the speaker/writer expresses is generally known but that he/she presents it as a reminder.

examples.japanese: 寿司が日本の代表的な料理であることは言うまでもない。
examples.english: It goes without saying that sushi is representative of Japanese cuisine.

examples.japanese: 言うまでもなく、日本の社会は世界一の高齢化社会になっている。
examples.english: That Japan has become the most rapidly aging society in the world goes without saying.

examples.japanese: 少子化が日本の社会を変えていくことは言うまでもない。
examples.english: It goes without saying that the shrinking population of children will change Japanese society.

examples.japanese: 「アジアの人々は貧しい」「貧しいのは可哀想」「開発援助しなくては」という固定観念が有害なのは言うまでありません。
examples.english: The set of ﬁxed ideas that "Asians are poor," "Being poor is pitiable," and "We should provide development assistance," is, needless to say, harmful.

examples.japanese: 二人はパーティーで会って、すぐ意気投合しました。そのあと毎日のようにデートをしたのは言うまでもありません。
examples.english: The two met at a party, and right away they hit it off. I hardly need to mention that after that they went out on a date almost every day.

examples.japanese: オープンネットワークコンピューティング環境では、日々増大するネットワークデータをいかに敏速にかつ効率よくバックアップするかが重要であることは言うまでもありません。
examples.english: Needless to say, in an open network computing environment, it is important how quickly and effectively you back up the continually expanding network data.

examples.japanese: 言うまでもありませんが、大学の成績の優秀な学生が社会で成功するとは限りません。
examples.english: Needless to say, students whose grades in college were superb do not always succeed in society.

examples.japanese: いまさら言うまでもなく、地球の温暖化は生態系に悪影響をもたらしている。
examples.english: It's obvious now, but global warming is having an adverse effect on the ecosystem.

meaning_en: So to speak; as it were; like; sort of
formation:
言わば | Sentence。 | | 
 | 言わば国に誕生日だ。 | Something is, as it were, the nation’s birthday | 
 | 言わば彼は二度死んだようなものだ。 | He died twice, so to speak |
explanation: An adverb that means "if I were to say it some way (or a different way)".

examples.japanese: この本は、言わば私のバイブルだ。
examples.english: This is, as it were, my Bible.

examples.japanese: この試験は言わばアメリカの大学に留学する際のTOEFLに当たる。
examples.english: This test is, so to speak, the equivalent of the TOEFL, which people take when they (want to) study at a university in the U.S.

examples.japanese: ここまでは、言わばウォーミングアップのようなもので、ここからが本番だ。
examples.english: This has been sort of a warm-up, and starting now, the real business begins.

examples.japanese: その判決は言わばこの国の良心を代弁したものだった。
examples.english: The court's ruling represented (literally: was something that represented) this country's conscience, so to speak.

examples.japanese: 言わば趣味で始めたことがいつの間にか大きなビジネスになってしまった。
examples.english: What I started as sort of a hobby became a large-scale business before I knew it.

examples.japanese: 当地区には、言わば幽霊人口である非合法居住者が7~10万人いますが、この人たちは補助金対象外となります。
examples.english: In this district there are 70,000 to 100,000 illegal residents, who form, as it were, a ghost population. These people are not eligible to receive assistance subsidies.

examples.japanese: こうして見てみると、かつてはサダム・フセインも、ソ連やイランと戦ってきた、言わばアメリカの盟友だったわけである。
examples.english: When we view it this way, (we realise that) Saddam Hussein, who fought against Soviet Russia and Iran, used to be America's bosom buddy, so to speak.

examples.japanese: ファッション写真は、１９３０年代までは、言わば「新参者」の分野と見られていたらしい。
examples.english: Up to the 1930s, fashion photography was apparently considered a "newcomer" ﬁeld, so to speak.

meaning_en: So-called; what we call; known as
formation:
いわゆる | Noun | | 
 | いわゆる天才 | What people call a genius |
explanation: A noun modifier that means "known generally by this term".

examples.japanese: 伊藤さんはいわゆる「エリート」の大学を卒業した。
examples.english: Ms. Ito graduated from one of the so-called "elite" universities.

examples.japanese: いわゆるリストラのために失業した人は非常に多い。
examples.english: Many people lost their jobs because of what is called restructuring.

examples.japanese: 1986年から９０年代初めにかけてのいわゆる「バブル経済」の時代には土地や株が高騰した。
examples.english: During the so-called "bubble economy," from 1986 through the early 90's, land and stocks prices soared.

examples.japanese: 21世紀には多くの国でいわゆる安楽死が合法化されていくだろう。
examples.english: In the 21st century what is called euthanasia will be legalized in many countries.

examples.japanese: いわゆる「いじめ」の問題は、自分と異なる人間を認めるメンタリティーが日本に根づかないと容易にはなくならないであろう。
examples.english: The problem we know as bullying will not easily be solved unless the mentality of accepting someone different from oneself takes root in Japan.

examples.japanese: いわゆるIT、すなわち情報技術の開発に、日本政府は本腰を入れ始めた。
examples.english: The Japanese government has started to put its weight behind developing "IT," or information technology.

examples.japanese: 内分泌撹乱化学物質、いわゆる環境ホルモンは、人間と野生生物へ悪影響を与えると言われている。
examples.english: Endocrine disrupting chemicals, also known as environmental hormones, are said to adversely affect humans and wildlife.

meaning_en: Oneself; in and of itself; the very
formation:
(i) NounPhrase | 自体 | | 
 | 技術自体 | Technology itself | 
 | 日本に行くこと自体 | The act of going to Japan (in and of) itself | 
(ii) NounPhraseそれ | 自体 | | 
 | 素材それ自体 | The materials themselves |
explanation: A dependent noun that is used to emphasize the referent of the preceding noun.

examples.japanese: インターネット自体は情報の通路であって、内容は持たない。
examples.english: The Internet is a path for information and does not contain any content itself.

examples.japanese: 私にとってはこの試合に出られること自体が光栄なことです。
examples.english: For me, being able to participate in this match in and of itself is an honour.

examples.japanese: ケータイ自体には問題はない。問題は使う人のマナーや気配りだ。
examples.english: There is no problem with cell phones in and of themselves. The problems exist in the manners and considerateness of the users.

examples.japanese: いまの仕事自体には満足していますが、職場の人間関係がうまくいかず悩んでいます。
examples.english: I'm satisﬁed with the job itself, but what troubles me is that I cannot maintain good relationships with the people at my workplace.

examples.japanese: 音声データ自体に異常があるので、どのプレーヤーで再生してもノイズが入ってしまう。
examples.english: The sound data itself contains some defects, so no matter what player you use to play it back, you'll get noise.

examples.japanese: 世の中が大きく変わった今、この組織の存在自体が疑われている。
examples.english: The world has changed greatly, and the very existence of this organization is now in doubt.

examples.japanese: この広告は、販売より広告それ自体が目的だ。
examples.english: The goal of this advertisement is the advertisement (of the product) itself rather than sales.

examples.japanese: 裁判所はこれらのファイル交換ソフト自体の違法性は認められないという判決を下した。
examples.english: The court ruled that these ﬁle-exchange software programs in and of themselves are not illegal.

meaning_en: extremely
formation:
Adjective い informal nonpast | 限りだ | Where adjectiveい＝emotive adjective | 
 | 嬉しい限りだ | I am extremely happy |
explanation: A phrase that indicates the extreme degree of the speaker’s/writer’s emotion — happiness, sorrow, envy, shame or loneliness, among others

examples.japanese: いろいろなところに行っておられるんですね。うらやましい限りです。
examples.english: You are traveling to all sorts of places. I'm extremely envious of you.

examples.japanese: 電子メールでご連絡いただければ、嬉しい限りです。
examples.english: I would be extremely happy if you would kindly contact me by e-mail.

examples.japanese: 私の講演が皆様の知性を刺激できれば喜ばしい限りです。
examples.english: If my lecture stimulates you intellectually, I will be extremely happy.

examples.japanese: あなたの明るい顔が見られなくなって、寂しい限りです。
examples.english: I cannot see your cheerful face any longer, and I couldn't feel lonelier.

examples.japanese: 私がかいた絵をお見せするのはお恥ずかしい限りです。

meaning_en: extremely
formation:
Adjective い informal nonpast | 限りだ | Where adjectiveい＝emotive adjective | 
 | 嬉しい限りだ | I am extremely happy |
explanation: A phrase that indicates the extreme degree of the speaker’s/writer’s emotion — happiness, sorrow, envy, shame or loneliness, among others

examples.japanese: いろいろなところに行っておられるんですね。うらやましい限りです。
examples.english: You are traveling to all sorts of places. I'm extremely envious of you.

examples.japanese: 電子メールでご連絡いただければ、嬉しい限りです。
examples.english: I would be extremely happy if you would kindly contact me by e-mail.

examples.japanese: 私の講演が皆様の知性を刺激できれば喜ばしい限りです。
examples.english: If my lecture stimulates you intellectually, I will be extremely happy.

examples.japanese: あなたの明るい顔が見られなくなって、寂しい限りです。
examples.english: I cannot see your cheerful face any longer, and I couldn't feel lonelier.

examples.japanese: 私がかいた絵をお見せするのはお恥ずかしい限りです。

meaning_en: Worth; meaning; effect; result
formation:
(i) Vinformal | 甲斐が{ある/ない} | | 
 | 来た甲斐がある | It is worth coming here; coming here pays off | 
 | 薬を飲んでいる甲斐がない | It isn’t worth taking medicine | 
(ii) Nounの | 甲斐が{ある/ない} | | 
 | 徹夜の甲斐がある | Something is worth staying up all night for/staying up all night pays off | 
 | 勉強の甲斐がない | Something isn’t worth studying | 
(iii) Vます | 甲斐 | | 
 | やり甲斐 | Meaning/worth in doing something | 
(iv) Sentence1 | その甲斐があって、Sentence2 | (only その can precede 甲斐) | 
 | 毎日運動をした。その甲斐があって、体重がだいぶ減った。 | I exercised every day. And it was worth it; I lost quite a bit of weight |
explanation: 甲斐・かい・がい A dependent noun that means something is worth someone’s effort.

examples.japanese: 日本語をよく勉強したかいがあって、日本語関係の会社に就職することができた。
examples.english: It was worth studying Japanese hard because (literally: and) I was able to get a Japan-related job.

examples.japanese: 社員一同の努力のかいがあって一時低調だった会社も上向きになった。
examples.english: The combined efforts of the company employees paid off, and the company, which had been in a slump for a while, started improving.

examples.japanese: あなたにとって生きがいとは何ですか。
examples.english: What makes life worth living for you?

examples.japanese: 彼は東南アジア諸国の旅行中、毎日詳しく日記をつけておいた。そのかいがあって、日本に戻って旅行記を書く時にとても書きやすかった。
examples.english: He kept a detailed diary during his trip to South East Asia. It paid off, as (literally: and) it made it easy for him to write his travelogue when he returned to Japan.

examples.japanese: 一生懸命やったかいがあって、マラソン大会ごとに順位が上がってきました。
examples.english: My efforts paid off, and I finished higher in the ranking with each race.

examples.japanese: 寒い中待っていたかいがあって、見事な日の出を見ることができた。
examples.english: Waiting in the cold paid off, as I was able to see a wonderful sunrise.

examples.japanese: せっかく富士山に登ったのに頂上からは下が全然見えず、登ったかいがなかった。
examples.english: I climbed Mt. Fuji with great effort, but I couldn't see anything from the summit, so it wasn't worth the climb.

examples.japanese: 弟は看病のかい(も)なく五歳の短い生涯を閉じた。
examples.english: In spite of all the medical care (he received), my little brother's life ended when he was only ﬁve.

meaning_en: Whether X or not
formation:
(i) {V/Adjectiveい} informal | か否か | | 
 | {来る/来た}か否か | Whether or not someone will come/came | 
 | {面白い/面白かった}か否か | Whether or not something is/was interesting | 
(ii) {Noun/Adjectiveな} stem | {∅/である/だった/であった}か否か | | 
 | 学生{∅/である/だった/であった}か否か | Whether or not someone is/was a student | 
 | 元気{∅/である/だった/であった}か否か | Whether or not someone is/was healthy | 
(iii) Vinformal nonpast | べき(である) か否か | | 
{Noun/Adjectiveなstem} | であるべきか否か | | 
 | 行くべき(である) か否か | Whether or not someone should go there | 
 | 学生であるべきか否か | Whether or not someone should be a student | 
 | 質素であるべきか否か | Whether or not someone should be frugal |
explanation: A conjunctive phrase indicating that the speaker/writer is wondering whether something is the case or not.

examples.japanese: このソフトが役に立つか否かは保証の限りではありません。
examples.english: I cannot say (literally: guarantee) whether this software is useful or not.

examples.japanese: 選挙の時に、有権者は候補者が倫理観のある政治家（である）か否かを見抜かなければならない。
examples.english: In an election, the voter has to judge (literally: see through) whether or not a candidate is a politician of integrity.

examples.japanese: 子供に携帯電話を持たせるべきか否かは議論が分かれる。
examples.english: Opinions differ as to whether we should allow a child to have a cell phone.

examples.japanese: アメリカの大学では教授が外国人であるか否かは問題にならないが、日本ではそれがよく問題になるようだ。
examples.english: In the U.S., whether or not a professor is a foreigner is not a problem, but in Japan, it appears that it is frequently an issue.

examples.japanese: 家を探す場合、その地域が安全であるか否かが一番大事なポイントになる。
examples.english: When you search for a house, whether or not the area is safe is the most important point.

examples.japanese: クラシック音楽を聞く時、私は旋律が美しいか否かよりその音楽が生命を感じさせるか否かに注意を払う。
examples.english: When I listen to classical music, I pay attention to whether or not it causes me to feel life rather than whether or not the melody is beautiful.

examples.japanese: 大学の入試要項をよく読んでから受験するか否かを決めるべきだ。
examples.english: You should decide whether or not to take the entrance examination after reading the university's guidelines carefully.

examples.japanese: 愛されたら愛しかえすべきか否かという疑問は愚問です。
examples.english: The question of whether or not one should return love when one is loved is a silly one.

meaning_en: As if
formation:
(i) {まるで/あたかも} | {V/Adjective い}informalかのように | | 
 | {まるで/あたかも}{怒っている/怒っていた}かのように | As if someone were/had been mad | 
 | {まるで/あたかも}{正しい/正しかった}かのように | As if someone/something were/had been correct | 
(ii) {まるで/あたかも} | {Noun/Adjective なstem}{である/であった}かのように | | 
 | {まるで/あたかも}神様{である/であった}かのように | As if someone were/had been God | 
 | {まるで/あたかも}贅沢{である/であった}かのように | As if something were/had been luxurious |
explanation: A conjunctive phrase that forms an adverbial clause which describes the way someone/something appears to the writer, contrary to reality.

examples.japanese: 彼女は(まるで)整形手術したかのようにきれいになった。
examples.english: Her looks improved (literally: She became beautiful), as though she had undergone cosmetic surgery.

examples.japanese: 彼女の病気は年内に治るかのように見えた。
examples.english: It looked as though her illness would be cured before the end of the year.

examples.japanese: あたかも日本の製造業全体の競争力は強いかのように思われてきた。
examples.english: The competitiveness of the Japanese manufacturing industry has been perceived as (though it were) strong.

examples.japanese: 彼は有能な政治学者であるかのように言われているが、実は無能極まりない。
examples.english: People say he is a capable political scientist, but actually he is extremely incapable.

examples.japanese: あの男は不確かなことをあたかも正確であるかのように断言する。
examples.english: That man speaks deﬁnitively about something uncertain as if it were a sure thing.

examples.japanese: その教師は私がまるでカンニングをしたかのように私を問いただした。
examples.english: The teacher pressed me hard as if I had cheated on the exam.

examples.japanese: 彼は心理学のことは何も知らないのにあたかもよく知っているかのように心理学のことを話したがる。
examples.english: He doesn't know anything about psychology, but he likes to talk about it as if he knows it very well.

examples.japanese: あたかも僕の心を解かすかのように、白くて透明な雪が降っている。
examples.english: White, transparent snow is falling as though it would melt my heart.

meaning_en: In terms of; from the viewpoint of; judging from
formation:
Noun | から言って | | 
 | 効率から言って | In terms of efficiency |
explanation: A phrase that means either "in terms of" or "judging from".

examples.japanese: 燃費から言ってこの車は非常に経済的だ。
examples.english: In terms of gas mileage, this car is extremely economical.

examples.japanese: 学生の評価から言って鈴木先生はいい先生に違いない。
examples.english: Judging from his student evaluations, Professor Suzuki must be a fine teacher.

examples.japanese: 性能から言って、このエンジンを凌ぐものは少ない。
examples.english: In terms of performance, few engines can surpass this one.

examples.japanese: この小説は内容から言って子供向きではない。
examples.english: The content of this novel is not suitable for children.

examples.japanese: 仕事の効率から言って週休二日の方がいい。
examples.english: In terms of efﬁciency a ﬁve-day work week (literally: two days off a week) is better.

examples.japanese: DNA鑑定から言って、彼が犯人であることは確実だ。
examples.english: Judging from the DNA evidence, there is no doubt that he is the culprit.

examples.japanese: 顔の色つやから言って、父は間違いなく健康だ。
examples.english: Judging from his facial complexion, my father is deﬁnitely healthy.

examples.japanese: 日本語能力試験の結果から言って、ジョンの日本語はすばらしいに違いない。
examples.english: Judging from the results of his Japanese Proﬁciency Test, John’s Japanese must be superb.

meaning_en: Consist of; be composed of
formation:
(i) (Xは) Noun1とNoun2(と…)(と) | から{なる/なっている} | | 
 | 委員会は男性５人と女性７人(と) から{なる/なっている} | The committee consists of five men and seven women | 
(ii) (Xは) Noun | から{なる/なっている} | | 
 | 委員会は１２名の教授から{なる/なっている} | The committee consists of 12 professors | 
(iii) Noun1(とNoun2(と…))(と) | からなるNoun3 | | 
 | 役員と理事（と）からなる委員会 | A committee that consists of officers and board members |
explanation: A phrase indicating that something consists of more than one member/constituent.

examples.japanese: 英語の"relax"はラテン語の"re-"(再び)と"laxare"（緩む）とからなっている。
examples.english: The English word "relax" consists of the Latin "re-" (again) and "laxare" (to loosen).

examples.japanese: タンパク質はアミノ酸からなっている。
examples.english: Proteins are composed of amino acids.

examples.japanese: 夫婦と子供からなる世帯は今後減るのだろうか。
examples.english: I wonder if households that consist of married couple and their children will decrease in the future.

examples.japanese: 日本の神社は拝殿と本殿とからなっている。
examples.english: A Japanese Shinto shrine consists of a front shrine and an inner shrine.

examples.japanese: この大学の東洋学科は言語、文学と歴史からなっている。
examples.english: This university’s East Asian Studies Department consists of language, literature and history (programs).

examples.japanese: 日本は島国で、本州と北海道と四国と九州と沖縄とからなっている。
examples.english: Japan is an island country consisting of Honshu, Hokkaido, Shikoku, Kyushu and Okinawa.

examples.japanese: 地球の内部構造は、何重もの階層構造からなっている。
examples.english: The structure of the inner part of the earth consists of multi-layered strata.

examples.japanese: ブラームスのレクイエムは演奏に約一時間半を要する大作で、全7楽章からなっている。
examples.english: Brahms’s Requiem is a magnum opus that takes about an hour and a half to perform and consists of a total of seven movements.

examples.japanese: 仮に一億円｛もらう/もらった｝と｛したら/すれば｝何に使いますか。
examples.english: Supposing you received 100 million yen, what would you use it for?

examples.japanese: 仮に月収が30万円｛ある/あった｝として、どのようなアパートを借りることができるだろうか。
examples.english: Supposing that I had an income of 300,000 yen, I wonder what kind of an apartment I could rent.

examples.japanese: 仮にこれが日本の教育の現状だったら、構造改革の余地は大いにある。
examples.english: If this were the current state of Japanese educational affairs, a lot would have to be restructured.

examples.japanese: 仮に手術が成功｛する/した｝としても、高齢だから父の体が元に戻ることはないだろう。
examples.english: Even if the operation is successful, my father, who is quite old, will probably not regain his original health.

examples.japanese: 仮にあなたがベンチャー企業の経営権を持っていたら、どのようなアプローチを取りますか。
examples.english: Supposing that you managed a business venture, what sort of approach would you take?

examples.japanese: よくある質問ですが、仮にあなたが今小さい島で一人で暮らすとして、一冊だけ本を持って行けるとしたら、どの本を持って行きますか。
examples.english: This is a common question, but supposing that you were going to live alone on a small island and were allowed to bring only one book, what would it be (literally: which book would you take there)?

examples.japanese: 仮に今の調子で老齢化が進むとすれば、21世紀後半には日本の人口の5割以上が６５歳以上になる可能性がある。
examples.english: If Japan ages at the current rate, in the latter half of the 21st century more than half of the Japanese population will be 65 or older.

examples.japanese: 仮に日本に一年ぐらい行って日本語を勉強すれば、君たちの日本語はすごく上達するよ。
examples.english: If you go to Japan to study Japanese for about a year, your Japanese will make an impressive progress.

meaning_en: As soon as (one notices that) ~; soon after; when one thinks/feels that ~
formation:
(i) Sentence1 informal past | かと思うと、Sentence2 | Where the predicate in Sentence2 is non-emotive; the subjects in Sentence1 and Sentence2 are the same | 
 | 食べたかと思うと、家を出た | As soon as someone has eaten, he left home | 
(ii) Sentence1 informal | かと思うと、Sentence2。 | Where the predicate in Sentence2 is emotive | 
 | 日本へ行けるかと思うと嬉しい。 | When I think that I can go to Japan, I am happy | 
 | 馬鹿にされたかと思うと悔しいい。 | When I think that I was despised, I feel distressed |
explanation: A phrase indicating that an action or state in the dependent clause occurs very closely with another action or state in the clause, or causes another action or state in the main clause.

examples.japanese: 最近は、肌寒くなったかと思うと、翌日には暖かくなったりする。
examples.english: These days, just when you think it's gotten chilly, the next day it turns warm again.

examples.japanese: 私の書いた小説が出版されるかと思うと、とても嬉しい。
examples.english: When I think that the novel I wrote will be published, I feel very happy.

examples.japanese: ハワイでは、雨が降ってきたかと思うと、すぐやんでしまう。
examples.english: In Hawaii, as soon as it begins to rain, it stops right away.

examples.japanese: 花火は、あがったかと思うとすぐ消えてしまうからいいのだ。
examples.english: I like ﬁreworks because they disappear as soon as they go up.

examples.japanese: うちの小学生の子供は、テレビを見終わったかと思うと、コンピュータゲームをやり始める。
examples.english: Our elementary school child starts to play computer games soon after he ﬁnishes watching TV.

examples.japanese: 妻がおいしい夕食を作ってくれているかと思うと、家に帰る足も速まる。
examples.english: When I think about my wife preparing a delicious dinner for me, I naturally start walking home faster.

examples.japanese: 会社のリストラで職を失うのではないかと思うと、気が重いです。
examples.english: When I think about how I might be laid off because of restructuring at my company, I feel depressed.

examples.japanese: 子供たちも大学を出て一人立ちしたので、もう学費もかからないかと思うと、ほっとします。
examples.english: When I think about how we no longer need to pay educational expenses because our children have graduated from college and are now on their own, I feel so relieved.

meaning_en: And; and also; yet; but; and ~ as well; as well as; moreover

 | 行かず、且つ | Someone will not go and |

explanation: 且つ・かつ A conjunction meaning "and" that connects words, phrases and sentences.

examples.japanese: スミス氏は流暢な日本語を話し、且つ日本の歴史や文化にも明るい。
examples.english: Mr. Smith is ﬂuent in Japanese and is also knowledgeable about Japanese history and culture.

examples.japanese: この本は、分かりやすく、且つ味わい深い言葉で書かれている。
examples.english: This book is written in language that is easy to understand but also profound.

examples.japanese: 彼女は一流のピアニストで、且つ優れた随筆家だ。
examples.english: She is a ﬁrst-class pianist, as well as a ﬁne essayist.

examples.japanese: 外国語は、楽しく、且つ効果的に勉強したい。
examples.english: We'd like to study foreign languages in an enjoyable yet effective way.

examples.japanese: 英語ができること、且つウェブサイトの作成経験があることがこの仕事の要件だ。
examples.english: Being able to speak English and having experience in constructing websites are the conditions required for this job.

examples.japanese: パソコンさえあれば自宅ででき、且つ高収入の仕事をご紹介します。
examples.english: We will introduce you to jobs that not only pay well, but can be done at home, as long as you have a computer.

examples.japanese: この図は、自動車を個人で利用できず、且つ家族とも共有できない６５歳以上の高齢者の外出頻度を示している。
examples.english: This ﬁgure shows how often senior citizens over 65 who cannot drive a car and do not share one with their family get out.

examples.japanese: 和太鼓による若々しく、且つたくましい演奏をご堪能下さい。
examples.english: Please enjoy the youthful, powerful performance on the Japanese drums.

meaning_en: Since; only
formation:
(i) Vinformal past | (っ) きり | | 
 | 出た(っ) きり(帰らない) | (someone has never returned) since he left home | 
 | 買った(っ) きり(使わない) | (someone has never used something) since he bought it | 
(ii) Noun | きり | Where Noun=noun of time | 
 | 今日きり | Only today | 
 | 今週きり | Only this week | 
 | 今年きり | Only this year | 
(iii) Demonstrative Pronoun | (っ) きり | | 
 | これ(っ) きり | Only this much/only this time | 
 | それ(っ) きり | (only that much/only that time); since then |

examples.japanese: 山下氏は1964年に日本を出た（っ）きり日本には一度も帰っていない。
examples.english: Mr. Yamashita hasn't returned to Japan even once since he left in 1964.

examples.japanese: ソウルにいるのも今夜きりです。
examples.english: This is my last night (literally: the only night left) in Seoul.

examples.japanese: 彼女とは十年以上も前にパリで会ったきりで、その後どうしているのか、全然知らない。
examples.english: I haven't seen her since we met in Paris more than 10 years ago and I have no idea how she's been doing since then.

examples.japanese: 小学校六年の時に別れたっきりの同級生に気づかれるなんて、ひょっとして私って小学校の時から顔が変わってないんだろうか。
examples.english: My classmate, whom I hadn't seen since we left 6th grade, recognized me. I wonder if I look the same as I did in elementary school (literally: my face has not changed since my grade school days).

examples.japanese: フロイトの本はずいぶん前に読んだっきりなので、内容のほとんどは忘れてしまいました。
examples.english: It's been a long time since I read Freud's books, so I've forgotten almost all of the content.

examples.japanese: 父は雪の日に倒れて、腰の骨を折ってから、寝たきりになってしまった。
examples.english: My father fell on a snowy day and broke his hip, and since then he's been lying in bed.

examples.japanese: それっきりなの？もっとたくさんちょうだい。
examples.english: Is this all (literally: only this much)? Give me more, please.

examples.japanese: もう会うのはこれっきりにしましょう。
examples.english: Let's make this the last (literally: only) time we see each other.

meaning_en: Extremely; utterly; very; so; cannot be more; extreme; utmost
formation:
(i) Adjective な stem | この上ない | | 
 | 不便この上ない | Extremely inconvenient | 
(ii) {Adjectiveいinformal nonpast/Adjectiveなstemな} | ことこの上ない | | 
 | 嬉しいことこの上ない | Someone cannot be happier | 
 | 危険なことこの上ない | Extremely dangerous | 
(iii) この上ない | Noun | | 
 | この上ない幸せ | Extreme happiness |
explanation: A phrase that indicates that something or someone is in an extreme state.

examples.japanese: 生まれたばかりの赤ん坊を車に残して買い物に行くとは非常識この上ない。
examples.english: It is utterly senseless to leave a newborn baby in the car and go shopping.

examples.japanese: この部屋はクーラーも扇風機もなく、風も全然通らないので、暑いことこの上ない。
examples.english: There is neither an air-conditioner nor a fan in this room, and no breeze, either, so it's extremely hot in here.

examples.japanese: 大任を無事に果たしてこの上ない充実感に浸っている。
examples.english: I'm enjoying the feeling of utmost fulfilment, having completed an important mission successfully.

examples.japanese: 最近よく食事時にセールスの電話がかかってくるが、迷惑この上ない。
examples.english: We often get sales calls at dinnertime these days, which is extremely annoying.

examples.japanese: 一人住まいの高齢者を狙って金を騙し取るなど卑劣この上ない。
examples.english: It is utterly contemptible to target old people living alone and cheat them of their money.

examples.japanese: こんな大事な仕事をアルバイトにさせるなんて無責任この上ない。
examples.english: It is extremely irresponsible to have a part-timer do such an important job.

examples.japanese: また選挙シーズンが来た。いつものことだが、選挙の車が連日うちの前を通り、マイクで候補者の名前を連呼する。うるさいことこの上ない。
examples.english: Here we are again in election season. As always, the campaign cars pass by my house every day, shouting out their candidate's name repeatedly on the microphone. It's extremely noisy and annoying.

examples.japanese: このコンピュータは日本語入力の時、いちいち入力方式を指定しないといけないので、面倒なことこの上ない。
examples.english: Because we have to specify the input method on this computer every time we want to type in Japanese, it's extremely cumbersome.

meaning_en: In addition; and additionally; what’s more
formation:
(i) Noun1、Noun2、(…、) | 加えてNoun | | 
 | 酒、ビール、加えてウイスキー | Sake, beer, and on top of that, whisky | 
(ii) Sentence1 (それに) | 加えてSentence2。 | | 
 | 彼は頭が切れる。(それに) 加えて人柄もいい。 | He is sharp. In addition, he has a good personality. |
explanation: A conjunction that means "in addition to what has just been mentioned".

examples.japanese: この冬のアメリカ東部は雪、雨、加えて強風の被害が大きかった。
examples.english: This winter the East Coast of the U.S. suffered terribly from snow, rain and, in addition, strong winds.

examples.japanese: この辺は物価が安い。（それに）加えて自然環境もすばらしい。
examples.english: Things are inexpensive in this neighbourhood. What's more, the natural environment is amazing.

examples.japanese: この作家の小説は想像力の豊かさ、鮮明な文体、加えて、極めて音楽的なリズム感がある。
examples.english: The novels of this author are richly imaginative, have a clear-cut style, and, in addition, have a highly musical rhythm.

examples.japanese: 金融業の倒産、失業率の上昇、加えて、不安定な政治状況によって、この国の経済は沈滞している。
examples.english: The bankruptcy of ﬁnancial institutions, the rise in the unemployment rate, and, additionally, political instability are causing the stagnation of this country's economy.

examples.japanese: 健康維持には正しい食事、適度な運動、加えて人との温かいコミュニケーションが必要であろう。
examples.english: In order to maintain your health, a proper diet, moderate exercise and, what's more, amiable communication with other people are necessary.

examples.japanese: 彼女はおしゃべりが好きで、とても明るい。それに加えて、なかなかユニークなキャラクターだ。
examples.english: She likes to chat and is very cheerful. In addition, she has a unique character.

examples.japanese: 北海道の秋は紅葉がきれいだ。加えて、空気がからっと乾燥していて気持ちがいい。
examples.english: The fall foliage in Hokkaido is beautiful. In addition, the crisp, dry air feels good.

examples.japanese: 京都は神社仏閣がたくさんある。加えて、魅力的な日本庭園も多い。
examples.english: Kyoto has many shrines and temples. In addition, it has many charming traditional gardens.

meaning_en: To say nothing of; not to speak of; let alone; still more; much less; all the more reason why
formation:
(i) Subordinate Clause、 | まして(や) Main Clause。 | 
 | (See key sentence A.) | 
(ii) Sentence1。 | まして(や)Sentence2。 | 
 | (See key sentence B.) |
explanation: まして（や）An adverb expressing the idea that because one statement is true, the subsequent statement is naturally true.

examples.japanese: アパートの家賃を払うのが精一杯なのに、まして（や）家を買うなんて夢物語だ。
examples.english: I am just managing to pay the rent for my apartment; how much more of a dream it is to imagine buying my own house!

examples.japanese: 彼女は日本語で講演もできる。まして（や）日常会話など問題ではない。
examples.english: She can give a speech in Japanese, to say nothing of (her ability to handle) everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: この小説は大人にも読みにくいのに、まして小学生に読めるはずがない。
examples.english: This novel is hard even for adults to read much less elementary school students.

examples.japanese: 彼は簡単な日本語すら話せない。ましてや、書くことなど思いもよらない。
examples.english: He cannot even speak Japanese, let alone write it.

examples.japanese: 僕は自転車さえ買えない。まして、車を買うなんて不可能だ。
examples.english: I can't even buy a bike, let alone a car.

examples.japanese: 国内での単身赴任でもつらい。ましてや、外国での単身赴任となるともっとつらい。
examples.english: To be sent alone to a new post within Japan is hard. It is still harder to go overseas to work without one's family.

examples.japanese: この数学の問題は教授でも解けないのだから、まして、学生の僕に解けるはずがない。
examples.english: Even a professor cannot solve this math problem much less a student like me.

examples.japanese: 65歳の人が毎日一キロ泳いでいるんです。まして、32歳のあなたが同じことができないわけがないですよ。
examples.english: There's a 65-year-old man who swims one kilometre every day. All the more reason why a 32-year-old like you should be able to do the same.

meaning_en: Again; also; too; (not) ~ either; and; additionally; or
formation:
(i) また | Verb | [repetition] | 
 | また来る | Someone will come again | 
(ii) Nounも | また | [addition] | 
 | 猫もまた(哺乳動物だ) | A cat is also a mammal | 
(iii) Nominalも | また | [addition] | 
 | 酒をオンザロックで飲むもまた(いい) | Drinking sake on the rocks is not bad either | 
 | 文化を学ぶこともまた大切だ | Studying culture is also important | 
(iv) ～{Vます/Adjectiveいstemく}、 | また、Sentence。 | [additional information] | 
 | 彼女はピアノを巧みに弾き、また、歌もうまい。 | She plays the piano well, and also sings well | 
 | ここは景色も素晴らしく、また、空気もきれいだ。 | The scenery is marvellous here, and the air is clean, too | 
(v) ～{Adjectiveなstem/Noun} | で(あり)、また、Sentence。 | [additional information] | 
 | 彼女は聡明で(あり)、また、性格もよい。 | She is bright, and her character is also fine | 
 | 彼はピアニストで(あり)、また、指揮者でもある。 | He is a pianist and also a conductor | 
(vi) Sentence1。 | また、Sentence2 | [additional information] | 
 | 登録はあらかじめして下さい。また、当日も受け付けいたします。 | Please register beforehand. You can register (literally: we will accept your registration) on the day of the conference, too | 
(vii) Sentence1し、 | また、Sentence2。 | [additional information] | 
 | 登録は学会の１か月前から受け付けますし、また、当日も受け付けいたします。 | We will accept your registration starting one month before the conference, but you can register on the day of the conference, too |
explanation: An adverb/conjunction that indicates repetition or addition.

examples.japanese: 来年の春、またお会いします。
examples.english: I will see you again next spring.

examples.japanese: 山田も東京出身だが、林もまた東京出身だ。
examples.english: Yamada is from Tokyo, and Hayashi, too, is from Tokyo.

examples.japanese: 机に座ってものを考えるのもいいが、歩きながら考えるのもまたいい。
examples.english: Thinking while sitting at a desk is ﬁne, but thinking while walking is also good.

examples.japanese: この日本語の教科書は内容も面白く、また文法の記述が正確だ。
examples.english: This Japanese textbook is interesting, and the grammar explanations are also accurate.

examples.japanese: 発表は英語でしてもよい。また、日本語でしてもよい。
examples.english: You may present your paper in English. Or, you may do so in Japanese.

examples.japanese: 発表は英語でしてよいし、また、日本語でしてもよい。
examples.english: You may present your paper in English or you may do so in Japanese.

examples.japanese: 今日もまた雪が降った。
examples.english: It snowed again today.

examples.japanese: また風邪をひいちゃった。
examples.english: I caught a cold again!

meaning_en: Rarely; seldom; hardly; almost never
formation:
滅多に～ | Vnegative ない | | 
 | 滅多に外国に行かない | Someone seldom goes abroad | 
 | 滅多に肉を食べない | Someone seldom eats meat |
explanation: 滅多に～ない A structure that indicates extremely low frequency.

examples.japanese: この辺りでは地震は滅多に起きない。
examples.english: Earthquakes seldom occur in this area.

examples.japanese: 日本の父親は忙しいので、週末でも滅多にうちにいない。
examples.english: Japanese fathers are so busy that even on weekends they are seldom at home.

examples.japanese: 大学時代の同級生とは滅多に合えない。
examples.english: I can hardly ever see my college classmates.

examples.japanese: 日本の車は滅多に故障しないので、外海で人気がある。
examples.english: Because Japanese cars rarely break down, they are popular abroad.

examples.japanese: 汚染のためにこの川では滅多に魚が泳いでいるのを見られなくなった。
examples.english: Due to pollution, we almost never see fish swimming in this river now.

meaning_en: Visibly; obviously; really look; can be easily recognised as; can tell just by looking at ~
formation:
(i) 見るからに | Adjective(い/な) stemそうだ | | 
 | 見るからに面白そうだ | Something is obviously interesting | 
 | 見るからに元気そうだ | Someone is obviously healthy | 
(ii) 見るからに | ～ | | 
 | 見るからに日本人だ | Someone is obviously Japanese | 
 | 見るからに失望している | Someone is obviously disappointed |
explanation: A phrase indicating that something can be (obviously) recognized through visual cues.

examples.japanese: 太陽の光をたっぷり浴びたみかんは、見るからにおいしそうだ。
examples.english: The sun-bathed mandarin oranges look really delicious.

examples.japanese: 彼女が身につけているものは見るからに高級品だった。
examples.english: What she wears is obviously of high quality.

examples.japanese: このパンは見るからに手作りという感じですね。
examples.english: This bread is obviously homemade.

examples.japanese: その青年は見るからに聡明そうだった。
examples.english: You could tell just by looking that the young man was intelligent.

examples.japanese: 老人が見るからに重そうな買い物袋を抱えて歩いている。
examples.english: The old man is walking with a shopping bag that is obviously heavy.

examples.japanese: その写真には見るからに寂しそうな孤児たちが写っていた。
examples.english: In that picture the orphans were obviously lonely.

examples.japanese: 半身・淡路大震災の時は見るからに新聞記者らしい人たちが大勢写真を撮っていた。
examples.english: At the time of the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake, a lot of people who could easily be recognized as news reporters were taking pictures.

examples.japanese: 彼の顔は青黒くむくみ、見るからに健康を害していた。
examples.english: His face was pale, dark and swollen. You could tell just by looking at him that he was in poor health.

meaning_en: Shouldn’t; not possibly; naturally cannot; cannot bear
formation:
(i) Vinformal nonpast | ものではない | | 
 | 食べるものではない | One shouldn’t eat something | 
(ii) Vpotential informal past | ものではない | | 
 | 食べられたものではない | One could not possibly eat something | 
(iii) Vpotential informal nonpast | ものではない | | 
 | 食べられるものではない | One naturally cannot eat something |
explanation: A sentence-ﬁnal phrase indicating that one shouldn’t do something, one could not possibly do something, or one naturally cannot do something.

examples.japanese: 夜遅く人に電話をかけるものではない。
examples.english: You shouldn't call people late at night.

examples.japanese: 彼の演奏は聴けたものではない。
examples.english: We cannot bear listening to his performance (literally: His performance isn't something we could possibly listen to).

examples.japanese: そんな時間のかかる仕事は引き受けられるものではない。
examples.english: That kind of time-consuming work isn't something I can accept.

examples.japanese: 日本では先生と話す時に帽子をかぶったまま話すものではない。
examples.english: In Japan, one shouldn't wear a hat while speaking to one's teacher.

examples.japanese: 日本では人のうちに訪ねて行く時には手ぶらで行くものではありません。
examples.english: In Japan, you shouldn't visit someone's house without bringing something with you.

examples.japanese: 未成年者は酒を飲むもんじゃない。
examples.english: Minors shouldn't drink.

examples.japanese: 女性に年齢を聞くものではない。
examples.english: You shouldn't ask a woman her age.

examples.japanese: こんなつまらない小説、読めたもんじゃない。
examples.english: I could not possibly read such a boring novel!

meaning_en: Definitely not; absolutely not; impossible
formation:
(i) {V/Adjectiveい}informal nonpast | ものか | | 
 | 行くものか | Someone definitely won’t go there | 
 | 珍しいものか | Something definitely isn’t rare | 
(ii) {Adjectiveな stem/Noun} | なものか | | 
 | 便利なものか | Something is definitely not convenient | 
 | 病気なものか | Someone is absolutely not ill |
explanation: ものか (2) A phrase indicating that the speaker wants to do something or is wondering what one he/she should choose.

examples.japanese: あんなやつとは二度と会うものか。
examples.english: I will never see that sort of guy again.

examples.japanese: A:彼は5年後には自分でコンピュータの会社をつくるって言っているよ。 B:そんなこと彼にできるもんか。
examples.english: A: He says he will establish a computer company by himself in five years. B: I bet he can't. (literally: Can he do it?)

examples.japanese: あんなケチな男とはもうつき合うものか。
examples.english: Who really wants to spend more time with such a stingy fellow?

examples.japanese: A:鈴木、TOEFLが650点だったってよ。B:まさか！そんなことがあるもんか。
examples.english: A: I heard that Suzuki got 650 points on the TOEFL. B: Unbelievable! That can't be true.

examples.japanese: 世話をしてもお礼の一言も言わないの。あんな人、もう世話をするもんですか。
examples.english: She didn't even thank me when I helped her out. Who really wants to help someone like that again?

examples.japanese: A:池田先生、親切な先生？B:親切なもんか。
examples.english: A: Is Professor Ikeda a kind teacher? B: Definitely not kind.

examples.japanese: A:そのパズル、やさしいんだろう。B:やさしいもんか。
examples.english: A: Isn't that puzzle easy? B: absolutely not.

examples.japanese: A:あいつは自分のことをいっぱしの政治家だと思っているようだな。B:あいつは政治家なもんか。政治屋しゃないか。
examples.english: A: He seems to think that he is a full-ﬂedged politician. B: He is absolutely not a politician. He's just being political.

examples.japanese: もう少し広い家に住めないもの（だろう）か。
examples.english: (i) I wish to live in a house that is a bit more spacious. (ii) I wonder if I can live in a slightly more spacious house.

examples.japanese: 修士論文の題目をどのように決めたものか（と）迷っています。
examples.english: I am at a loss as to how I should choose my MA thesis topic.

meaning_en: or
formation:
(i) Noun1(か)、 | もしくはNoun2 | | 
 | 電子メール(か)、もしくはファックス | Email or fax | 
 | 研究(か)、もしくは教育 | Research or education | 
(ii) V1 informal nonpastか、 | もしくはV2 | | 
 | 権利を売るか、もしくは譲渡する | Sell one’s right or transfer it to someone |
explanation: A conjunction to disjunctively connect two items or ideas.

examples.japanese: この申込書は本人（か）、もしくは保証人が記入しなければならない。
examples.english: This application has to be filled in by the applicant or by his/her guarantor.

examples.japanese: ワークショップに出席なさりたい方はオンラインで登録するか、もしくは、メールでお申し込みください。
examples.english: If you want to participate in the workshop, please register online or apply by e-mail.

examples.japanese: 基調講演者は日本研究もしくは関連領域の研究について話すことになっている。
examples.english: The keynote speaker is expected to talk about Japan studies or related areas.

examples.japanese: この予算は研究費、もしくは研究補助費にのみ使用できる。
examples.english: This budget is to be used exclusively for research or research-related expenses.

examples.japanese: 大学のプールは学生か、もしくは使用料を支払った大学関係者のみ利用できる。
examples.english: The college pool is open only to students or those afﬁliated with the college who have paid the fee.

examples.japanese: 夏季のドライブシーズンを迎える頃には、ガソリンの在庫が昨年とほぼ同水準まで下がるか、もしくはそれ以下に減少する見通しである。
examples.english: It is predicted that by the time of the summer driving season, the reserves of gasoline will fall approximately to the same level as last year or will go below it.

examples.japanese: 日本の経済力が弱まってきている現在、日本が世界で生き残る道はテクノロジーで時代の先取りをするか、もしくは、モノとしての日本の文化をより積極的に海外に輸出することであろう。
examples.english: These days Japan's economic strength has decreased. For Japan to survive in the world, it must either take leadership in the ﬁeld of technology in the future, or export Japanese culture as a product more aggressively.

meaning_en: Although; though; but; yet; however
formation:
Sentence1。 | もっともSentence2({が/けれども})。 | | 
 | 息子はよく病気をする。もっとも大病をしたことはない({が/けれども})。 | Our son often gets sick, although he has never fallen seriously ill. |
explanation: A conjunction used to add a comment indicating that what the speaker/writer has just expressed is not sufﬁcient.

examples.japanese: 運動は体にいいと言われている。もっとも、やりすぎると逆効果だ（が）。
examples.english: They say that exercise is good for you (literally: your body), but doing too much will bring about the opposite effect.

examples.japanese: あの政治家は保守的だと言われている。もっとも、時々革新的なことを言うこともあるが。
examples.english: That politician is said to be conservative, although he sometimes makes innovative statements.

examples.japanese: 彼は女性にとても親切だ。もっとも、それには下心がある場合が多いようだ。
examples.english: He is very kind to ladies. But, apparently, he often has an ulterior motive.

examples.japanese: 今日は魚がよく釣れた。もっとも、いつもこのように幸運だとは限らない。
examples.english: I caught (literally: was able to catch) a lot of ﬁsh today, although I'm not always this lucky.

examples.japanese: このドイツの車の方があの日本の車よりいいんじゃない。もっとも、僕はドイツの車を運転したことはないけどさ。
examples.english: Don't you think that this German car is better than that Japanese one? I've never driven a German car, though.

examples.japanese: 顔写真の入った名刺というのも、強い印象を与えるからいいかもしれない。もっとも私はそこまでやりたいとは思わないけれども。
examples.english: It may be a good idea to make business cards with your picture on them because they would create a stronger impression. But I am kind of reluctant to go that far.

examples.japanese: 若い頃は漠然としていたものが歳を重ねるごとにハッキリと見えるようになり、目標を見据えてよりポジティブに生きるようにしています。もっとも私はまだ、その途上にありますが。
examples.english: As I grow older, I begin to see more clearly things that were not clear when I was younger. I'm trying to keep the goal in focus and live more positively. But I haven't gotten there yet.

meaning_en: Rather; instead
formation:
(i) V1informal nonpastより({は/も}) | むしろV2informal nonpast (方が～) | | 
 | 外に行くより(は) むしろ家でテレビを見る方がいい。 | I would rather watch TV at home than go outside | 
(ii) Noun1より({は/も}) | むしろNoun2(の方)が～ | | 
 | コーヒーより(は) むしろ紅茶(の方)が好きだ。 | I like black tea rather than coffee | 
(iii) {V/Adjectiveい}informal | というより({は/も}) むしろ～ | | 
 | {食べる/食べた}というより(は) むしろ{飲み込む/飲み込んだ}。 | He swallows/swallowed rather than eats/ate | 
 | {涼しい/涼しかった}というより(は) むしろ{寒い/寒かった}。 | It is/was cold rather than cool | 
(iv) {Adjectiveなstem/Noun} | {∅/だ/である/だった/であった}というより({は/も}) むしろ～ | | 
 | 丁寧{∅/だ/である/だった/であった}というより(は) むしろばか丁寧{だ/だった}。 | Something is/was overly polite rather than polite | 
 | 先生{∅/だ/である/だった/であった}というより(は) むしろビジネスマン{だ/だった}。 | Someone is/was a businessman rather than a teacher | 
(v) V1informal nonpast{ぐらい/くらい/の/ん} | {なら/だったら}むしろ～ | | 
 | 仕事を辞める{ぐらい/くらい/の/ん}{なら/だったら}むしろ死んでしまいたい | I would rather die than quit my job |
explanation: An adverb that indicates one of two things/people/characteristics has been chosen rather than the other to express speaker’s/writer’s desire, preference or judgment.

examples.japanese: 夏休みはアルバイトをするよりもむしろ海外旅行がしたい。
examples.english: During summer vacation I would rather travel abroad than work part-time.

examples.japanese: 僕は寿司よりむしろ刺身(の方）が好きだ。
examples.english: I prefer sashimi rather than sushi.

examples.japanese: 彼は秀才というよりはむしろ努力家だ。
examples.english: He is a man of effort rather than a man of great talent.

examples.japanese: 無為の生活をするぐらいなら、むしろ死んだ方がいい。
examples.english: I would rather die than lead a good-for-nothing life.

examples.japanese: 英語は話すよりむしろ読むのが好きだ。
examples.english: I like reading English rather than speaking it.

examples.japanese: 時間がある時は、観光バスに来るよりはむしろ歩いた方がずっとよく観光できる。
examples.english: When you have the time, you can sightsee much better if you walk rather than ride a sightseeing bus.

examples.japanese: 休みの日は、人の多い行楽地に行くよりは、むしろ、家でテレビでも見ている方がましだ。
examples.english: On a holiday it is better to watch TV or something at home rather than go to a crowded tourist spot.

examples.japanese: 静脈を見つけ、正確に注射するという作業は、人間の手よりもむしろコンピュータを使ってロボットが行った方が、ミスが少ないと思う。
examples.english: I think that the action of ﬁnding a vein and injecting it accurately can be done with less failures if we use a computer and a robot rather than human hands.

meaning_en: Seem to ~; somewhat; rather; may
formation:
Vnegative | ないでもない | | 
 | 思わないでもない | Someone kind of thinks that ~ | 
 | 食べないでもない | Someone may eat something | 
 | しないでもない | Someone may do something |
explanation: A phrase that indicates the speaker/writer hesitantly feels or expresses that something is the case.

examples.japanese: 今が私の人生で一番幸せな時期だという気がしないでもない。
examples.english: I seem to feel that right now is the happiest time of my life.

examples.japanese: あの時大学を辞めたことを、今では少し早まったなと思わないでもない。
examples.english: Now I rather feel that leaving the university at that time was a bit too hasty.

examples.japanese: そういえば、そういう話、どこかで聞いたことがあるような気がしないでもないです。
examples.english: Come to think of it, I seem to feel that I've heard something like that somewhere.

examples.japanese: 私は「結婚しない主義」でもないし、一度結婚してみたいという気もないでもないんですが、なかなかいい相手が見つかりません。
examples.english: I am unmarried not because of principle, and I wouldn't mind getting married, but it is really hard to ﬁnd a good partner.

examples.japanese: 日本人として、アメリカ企業におけるリストラを見ると非情さを感じないでもない。
examples.english: For me, as a Japanese, the way American companies lay off workers strikes me as rather inhumane.

examples.japanese: あなたの苦しい気持ちが分からないでもない。
examples.english: I do somewhat understand the pain you are feeling.

examples.japanese: 白衣に眼鏡なら、一見普通の医者に見えないでもない。
examples.english: Wearing a white gown and eyeglasses, he could be taken for a doctor at first sight.

examples.japanese: 心底謝れば許してやらないでもないけど。
examples.english: If he really apologizes to me from the bottom of his heart, then I may ﬁnd it in me to forgive him (, but . . .).

meaning_en: From ~ to ~; between ~ and ~; or
formation:
(i) Number1(+Counter) | ないし(は)Number2(+Counter) | | 
 | ３０マイルないし(は)４０マイル | From 30 to 40 miles | 
(ii) Noun1(か) | ないしはNoun2 | | 
 | 英語(か) ないしはドイツ語で | In English or German | 
(iii) S1informal(か)、 | ないしはSentence2。 | | 
 | 日本語集中講座を受ける(か)、ないしは日本へ短期留学をする。 | Someone will take an intensive Japanese course or go to Japan for short-term study |
explanation: ないし（は） A particle that presents two possible choices or the minimum and maximum possible numbers/lengths/weights/etc. of something; or a conjunction that links two possible actions or events.

examples.japanese: このクラスの学生のほとんどは3年ないし（は）4年の日本語学習歴を持っている。
examples.english: Most students in this class have three to four years of experience studying Japanese.

examples.japanese: この論文集の論文はすべて日本語（か）ないしは英語で書かれている。
examples.english: The papers in this collection are written in Japanese or English.

examples.japanese: 生産量を20%減らす（か）、ないしは新しい市場を急遽開拓するしかない。
examples.english: We have no choice but to either reduce production by 20 percent or quickly develop a new market.

examples.japanese: 細菌の大きさは1ミクロンないし数ミクロンだ。
examples.english: Bacteria are between one and several microns large.

examples.japanese: 電子メールは、忙しい人でも、1日に1回ないしは数回チェックしているはずだ。
examples.english: I expect that even busy people check their e-mail once or even several times a day.

examples.japanese: サン・モリッツでは５つ星ないしは３つ星クラスのホテルに滞在し、4日間、スイスの冬を満喫していただきます。
examples.english: In St. Moritz, you will stay at a three to ﬁve star hotel (literally: a ﬁve to three star hotel), and fully enjoy a Swiss winter for four days.

examples.japanese: 本冊子の購入希望者は、氏名、住所、購入希望冊数を明記の上、ファックス、ないしは電子メールで協会事務局までお申し込み下さい。
examples.english: If you would like a copy of this booklet, please send a request to the association's ofﬁce via fax or e-mail with your name, address and the number of copies you want.

examples.japanese: 本アンケートでは、2004年鉛全廃について、「必要」ないしは「やむを得ない」とするものが74%を占めた。
examples.english: In this survey, regarding the total ban on (the use of) lead in 2004, 74 percent (of respondents) indicated it would be either "necessary" or "inevitable."

meaning_en: In the midst of; when; while; through; among
formation:
(i) Vinformal nonpast | 中を | | 
 | 雨が{降る/降っている}中を | When it is raining | 
(ii) Adjectiveいinformal nonpast | 中を | | 
 | 忙しい中を | When someone is busy | 
(iii) Adjectiveなstemな | | | 
 | 危険な中を | In the midst of danger | 
(iv) Nounの | 中を | | 
 | 嵐の中を | In the midst of a storm |
explanation: A phrase that specifies space or time in/through which someone/something does something.

examples.japanese: 冷たい風が｛吹く/吹いている｝中を１０キロも歩いた。
examples.english: When a cold wind was blowing I walked as much as 10 kilometres.

examples.japanese: お忙しい中をいらしていただき、申し訳ございません。
examples.english: Thank you very much (literally: I'm sorry) for coming when you are (so) busy.

examples.japanese: 赤十字の人たちがハリケーン被災者たちの中を歩き回って食料を配った。
examples.english: People from the Red Cross walked among the victims of the hurricane and distributed food.

examples.japanese: 子供たちが遊んでいる中を子犬がちょろちょろ走り回っていた。
examples.english: A puppy was darting around among the kids who were playing.

examples.japanese: 公園では、人が集まっている中を、アイスクリーム屋が歩いていた。
examples.english: In the park, an ice cream seller was walking through the crowd of people.

examples.japanese: 雪の降る中を頑張って走っている人を見ていたら、自分が軟弱に思えてきました。
examples.english: When I watched people out running in the snow, I began to think of myself as fragile and weak.

examples.japanese: 私たちが呆然として見ている中を、二人は一つの傘の下に入って行ってしまいました。
examples.english: As we were watching with astonishment, the two walked away under the same umbrella.

examples.japanese: 本日は、雨で足元が大変悪い中を、このようにたくさんの方にご参加いただきまして、誠にありがとうございました。
examples.english: Thank you very much for coming to this meeting today; it's nice to see so many of you when it is so treacherous to walk due to the rain.

meaning_en: Without; if it were not for ~
formation:
Noun | なくして(は) | | 
 | 協力なくして(は) | Without cooperation |
explanation: なくして（は）A compound particle meaning "without something".

examples.japanese: 努力なくして（は）この事業はできない。
examples.english: Without effort we won't be able to ﬁnish this undertaking.

examples.japanese: 山川教授なくしては今の私は存在しなかったであろう。
examples.english: Without Professor Yamakawa, I wouldn't be what I am now.

examples.japanese: コンピュータなくして現在の生活は不可能だ。
examples.english: Without computers, our current lifestyle would be impossible.

examples.japanese: ITの活用なくして企業の成長は望めません。
examples.english: If we don't make good use of IT, we can't expect our business to grow.

examples.japanese: 日本の平和と繁栄は、世界の平和と安定なくしてはあり得ない。
examples.english: Peace and prosperity in Japan is not possible without peace and stability throughout the world.

examples.japanese: あらゆる生物は水なくして生きていけない。
examples.english: No creature can live without water.

examples.japanese: コミュニケーションなくしては、人間が関与する一切の活動は成立し得ない。
examples.english: Without communication, no human activity could occur.

examples.japanese: 関係者の密接な共同作業なくしてはこの計画の実現は不可能であったろう。
examples.english: If it had not been for the close cooperation of the people involved in this project, it would have been impossible to make it a reality.

meaning_en: Halfheartedly; slightly; thoughtlessly; unwisely; inadequately; imperfectly; sort of; a little; somewhat; a bit of
formation:
(i) なまじ(っか) | ～Conjunction | | 
 | なまじ(っか)できるから | Because someone can do something (a little) | 
 | なまじ(っか)安いために | Because something is (somewhat) cheap | 
 | なまじ(っか)美人なだけに | Because she is (sort of) a beauty | 
 | なまじ(っか)元気なので | Because someone is (sort of) healthy | 
 | なまじ(っか)でき{たら /ると} | If someone can do something (a little) | 
 | なまじ(っか){安かったら/安いと} | If something is (somewhat) cheap | 
 | なまじ(っか)美人だ{ったら /と} | If she is (sort of) a beauty | 
 | なまじ(っか)元気だ{ったら /と} | If someone is (basically) healthy | 
(ii) なまじ(っか) | {の/な}Noun | | 
 | なまじ(っか){の/な}努力 | Halfthearted efforts | 
 | なまじ(っか){の/な}勉強 | Halfhearted study | 
(iii) なまじ(っか) | ～Vinformal nonpastのは～ | | 
 | なまじ(っか)投資をするのは危ない。 | It’s dangerous to invest halfheartedly |
explanation: なまじ（っか）An adverb indicating that something (including an action/state) has a positive value which hasn’t been reached, causing something negative.

examples.japanese: 僕はなまじ（っか）英語ができるばかりに、会社で重宝がられて困っています。
examples.english: Because I know a little English, the office treasures me, which is causing me problems.

examples.japanese: なまじ（っか）｛の/な｝学問は、ひけらかすと人に軽蔑される。
examples.english: People disdain those who show off (their scant knowledge) but are uneducated (literally: have inadequate scholarship).

examples.japanese: なまじ（っか）政治に手を出すのはやめた方がよい。
examples.english: You'd better not get involved in politics half-heartedly.

examples.japanese: なまじっか手伝ってもらうより、一人でやった方が早くできそうです。
examples.english: I think it'll be quicker to do it by myself than for someone to help me in a half-hearted way.

examples.japanese: 彼はなまじっか自信があるために、失敗した時にひどい挫折感を味わう。
examples.english: Because he has only a little self-conﬁdence, he experiences a horrible sense of failure when something doesn't work out.

examples.japanese: なまじっか財産など持っていたら、最低の人間になってしまうのではないかと思う。
examples.english: I think that we turn into the worst people with just a bit of wealth.

examples.japanese: なまじ見る目が肥えてくると、アニメだったら何でもいいってわけにはいかなくなる。
examples.english: When you acquire a bit of an eye for anime, you discover that not every work lives up to what it's supposed to be.

examples.japanese: なまじっか物を知ってる人よりは全然知らない人の方が、「知らないことを知る楽しみ」を感じられると思う。
examples.english: I think that a person who knows nothing can feel "the joy of discovery (literally: of knowing what he doesn't know)" more than someone who knows a little bit.
