meaning_en: About the same level as; like; as (much ~) as; to match; to rival; on a par with; equivalent to
formation:
(i) Noun | 並みだ | | 
 | 真冬並みだ | Something is about the same as that in mid-winter | 
(ii) Noun1 | 並みのNoun2 | | 
 | 大人並みの力 | Power as strong as an adult’s | 
(iii) Noun | 並みに | | 
 | 人並みに | Like ordinary people |
explanation: A noun sufﬁx that adds the meaning "to match".

examples.japanese: マイクさんのゴルフはプロ並みだ。
examples.english: Mike's golf skills are about the same level as a pro's.

examples.japanese: 吉田さんは植物については専門家並みの知識を持っている。
examples.english: Regarding plants, Ms. Yoshida has as much knowledge as a specialist.

examples.japanese: 日本人も欧米人並みに肉や乳製品を食べるようになった。
examples.english: Japanese people now eat (literally: have come to eat) as much meat and dairy products as Westerners (literally: Europeans and Americans) do.

examples.japanese: 今月の降水量は平年並みだそうだ。
examples.english: It is said that this month's precipitation is about the same as (that of the same month) in an average year.

examples.japanese: 当社に登録されている通訳の英語力はネイティブ並みです。
examples.english: The interpreters registered with our company have a native level of English proﬁciency.

examples.japanese: 今日はまだ5月だというのに8月並みの暑さだ。
examples.english: Although it is still May today, it is as hot as August.

examples.japanese: ダイエット用品、スポーツ器具、美容雑貨など、アメリカのヒット商品を現地並みの価格でお届けします。
examples.english: We deliver top-selling (literally: hit) products from America, including diet products, athletic equipment and beauty goods, at U.S. prices.

examples.japanese: 今日はリハーサルだったが本番並みの緊張感を味わった。
examples.english: Although today's (performance) was a rehearsal, I felt the same level of tension as if it were the real performance.

meaning_en: Some; some kind of
formation:
何らかの | Noun | | 
 | 何らかの事情 | Some circumstance | 
 | 何らかの形 | Some form |
explanation: A phrase used to indicate that the exact nature of something represented by the noun cannot be speciﬁed.

examples.japanese: 何らかの原因で走行中で電車が急停車した。
examples.english: Due to some (unknown) cause the train stopped suddenly.

examples.japanese: 私たちが患う病気は、たいてい、何らかの意味でゲノム関係があります。
examples.english: Most of the illnesses that we get are linked in some way with genomes.

examples.japanese: 世界の総人口のおよそ半数の人々が、何らかの形で米を食べている。
examples.english: Approximately half the total population of the world eats rice in some form.

examples.japanese: 何らかの理由で会議に参加できなくなった場合は、学会事務局へご連絡下さるようお願い申し上げます。
examples.english: If it turns out that you are unable to attend the conference for some reason, we would appreciate it if you would kindly contact the conference ofﬁce.

examples.japanese: 食品添加物が我々の身体に何らかの悪影響を与えると考える人は多い。
examples.english: Many people think that food additives have some bad effect on our bodies.

examples.japanese: 火星表面の「運河」と呼ばれる溝は、何らかの液体によって作られたと考えられていた。
examples.english: The grooves on Mars' surface that are referred to as ""canals"" were (originally) presumed to have been caused by some liquid.

examples.japanese: 我々はそれぞれ何らかの人生観、社会観を持って生きています。各人の生涯の生活設計に関しても、漠然とした形ではあっても、何らかのデザインをしていると思います。
examples.english: Each of us is living with a certain outlook on life and society. And no matter how vague it may be, I believe each person is designing a life plan in his/her own way.

meaning_en: What; how ~!; what a(n) ~!; so
formation:
(i) なんて | V | Where V=verb of communiation | 
 | なんて言う | What does someone say? | 
 | なんて書く | What does someone write? | 
(ii) なんていう | Noun | | 
 | なんていう人ですか。 | What is his/her name? | 
 | なんていう建物ですか。 | What is the name of the building? | 
(iii) なんて | {Adjectiveいinformal/ Adjectiveなstemな/Nounな}んだろう | | 
 | なんて難しいんだろう。 | How difficult something is! | 
 | (彼女) なんてきれいなんだろう。 | How pretty (she) is! | 
 | なんていい天気なんだろう。 | What a beautiful day! |
explanation: なんて (2) A colloquial particle used to express a strong feeling such as astonishment, incredulousness, envy, disdain, dislike, happiness, etc.

examples.japanese: レポートのこと、社長はなんて言っていましたか。
examples.english: What did the president say about the report?

examples.japanese: きのう見た映画、なんていう映画だったっけ？
examples.english: What was the title of the movie we saw yesterday?

examples.japanese: これぐらいの宿題、なんて（いう）ことはないよ。
examples.english: This much homework is nothing / not a big deal!

examples.japanese: 日本のアニメはなんて面白いんだろう。
examples.english: How interesting Japanese anime is!

examples.japanese: うちにホームステイしている留学生がテレビを観ていると「今なんて言った？」「英語だとなんて言うの？」と質問の連続だ。
examples.english: When the foreign student staying with us watches TV, he keeps asking questions like ""What did he say?"" or ""What is that in English?

examples.japanese: 推薦状を書くのを頼まれると、時々なんて書いたらいいのか分からないことがある。
examples.english: Sometimes I don't know what to say (literally: write) when I get asked to write a letter of recommendation.

examples.japanese: なんていう人か名前を忘れたけれど、なかなか魅力的な女性に出会った。
examples.english: I met a very charming lady, although I've forgotten her name.

examples.japanese: 彼はつらい目にたくさん遭っているのに、「なんていうことはない」という感じでひょうひょうと生きている。
examples.english: He's had a rough time, but he lets it all roll off his back as if it were nothing to him.

examples.japanese: 小学校からのいじめが中学まで続くなんてひどい。
examples.english: It's terrible that bullying continues after grade school into junior high.

examples.japanese: 最近は電子メールばかり使っていて、手紙なんて滅多に書かない。
examples.english: Lately I've been using only e-mail, and seldom write (a thing like) a letter.

meaning_en: Somehow; in some way; in one way or another; manage to
explanation: An adverb expressing that someone somehow does something, or something somehow occurs.

examples.japanese: 我々は今の日本の政治状況を何とか変えようと努力しています。
examples.english: We are making an effort to change the current Japanese political situation somehow.

examples.japanese: 一見無理なことも、やってみれば何とか形になる。
examples.english: Something which appears to be impossible to do can take shape in one way or another, if you try.

examples.japanese: この夏は友達と一緒に何とか富士山に登ってきました。
examples.english: This past summer I managed to climb Mt. Fuji with my friend.

examples.japanese: 夜型の生活を何とかしたいと思いながら、今でもそれを続けている。
examples.english: Although I keep thinking I want to do something about my night owl lifestyle, (literally: even now) I still stay up late.

examples.japanese: ボスにせかされているから、この書類を何とか明日までに仕上げなければならないんだ。
examples.english: My boss keeps pressing me, so somehow I have to complete this document by tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 患者：おでこから血が出ることがあるんです。医者：おでこから血が？うーん。そんな症例は聞いたことがないなあ…。患者：ほんとなんです。お願いします、先生。何とかして下さい。
examples.english: Patient: Sometimes my forehead bleeds. Doctor: Your forehead bleeds? I haven't heard of a case like that before. Patient: It's true. Doctor, please do something about it.

examples.japanese: 母親：あら、有香、もう勉強は終わったの。娘：勉強なんかやってらんないわよ。母親：まったくしょうがない子ねえ。お父さん、何とか言って下さいよ。
examples.english: Mother: Oh, Yuka, you've already ﬁnished studying? Daughter: I hate studying! Mother: You're impossible! Dear, say something to her.

examples.japanese: 何とかホームページができたのでみんなに見せたい。
examples.english: Somehow I managed to make my home page, so now I want to show it to everybody.

meaning_en: Still; even more; all the more for ~; additional; and; additionally; furthermore
formation:
(i) なお | Vている | | 
 | 噴火はなお続いている | The eruption is still going on | 
(ii) なお | Adjective (い/な) | | 
 | なおいい | Even better | 
 | なお立派だ | Even more magnificent | 
(iii) なお | {Adjectiveいstemく /Adjectiveなstemに}(なる) | | 
 | なお大きく(なる) | (become) even larger | 
 | なおきれいに(なる) | (become) even prettier | 
(iv) なお | Number+Counter | | 
 | なお十年 | Another 10 years | 
(v) Sentence1。 | なおSentence2。 | | 
 | 会は毎週月曜日です。なお詳しい情報は会のサイトをご覧下さい。 | The meeting is every Monday. And for detailed information, please look at the meeting’s site |
explanation: An adverb that indicates that an action or state is still going on or the degree of something increases; a conjunction indicating that an additional comment follows what has just been said in the preceding sentence.

examples.japanese: 宮崎駿のアニメは、20年、30年たっても、なお古典アニメとして残っているだろう。
examples.english: Anime by Hayao Miyazaki will still remain even in 20 or 30 years as anime classics.

examples.japanese: この小説はパリを知っている人が読めばなお面白いだろう。
examples.english: This novel must be all the more interesting if you know Paris.

examples.japanese: 日本へ行く前から日本が好きだったが、日本へ行ったらなお好きになった。
examples.english: I liked Japan before I went there, but after going there I became even more fond of it.

examples.japanese: 来週の金曜日午後6時から拙宅で夕食会をしますので、お知らせいたします。なお、ご都合のつかない方はお電話下さい。
examples.english: Let me inform you that there will be a dinner at my residence starting at 6:00 p.m. next Friday. Please call us if you can't come.

examples.japanese: 欧米やアジアでは景気は拡大し、総じて良好な状態がなお続いている。
examples.english: In Europe, the United States and Asia the economy has expanded and, generally speaking, favourable conditions continue to prevail.

examples.japanese: テレビで「3億円強奪事件」というドラマを見たが、面白かった。実話をもとにしているから、なお面白い。
examples.english: I saw a drama called ""The ¥300,000,000 Robbery"" and found it interesting. It was even more so because it is based on a true story.

examples.japanese: 考えていることを書くのは勉強になる。その文章を先生が読んで感想を書いてくれるから、なお勉強になる。
examples.english: It is instructive to write down what we think, and still more instructive when our teacher reads our essays and gives comments on them.

examples.japanese: 日本語で話すことは難しいが、書くことはなお難しい。
examples.english: It is difﬁcult to speak in Japanese, but it is even harder to write it.

meaning_en: Still more; much more; all the more; even more
explanation: An adverb indicating that the degree of something increases due to an additional circumstance.

examples.japanese: 前からタイに行きたいと思っていたが、すでに行ったことのある友人が強く勧めたので、なおさら行きたくなった。
examples.english: I've wanted to go to Thailand for a long time, and then a friend who has been there strongly recommended it, so I feel like going there even more now.

examples.japanese: 悪人さえも往生するのなら、まして善人はなおさらだ。
examples.english: If even a bad person can go to heaven, then a good person has an even better chance.

examples.japanese: 貧乏を弁解すると、なおさら貧乏くさく聞こえる。
examples.english: If you make excuses for being poor you will seem (literally: sound) still poorer.

examples.japanese: このチーズは搾りたての新鮮な牛乳で作るから、なおさらおいしい。
examples.english: This cheese is made from milk fresh from the cow so it tastes even more delicious.

examples.japanese: 旅で足を踏み入れるだけで、沖縄はいまだに戦争を引きずっていることを感じる。まして、現地の人ではなおさらであろう。
examples.english: When you just go there as a traveller, you get a sense that Okinawa still hasn't gotten over the war. The local people must feel that way even more so.

examples.japanese: 英語を書くのは難しいが、正確さが要求される科学論文を書くのはなおさらだ。
examples.english: It is hard to write in English, but it is still harder to write a scientiﬁc paper that requires accuracy.

examples.japanese: アジア諸国の学者や政府が、この教科書を詳細かつ適確に批判し、発行しないよう強く求めたにもに関わらず検定を通ったということは、なおさら重大です。
examples.english: It is all the more serious that this textbook has passed the inspection even though scholars and governments of Asian countries aptly criticized it in detail and urged the publisher not to print it.

meaning_en: Impossible if it’s not ~; only possible with/by/at/etc.; not possible with/by/at/etc. other ~; very difficult with/by/at/etc. any other ~ but; you can expect only/at/from/etc.; unless
formation:
(i) NP1 | ならではのNP2 | | 
 | この店ならではのサービス | Service you can expect only at this shop | 
(ii) NP | ならではだ | | 
 | 学生ならではだ | Impossible unless someone is a student | 
(iii) NP | ならではVpotential negativeない | | 
 | 彼ならではできない | Only he can do something (literally: something cannot be done by anyone else but him) |
explanation: ならでは（の）A phrase indicating something is "impossible if it’s not X".

examples.japanese: 丸山博士の講演は、一流の科学者ならではの示唆に富む内容だった。
examples.english: Dr. Maruyama's lecture was rich with suggestion, the likes of which could only be heard from a ﬁrst-class scientist (like himself).

examples.japanese: 四季を通じて美しい景色が楽しめるのはこの地ならではだ。
examples.english: Only here can we enjoy beautiful scenery through all four seasons.

examples.japanese: 女性ならではできない仕事や役割もあるはずだ。
examples.english: There also must be jobs and roles that only women can perform (literally: that cannot be done unless you are a woman).

examples.japanese: この大学の法律図書館には、この大学ならではの充実した資料が揃っている。
examples.english: The law library of this university houses a rich collection of documents, the likes of which do not exist at other institutions.

examples.japanese: プロショップならではの品揃え。人気商品を特別価格でお求めいただけます。
examples.english: We have a range of products that would only be available at a shop for pros. Popular items are available at special prices.

examples.japanese: このマンションは都心の住居ならではの便利さと快適さをお約束します。
examples.english: These condominiums promise the kind of convenience and comfort you can enjoy only in dwellings at the heart of the city.

examples.japanese: 興味がわいたら、その分野を徹底して勉強してみる時間があるというのは学生ならではだ。
examples.english: It is only because they are students (literally: It is not possible unless they are students) that they have the time to thoroughly pursue ﬁelds they ﬁnd they have an interest in.

examples.japanese: 近郊にはゴルフコースが数多く、仕事帰りにハーフを回れるのは、緯度が高く日没の遅いカナダならではだ。
examples.english: There are many golf courses near Canadian cities, and, uniquely in Canada, where the sun sets late because of the high latitude, people play a half round on their way home from work.

meaning_en: And; both ~ and ~; as well as
formation:
Noun1 | 並びにNoun2 | | 
 | 学長並びに副学長 | The university president and the vice president |
explanation: A conjunction used to combine two nouns or noun phrases.

examples.japanese: 国連総会には首相並びに外務大臣が出席した。
examples.english: The prime minister and the foreign minister attended the U.N. General Assembly.

examples.japanese: 県並びに県内各市町村では、地域イントラネット構築して、行政や福祉情報の円滑な提供に努めている。
examples.english: The prefecture and its municipalities have constructed local intranets, and are working to provide administrative and welfare information smoothly to their residents.

examples.japanese: 以下は犬及びねこの引き取り並びに負傷動物の収容に関する措置要領である。
examples.english: What follows is an outline of procedures for caring for dogs and cats, and admitting injured animals.

examples.japanese: その政党は、夫婦間における暴力の防止並びに被害者の保護に関する法律案を発表した。
examples.english: The political party announced laws for the prevention of spousal violence as well as the protection of the victims.

examples.japanese: 今日は、大気や河川の汚染並びに酸性雨が環境に及ぼす影響についてお話しいたします。
examples.english: Today I am going to talk about the contamination of our air and rivers as well as acid rain's effect on them.

examples.japanese: このホームページ並びにメールマガジンのスタッフをご紹介します。
examples.english: Let me introduce you to the staff of our website and mail magazine.

examples.japanese: 本学学長の選挙資格者は、選挙公示の日における学長並びに専任の教授、准教授及び講師とする。
examples.english: Those who are qualiﬁed to be a candidate for president of this college are those who are full-time professors, associate professors and lecturers as well as the president at the time the election is announced.

examples.japanese: 本日ここに、大統領、並びに国務長官ほか、御一行の歓迎の宴を開くことができましたことは、私の最も欣快とするところであります。
examples.english: It is my great pleasure that today we welcome the President, the Secretary of State and other honourable visitors to this reception.

meaning_en: Indeed; it is true ~ (but); really; I see
formation:
(i) Sentence1{が/けれど}、 | なるほどSentence2。 | | 
 | 若い{が/けれど}、なるほど、才能が豊かだ。 | Someone is young, but is richly talented indeed | 
(ii) なるほど、 | Sentence1{が/けれど}、Sentence2。 | | 
 | なるほど、一見くだらない{が/けれど}、研究の価値がある。 | It looks worthless at first sight, but it is worth researching | 
(iii) なるほど | (ね)。 | I see/Indeed/It makes sense |
explanation: An adverb indicating that the speaker/writer afﬁrms the correctness of something he/she has heard/read/observed.

examples.japanese: パリはきれいだと聞いていたが、なるほどその芸術性には舌を巻いた。
examples.english: I had heard that Paris was a beautiful city, and (literally: but) indeed I was astounded by its artistry.

examples.japanese: なるほど、日本の官僚はいろいろと批判されているが、戦後の日本の復興は彼らに負うところが多い。
examples.english: It is true that Japanese bureaucrats are criticized in various ways, but we owe them for much of Japan's post-war recovery.

examples.japanese: A:文化って、宗教のように倫理的な決まりが多いですね。B:なるほどね。
examples.english: A: Culture, like religion, has a lot of ethical rules. / B: I see.

examples.japanese: この大学のことは大学案内で読んではいたが、実際に来てみると、なるほど、学生たちはずばらしい教育を受けているようだ。
examples.english: I had read about this college in a college guide, but by actually coming here myself I can see the students really seem to be getting a great education.

examples.japanese: この辺りでは菜の花畑が4月中旬ごろ特にきれいだと聞いていたが、なるほど見事である。
examples.english: I had heard that the ﬁelds of rape blossoms around here are particularly beautiful around mid-April, and now that I've seen them myself, I have to say that they are indeed impressive.

examples.japanese: 本日、川上弘美『椰子・椰子』を読了。なるほど面白い本だ。
examples.english: Today I finished reading Hiromi Kawakami's ""Yashi, Yashi (Palm, Palm)."" It's indeed an interesting book.

examples.japanese: なるほど、これだけの規模のテロが起きると人々は恐怖に捕われるけれど、自分でコントロールできないことをくよくよ心配しても仕方がないだろう。
examples.english: It's true people are caught by fear when terrorism of this magnitude occurs, but it is no use worrying too much about what you cannot control.

examples.japanese: なるほど日本の文化とドイツの文化は違っている点があるが、実は共通点の方が多いようだ。
examples.english: Indeed there are differences between Japanese culture and German culture, but actually it seems they have more similarities than differences.

meaning_en: Do; perform; make; change; constitute
formation:
(i) Noun1をNoun2と | なす | | 
 | 醜を美となす | Someone changes ugliness to beauty | 
(ii) Nounが | なされる | | 
 | 外国語教育がなされる | Foreign language education is provided | 
(iii) Nounを | なす | | 
 | 善をなす | Someone does good deeds | 
 | 基本をなす | Something constitutes the foundation |
explanation: A verb that means "to cause something to happen"

examples.japanese: 災い（を）転じて福となす。
examples.english: One can turn misfortune into a blessing. [proverb]

examples.japanese: 比喩に関しては現在多くの研究がなされている。
examples.english: A large amount of research is being done on metaphors now.

examples.japanese: 人間というものは、悪をなす存在である。
examples.english: Human beings exist in order to do evil.

examples.japanese: 民主主義はアメリカ合衆国の基盤をなす思想である。
examples.english: Democracy is the founding ideology (literally: the ideology that constitutes the foundation) of the United States of America.

examples.japanese: 顧客創造のためには自社製品の潜在利益を利益となす努力を払わなければならない。
examples.english: We have to make the effort to turn our products' potential proﬁt into (real) proﬁt in order to gain more customers.

examples.japanese: 患者が入院時に病名や病状について理解していない場合は、必要に応じて適切な説明がなされるべきである。
examples.english: If patients do not understand the name of their disease and its symptoms at the time of hospitalization, they should be given an appropriate explanation as needed.

examples.japanese: インターネットに関してこのような質問がなされる可能性は高い。
examples.english: Such questions are likely to be asked regarding the Internet.

examples.japanese: 善をなすのを急げ。悪から心を退けよ。
examples.english: Hurry to do good. Turn your mind away from evil.

meaning_en: I don’t know why; without knowing why; for an unknown reason
explanation: An adverb indicating that the speaker/writer doesn’t know the cause of/reason for something

examples.japanese: このところなぜか体の調子が悪い。
examples.english: I don't know why, but I haven't felt well lately.

examples.japanese: ヨーロッパやアジアには受け入れられなかったSFが、なぜか日本には根づいた。
examples.english: Science ﬁction, which did not catch on in Europe and Asia, took root in Japan for some unknown reason.

examples.japanese: なぜか僕は日本語の難しさにはまってしまった。
examples.english: For some reason, I got hooked by the difﬁculty of Japanese language.

examples.japanese: 最近私が住んでいる町ではなぜか古本屋が増えている。
examples.english: I don't know why, but lately the number of used bookstores (in the town) where I live has grown.

examples.japanese: ログインの手順を教えて下さい。なぜかできなくなってしまったんです。
examples.english: Please teach me how to log in. I don't know why, but I can't do it anymore.

examples.japanese: 自分の文化のリズムには、なぜか体が自然と反応し、踊りたくなる。
examples.english: For some unknown reason, our bodies respond spontaneously to our own cultural rhythms, and we feel like dancing!

meaning_en: The reason is that ~; because
formation:
Sentence。 | なぜなら(ば)～からだ。 | | 
 | 食べない。なぜなら(ば)食欲がないからだ。 | I won’t eat it. The reason is that I don’t have an appetite |
explanation: なぜなら（ば）～からだ A structure used to introduce a reason for the statement in the preceding sentence.

examples.japanese: 彼はみんなに好かれている。なぜなら（ば）、誰にでも親切だからだ。
examples.english: Everybody likes him. The reason is that he is kind to everybody.

examples.japanese: 私は自分が好きです。なぜならば、今を自由に生きているからです。
examples.english: I like myself. The reason is that I am living freely in the moment.

examples.japanese: ゲームにおいて最も重要な要素は、目的です。なぜならば、ゲームは本能ではなく理性で行われるものだからです。
examples.english: The most important element of a game is the objective. This is because games are played not by instinct but by reason.

examples.japanese: 外国語学習者は物事を考える時、自分の母語で考える。なぜならば、目標言語では考えがまとめられないからだ。
examples.english: People who are learning a foreign language think in their mother tongue (literally: when they think). The reason is that they cannot think coherently in the target language.

examples.japanese: 変化を遂げない経営は当然効率が悪くなります。なぜならば顧客も競合他社も常に変化しているからです。
examples.english: Management that doesn't change will become ineffective, as a matter of course. The reason is that both customers and competitors are always changing.

examples.japanese: 近現代の日本が本当に正しい道を歩んできたのかどうかは吟味に値する。なぜならば、その過程で日本が失ったものも多いからである。
examples.english: Whether modern Japan has actually been taking the right path should be examined. The reason is that Japan has lost many things during that process.

meaning_en: The reason is that ~; because
formation:
Sentence。 | なぜなら(ば)～からだ。 | | 
 | 食べない。なぜなら(ば)食欲がないからだ。 | I won’t eat it. The reason is that I don’t have an appetite |
explanation: なぜなら（ば）～からだ A structure used to introduce a reason for the statement in the preceding sentence.

examples.english: Everybody likes him. The reason is that he is kind to everybody.

examples.english: The most important element of a game is the objective. This is because games are played not by instinct but by reason.

examples.english: People who are learning a foreign language think in their mother tongue (literally: when they think). The reason is that they cannot think coherently in the target language.

examples.english: Management that doesn't change will become ineffective, as a matter of course. The reason is that both customers and competitors are always changing.

examples.japanese: 近現代の日本が本当に正しい道を歩んできたのかどうかは吟味に値する。なぜならば、その過程で日本が失ったものも多いからである。
examples.english: Whether modern Japan has actually been taking the right path should be examined. The reason is that Japan has lost many things during that process.

meaning_en: When it comes to ~; as for; for example
formation:
Noun | にいたっては | | 
 | 学生にいたっては | When it comes to students |
explanation: A compound particle that indicates an extreme example.

examples.japanese: 人間の体は60%が水、魚は75%、くらげにいたっては96%が水だ。
examples.english: Human bodies are 60 percent water, while ﬁsh are 75 percent water. As for jellyﬁsh, the ﬁgure is 96 percent.

examples.japanese: 私自身は社会人になってからコンピュータを使い始めたが、新入社員は中学生の頃から、私の子供たちにいたっては、生まれた時から家にコンピュータがある世代だ。
examples.english: I myself started to use a computer after I graduated and got a job, but the new hires got started on computers when they were still junior high school students. As for my children, they belong to the generation for whom a computer is available at home from the time of their birth.

examples.japanese: 一年間に日本中の廃棄物は5、１６０万トン、しかまこれは家庭や飲食店などから出る一般廃棄物で、産業廃棄物にいたってはその8倍近くの4億8百万トンも出ているのです。
examples.english: In a year, 51,600,000 tons of waste is produced across Japan. And, this is just general waste from homes and eating places. When it comes to industrial waste, as much as 408,000,000 tons of waste, or nearly eight times as much as general waste, is produced.

examples.japanese: 少林寺拳法では女性拳士の数が増加傾向にあり、高校や大学の部活動にいたっては、部員の半数近くが女性だ。
examples.english: In the case of Shourinji Kenpou, the number of female practitioners is increasing; in clubs at high schools and colleges, for example, almost half of the members are girls.

examples.japanese: 今私たちの生活には多くの椅子が使われている。ダイニングにいたっては、ダイニングテーブルと椅子は、もはや一般的である。
examples.english: Today we use many chairs in our daily life. As for the dining room, a (set of) dining table and chairs is the standard.

examples.japanese: 日本には、一般紙やスポーツ紙、専門的な業界紙など様々な新聞があるが、雑誌にいたっては、どんな分野のものでもある。
examples.english: In Japan there are various newspapers, such as general papers, sports newspapers, or papers that specialize in certain industries, but as for magazines, they cover all ﬁelds.

examples.japanese: アジア太平洋地域以外にも、旅行者の注目を集めている地域がある。中央アメリカは昨年、旅行者数が23%増、中東も17.5％増となった。スペインも９％増加したし、モロッコにいたっては、２２％も増えた。
examples.english: Areas outside the Asia Paciﬁc region have been drawing the attention of travellers as well. Last year Central America saw a 23 percent increase in travellers; in the Middle East, it was 17.5 percent. Spain saw 9 percent more travellers, and travel (literally: travellers) to Morocco, of all places, grew 22 percent.

meaning_en: Regardless of; independent of; without reference to; without distinguishing; whether X or Y; whether X or not; whatever/whoever/etc.
formation:
(i) Noun | に関わらず | | 
 | 学生数に関わらず | Regardless of the number of students | 
(ii) XかYか | に関わらず | Y contrasts with X or is the negative form of X | 
 | 英語か日本語かに関わらず | Whether something is English or Japanese | 
 | 多いか少ないかに関わらず | Whether there are many or few | 
 | 便利か不便かに関わらず | Whether something is convenient or inconvenient |

meaning_en: Not hard; easy ~
formation:
VN | に難くない | Where VN=Sino-Japanese compound | 
 | {想像/推測/予測}に難くない | It is not hard to imagine/guess/predict |
explanation: にかたくない・に難くない A phrase that indicates that it is not hard to imagine or guess a situation.

examples.japanese: 給料が低いために教師の質が低下した（であろう）ことは想像にかたくない。
examples.english: It is not hard to imagine that the quality of teachers fell because of the low salary.

examples.japanese: 幼い時に両親を失った彼女の生活が｛いかに/どれほど｝悲惨だったかは推測にかたくない。
examples.english: It is easy to guess how miserable her life was after she lost her parents.

examples.japanese: この新宅には相当お金をかけたであろうことは想像にかたくない。
examples.english: It is easy to imagine them spending a lot of money on this new house.

examples.japanese: 日本語教育のめざましい進歩の裏には、日本語教育者・研究者の並々ならぬ努力があったことは、想像にかたくありません。
examples.english: It is not hard to imagine that behind the eye-opening progress Japanese language education has made are the extraordinary efforts of Japanese language educators and researchers.

examples.japanese: 留学生にとって日本の伝統文化を見つけることがいかに難しくなっているかは想像にかたくないことでしょう。
examples.english: It isn't hard to imagine how difﬁcult it has become for foreign students to ﬁnd (examples of) traditional Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: 好きな文芸の道と経営者としての責任の間で、多才な彼が苦悩していたことは想像にかたくない。
examples.english: It isn't hard to imagine that a man of his versatile talents struggled (to choose) between his beloved world of literature and his managerial responsibilities.

examples.japanese: その青年が非常に心優しく生真面目かつ勉学熱心な人間だったことは推測にかたくない。
examples.english: It is easy to imagine that young man as a gentle, serious and diligent person.

examples.japanese: 海外に在住して母国の軍事政権への反対活動を行っている人が帰国すれば、拘禁や拷問にさらされるであろうことは予測にかたくない。
examples.english: It isn't hard to predict that if people who live overseas and actively criticize the military regime of their country go home, most likely they will be put into prison and tortured.

meaning_en: When; if; as
formation:
(i) Noun | {に/と}もなると | | 
 | 五月{に/と}もなると | Literally: when it becomes May; in May | 
(ii) Vinformal nonpast | ともなると | | 
 | 退職するともなると | When someone retires |
explanation: に/ともなると A phrase that is used when something or some situation is perceived to be special.

examples.japanese: 桜の季節｛に/と｝もなるとこの公園は花見客でにぎわう。
examples.english: In the cherry blossom season (literally: When it becomes the cherry blossom season), this park is packed with cherry blossom viewers.

examples.japanese: 外国へ行くともなると、その国の言語や文化を勉強したくなるはずだ。
examples.english: When you go abroad, most likely you will want to study that country's language and culture.

examples.japanese: 正月ともなると、友人同士、お互いの家を行き来して、正月酒を楽しむ。
examples.english: On New Year's Day my friends and I go to each other's houses and enjoy New Year's Day sake.

examples.japanese: ここは紅葉が始まると訪れる人が増え始め、11月半ばともなると大勢の人でごったがえす。
examples.english: When the leaves begin turning red, the number of visitors starts to increase, and in mid-November, this place is packed with people.

examples.japanese: 社会人にもなると、先輩や友人の結婚式に招かれる機会が出てきます。
examples.english: Once you (graduate and) get out in the real world, you will start getting invited to the weddings of your elders and friends.

examples.japanese: 高校生にもなると、自分のお小遣いくらいは、バイトして稼ぐようになる。
examples.english: When you become a high school student, you get a part-time job and start earning your own pocket money.

examples.japanese: 大きなホテルともなると、一日に数千人もの利用者が集まってくる。
examples.english: At a big hotel, thousands of people come through daily.

examples.japanese: 『美人と野獣』ともなると人気の作品だから、当日券なんてなかなか買えない。
examples.english: "Beauty and the Beast" is a popular show, so it's hard to ﬁnd same day tickets.

Unusually; more ~ than usual
-------------
 〖example〗:  (ks).　
 彼女は今日はいつに（も）なく陽気だった。
 She was unusually cheerful today.
explanation: に（も）なく A phrase that means something unusual happens or someone does something unusual.

examples.japanese: 宏は「ただいまー」といつになく明るい声で帰ってきた。
examples.english: Hiroshi came home and said "I'm home!" in an unusually cheerful voice.

meaning_en: Toward; to; at; aiming at; targeting; for; for the purpose of; in order to
formation:
(i) Noun | に向けて | | 
 | ロンドンに向けて | Toward/to/for London | 
(ii) VN | に向けて | | 
 | 体制の改革に向けて | For the purpose of reforming the system | 
(iii) Noun1 | に{向けての/向けた}Noun2 | | 
 | ２１世紀に{向けての/向けた}社会保障 | Social security for the 21st century |
explanation: に向けて・に向けた A compound particle that indicates the destination/direction of movement, the target/direction of an action, or the goal/purpose of an action.

examples.japanese: 報道班は次の目的地に向けて出発した。
examples.english: The team of reporters left for the next destination.

examples.japanese: このテレビコマーシャルは20、30代の独身女性に向けて発信されている。
examples.english: This TV commercial is being marketed to single women in their twenties and thirties.

examples.japanese: 今、来年の入学試験に向けて頑張っています。
examples.english: I'm studying hard now for the next year's entrance exam.

examples.japanese: 新しいエネルギーの開発に向けて研究が進んでいる。
examples.english: Research is progressing toward (the goal of) developing new energy.

examples.japanese: 地球温暖化防止に｛向けての/向けた｝動きが活発化している。
examples.english: Efforts to prevent (literally: Movement for the purpose of preventing) global warming are gaining vigour.

examples.japanese: 救援物資を積んだヘリコプターが被災地に向けて飛び立った。
examples.english: A helicopter loaded with relief supplies left for (literally: took off toward) the site of the damage.

examples.japanese: 機動隊はデモ隊に向けて催涙弾を発射した。
examples.english: The riot police shot tear gas bombs at the ranks of demonstrators.

examples.japanese: K社は1月から九州で生産した高級車を中国に向けて輸出する。
examples.english: Starting in January, K Company is going to export luxury cars to China which were manufactured in Kyushu.

examples.japanese: 天候や道路状況に応じた適切な運転を心がけましょう。
examples.english: Please make sure your driving is appropriate for the weather and road conditions.

examples.japanese: 当社では要請に応じて講師を学校に派遣することもできます。
examples.english: We can also dispatch a lecturer to the school in response to their request.

examples.japanese: 病院でもらう薬は、医師が患者の体質や症状に応じて処方します。
examples.english: The drugs a patient receives at the hospital are prescribed by the doctor according to the patient's physical condition and symptoms.

examples.japanese: 湯沸かし器の設定温度は、目的に応じてその都度調節するのが賢い使い方だ。
examples.english: A wise way of using a water heater is to adjust the (pre-set) temperature each time, according to the purpose.

examples.japanese: 今年行われた「今後の大学教育のあり方に関する世論調査」によると、外国語教育の効果的だと思われる授業のあり方に関して、33.7％が「学生個人の能力に応じてクラスを分けて授業を行う」と答えた。
examples.english: According to the ""Survey of How Future Higher Education Should Be,"" which was conducted this year, 33.7 percent (of respondents) agreed that for effective foreign language education, ""classes should be taught by dividing students according to their ability"".

examples.japanese: 髪のケアには欠かせないシャンプーには症状に応じて様々なタイプがある。
examples.english: Shampoo, which is indispensable for hair care, comes in various types, depending on the condition of your hair.

meaning_en: Even though (it is/was the case that); even if (it is true that); although (it is/was the case that); whatever/whoever/etc.; no matter what/who/how/etc.; whether X or Y
formation:
(i) Vinformal | に{しろ/せよ} | | 
 | {行く/行った}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though someone goes/went | 
(ii) Adjectiveいinformal | に{しろ/せよ} | | 
 | {高い/高かった}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though something is/was expensive | 
(iii) Adjectiveなstem | {∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | | 
 | 不十分{∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though something is/was insufficient | 
(iv) Noun | {∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | | 
 | 子供{∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | Even though it is/was a child | 
 | 誰{∅/である/だった/であった}に{しろ/せよ} | Whoever it may be/have been | 
 | いずれに{しろ/せよ} | Whichever it may be; at any rate | 
(v) Adverb | に{しろ/せよ} | | 
 | ゆっくりに{しろ/せよ} | Even though something happens slowly |
explanation: にしろ・せよ A conjunctive phrase that carries the meaning of concession.

examples.japanese: 時間があまりなかったに｛しろ/せよ｝、この仕事はひどすぎる。
examples.english: Even though he didn't have much time, this work is too sloppy.

examples.japanese: 誰が書くに｛しろ/せよ｝、絶対間違いがあってはいけない。
examples.english: No matter who writes it, there can be absolutely no mistakes.

examples.japanese: 行くに｛しろ/せよ｝、行かないに｛しろ/せよ｝、後で電話を下さい。
examples.english: Whether you go or not, please give me a call later.

examples.japanese: 何に｛しろ/せよ｝、このままでは問題は解決しない。
examples.english: At any rate (literally: whatever it is), leaving the situation as it is won't solve the problem.

examples.japanese: たとえ練習に｛しろ/せよ｝、真面目にやらなければならない。
examples.english: Even though it is just practice, you have to take it seriously.

examples.japanese: 程度の差はあるにせよ、性差別のない国はないだろう。
examples.english: Although the degree may differ from country to country (literally: there may be differences in degree), there is no country without gender discrimination.

examples.japanese: 薬を飲むことですべての問題が解決はしないにしろ、あなたの場合は薬で症状を軽減させることが先決です。
examples.english: Even if (it's true that) taking the drug will not solve all your problems, in your case, you have to alleviate the symptoms ﬁrst (by taking it).

examples.japanese: 誰かに書いてもらうにしろ、内容は我々が考えなければならない。
examples.english: Even if we ask someone to write it for us, we will have to think of what to say (literally: the content) ourselves.

meaning_en: Also; (even) for ~
formation:
Noun | にしたところで | | 
 | その教授にしたところで | The professor is also ~/even the professor |
explanation: A compound particle that means "even" or "also".

examples.japanese: 彼は日本語を20年も勉強しているが、その彼にしたところで、まだ分からない文法に時々出くわすそうだ。
examples.english: He has studied Japanese for 20 years, but he told me that even he still encounters grammar he doesn't understand.

examples.japanese: 子供はいつか手の届かないところへ行ってしまうものだ。自分の子だけはそうでないと思うかもしれないが、あなたの子にしたところで同じだ。
examples.english: Children go (places) beyond their parents' reach sooner or later. You may think that your own children will be different, but they, too, will be the same.

examples.japanese: 昔の浮気が発覚した夫は「10年たってるんだからもう時効だ」と開き直りの態度です。私にしたところで二人の子供のことを考えると離婚にはなかなか踏み切れません。
examples.english: My husband, whose past affair was discovered, turned deﬁant, saying, ""It was 10 years ago, so it's too late (to do anything)"" I, too, couldn't bear to go forward with a divorce when I thought about our two children.

examples.japanese: 最近は万年筆で字を書く人というのを、ほとんど見なくなって残念だ。もっとも、そういう私にしたところで、普段使っているのはボールペンだ。
examples.english: Lately, you seldom see people writing with a fountain pen, and that makes me feel terribly disappointed. But even I usually use a ball-point pen.

examples.japanese: 三島由紀夫は産湯に浸かった記憶があると書いているが、彼にしたところで、死ぬまでのすべての記憶があるわけではない。
examples.english: Yukio Mishima wrote that he remembered (literally: had a memory of) taking his ﬁrst bath as a baby, but there's no way even he remembered everything he did from birth until death (literally: until he died).

meaning_en: even
formation:
Noun | にしてからが | | 
 | 首相にしてからが | Even the prime minister |
explanation: A compound particle indicating that something unexpected occurs.

examples.japanese: ワールドカップの時はサッカーファンでもない私にしてからが興奮状態でした。
examples.english: I am not a soccer fan, but during the World Cup, even I got excited.

examples.japanese: 警察にしてからが、いざ事件が起きないと市民を暴力から守ってくれない。
examples.english: Even the police don't protect citizens from violence unless an incident actually occurs.

examples.japanese: ギリシャやローマの彫刻や壁画などに、痩せた女性は皆無だ。美の女神、ヴィーナスにしてからが、かなり太めだ。
examples.english: In Greek or Roman sculptures and mural paintings there are no emaciated-looking women. Even Venus, the Goddess of Beauty, is quite full-ﬁgured.

examples.japanese: 当代随一の知性人である彼にしてからが、恋愛にたぶらかされている。
examples.english: Even he, the greatest intellectual of the day, was deceived by love.

examples.japanese: 息子は父から受け継いだ作風で作品を描いていたが、すでにその父にしてからが、古くさいと言われていた。
examples.english: He produced paintings in the mode he inherited from his father, but that style was already considered outdated in his father's time.

examples.japanese: 首相の構造改革案にしてからが、官僚の強い抵抗にあっている。
examples.english: Even the prime minister's plan for structural reform met with strong resistance from bureaucrats.

meaning_en: Even if (someone decides to/it is true that); although/even though (it is true that/it is the case that/we admit that/we agree that/etc.); whatever/whoever/etc.; no matter what/who/how/etc.; whether X or Y; as for ~, too; even (so)
formation:
(i) Sinformal | にしても | だ after Adjectiveなstem and Noun is omitted | 
 | {行く/行った}にしても | Even if someone decides to go/even though (it is the case that) someone went | 
 | {高い/高かった}にしても | Even if (it is true that) something is expensive/even though (it is true that) something was expensive | 
 | 便利{∅/である/ だった/であった}にしても | Even if (it is true that) something is convenient/even though (it is true that) something was convenient | 
 | 学生{∅/である/ だった/であった}にしても | Even if (it is true that) someone is a student/even though (it is true that) someone was a student | 
(ii) NP | にしても | | 
 | この国の文化にしても | This country’s culture, too |
explanation: A conjunction that represents the idea of "even if someone decides to do something," or "even if/though someone decides that something is true/the case".

examples.japanese: ピアノを買うにしても、こんな狭いアパートでは置くところがない。
examples.english: Even if we decide to buy a piano, we won't have a place to put it in such a small apartment.

examples.japanese: 美紀の言ったことは大げさだったにしても、すべてがウソというわけではないだろう。
examples.english: Even though (we agree that) Miki's story was exaggerated, probably not all of it was untrue.

examples.japanese: 誰がこの仕事をやるにしても失敗は許されない。
examples.english: No matter who is going to do this job, we have no room for mistakes.

examples.japanese: 君が行くにしても他の誰かが行くにしても今回の会議はかなりの準備が必要だ。
examples.english: Whether you go or someone else does, this meeting will take a lot of preparation.

examples.japanese: 敬語の使い方にしても近頃は間違った言い方が目につく。
examples.english: With honorific language, too, we often notice incorrect usage these days.

examples.japanese: 今すぐ帰るにしても、飛行機の切符が取れるだろうか。
examples.english: Even if we (decide to) go home right now, I wonder if we will be able to get plane tickets.

examples.japanese: 京都は見るところがたくさんあるので、市内だけ回るにしても3日くらいとっておいた方がいいでしょう。
examples.english: Kyoto has so many places to see, so even if you (decide to) stay within the city, you should plan on spending about three days.

examples.japanese: この作品は中国大陸の影響が濃厚であるにしても、日本の画工の高い水準を示している。
examples.english: Even taking the strong inﬂuence from China into account, this work demonstrates the high quality craftsmanship of Japanese painters.

meaning_en: For; over; extending; stretching; ranging; covering
formation:
(i) Noun | にわたって | | 
 | １か月にわたって | For one month | 
 | 全ページにわたって | Over the entire page/all the pages | 
 | ５回にわたって | Extending to five times | 
 | 十キロにわたって | Extending over 10 kilometers | 
 | 東海地方全体にわたって | Over the entire Tokai region | 
(ii) Noun1からNoun2 | にわたって | | 
 | 一時から六時にわたって | From 1 o’clock to 6 o’clock | 
 | 東部から中部にわたって | Ranging from the eastern part to the central part | 
(iii) (Noun1から)Noun2 | にわたるNoun3 | | 
 | 百ページにわたる報告 | A report which extends to one hundred pages | 
 | 五月から九にわたる月乾期 | A dry season from May through September |
explanation: にわたって・わたる A compound particle indicating that something takes place over a particular span of time or physical space.

examples.japanese: オリンピックが16日間にわたって開かれた。
examples.english: The Olympic Games were held for sixteen days.

examples.japanese: 干ばつのため広範囲にわたって作物が被害を受けた。
examples.english: Due to the drought, crops were damaged over a wide area.

examples.japanese: 配管工事のため、明日午前１時から午前9時ごろにわたって断水する。
examples.english: Due to work on the pipes, the water supply will be cut off from 1 a.m. to about 9 a.m. tomorrow.

examples.japanese: その記事は8回にわたって新聞に連載された。
examples.english: The articles appeared serially in the newspaper over eight issues (literally: extending to eight times).

examples.japanese: 約40年にわたる冷戦がついに終わった。
examples.english: The Cold War, which lasted for about 40 years, ﬁnally came to an end.

examples.japanese: A社の携帯電話サービスで、関東の一部で昨夜午後9時ごろから約6時間にわたって接続障害があった。
examples.english: Last night there was an interruption (literally: connection difficulties) in Company A's mobile phone service in a certain area of Kanto for about six hours starting about 9 o'clock.

examples.japanese: コミック『ピーナッツ』は、１９５０年に誕生して以来半世紀以上にわたって世界中のファンを魅了してきた。
examples.english: From the time of its debut in 1950, the cartoon ""Peanuts"" has fascinated fans all over the world for over half a century.

examples.japanese: その川の両側には２０エーカーにわたって森が広がっている。
examples.english: On both sides of the river, the forest stretches for 20 acres.

meaning_en: Without; without ~ing; regardless of; independently of; without reference to; whether X or Y; whether X or not; whatever/whoever/etc.; no matter what/who/how/etc.
formation:
(i) Noun | によらず | | 
 | 紹介によらず | Without introduction | 
 | 学生数によらず | Regardless of the number of students | 
(ii) Wh-word (Noun/NP) | によらず | | 
 | 誰によらず | Whoever it may be (literally: regardless of who it is) | 
 | どんな仕事によらず | Whatever work it may be (literally: regardless of what kind of work it is) | 
(iii) XかYか | によらず | Where X, Y=contrastive words; usually nonpast forms | 
Noun1かNoun2 | 英語か日本語かによらず | Regardless of whether something is English or Japanese | 
V1informalかV2informalか | 勝つか負けるによらず | Regardless of whether someone wins or loses | 
Adjectiveい1informalかAdjectiveい2informal | 高いか安いかによらず | Regardless of whether something is expensive or cheap | 
Adjectiveな1stemかAdjectiveな2stem | 偶然か意図的かによらず | Regardless of whether something is accidental or intentional | 
(iv) Xか{どう/ 否}か | によらず | | 
 | 存在するか{どう/否}かによらず | Regardless of whether something exists or not | 
 | 高いか{どう/否}かによらず | Regardless of whether something is expensive or not | 
 | 偶然か{どう/否}かによらず | Regardless of whether something is coincidental or not | 
 | 学生か{どう/否}かによらず | Regardless of whether someone is a student or not | 
(v) X(affirmative)かX(negative)か | によらず | | 
 | 行くか行かないかによらず | Regardless of whether someone goes or not | 
 | 高いか高くないかによらず | Regardless of whether something is expensive or not | 
 | 偶然(である)か偶然でないによらず | Regardless of whether something is coincidental or not | 
 | 英語(である)か英語でないによらず | Regardless of whether something is English or not | 
(vi) X(affirmative)+X(negative)か | によらず | Where X={V/Adjectiveい}informal; usually nonpast forms | 
 | 行く行かないによらず | Regardless of whether someone goes or not | 
 | うまいうまくないによらず | Regardless of whether something is good or poor (at going something) | 
(vii) X+Y | によらず | Where X, Y=Adjectiveいinformal nonpast/Adjectiveなstem; Y=X’s antonym | 
 | 上手下手によらず | Regardless of whether someone is skillful or unskillful | 
 | うまい下手によらず | Regardless of whether someone is good or poor (at going something) | 
(viii) {Noun/Adjectiveなstem} | であるなしによらず | | 
 | 会員であるなしによらず | Regardless of whether someone is a member or not | 
 | 経済的であるなしによらず | Regardless of whether something is economical nor not | 
(ix) Nounのあるなし | によらず | | 
 | 学位のあるなしによらず | Regardless of whether someone has a degree or not | 
(x) Nounのいかん | によらず | | 
 | 方法のいかんによらず | Regardless of the method (literally: regardless of what the method is) |
explanation: A compound particle that means "without depending on".

examples.japanese: リストラによらず(に)この会社を救う方法はない。
examples.english: There is no way to save this company without restructuring it.

examples.japanese: この会社では学歴によらず、実力があればどんどん大きい仕事をまかされる。
examples.english: At this company, if you are capable, you will be given big assignments one after another, regardless of your educational qualiﬁcations.

examples.japanese: 何事によらず困ったことがあったらいつでも相談して下さい。
examples.english: Whatever it may be, if you have trouble, please consult me anytime.

examples.japanese: 国産(である)か輸入(である)かによらず牛肉は食べないことにしている。
examples.english: (Regardless of) Whether it is domestically produced or imported, as a rule I do not eat beef.

examples.japanese: この会社は経験のあるなしによらず面接してくれる。
examples.english: This company will interview you regardless of your experience (literally: whether or not you have experience.)

examples.japanese: 天候のいかんによらず試合は予定通り行われます。
examples.english: No matter what the weather (literally: whatever the weather is like), the game will be held as scheduled.

examples.japanese: 誰がそのプロジェクトを担当するかによらず担当者には特別手当が支給される。
examples.english: Regardless of who it is (literally: who takes the project), the project manager will be given special compensation.

examples.japanese: 理想は武力によらず紛争を解決することだ。
examples.english: The ideal is to resolve disputes without using armed force.

meaning_en: So (~ that); so much/well (~ that); so ~ and
formation:
(i) {V/Adjectiveい}informal | のなんのって | | 
 | {効く/効いた}のなんのって | Something is/was so effective that ~ | 
 | {速い/速かった}のなんのって | Something is/was so fast that ~ | 
(ii) Adjectiveなstem{な/だった} | のなんのって | | 
 | 下手{な/だった}のなんのって | Someone is/was so bad at something that ~ |
explanation: A phrase to emphasize that something/someone is/was in an extreme state or that someone does/did something to a great extent

examples.japanese: 甘いのなんのって私は一口食べて全部残してしまいました。
examples.english: It was so sweet that I ate one bite and left the rest.

examples.japanese: 飲んだのなんのって彼らは5本の酒を全部空けてしまった。
examples.english: They drank so much; they completely emptied ﬁve bottles of sake.

examples.japanese: かゆいのなんのって一晩中寝られなかった。
examples.english: It was so itchy that I couldn't sleep all night.

examples.japanese: 重いのなんのって二人でも持ち上がりませんでした。
examples.english: It was so heavy that even two people couldn't lift it.

examples.japanese: 海の醍醐味を味わうなら、ホエールウォッチングだ。実際に見るクジラは、大きいのなんのって、すごい迫力だよ。
examples.english: If you want to experience the true charm of the ocean, try whale watching. When seen in real life, whales are so huge they take your breath away.

examples.japanese: もう少しで釣れたのに糸が切れて魚は海の中。結構大きかったので悔しかったのなんのって！
examples.english: I almost had it, but the line broke and the ﬁsh went back into the sea. It was really big, so I was so disappointed!

examples.japanese: A:試合はどうだった？ B:いやもう、ひどいのなんのって、話したくもないよ。
examples.english: A: How was the game? B: Oh, no, it was so terrible! I don't even want to talk about it.

examples.japanese: 不便なのなんのって一番近くのスーパーに行くのに1時間もかかるんです。
examples.english: It's so inconvenient; it takes up to an hour to get to the nearest supermarket.

meaning_en: Lack of; absence of
formation:
Noun | の無さ | | 
 | 能力の無さ | Lack of ability | 
 | 元気の無さ | Lack of spirit |
explanation: の無さ・のなさ A phrase that indicates a state where something is lacking.

examples.japanese: 私は彼の常識の無さにあきれている。
examples.english: I am appalled by his lack of common sense.

examples.japanese: 跳びたいと思っても跳べない。体力、筋力の無さを痛感しました。
examples.english: I wanted to jump, but I couldn't. I became painfully aware of my lack of physical and muscular strength.

examples.japanese: 今回の一連の貴社の対応は、私たちには全く納得できるものではなく、貴社の誠意の無さに大変な憤りを感じます。
examples.english: We cannot accept your company's response to this situation, and we are ﬁlled with anger at your company's lack of sincerity.

examples.japanese: 辞書の使用を許可してもらったものの、時間不足で思ったように答えられない問題があり、自分の英語力の無さに落ち込みました。
examples.english: Although I was allowed to use a dictionary, because of the time constraint there were parts I couldn't answer, and I felt depressed about my lack of English proﬁciency.

examples.japanese: 親しみやすさと、温かさと、飾り気の無さが、さやの絶対的な魅力である。
examples.english: Friendliness, warmth and a lack of affectation are what makes Saya so absolutely charming.

examples.japanese: 最近の映画やドラマは、その内容の無さにがっかりさせられる。
examples.english: I am disappointed with recent movies and dramas because of their lack of content.

examples.japanese: 調査によると日本の子供の自信の無さは世界一だそうである。
examples.english: According to a survey, Japanese children are the least self-conﬁdent in the world.

examples.japanese: このマンガは設定は面白かったが、物語が進むにつれて話が大きくなり、リアリティの無さについていけなくなってしまった。
examples.english: This comic had an interesting plot, but as the story went on, it became so exaggerated that I couldn't take the lack of reality.

meaning_en: Try to do; be about to
formation:
Vnegative | んとする | Exception:する→せんとする | 
 | 行かんとする | Someone tries to go there | 
 | 起きんとする | Someone is about to get up | 
 | 研究せんとする | Someone tries to do research |
explanation: A phrase meaning for "someone to try to do something" or for "something to be about to occur".

examples.japanese: 教授の言わんとすることが学生に伝わらないのは、たいてい教授の方が悪いのだ。
examples.english: It is usually a professor who is to blame when his students don't comprehend what he tries to convey.

examples.japanese: 太陽はまさに山の稜線に沈まんとしていた。
examples.english: The sun was about to sink behind the mountain ridge.

examples.japanese: あの政治家は言わんとしているところがよく分からない。
examples.english: I don't comprehend what that politician is trying to say.

examples.japanese: 善意で何事かを行わんとすると、必ずそれに水を差す人間がいる。
examples.english: Whenever someone tries to do something with good intentions, inevitably there is someone who discourages it.

examples.japanese: 専門家でない者を排除せんとする科学者の過剰防衛には辟易させられる。
examples.english: I am fed up with overprotective scientists (literally: the overprotection of scientists) who try to eliminate non specialists.

examples.japanese: 死なんとする者は本音を吐くものだ。
examples.english: A person who is about to die gives vent to his true feelings.

examples.japanese: 暴風のために木々が倒れんとしている。
examples.english: The trees are about to be blown over by the violent wind.

examples.japanese: まさに輝かんとする月が雲で隠れた。
examples.english: The moon, which was just about to shine, was concealed by the clouds.

meaning_en: Through; via; by means of; by ~ing
formation:
(i) Noun | を介して | | 
 | 知り合いを介して | Through an acquaintance | 
(ii) Noun1 | を{介しての/介した}Noun2 | | 
 | 通信網を{介しての/介した}データ送信 | Data transmission via a network |
explanation: を介して/介した A compound particle that introduces a medium through which someone does something or something happens to someone or something.

examples.japanese: 今、現地の代理人を介して製造元と価格の交渉をしている。
examples.english: We are negotiating the price with the manufacturer through a local agent now.

examples.japanese: インターネットを介して音楽や映画を配信できるようになった。
examples.english: Music and movies can be distributed via the Internet now.

examples.japanese: 我々はボランティア活動を介して地域の交流を図ろうとしている。
examples.english: We are trying to promote interaction among the local (units) through volunteer activities.

examples.japanese: 通訳を｛介しての/介した｝商談は効率が悪い。
examples.english: Business talks via an interpreter are inefficient.

examples.japanese: 日本にいる友達を介してこの情報を手に入れた。
examples.english: I got this information with the help of (literally: through) a friend of mine in Japan.

examples.japanese: このウイルスはそれに感染した鳥から蚊を介して人に感染する。人から人や人から蚊を介しての感染はない。
examples.english: This virus is transmitted to people from infected birds via mosquitoes. It is not transmitted between people either directly or via mosquitoes.

examples.japanese: 自殺系サイトを介して知り合った男女が、初対面でいきなり一緒に自殺するという事件が続き、社会問題となった。
examples.english: There have been several incidents in which a man and a woman who had met through a suicide website committed suicide together right after meeting in person for the first time, and such incidents have become a social problem.

examples.japanese: このテロ組織は海外の金融機関を介して資金の調達と仕送りをしているらしい。
examples.english: This terrorist organization seems to be collecting and distributing money via overseas ﬁnancial institutions.

meaning_en: Cannot hold; cannot hold back; cannot keep back; cannot help ~ing; cannot keep ~ from ~ing
formation:
(i) Noun | を禁じ得ない | | 
 | 喜びを禁じ得ない | Cannot keep back one’s joy | 
(ii) Vinformal nonpastの | を禁じ得ない | | 
 | 足が震えるのを禁じ得ない | Cannot keep someone’s legs from trembling |
explanation: A phrase that is used when one cannot control emotions or reactions caused by emotions.

examples.japanese: このような無責任な行いに対して怒りを禁じ得ない。
examples.english: I cannot hold back my anger at such an irresponsible deed.

examples.japanese: その感動的な光景を見て、涙がこみ上げてくるのを禁じ得なかった。
examples.english: Seeing the moving scene, I could not keep my tears from welling up.

examples.japanese: 24年の苦悩と空白の後、ついに実現した家族との再会に、周囲の者も涙を禁じ得なかった。
examples.english: (Seeing) the family reunited, an occasion that finally became reality after twenty-four years of agony and separation, people around them couldn't help but cry, too.

examples.japanese: その美しい早春の風景画に作者の温かい郷土愛を感じ、深い感動を禁じ得なかった。
examples.english: Looking at the beautiful early spring landscape painting, I felt the painter's love for his homeland, and couldn't help but be moved profoundly.

examples.japanese: 出版社による無神経な個人写真の扱い方に、驚きと憤りを禁じ得ない。
examples.english: I can't hold back my surprise and anger at the publisher's thoughtless way of treating those personal photos.

examples.japanese: 大統領の声明は、せっかく第一歩を踏み出した両国の平和統一の働きに水を差すのではないかという疑問を禁じ得ない。
examples.english: I cannot keep myself from wondering if the president's announcement will pour cold water on the two nations' hard-won first step toward peaceful uniﬁcation.

examples.japanese: 長い間憧れていた人に会う瞬間が近づいて、次第に動悸が速まるのを禁じ得なかった。
examples.english: As the moment approached when I was to meet with the person I'd admired for a long time, I could not stop my heart from beating faster and faster.

examples.japanese: この業界の救いようのない保守性に、深いため息が出るのを禁じ得なかった。
examples.english: (Looking at) this industry's hopeless conservatism, I couldn't help but let out a deep sigh.

meaning_en: Centering around; in connection with; over; concerning; regarding; with regard to
formation:
(i) Noun | をめぐって | | 
 | この報道をめぐって | Concerning this news report | 
(ii) Noun1 | をめぐるNoun2 | | 
 | 基礎研究をめぐって現状 | Current status of (literally: around) basic research | 
(iii) Embedded Question | をめぐって | | 
 | 日本がこの問題にどう対応するべきかをめぐって | Regarding how Japan should handle this problem | 
(iv) Noun1かNoun2か | をめぐって | | 
 | 実行か中止かをめぐって | Concerning whether we should execute something, or hold off on it | 
(v) Embedded Question1+Embedded Question2 | をめぐって | | 
 | 単独で行うかパートナーを探すかをめぐって | Regarding whether we want to do it by ourselves or look for a partner |
explanation: をめぐって・めぐる A compound particle meaning "concerning; over", which is used with an issue over which different opinions, ideas, etc., are expressed or exchanged.

examples.japanese: モノレール建設をめぐって市民の意見が対立している。
examples.english: Citizens' opinions are divided over the monorail construction.

examples.japanese: 無駄な公共事業をめぐる批判の声が強まっている。
examples.english: (Voices of) Criticism concerning wasteful public projects is growing stronger.

examples.japanese: 大学運営は今後どうあるべきかをめぐって活発に意見が交わされた。
examples.english: Opinions were exchanged actively regarding how universities should be run from now on.

examples.japanese: 進攻か撤退かをめぐって激しい議論が戦わされた。
examples.english: There was a heated discussion over whether we should advance or retreat.

examples.japanese: 新制度に即時切り替えるべきか来年度まで待つべきかをめぐって委員の間で意見が分かれた。
examples.english: Opinions were divided among the committee members regarding whether we should shift to the new system immediately or wait until next year.

examples.japanese: 新しい歴史教科書をめぐって激しい議論が続いている。
examples.english: The ﬁerce debate over the new history textbook continues.

examples.japanese: 審判の判定をめぐって選手が乱闘し試合が約１時間中断した。
examples.english: The players had a ﬁght over the umpire's decision, and the game was interrupted for about an hour.

examples.japanese: 自衛隊派遣の是非をめぐって激しい議論が交わされた。
examples.english: There were ﬁerce arguments over the pros and cons of dispatching the Self-Defence Forces.

meaning_en: Come ot think of it; when I think back; on reflection
explanation: An adverb that indicates feelings of nostalgia or regret when recollecting one’s past experiences.

examples.japanese: 思えば、大学時代はとても楽しかった。
examples.english: When I come to think of it, I had a great time when I was in college.

examples.japanese: 思えば、あの頃私は彼と政治問題について毎日のように議論したものだ。
examples.english: When I think back, I discussed political issues with him almost every day.

examples.japanese: 思えば、終戦後数年は、ほとんどの日本人が野菜を庭で育てていた。
examples.english: Come to think of it, for a few years after the war, almost all Japanese people grew vegetables in their backyards.

examples.japanese: 今思えばどうしてこんなCDを買ったのだろう。
examples.english: Now that I think about it, why did I buy such a (terrible) CD?

examples.japanese: 思えば心筋梗塞の前兆はあった。
examples.english: Come to think of it, there were warning signs of a cardiac seizure.

examples.japanese: 小学校3年生の時、祖母と銀座で映画を見た。今にして思えば、あれが祖母と見た最初で最後の映画だった。
examples.english: I saw a movie in Ginza with my grandmother when I was a third grader. When I think back on it now, that was the first and the last movie I ever saw with her.

examples.japanese: 今から思えば、私が同僚の男性と結婚すると言った時、父は猛然と反対した。あの時父の忠告を聞いておけばと悔やまれる。
examples.english: As I think of it now, my father was vehemently opposed when I told him that I was going to marry my colleague. I regret that I didn't listen to his advice.

examples.japanese: 自転車で出かけようとした途端、チェーンが外れてしまった。今から思えば、あれがケチのつき始めだった。
examples.english: The moment I went out on my bicycle, the chain came off. When I come to think of it now, that was the beginning of (a period of) bad luck.

meaning_en: In my view; it seems to me that ~; when I think (about ~); considering
formation:
(i) 思うに、 | Sentence。 | | 
 | 思うに、コンピュータは良し悪しだ。 | In my view computers are good and bad | 
(ii) NPを | 思うに | | 
 | この一年を思うに、つらいことが多かった。 | When I think about this past year, it was full of trying things |
explanation: A phrase indicating that the subsequent statement is the speaker’s/writer’s personal view.

examples.japanese: (私が)思うに、文化は宗教の一種だ。
examples.english: In my view, culture is a kind of religion.

examples.japanese: 医学界の体質を思うに、当然医者と製薬会社の癒着はあると思う。
examples.english: Considering the nature of the medical world, I believe there is collusion between doctors and pharmaceutical companies.

examples.japanese: 思うに、情報を発信するマスコミと受信する我々国民は、完全に分化され固定化されてしまっているのが現状だ。
examples.english: In my view, the present state is that the media, which distribute information, and the citizens, who receive it, are completely separate and static.

examples.japanese: 「思うに、快楽に耽る人生ほど快楽から遠いものはない。」ージョン・D・ロックフェラー2世
examples.english: I can think of nothing less pleasurable than a life devoted to pleasure. ― John D. Rockefeller, Jr.

examples.japanese: 私が思うに、大学時代の部活はお薦めだ。きっと一生の宝物になるだろう。
examples.english: I would recommend joining a club activity at college. I'm sure it would be something you'd treasure for the rest of your life.

examples.japanese: 思うに、優れた画家であっても、生命感あふれる作品を生み出せるのはほんの一時期ではないだろうか。
examples.english: It seems to me that even an outstanding painter can create dynamic artworks only during a certain period of his or her life.

examples.japanese: 思うに、「人を使う」ことが上手な人間というのは魅力のない人間である。
examples.english: In my view, people who excel at getting things from others (literally: using people) are unattractive people.

examples.japanese: 自分の来し方を思うに、常に幅広い好奇心を持ち続けてきたことが、研究を続ける原動力ではなかっただろうか。
examples.english: When I reﬂect upon my past, it appears to me that my constant sense of curiosity in everything has served as a driving power for me to keep on doing my research.

meaning_en: (there is) no ~ but X; X is the only one; nothing else is ~ but X; no other ~ are/do something as ~ as X
formation:
Noun | をおいてほかに(は)～ない | | 
 | サッカーをおいてほかに(は)例がない | There is no example but soccer | 
 | リサをおいてほかに(は)いない | There is no one else but Lisa |
explanation: をおいてほかに（は）～ない A phrase that means "there is nothing else besides X".

examples.japanese: 日本語を短期間で習得したいのならこの学校をおいてほかに(は)ない。
examples.english: If you want to learn Japanese in a short period of time, there is no other school (that you should consider) but this one.

examples.japanese: これほど多くの作品を手がけた監督はY氏をおいてほかにいない。
examples.english: No other director has been involved with as many works as Mr. Y.

examples.japanese: あなたを救うのはあなた自身をおいてほかにない。
examples.english: There is no one to save you but yourself.

examples.japanese: これほどのプロフェッショナリズムと豊かな経験を提供できる会社は、日本中で当社をおいてほかにはありません。
examples.english: There is no company in Japan but ours that can provide this level of professionalism and rich experience.

examples.japanese: 契約に対してこれだけ無神経な国はこの国をおいてほかに思いつかない。
examples.english: I cannot think of another country that is as indifferent to contracts as this one is.

examples.japanese: この役割をこなせるのはジェーンをおいてほかに考えられない。
examples.english: We cannot think of anyone who can handle this role but Jane.

examples.japanese: 味のよさと形の美しさ、この二つの要件を満たす桃は、山梨県産をおいてほかにない。
examples.english: The only peaches that satisfy the two requirements of good taste and beautiful shape are the ones from Yamanashi Prefecture. (literally: No peaches satisfy the two requirements, i.e., good taste and a beautiful shape, but those from Yamanashi Prefecture.)

examples.japanese: 非母国語話者の間のコミュニケーションにおいてこれほど広範囲に用いられている言語は、英語をおいてほかには存在しない。
examples.english: There is no language but English that is used as widely for communication among non-native speakers.

examples.japanese: 室内及び廊下での喫煙は禁止されています。

examples.japanese: 今月号では広島及び近郊他県の観光名所を紹介します。
examples.english: In this month's issue we introduce sightseeing spots in Hiroshima and neighbouring prefectures.

examples.japanese: 本店移転及び商号変更についてお知らせいたします。
examples.english: We hereby notify you of the relocation of the head office and the change of our company name.

examples.japanese: A社は２００２年及びそれ以前の製品のサポートの打ち切りを発表した。
examples.english: Company A announced that it would no longer offer technical support for products made before 2003 (literally: in and before 2002).

examples.japanese: これは昨年度における全国の一般廃棄物の排出及び処理状況に関する報告である。
examples.english: This is a report on the status of the discharge and treatment of general waste nationwide last year.

examples.japanese: 記者会見の前に、情報が正確であること、及びそれが公表してもいい情報であることを確認しておく必要がある。
examples.english: Before holding a press conference it is necessary to make sure that the information is accurate and that it can be (literally: it is information which can be) released to the public.

examples.japanese: 彼女はこういう根気のいる仕事にはおよそ向いていない。
examples.english: She is not at all suited for work that requires perseverance like this work does.

examples.japanese: 彼の考えていることはおよそ想像がつく。
examples.english: I can make a fairly good guess about what he's thinking.

examples.japanese: その学会にはおよそ１５００人の会員がいる。
examples.english: That academic association has approximately 1,500 members.

examples.japanese: およそ楽をして得られる技能で身につくものはない。
examples.english: Generally, none of the skills you can learn easily will become second nature.

examples.japanese: およそ天才と言われる人は誰でも人には知れない重荷を背負っているものだ。
examples.english: Generally, anyone who is called a genius carries a heavy burden others can't see.

examples.japanese: 我々はおよそ不合理なこの制度に長い間縛られている。
examples.english: We've been bound by this utterly irrational system for a long time.

examples.japanese: 田宮先生は大学の政治的なことにはおよそ縁遠い人だった。
examples.english: Professor Tamiya was totally removed from university politics.

examples.english: Furuta talks as if he suffered alone, but the truth of the matter is that he just complained and didn't do any work.

examples.japanese: 今すぐ病院に連れて行こう。さもないと手遅れになる。
examples.english: Let's take him to the hospital right now. If we don't, it's going to be too late.

examples.japanese: 係員はさも面倒くさそうに私の苦情を聞いていた。
examples.english: The person in charge listened to my complaint with an expression that revealed it was truly bothersome.

examples.japanese: 彼女はさも忙しそうにしているが、本当は大した仕事なんかないのだ。
examples.english: She acts as if she were truly busy, but really she doesn't have anything signiﬁcant to work on.

examples.japanese: 子供たちはさも退屈そうな顔をして授業を聞いている。
examples.english: The children are listening to the lecture looking really bored.

examples.japanese: 川村はいつもその話をさも自分自身の体験みたいに話しているが、本当はそれは私が彼に話したことなのだ。
examples.english: Kawamura always tells that story as if it were his own experience, but actually I told it to him.

examples.japanese: 部長はさも当然のごとく私に日曜出勤を命じた。
examples.english: The division chief ordered me to come to the ofﬁce on Sunday as if it were a matter of course.

examples.japanese: D社のノート型コンピュータが更に薄くなった。

examples.japanese: 電化製品をディスカウントショップより更にお安く提供しております。
examples.english: We provide electrical appliances even more cheaply than discount shops do.

meaning_en: Well; now; well now; so
explanation: An interjection indicating that the speaker/writer is going to talk about something different.

examples.english: Well, I should be going now.

examples.japanese: さて、ここで今までお話ししたポイントを復習してみましょう。

examples.english: The World Cup has begun! So, which country's going to win this time?

examples.english: Now, I'm going to continue where we left off in the previous lecture. Do you remember (what we covered before)?

meaning_en: In the first place; to begin with; first of all; the very (beginning/origin/etc.); original; first; fundamental

 | そもそもの動機 | The original motivation |
explanation: そもそも（の）A sentence-modifying adverb used when the speaker/writer comments on or questions a fundamental point.

examples.english: To begin with, I cannot agree with our way of judging where we point out only the ﬂaws of a piece and never mention the good points.

examples.english: How was such a ridiculous plan approved in the ﬁrst place?

examples.japanese: 今回の事件のそもそもの起こりは、一人の社員が会社のパソコンをうちに持ち帰ったことにあった。

examples.japanese: そもさも電波って何なんでしょう。
examples.english: So, what are radio waves in the ﬁrst place?

examples.japanese: そもそも一体何で君がこのパーティーにいるんだ？
examples.english: To begin with, why on earth are you at this party?

examples.japanese: 彼に期待したことがそもそもの間違いだった。
examples.english: That we were hoping for great things from him was our ﬁrst mistake.

examples.english: If you remain a negative thinker, your life itself will be ruined.

examples.japanese: 企画そのものは悪くない。
examples.english: The plan itself is not bad.

examples.japanese: この国は独裁国家そのものだ。
examples.english: This country is the perfect deﬁnition of an autocracy.

examples.japanese: わいせつ画像は、それそのものが問題なのではなく、それを誰が見るかが問題だと思う。
examples.english: I think that obscene images themselves are not the problem; who sees them is the problem.

examples.japanese: 武田さんは今年８０歳だが、健康そのものだ。
examples.english: Mr. Takeda is 80 this year and the picture of health.

examples.japanese: 私はこの団体の存在そのものを疑っている。
examples.english: I doubt this group's very existence.

examples.japanese: 我々は外務省改革にとどまらず、現在の外交そのものの転換を望む。
examples.english: Not only do we want to reform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, but we hope the current diplomacy itself will change.

examples.japanese: 人間はその人の考えそのものである。
examples.english: The epitome of a person is his or her thinking. (literally: A human being is his or her thought itself.)

explanation: An adverbial phrase indicating that the degree of something is proportionate to the degree of the state, action or event mentioned in the preceding sentence.

examples.japanese: 株式投資は当たった時の利益は大きいが、それだけリスクも大きい。
examples.english: You can make a big proﬁt when you invest in the right stocks, but the risk (of loss) is just as big.

examples.japanese: この仕事は苦労も多いが、それだけやりがいもある。
examples.english: This job is hard work, but to the same extent I also ﬁnd it rewarding.

examples.japanese: 彼らは同じ宗教内の派閥だから、それだけ憎しみも大きいのかもしれない。
examples.english: It might be that they hate each other that much more because they are in different sects of the same religion.

examples.japanese: 期待が大きいとそれだけ失望も大きくなってしまう。
examples.english: If your expectations are high, your disappointment will be equally high.

examples.japanese: 大きな仕事をまかされたということは、それだけ期待されているということだろう。
examples.english: That he was assigned a big job just shows what high hopes people have for him.

examples.japanese: たくさんのオプションがあるのはいいのだが、それだけ選択に悩むことにもなる。
examples.english: It is good to have many options, but it means that it's that much harder to choose.

examples.japanese: 花粉症の薬は、眠くなるからそれだけ効くというわけではありません。
examples.english: It's not true of pollen allergy drugs that the sleepier they make you, the more effective they are.

examples.japanese: できるだけ多く条件を指定すると、それだけ理想に近い人が検索されるはずです。
examples.english: If you specify as many conditions as you can, your search should turn up someone that is much closer to your ideal.

meaning_en: In one’s own way; accompanying; proportionate; suitable; expected; agreeable; reasonable; one’s own; proper to
formation:
(i) それなりに | {V/Adjective(い/な)/Noun+Copula} | | 
 | それなりに楽しめる | Something can be enjoyed in its own way | 
 | それなりに美味しい | Something is tasty in its own way | 
 | それなりに便利だ | Something is convenient in its own way | 
 | それなりに傑作だ | Something is an excellent work in its own way | 
(ii) それなりの | Noun | | 
 | それなりの利点 | Merits proper to something |
explanation: それなりに・の A phrase representing the idea that someone/something does something or is in a state in his/her/its own way, or in a way suitable to the situation or generally expected from the situation.

examples.japanese: 天才と言われる人にはそれなりの苦しみがあると思う。
examples.english: I think people who are called geniuses suffer in their own way.

examples.japanese: クラシックもジャズもロックも、聞いてみればみなそれなりに面白い。
examples.english: If you (really) listen to classical music, jazz and rock, each of them is interesting in its own way.

examples.japanese: 外国で仕事をするのは面白いが、それなりの苦労は覚悟しなければならない。
examples.english: Working abroad is interesting, but you must expect a certain amount of hardship, too.

examples.japanese: 買った参考書はどれもみなそれなりに役に立っている。
examples.english: All the reference books I have bought have been helpful in their own way.

examples.japanese: 選手たちはみんなそれなりに精一杯やっている。ただ結果が出ないだけだ。
examples.english: All the players are giving it their best in their own way. We just haven't had the (expected) result.

examples.japanese: お金がなくてもそれなりに余暇を楽しむ方法はある。
examples.english: Even if you don't have money, there are ways to enjoy your leisure in your own way.

examples.japanese: ほとんどの人は、悩みや問題があってもそれなりに暮らしているのだと思います。
examples.english: I think that even though most people have worries and problems, they are living the best they can (literally: in their own ways).

examples.japanese: 上の地位にいればそれなりの責任がかかってくる。
examples.english: If you are in a high-ranking position, you have to assume the responsibilities that come with it.

examples.english: If you are in a high-ranking position, you have to assume the responsibilities that come with it.

meaning_en: Take/cost/need/etc. only ~; do/manage (without/only with); get by/get away (without/only with); be let off (without/only with); be enough (if); be all right (if); not to have to: there is no need for
formation:
(i) Number(+Counter)で | 済む | | 
 | ２０ドルで済む | Something costs only 20 dollars | 
(ii) Noun {(だけ)/なし}で | 済む | | 
 | 電話(だけ)で済む | (just) a telephone call is enough | 
 | 検査なしで済む | Not have to have/give an examination; do without an exam | 
(iii) Nounがなくても | 済む | | 
 | 携帯電話がなくても済む | Manage without a cell phone | 
(iv) {Vて/Adjectiveいstem} | くて済む | | 
 | 謝って済む | Get away with just apologising | 
 | 安くて済む | Something costs only a little | 
(v) Vinformalだけで | 済む | | 
 | 行くだけで済む | Just going is enough; get by with just going | 
(vi) Vnegative {ずに/なくて(も)/ないで} | 済む | Exception: する→せずに | 
 | 行か{ずに/なくて(も)/ないで}済む | Do not have to go; be all right if someone doesn’t go | 
(vii) {Vconditionalば/Vinformal past}ら | 済む | | 
 | {借りれば/借りたら}済む | Be all right if someone borrows something |
explanation: A verb that means "to be finished; to do (in the sense of being enough)".

examples.japanese: ちょっと顔を見せるだけで済むと思う。
examples.english: I think just showing up for a while will be enough.

examples.japanese: 面接は20分で済んだ。
examples.english: The interview took only 20 minutes.

examples.japanese: あまり難しい日本語ではなかったので、辞書なしで済んだ。
examples.english: Because the Japanese (in it) was not very difﬁcult, I managed (to read it) without a dictionary.

examples.japanese: 旅行先ではどこでもクレジットカードが使えたので、現金がなくても済んだ。
examples.english: Everywhere I travelled I was able to use my credit card, so I could travel without cash.

examples.japanese: これは黙っていて済む問題ではない。
examples.english: This is not the kind of problem where you can get away with staying silent.

examples.japanese: 奨学金をもらったので、お金を借り{ずに/なくて(も)/ないで}済むと思う。
examples.english: I've been given a scholarship, so I think I can get by without borrowing money.

examples.japanese: 解約したい時は、入会金だけ損をすれば済む。
examples.english: When you want to cancel the agreement, all you will lose is the enrolment fee.

examples.japanese: この程度の翻訳なら3日で済むだろう。
examples.english: Three days should be enough for a translation like this.

meaning_en: However; but; only; here; provided that
formation: Sentence1。 | 但し、Sentence。 |
explanation: 但し・ただしA conjunction indicating that there is a condition, restriction, proviso, etc., to the preceding statement.

examples.japanese: この部屋にある雑誌や本はどれを見てもいいです。但し、部屋からは持ち出さないで下さい。
examples.english: You may look at any of the magazines or books in this room. However, please do not take them out of the room.

examples.japanese: 当館の開館時間は午前9時から午後６時まで。但し、特別行事がある場合はこの限りではない。
examples.english: This hall is open from 9 a.m. to 6 pm. However, for special events, the hall is not limited to these hours.

examples.japanese: 試験の時、辞書を見てもいいです。但し、和英辞典だけです。
examples.english: You may consult dictionaries' during the exam. However, (you may use) only Japanese-English dictionaries.

examples.japanese: この製品は定価の3割引きで販売しています。但し、返品はできません。
examples.english: We sell this product at 30 percent off the list price. But we cannot accept returns.

examples.japanese: 問題があったらいつでも相談して下さい。但し、お金の問題は相談に乗れません。
examples.english: Please (feel free to) talk to me whenever you have a problem. However, I cannot help you with money matters.

examples.japanese: 発表のトピックは何でもかまいません。但し、発表時間は20分以内です。
examples.english: You can choose any topic for your presentation. However, the presentation should be 20 minutes or fewer.

examples.japanese: 実習時間は午前8時30分から午後5時30分まで。但し、12時から1時までは休憩時間とする。
examples.english: The hours of the internship are from 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. However, there will be a break from 12:00 to 1:00.

examples.japanese: 総会の議決は会員の過半数を以って決定される。但し、規定改定はこの限りではない。
examples.english: Decisions at the general meeting are passed by a majority of the members. However this does not apply to revisions of the regulations.

meaning_en: Only; just; mere
formation:
(i) たかが | Nounだ | | 
 | たかが子供だ | Someone is only a child | 
(ii) たかが | {Noun/Number(+Counter)}　(くらい){と/で} | | 
 | たかがレポート(くらい)と | Thinking/saying that it’s only a report | 
 | たかがレポート(くらい)で | Over just a report | 
 | たかが二人(くらい)と | Thinking/saying that (there are only) two people | 
 | たかが二人(くらい)で | With just two people | 
(iii) たかが～ | {V/Adjectiveい}informal くらい (のこと)で | | 
 | たかが英語が{できる/できた}くらい (のこと)で | Just because someone can/could speak English; just for (things like) being able to speak English | 
 | たかが成績{悪い/悪かった}くらい (のこと)で | Just because someone’s performance is/was poor; just for (things like) someone’s poor performance | 
(iv) たかが～ | Adjectiveなstem{な/だった} くらい (のこと)で | | 
 | たかが料理が下手{な/だった} くらい (のこと)で | Just because someone is/was bad a cooking; just for (something like) being a poor cook |
explanation: A noun modiﬁer used when the speaker thinks little of the referent of the modiﬁed noun or noun phrase.

examples.japanese: たかが子供の言ったことだ。そんなに深刻に考えることはない。
examples.english: It's just something a child told you. You don't have to take it so seriously.

examples.japanese: たかが漫画(くらい)と馬鹿にしてはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't make light of it saying it's just a cartoon.

examples.japanese: たかが車の故障(くらい)でそんなに大騒ぎする必要はない。
examples.english: You don't need to make such a big fuss over a little car trouble.

examples.japanese: たかが無断で自転車を借りたくらい(のこと)でそんなに怒らなくてもいいでしょう。
examples.english: You don't have to get so mad at me just for borrowing your bicycle without asking.

examples.japanese: 人間一人の知恵などたかが知れている。
examples.english: One person's wisdom doesn't amount to much.

examples.japanese: たかが喫煙じゃないか。どうしてそんなに犯罪者のように言われなきゃならないんだ。
examples.english: It's only smoking. Why do they have to talk about us as if we were criminals?

examples.japanese: たかがノートくらいと言われるかもしれませんが、僕にとってはとても大事なものなんです。
examples.english: You may say it's just a notebook, but to me it's very important.

examples.japanese: たかが１０万円で何ができると言うのですか。
examples.english: What do you expect us to do with only 100,000 yen?

meaning_en: Without; while ~ staying; while ~ keep ~ing
formation:
(i) Vinformal past | なり(で) | | 
 | 行ったなり(で) | Someone went there never to return | 
 | 横になったなり(で) | Someone lay down (without getting up) | 
(ii) Vinformal past | なりのNoun | | 
 | 立ったなりの姿勢 | A standing posture (maintained) |
explanation: たなり（で）A conjunction indicating that a situation or condition remains unaltered.

examples.japanese: 彼は椅子に腰掛けたなり(で)、ずっと黙っていた。
examples.english: He sat in the chair and stayed there, silent the whole time.

examples.japanese: 片足を上げたなりの格好で、数秒間目をつぶるように言われた。
examples.english: I was told to close my eyes for a few seconds while I kept lifting one foot off the ground.

examples.japanese: 純一は17歳の時にフランスに行ったなりで、日本には帰らず画家になって、今ではモンマルトルに住みついている。
examples.english: Junichi went to France when he was 17 and never came back to Japan; he became a painter and now has settled in Montmartre.

examples.japanese: エリサは『源氏物語』を買ったなり、一ページも読まず、本棚に置きっぱなしだった。
examples.english: Elisa bought The Tale of Genji, but she left it on the bookshelf without reading a single page.

examples.japanese: 彼は私の部屋の入り口に突っ立ったなりでニヤニヤ笑っていた。
examples.english: My sweetheart stood at the entrance to my room, grinning.

examples.japanese: 妻がドアを開けてくれたんですけど、私はもう倒れたなりで、体が動きませんでした。
examples.english: My wife opened the door for me, but I had fallen down and couldn't move an inch.

examples.japanese: 腰をよじったなりの姿勢で長時間座っていたので、立てないほど腰が痛くなった。
examples.english: Because I was sitting for a long time with my lower back twisted, it hurt so much I couldn't stand up.

examples.japanese: 人形がほこりをかぶったなりで棚に乗っかっている。
examples.english: The doll sits on a shelf, covered with dust.
