meaning_en: By the; in sets/groups/lots/etc. of; in multiples of; each; every
formation:
(i) (Number+) Counter | 単位で | | 
 | 十人単位で | In groups of ten | 
(ii) Unit | 単位で | | 
 | 市単位で | By city |
explanation: A phrase that indicates the smallest amount, number or unit of something (or people) involved.

examples.japanese: このATMは千円単位でお金を引き出すことができる。
examples.english: You can withdraw money from this ATM in multiples of 1,000 yen.

examples.japanese: この社内調査では課単位でリサイクル実施率を調べる。
examples.english: This in-house investigation will examine the recycling rate for each section.

examples.japanese: 日本では湯飲みは5個単位で売られることが多い。
examples.english: In Japan, tea cups are often sold in sets of ﬁve.

examples.japanese: 我が社は今回のアジアからの労働者派遣が成功した場合には、次回から規模を大幅に拡大し、千人単位で派遣する予定だ。
examples.english: If our company's plan to send labourers from Asia is successful this time, next time we will greatly expand the scale and send labourers in groups of 1,000.

examples.japanese: B社の新しいデータ通信サービスは、最低契約量である１５０時間分のデータ通信を１分単位で利用できる。
examples.english: B Company's new data communication service allows the user to transmit and receive data in one-minute units for a minimum contract amount of 150 hours.

examples.japanese: オンライン書店のZ社は、本をページまたは章単位で販売するそうだ。
examples.english: They say the online bookstore Z is going to sell books by the page or the chapter.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクト管理ソフトの新バージョンでは、これまで日単位で行われていた計画と管理を時間・分単位で行えるようになった。
examples.english: This new version of the project management software application allows us to plan and manage (our operations) by the hour and minute, instead of the day.

meaning_en: Just; only; simply; no more than; nothing but; solely; merely; alone
formation:
(i) 単に | NPだ | | 
 | 単に選択の問題だ | Something is simply a matter of choice | 
(ii) 単に | {V/Adjectiveい}informalだけ | | 
 | 単に(英語を){話す/話した}だけ | Simply that someone speaks/spoke (English) | 
 | 単に(手数料が){安い/安かった}だけ | Simply that (the handling charge) is/was low | 
(iii) 単に | Adjectiveなstem {な/である/だった/であった}だけ | | 
 | 単に(周りが)静か{な/である/だった/であった}だけ | Simply that (the neighbourhood) is/was quiet | 
(iv) 単に | Noun{である/だった/であった}だけ | | 
 | 単に(先生が)外国人{である/だった/であった}だけ | Simply that (the teacher) is/was a foreigner | 
(v) 単に | NPだけParticle | | 
 | 単に学会の報告がけ(が/を/に/で/etc.) | Just the conference report (is/was/etc.); (read/copy/etc.) just the conference report; just (in/with/etc.) the conference report | 
(vi) 単に | NPに過ぎない | | 
 | 単に根拠のない噂に過ぎない | Something is nothing more than a groundless rumour |
explanation: An adverb that means "simply"

examples.japanese: これは単に文化の違いの問題だ。
examples.english: This is simply a matter/problem of cultural differences.

examples.japanese: この車は単にボディーのデザインを変えただけだ。
examples.english: They did nothing more to this car than change the body design.

examples.japanese: 仕事が難しいのではなく、単に私が不器用なだけです。
examples.english: It's not that the job is difficult; it's simply that I'm clumsy.

examples.japanese: 円高の影響は単に輸出だけにとどまらない。
examples.english: The effects of the high yen are not limited to exports.

examples.japanese: これは単に私個人の意見に過ぎない。
examples.english: This is nothing more than my personal opinion.

examples.japanese: それは単に解釈の問題だ。
examples.english: It's simply an issue of interpretation.

examples.japanese: これは単にあなた一人の問題ではない。
examples.english: This is not just a problem for you alone.

examples.japanese: この文章は単に原文を直訳しただけだ。
examples.english: This text is simply something that was translated literally from the original.

meaning_en: When it comes to ~; speaking of
formation:
Noun | たるや | | 
 | その成績たるや | When it comes to someone’s performance |
explanation: A compound particle used to present a subtopic about which the writer provides surprising or impressive information.

examples.japanese: この湖にはここにしかいないという生物がおり、その数たるや50種類を超える。
examples.english: There are creatures in this lake that exist only here; in fact, there are more than 50 species.

examples.japanese: ノーベル文学賞はどうやって選考するのだろう。1年間に世界で発表される文学作品の数たるや膨大なものだと思うのだが。
examples.english: How do they ever choose (who wins) the Nobel Prize in Literature? (I think) The number of works of literature published around the world in a year must be enormous.

examples.japanese: １９８７年春、彼はついにデビューを果たした。しかし、その初戦の結果たるや散々なものだった。
examples.english: In the spring of 1987, he ﬁnally made his debut. But, the result of that ﬁrst match was so miserable.

examples.japanese: 彼のバンジョーは最高だ。特にその速弾きテクニックたるやたぶん世界でも彼の右に出る者はいないのではないだろうか。
examples.english: His banjo playing is the best. Particularly when it comes to his fast plucking technique, I can't imagine anyone in the world who could do it better.

examples.japanese: このダイエット教室の参加費は決して安くはないが、その効果たるや絶大である。
examples.english: The fee for joining this diet class is certainly not cheap, but the results are tremendous!

examples.japanese: ロボカップは、サッカーをするロボットの世界一を競う大会である。１９９７年に名古屋で第1回大会が開かれて以来、国際大会が毎年開かれてきたが、その間の「選手」の技量の向上たるや著しい。
examples.english: RoboCup is a competition where soccer-playing robots compete to be ﬁrst in the world. Since the ﬁrst championship was held in Nagoya in 1997, an international competition has been held every year, and the ""players'"" skills have shown remarkable improvement since the first tournament.

(ii) VN | {してばかりはいられない/ばかりはしていられない} | |

(iii) Noun | {Particle+Vてばかりはいられない/ (Particle) ばかりVてはいられない} | | 
 | 本を読んでばかりはいられない | Cannot just read books; cannot always read books | 
 | 本ばかり読んではいられない | Cannot read just books; cannot always read books | 
 | 親から借りでばかりはいられない | Cannot just borrow something from one’s parents; cannot always borrow something from one’s parents | 
 | 親からばかり借りてはいられない | Cannot just borrow something from one’s parents; cannot always borrow something from one’s parents |
explanation: A phrase representing the idea that someone cannot just keep doing something or waste time being consumed by some emotion.

examples.japanese: 過去の業績に安住してばかりはいられない。
examples.english: We just cannot be content with our past performance.

examples.japanese: 確かにこれは深刻な事態だが、議論ばかりしてはいられない。
examples.english: Indeed, this is a serious situation, but we cannot just keep discussing it.

examples.japanese: 周りの人が助けてくれるからと言って、いつまでも人にばかり頼ってはいられない。
examples.english: Just because the people around me have helped me out in the past, I can't depend on others endlessly.

examples.japanese: やっと長年の夢であったマイホーム手に入れたが、喜んでばかりはいられない。これから大きなローンを返していかなければならないのだ。
examples.english: I ﬁnally own a house, which I have hoped to do for years, but I can't remain excited for long. Now I have a huge loan to repay.

examples.japanese: リストラのショックからまだ完全に立ち直ったわけじゃないけど、いつまでも落ち込んでばかりもいられない。すぐに仕事探しを始めなければ。
examples.english: I haven't fully recovered from the shock of being laid off (literally: the restructuring shock), but I cannot waste my time just feeling depressed. I have to start looking for a job right away.

examples.japanese: 希望の学校に入れなかったからと言って、くじけてばかりはいられない。
examples.english: I just can't let it get me down because I didn't get into the school I wanted.

examples.japanese: 人の成功に感心ばかりしてはいられない。我々ももっと頑張らなければ。
examples.english: We can't just sit around being impressed by someone else's success. We have to work harder, too.

examples.japanese: 障害の原因ばかり考えてもいられない。早急に失われたデータを回復する必要がある。
examples.english: We can't just keep thinking about what caused the trouble. We have to recover the lost data immediately.

meaning_en: Cannot help ~ing; cannot stop feeling; (so ~ and) cannot control ~; so ~ and ~ cannot bare it; so; unbearably
formation:
(i) Verb | て仕方がない | | 
 | 喉が乾いて仕方がない | (I) am so thirsty (and cannot bear it) | 
(ii) Adjectiveいstemく | て仕方がない | | 
 | 悲しくて仕方がない | (I) am so sad (and can hardly control (my) emotion) | 
(iii) Adjectiveな | で仕方がない | | 
 | いやで仕方がない | (I) dislike it so much (and (I)) can hardly control (my) emotion |
explanation: A phrase that represents emotions the speaker/writer cannot control or sensations/situations he/she cannot bear.

examples.japanese: 会社の理不尽なリストラに腹が立って仕方がない。
examples.english: I'm so mad at the company's unreasonable restructuring (i.e., laying off workers) (and cannot control my anger).

examples.japanese: 久しぶりに妻や子供たちに会えるので嬉しくて仕方がない。
examples.english: Because I get to see my wife and children for the ﬁrst time in a long while, I am so happy (and can hardly control my emotion).

examples.japanese: ここは何もすることがないので退屈で仕方がない。
examples.english: Because I have nothing to do here, I'm unbearably bored.

examples.japanese: アンディーがアメリカに帰ってまだ二日しか経っていないのに、寂しくて仕方がない。
examples.english: Although it's been only two days since Andy went back to America, I miss him so much (literally: I'm so lonely and can hardly control my emotion).

examples.japanese: こんなすばらしい建物が取り壊されるのかと思うと残念で仕方がない
examples.english: I feel so bad when I think that such a wonderful building is going to be demolished.

examples.japanese: ボーイフレンドが一年の日本留学を終えて来週帰ってくる。早く会いたくて仕方がない。
examples.english: My boyfriend is coming back next week after finishing his year of study in Japan. I'm dying to see him (literally: I want to see him soon so much)!

examples.japanese: 悪い風邪を引いたらしい。咳が出て仕方がない。
examples.english: I seem to have a bad cold. I cannot control my coughing.

examples.japanese: ここは空港のすぐ近くなので飛行機の音がうるさくて仕方がない。
examples.english: Because this place is close to an airport, the noise from the airplanes is unbearable.

meaning_en: If it is true that; if it is the case that; if; because; since
formation:
(i) NP | とあっては | | 
 | 病気とあっては | If it’s true that someone is ill | 
(ii) Sinformal | とあっては | だ after Adjectiveなstem and Noun is omitted | 
 | 由美も行くとあっては | If it’s true that Yumi is going, too | 
 | タクシーの方が安いとあっては | If it’s true that a taxi is cheaper | 
 | バスの方が便利とあっては | If it’s true that the bus is more convenient | 
 | 締め切りが今週末とあっては | If it’s the case that the deadline is the end of this week |
explanation: A conditional phrase that indirectly presents a factual situation as a reason.

examples.japanese: 社長の頼みとあっては断るわけにはいかない。
examples.english: If (it's true that) it's a favour for the president, I can't say no.

examples.japanese: 全商品が3割引きで買えるとあっては、遠方からわざわざ人が買いに来るのもうなずける。
examples.english: If (it's true that) you can buy everything at 30% off, I understand why people come from far away to shop (here).

examples.japanese: この大学が他の大学に統合されるのは残念だが、国の方針とあっては致し方ない。
examples.english: It is a pity that this university is going to be integrated into another university, but if that's the national policy, it cannot be helped.

examples.japanese: ブラジル・ドイツ戦のすぐ後とあっては国内チーム同士の試合が物足りなく感じられたのも仕方がない。
examples.english: Because it came right after the game between Brazil and Germany, it was inevitable that people did not feel the game between the domestic teams was very exciting.

examples.japanese: 皆が多忙な身とあっては30人以上の家族が集まれるのはクリスマスの休みしかない。
examples.english: Since everyone is so busy, Christmas vacation is the only time our family of more than 30 can get together.

examples.japanese: スカイダイビングがここサイパンで楽しめるとあっては、挑戦してみない手はない。
examples.english: If it's true that we can enjoy skydiving here in Saipan, there's no reason not to try it.

examples.japanese: どんなに短い作文でも、他の人に読まれ、コメントがつくとあっては、書く時の真剣味が増す。
examples.english: No matter how short your composition is, if it is read by others and they make comments, it makes you think more seriously when you write.

examples.japanese: 役人の飲食費に税金が使われたとあっては、誰もが腹立たしく思うのは当たり前だ。しかも、そのことが明るみに出そうになると、今度は圧力をかけて「口封じ」をやったとあっては、もう救いようがない。
examples.english: If tax money was used to pay for government officials' dining and drinking, of course people would be angry. But there's no hope if the ofﬁcials pressured those involved to keep their mouths shut when the practice was about to be exposed.

meaning_en: As if; as if to say that; as if ~ were convinced that; as if ~ believed that; as if ~ decided that
formation:
(i) Direct Quotation | とばかりに | | 
 | 「それ！」とばかりに | As if to say, "there you go!" | 
(ii) Indirect Quotation | とばかりに | | 
 | そうはさせないとばかりに | As if so to say that someone wouldn’t let someone do that | 
(iii) Noun | とばかりに | | 
 | チャンスとばかりに | As if someone had decided that this were someone’s great opportunity |
explanation: A phrase that indicates that someone does something in order to convey something or in such a way that someone is convinced that something is the case.

examples.japanese: 悟は「黙ってついてこい」とばかりに先に立って歩き出した。
examples.english: Satoru started off (literally: began to walk ahead) as if to say: ""Don't say anything and follow me.""

examples.japanese: 課長は余計な質問はするなとばかりに私をにらみつけた。
examples.english: My section chief glared at me as if to tell me not to ask any unnecessary questions.

examples.japanese: 霧が晴れたので、私は今がチャンスとばかりに写真を撮りまくった。
examples.english: The fog had cleared, so I took pictures furiously, as if it were my only chance.

examples.japanese: 竹本はこの時とばかりに日頃の不満を吐き出した。
examples.english: Takemoto vented his long-held complaints as if he were convinced this was the time (to do so).

examples.japanese: 彼女は「えい！」とばかりに侵入者を投げ飛ばした。
examples.english: She threw off (literally: ﬂung) the intruder with a yell (literally: as if yelling, ""Ei.!"").

examples.japanese: 庭園の花たちは早く撮ってとばかりに美しく咲いていました。
examples.english: The ﬂowers in the garden were blooming beautifully, as if they wanted us to take their pictures.

examples.japanese: 思い立ったが吉日とばかりにエアロビクスを始めました。
examples.english: I began aerobics believing that the day you think of something is an auspicious day to start it.

examples.japanese: 新鮮な魚を食べられるのは今日が最後とばかりに、刺身を食べられるだけ食べた。
examples.english: I ate as much sashimi as I could, as if I were convinced it was the last day I could eat fresh ﬁsh.

meaning_en: Which could/may be called; which can/could be described as
formation:
(i) Noun1 | とでも言うべきNoun2 | | 
 | 革命とでも言うべき出来事 | An event that could be called a revolution | 
(ii) Noun | とでも言うべき | | 
 | 「現代版シンデレラ」とでも言うべき | We could call (her) a modern version of Cinderalla |
explanation: A phrase that introduces a noun (or noun phrase) to describe the nature of someone or something.

examples.japanese: あれは運命とでも言うべき出来事だった。
examples.english: That was an incident that could be called fate.

examples.japanese: これはエッセイ的なサイトとでも言うべきでしょう。
examples.english: This should probably be described as an essay-like website.

examples.japanese: 近いうちに試用版とでも言うべきものをお送りします。
examples.english: I'll send you something before long that could be called a trial version.

examples.japanese: ミュンヘンのシンボルとでも言うべきこの市役所は１８６７年から１９０８年にかけて建てられたものです。
examples.english: This city hall, which could be called Munich's symbol, was built between 1867 and 1908.

examples.japanese: 我々は20世紀の技術の賜物とでも言うべき明石海峡大橋を渡った。
examples.english: We crossed the Akashi Strait Bridge, which could be described as a gift of 20th century technology.

examples.japanese: マイホーム計画最大のポイントとでも言うべきローンの組み方には、大きく分けると公的融資と民間融資の2種類があります。
examples.english: The ways of arranging a mortgage, which could be described as the most important consideration when planning to buy a home, can be classiﬁed into two types; government mortgages and private mortgages.

examples.japanese: 彼を一言で表現するとしたら「ネットワークの旅人」とでも言うべきだろうか。
examples.english: If I had to describe him in a word, I would call him a ""network traveller.""

meaning_en: I would say ~; ~ is how I’d put it
formation:
(i) {V/Adjectiveい}informal | といったところだ。 | | 
 | やっと終わったといったところだ。 | I’d say that it’s finally over | 
 | 良くもなく悪くもないといったところだ。 | I’d say that it is neither good nor bad | 
(ii) {Noun/Adjectiveなstem} | といったところだ。 | | 
 | 典型的な日本人といったところだ。 | I’d say that he/she is a typical Japanese | 
 | 不健康といったところだ。 | I’d say that someone is unhealthy | 
(iii) {Adverb/Interjection} | といったところだ。 | | 
 | もうちょっとといったところだ。 | I’d say that it will be done very soon | 
 | まあまあといったところだ。 | I’d say that something is so-so |
explanation: A phrase the speaker/writer uses to explain something in a brief/rough manner.

examples.japanese: 9月になって猛暑も一段落といったところです。
examples.english: I'd say the searing heat levelled off in September.

examples.japanese: ここは山というよりは、小高い丘といったところだ。
examples.english: I'd say that this is more of a (small) hill than a mountain.

examples.japanese: ホテルの部屋の広さはまあまあといったところでした。
examples.english: I'd say that the space in the hotel room was so-so.

examples.japanese: この大学の学部生と院生は合わせて6、000人といったところだ。
examples.english: Together, the number of undergraduates and graduates at this college is about 6,000.

examples.japanese: ヤンキースとレッドソックスはほぼ互角といったところだ。
examples.english: I'd say that the Yankees and the Red Sox are even.

examples.japanese: たった1年間の経験だけでは、図書館「達人」と呼ばれるには、まだまだといったところです。
examples.english: With only one year of experience, I'd say I have a long way to go before people call me a library expert.

examples.japanese: 英語の""Sorry""は日本語の「すみません」よりも「謝罪」の意味合いが強い。いわゆる「ごめんなさい」「申し訳ありません」といったところだ。
examples.english: "Sorry" in English is more of an apology than the Japanese "sumimasen." I would say that it corresponds to "gomennasai" or "moushiwake arimasen."

examples.japanese: この小説の主人公の男の性格を一言で表すとすれば、「自分には厳しいけれど、人にはとても優しい」といったところです。
examples.english: If I were to describe the personality of this novel's main character in short (literally: in a word), I would say he is very hard on himself but very kind to others.

meaning_en: However; but; having said that
formation:
Sentence1。 | と言って、Sentence2。 | | 
 | 時間がない。と言って、この仕事をそのままにしておくことはできない。 | I don’t have time. But, I can’t leave this job just as it is |
explanation: A conjunction used at the beginning of a sentence to convey the idea of "however".

examples.japanese: あと１０００万円あればなんとか欲しい家が買える。と言って、そんな大金を借りられるあてはない。
examples.english: If we had another ten million yen, we could manage to buy the house we want. Having said that, we don't know how we could borrow that much money.

examples.japanese: 外食は飽きたし自分で料理するのも億劫だ。と言って、何も食べずにいるというわけにもいかない。
examples.english: I've gotten tired of eating out, and cooking for myself is tiresome, too. But, I have to eat something (literally: I can't just not eat).

examples.japanese: いくら考えても名案は浮かばない。と言って、何もしなければ事態は悪化する一方だ。
examples.english: No matter how hard I think, I cannot come up with a good idea. However, the situation will get only worse if I don't do anything about it.

examples.japanese: 彼女と別れるのは絶対いやだ。と言って、妻と離婚する勇気もない。
examples.english: I deﬁnitely don't want to leave my girlfriend. Having said that, I don't have the courage to divorce my wife, either.

examples.japanese: 最近は少し運動するとすぐ疲れてしまう。と言って、何もしないと体が衰えるばかりなので何かしなければならない。
examples.english: These days I get tired quickly after doing a little exercise. However, I have to do something because if I don't do anything, l'll only get weaker.

examples.japanese: アメリカで自分の能力をためすのも面白いかもしれない。と言って、英語ができなければどうしようもないが。
examples.english: It might be interesting for you to try out your skills in America. But, it won't do any good if you cannot speak English.

meaning_en: Or; or rather; or I’d (rather) call it; or I may call it; or I’d (rather) say; or I may say
explanation: A phrase used to restate what was just said in order to be more accurate or appropriate.

examples.japanese: 自分の勘違いと言うか、不注意でした。
examples.english: It was my misunderstanding . . . or carelessness, rather.

examples.japanese: 彼のことは諦めたと言うか、もうどうでもよくなった。
examples.english: I'm through with him. Or rather, I don't care anymore.

examples.japanese: 我が社の話は何もできません。と言うか、何も話すことはありません。
examples.english: I cannot talk about our company. Or, I should say, I have nothing to say about it.

examples.japanese: 彼は議論好きと言うか、いつも人の意見に反対したがります。
examples.english: He is argumentative, or should I say, he always wants to disagree with others.

examples.japanese: この事件については、私たちも驚いていると言うか、困惑しています。
examples.english: We are also surprised by this incident, or perplexed, rather.

examples.japanese: 今日来た人は、商魂たくましいと言うか、本当に厚かましい人でした。
examples.english: The person who visited us today was an aggressive salesman, or maybe I should just say he was a really shameless person.

examples.japanese: 何度裏切られても涙を見ると許してしまう自分に腹が立つと言うか、愛想が尽きる。
examples.english: No matter how many times I get betrayed, I end up forgiving him when I see his tears. I'm angry at myself, or I should say, I'm sick of myself. (literally: I'm angry at myself, who ends up...)

examples.japanese: これは何と言うか、まあ、一種の妥協でしょうね。
examples.english: What should I call it? Hmm, it's a kind of compromise, I guess.

meaning_en: (I’m saying this) because; the reason (why I’m saying this) is that; by ~ I mean that; what I mean is that
formation:
(i) Sentence1。 | と言うのは、Sentence2。 | | 
 | 行けないかもしれない。と言うのは同じ日に試験があるんだ。 | I may not be able to go because I have an exam on the same day | 
(ii) Sentence1。Word/Phrase | と言うのは、Sentence2。 | Where Word/Phrase is taken from S1 | 
 | 今ならできる。今ならと言うのは来月になると忙しくなるからだ。 | I could do it (if it’s) now. I’m saying "(If it’s) now" because I’m going to be busy next month |
explanation: A phrase that introduces the reason for what has just been said.

examples.japanese: 来月の旅行は取りやめます。と言うのは、同じ頃に大事なお客が来ることになったんです。
examples.english: We are cancelling next month's trip. I'm saying this because it turns out that we're going to have an important guest around the same time.

examples.japanese: 今まで読めていた画像ファイルがほとんど読めなくなってしまいました。ほとんどと言うのは、少しですが読めるファイルもあるのです。
examples.english: Almost all the image ﬁles that I have been able to read until now have become unreadable. I say ""almost"" because, even though there are only a few, there are ﬁles that are still readable.

examples.japanese: 社長に直接話してみたらどうですか。と言うのは、実は社長も以前そういうアイディアについて話していたことがあるんです。
examples.english: Why don't you talk to the (company) president (about it)? I'm saying this because he was talking about a similar idea before.

examples.japanese: もう少し詳しく話してもらえませんか。と言うのは、私も少し前、同じような男から同じような被害に遭ったんです。
examples.english: Could you talk about it a little more in detail? (Because) I also ran into similar trouble with the same kind of man a little while ago.

examples.japanese: それは一度専門家に調べてもらった方がいいでしょう。と言うのは、素人が勝手に直すと、知らないうちに部品を傷めてしまう可能性があるからです。
examples.english: I think it's better to have it checked out by an expert, because if an amateur tries to fix it himself, he could damage a part without knowing it.

examples.japanese: 最近のパソコン用OSの普及で視覚障害者が困っている。と言うのは、これらのOSは画像中心で文字情報が少なく、文字を音声で読ませる方法があまり使えないからだ。
examples.english: People with vision problems are having trouble with the spread of the latest operating systems for personal computers because these operating systems are image-oriented with little word-based information, so there's not much of a chance to use software that reads words aloud.

examples.japanese: これらのゲームは、より正確に言えば、「一人用ゲーム」というより「一人でもできるゲーム」と言うべきでしょう。と言いますのは、これらのゲームはやり方によっては二人以上でもできるからです。
examples.english: To be more accurate, these games should be called ""games that can also be played alone"" rather than ""games for one person."" What I mean is, depending on how you play them, these games can be played by two or more people.

examples.japanese: あの提案書はたぶん通ると思う。たぶんと言うのは、審査委員の中に一人だけ反対するかもしれないのがいるんだ。
examples.english: I think that proposal will probably be approved. I say ""probably"" because there is one person on the review committee who might oppose it.

meaning_en: A, B and many other ~; A, B and every ~ else; including: whether X or Y
formation:
Noun1 | と言わずNoun2と言わず | | 
 | 窓と言わずドアと言わず | Including the windows and the doors |
explanation: ~言わず~と言わず A structure indicating that something is the case not only for A and B but also for many other places, things, etc., of X, to which A and B belong

examples.japanese: 友達の引っ越しを手伝ったら、翌日肩と言わず腰と言わず体のあちこちが痛んだ。
examples.english: I helped my friend move. Then, the next day my shoulders, my back and every other part of my body ached.

examples.japanese: 武史の部屋は、壁と言わず天井と言わず、いたるところにサッカーの写真が貼ってあった。
examples.english: In Takeshi's room, pictures of soccer were posted on the walls, the ceiling and everywhere else.

examples.japanese: しばらくすると、発疹が首と言わず手足と言わず、全身に広がった。
examples.english: Sometime later, a rash spread over my neck, hands, feet and all over the rest of my body.

examples.japanese: イベント会場は廊下と言わず階段と言わず、参加者で溢れていた。
examples.english: The participants were everywhere at the event site, even in the halls and on the stairs.

examples.japanese: 彼女が身につけているものは、靴と言わず、時計と言わず、スカーフと言わず、すべてブランドものだ。
examples.english: Everything she wears, including her shoes, her watch and her scarf, is a famous brand.

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事中と言わず休み時間と言わず、一時もコンピュータから離れることがない。
examples.english: He doesn't leave his computer even for a moment, whether it's work time or break time.

examples.japanese: 姉のうちは昼と言わず夜と言わず、一日中テレビをつけっぱなしにしている。
examples.english: At my (elder) sister's house, the TV set is on all the time, day or night.

examples.japanese: 男と言わず女と言わず、誰もがこの物語のヒロインには共感するはずだ。
examples.english: Anyone—man or woman—would sympathize with the heroine of this story.

meaning_en: Because; be caused by the fact that ~; from the fact that ~
formation:
(i) {V/Adjectiveい}informal | ところから | | 
 | {する/した}ところから | Because someone does/did something | 
 | {高い/高かった}ところから | Because something is/was expensive | 
(ii) Adjectiveなstem | {な/である/だった/であった}ところから | | 
 | 便利{な/である/だった/であった}ところから | Because something is/was convenient | 
(iii) Noun{である/だった/であった} | ところから | | 
 | 日本人{である/ だった/であった}ところから | Because someone is/was a Japanese |
explanation: A phrase that introduces the origins of names, theories, ideas and events.

examples.japanese: この宝石は猫の目に似ているところから「猫目石」と名づけられている。
examples.english: This gem is called ""cat's-eye"" because it resembles a cat's eye.

examples.japanese: 私が両者にそのことを十分説明しなかったところから誤解が生じた。
examples.english: The misunderstanding was caused by the fact that I didn't explain it to both of them fully.

examples.japanese: 田中先生はいつも蝶ネクタイをしていたところから「蝶ネクタイ先生」と呼ばれていた。
examples.english: Dr. Tanaka was called ""Professor Bow Tie"" because he always wore one.

examples.japanese: 日本は憲法が戦力の保持を禁止しているところから、「軍隊」ではなく「自衛隊」を持っている。
examples.english: Because its constitution bans the possession of military power, Japan has ""Self-Defence Forces,"" but not an ""army.""

examples.japanese: この説は、両者が生物的に多くの共通点を持っているところから来ている。
examples.english: This theory comes from the fact that, biologically, the two species have many things in common.

examples.japanese: 論語に「何もしないでいるよりは碁を打つ方がましだ」という教えがあるところから、碁は孔子以前にかなり普及していたとみられる。
examples.english: Because the Analects teach us that ""It is better to play Go than to not do anything,"" it appears that Go was already fairly popular before Confucius' time.

examples.japanese: そのイギリス人とは家が近くだったところから、よく遊びに行って英語や英語の歌を教えてもらったりした。
examples.english: Because my house was close to the Englishman's, I visited him often and he taught me English and English songs and other things.

examples.japanese: この雑誌は最初、ある有名月刊誌の別冊として刊行されたのが好評だったところから、後に単独の雑誌として独立したものだ。
examples.english: This magazine was ﬁrst published as a separate volume of a famous monthly magazine and later became an independent publication because it was so well received.

meaning_en: Without intending to; without paying much attention; unconsciously; mindlessly; don’t know (exactly) who/where/etc. (but); cannot tell (exactly) who/where/etc. (but); (to/from) no particular (person, etc.)
formation:
(i) V1informal nonpast | ともなくV2 | Where V1=V2 | 
 | 見るともなく見る | Look at something unconsciously | 
(ii) Wh-word+Particle | ともなく | | 
 | どこからともなく | (Cannot tell from where but) from somewhere | 
 | 誰にともなく | To no one in particular |
explanation: A phrase indicating that the subject does something without paying much attention, or that when, where, to whom, etc., something took place is unclear.

examples.japanese: 散歩をしているうちに、来るともなく駅まで来てしまった。
examples.english: While I was taking a walk, I came as far as the station without intending to.

examples.japanese: 我が家ではいつからともなく正月にスキーに行く習慣が始まった。
examples.english: We do not know when, but my family started a tradition of going skiing on New Year's Day.

examples.japanese: 聴くともなく聴いていたら、だんだんその演奏に引き込まれていった。
examples.english: As I was listening to the performance without paying much attention, I was gradually pulled into it.

examples.japanese: 大学時代のことを考えるともなく考えていると、次々にクラスメートの顔が浮かんできた。
examples.english: When I was thinking mindlessly about my university days, the faces of my classmates came to my mind one after another.

examples.japanese: 目撃者の話を聞くともなく後ろで聞いていたが、突然その話の中に事件解決のための重要な情報が含まれていることに気がついた。
examples.english: I was listening to the witness's story from behind without paying much attention when, all of sudden, I realised that it contained an important piece of information for solving the case.

examples.japanese: どこからともなくいい匂いが漂ってきた。
examples.english: (I couldn't tell from where, but) a good smell wafted from somewhere.

examples.japanese: 「やっと終わった」。彼は誰にともなくつぶやいた。
examples.english: Finally, it's over, he muttered (literally: muttered to no one in particular).

examples.japanese: 二人はどちらからともなく顔を見合わせて微笑んだ。
examples.english: The two smiled at each other almost at the same time. (literally: I cannot tell which one did it ﬁrst, but the two looked at each other and smiled.)

meaning_en: Tend to; apt to; be likely to; easily; be bound to
formation:
ともすると | Verb | | 
 | ともすると悲観的になる | Be likely to be pessimistic |
explanation: A phrase that expresses the idea that something is likely to take place.

examples.japanese: 切れ味のよい議論はともすると言葉の暴力となる。
examples.english: A sharp debate is apt to lead to a violent argument.

examples.japanese: 親は自分の子供にはともすると点数が甘くなりがちだ。
examples.english: Parents tend to be more permissive (literally: lenient in grading) when it comes to their own children.

examples.japanese: 大きな組織はともするとセクショナリズムに陥る危険性がある。
examples.english: Large organizations are likely to be in danger of falling into sectionalism.

examples.japanese: 商品づくりにおける標準化活動はともすると社内設計部門から嫌われる。
examples.english: Activities to promote standardization in product manufacturing are bound to be disliked by the design division.

examples.japanese: 日本ではともすると議論が感情的になってしまい、知的なディベートの場が育ちにくいと言われる。
examples.english: People say that in Japan arguments tend to be emotional, and, therefore, that it is hard to develop occasions for intellectual debate.

examples.japanese: スポーツ選手がいい記録を出すと、世間の期待が高くなり、ともするとその重圧に押しつぶされるようなケースも出てくる。
examples.english: When athletes make good records, the public raises its expectations, and this leads to cases where athletes are more likely to be crushed by the heavy pressure.

examples.japanese: 日本語が論理的な表現に不適だとは思わないが、日常会話的な表現を安易に使うと、ともすると論理が曖昧になりやすい。
examples.english: I don't believe that Japanese is ill-suited for expressing logic, but if you use expressions from daily conversation carelessly, your logic is apt to become ambiguous.

examples.japanese: 国際協力と言うと、ともすると富める国が貧しい国に援助を施すというように受け取られやすい。
examples.english: When we mention international cooperation, the tendency is to interpret it as rich countries giving aid to poor countries.

meaning_en: That
formation:
Sinformal | とのNoun | だ after Adjectiveなstem and Noun is often omitted | 
 | 提案が通ったとの報告 | A report that the proposal was accepted | 
 | 危険(だ) との意見 | An opinion that something/someone is dangerous |
explanation: A phrase that presents the content of the referent of the following noun (e.g., a report, notice, news, view).

examples.japanese: 経済情勢は悪化しているとの見方が優勢だ。
examples.english: The view that the economic situation is worsening is dominant.

examples.japanese: 邦画の入場者数がハリウッド映画を上回って1位になったのは始めて(だ)とのことだ。
examples.english: (It is said that) Apparently this is the first time that the size of the audience for a Japanese movie has exceeded that of a Hollywood movie, making it No. 1.

examples.japanese: 伊豆半島付近で地震があったとの知らせを受けた。
examples.english: I received the news that there was an earthquake near the Izu Peninsula.

examples.japanese: 探検隊が日本時間の13時30分にベースキャンプに到着したとの報告がもたらされた。
examples.english: There was a report that the expedition party arrived at the base camp at 1:30 p.m. Japan time.

examples.japanese: この研究テーマは社会のニーズに合っていないとの指摘がなされた。
examples.english: It was pointed out that this research topic does not meet society's needs.

examples.japanese: 副大臣の数をあまり多くすると行政を混乱させるとの意見がある。
examples.english: There is a view that having too many vice-ministers will make governing chaotic.

examples.japanese: 無断リンクは著作権侵害との見解が発表された。
examples.english: The view was announced that making a link (to a website) without permission infringes on the site owner's copyright.

examples.japanese: 当地からは遠隔で不便との理由で患者さん自身が受診を希望しない場合が多い。
examples.english: Patients often don't want to come in for their examination because they are far away and it is inconvenient (to come here).

meaning_en: Although (it is said that/someone says that); even though (it is said that/someone says that); admitting that; that being said; however; nevertheless
formation:
(i) Sinformal | とは言え | だ after Adjectiveなstem and Noun is omitted | 
 | {知らない/知らなかった}とは言え | Although someone doesn’t/didn’t know | 
 | {寒い/寒かった}とは言え | Although it is/was cold | 
 | 不便{∅/だった}とは言え | Although something is/was inconvenient | 
 | 子供{∅/だった}とは言え | Although someone is/was a child | 
(ii) Sentence1。 | とは言えSentence2。 | |
explanation: A conjunctive phrase meaning "although it is said that"

examples.japanese: 夏とは言え、ここはまだちょっと肌寒いくらいの涼しさだ。
examples.english: Although it is summer, it is still cool here—almost to the extent that it can be called a little chilly.

examples.japanese: 時間がなかったとは言え、ジェーンにこれくらいのレポートが書けないはずはない。
examples.english: (i) Even admitting that Jane didn't have much time, I don't believe that she couldn't write a (simple) report like this. (ii) Although Jane says that she didn't have much time (or you say that Jane didn't have much time), I don't believe that she couldn't write a (simple) report like this.

examples.japanese: 今度の学会が楽しみだ。とは言え、まだ発表準備は全然できていない。
examples.english: I'm looking forward to the next academic conference. That being said, I haven't prepared for my presentation at all yet.

examples.japanese: 子供がやったこととは言え、これは立派な犯罪だ。
examples.english: Although this was done by a child, it practically amounts to a crime.

examples.japanese: 予想していた返答だったとは言え、やはりそれを聞いた時はショックだった。
examples.english: Although it was the response I'd expected, it really did shock me to hear it.

examples.japanese: ノートブック型とは言え、ディスプレイは１７インチ、プロセッサーは2.4GHz、内臓ドライブは２５０GBもあり、DVD/CD-RWコンボドライブ付きという優れものだ。
examples.english: Although it is a laptop, it is an excellent machine, with a 17-inch display, a 2.4GHz processor, a voluminous 250GB internal drive and a DVD/CD-RW combo drive.

examples.japanese: 安いとは言え、都会の高級マンションだ。普通の者が簡単に買える代物ではない。
examples.english: Although I say (it is) reasonable, it is an upscale condominium in the city. It's not something ordinary people can easily afford.

examples.japanese: いかに暫定的処置とは言え、これはずさんすぎる。
examples.english: No matter how temporary these measures are supposed to be, this is just too slipshod.

meaning_en: Unintentionally; without being able to control onself; without meaning to; carelessly; involuntarily; in spite of oneself; just; only
formation:
(i) つい | Verb | | 
 | つい居眠りをする | Someone dozes carelessly/unintentionally | 
(ii) つい | Adverb | (time) | 
 | つい最近 | Just recently |
explanation: An adverb used to describe someone doing something without being able to control himself/herself or used to indicate the closeness of a time or a place.

examples.japanese: 楽しかったので、つい飲みすぎてしまった。
examples.english: Because I had such a good time, I ended up drinking too much (without meaning to).

examples.japanese: ついさっきまで山口さんが来ていたんです。
examples.english: Mr. Yamaguchi was here until just a little while ago.

examples.japanese: 人のお金を使うのは悪いとは知りながら、つい使ってしまった。
examples.english: I know it's a bad thing to use someone else's money but I just couldn't control myself (and used it).

examples.japanese: 安かったのでつい買ってしまった。
examples.english: It was cheap, so I just bought it (even though I didn't mean to).

examples.japanese: 恵美につい亜紀の秘密を話してしまった。
examples.english: I carelessly told Aki's secret to Emi.

examples.japanese: 彼の仕事を見ているとじれったいのでつい手を貸してしまう。
examples.english: I feel impatient when I see him doing his work, so, without intending to, I end up extending a hand.

examples.japanese: あの人は面白いのでついからかいたくなる。
examples.english: He's so funny it's hard to resist teasing him (literally: I come to want to tease him without meaning to).

examples.japanese: この店は感じがいいのでつい入ってみたくなる。
examples.english: This shop has such a good atmosphere that I can't help wanting to go in.

meaning_en: Therefore; thus; so; because of this; for this reason; with regard to this
explanation: A sentence-initial conjunction that means "with regard to this," referring to what is stated in the preceding sentence.

examples.japanese: コンピュータウイルスが全国的に広がっています。ついては、不審なメールが届いた場合は、添付ファイルを開くことなく当該メールを削除して下さい。
examples.english: Computer viruses are spreading across the country. Because of this, if you receive a suspicious e-mail (literally: in the event a suspicious e-mail arrives), delete the email without opening the attached ﬁle.

examples.japanese: この書類は契約文の日本語抄訳です。ついては、本訳をご参照の上、ウェブの英文契約書にご同意いただく必要があります。
examples.english: This document is the abridged Japanese translation of the agreement. Therefore, it is necessary for you to refer to this translation and accept the English agreement posted online.

examples.japanese: 11月分授業料は10月15日に指定預金口座から引き落とさせていただきます。ついては、前日までに預金残高の確認をお願いします。
examples.english: We are going to withdraw the November tuition and fees from your designated bank account on October 15. Therefore, please be sure to check the account balance by the previous day.

examples.japanese: 夏の省エネ対策について本社から通知がありました。ついては、別紙を参照の上、夏季のエネルギー節約にご協力をお願いいたします。
examples.english: Headquarters has sent a notification with regard to summer energy conservation measures. We therefore request your cooperation with the summer energy saving in accordance with the measures listed in the attachment (literally: after referring to the attachment).

examples.japanese: 深刻な雇用問題に対しては、再就職や雇用流動性を促進させる必要がある。ついては、以下の施策を積極的に展開されたい。
examples.english: To counter the serious unemployment (literally: employment) problem, it is necessary to promote reemployment and employment mobility. With regard to this, we'd like the following measures to be actively implemented.

examples.japanese: 新しくインターネット販売の事業を始める計画です。つきましては、その資金を融資していただきたいのです。
examples.english: We plan to launch a new Internet sales business. Therefore, we would like to request ﬁnancing for it.

examples.japanese: 今月は「リサイクル強化月間」になっています。つきましては、皆様方のご理解とご協力をお願いいたします。
examples.english: This is a ""recycling reinforcement month."" We therefore request your understanding and cooperation.

meaning_en: So; extremely; indescribably; indescribable; incredibly; awfully; terribly; cannot tell you/describe/etc. how; too much of
formation:
(i) {V/Adjectiveい}informal nonpast | (と言)ってらない | | 
 | 腹が立つ(と言)ってらない | (I’m) so mad | 
 | つまらない(と言)ってらない | (It’s) so boring | 
(ii) Adjectiveなstem | (と言)ってらない | | 
 | 退屈(と言)ってらない | (I’m) so bored | 
(iii) Adjective(い/な)さ | (と言)ってらない | | 
 | その面白さ(と言)ってらない | (something is) so interesting | 
 | その下手さ(と言)ってらない | (someone is) so bad at it | 
(iv) Vinformal nonpast | こと(と言)ってらない | | 
 | 疲れること(と言)ってらない | Something is so tiring | 
(v) Adjectiveいinformal nonpast | こと(と言)ってらない | | 
 | 美味しいこと(と言)ってらない | Something is so delicious | 
(vi) Adjectiveなstemなこと | (と言)ってらない | | 
 | 新鮮なこと(と言)ってらない | Something is so fresh |
explanation: （と言）ったらない A phrase used to express a strong sensation or emotion.

examples.japanese: つまらないミスで試合に負けて悔しい(と言)ったらない。
examples.english: I'm so mortiﬁed because I lost the game due to a stupid mistake.

examples.japanese: 老眼が進んで眼鏡なしでは近くの字が読めないので、不便(と言)ったらない。
examples.english: My farsightedness has gotten worse so I can't read words up close without my glasses—it's so inconvenient!

examples.japanese: 大きな書類を保存するのを忘れてコンピュータがフリーズした時の情けなさ(と言)ったらない。
examples.english: The miserable feeling you get when the computer freezes and you forgot to save a large ﬁle is indescribable.

examples.japanese: この辞書は使いにくいこと(と言)ったらない。
examples.english: This dictionary is incredibly hard to use.

examples.japanese: 5分ごとにジェット機が離陸するのでうるさいと言ったらない。
examples.english: There's a jet taking off every ﬁve minutes—I can't even describe (to you) how noisy it is.

examples.japanese: いつもよくしゃべる俊子が慎一の前で赤くなって何も言えないので、おかしいったらなかった。

meaning_en: Even though there is; although there is; there is ~ but
formation:
Noun | はあれ | | 
 | いろいろ問題はあれ | Even though there are various problems |
explanation: A phrase expressing the idea "even though there is something"

examples.japanese: インターフェースに若干の違いはあれ、この二つのプログラムは機能的には全く変わらない。
examples.english: Although their interfaces are slightly different, these two programs are just the same in terms of their functions.

examples.japanese: 歴史の違いはあれ、米国には１２０万を越す非営利団体(NPO)が存在します。
examples.english: Although their histories are different (literally: there are differences in their histories), there are more than 1,200,000 non-profit organizations in America.

examples.japanese: ほとんどの者が、程度の差はあれ、マスメディアの影響を受けていると言える。
examples.english: One can say that most people are affected by mass media, although there are differences in degree.

examples.japanese: レベルに違いはあれ、この課にいる者は全員英語を話せる。
examples.english: Although their (skill) levels are different (literally: there are differences in their skill levels), everybody in this section can speak English.

examples.japanese: 海外旅行に興味はあれ、先立つ費用がない。
examples.english: Even though I'm interested in traveling abroad, I don't have the money for it.

examples.japanese: 若干の不満はあれ、今の職場を離れるつもりはない。
examples.english: Even though I have some complaints (literally: dissatisfaction), I don't intend to leave my current job.

examples.japanese: 今まで自分を使ってくれた上司に対して感謝する気持ちはあれ、非難する気持ちは全くありません。
examples.english: I feel thankful for my boss, who has given me work to do all this time, and (literally: but) have no intention of criticizing him.

meaning_en: Be all right, but; might be all right, but; would be fine, but; would accept ~, but; even if ~ accept; even though ~ accept; although ~ accept

 | 借金はいいとしても | Borrowing money may be all right, but | 
 | 彼はいいとしても | Even if he accepts it |

 | 出席できないのはいいとしても | Not being able to attend may be all right, but |

explanation: A phrase that conveys the meaning "even if I/we accept something, something else is not acceptable".

examples.japanese: 友達を助けようという動機はいいとしてもやり方が間違っている。
examples.english: Your motivation for helping your friend is all right, but your way (of doing it) is wrong.

examples.japanese: 私はいいとしても他の人がこの部屋では満足しないだろう。
examples.english: Even if I accept it, other people wouldn't be satisﬁed with this room.

examples.japanese: 部屋が狭いのはいいとしてもエアコンがないのは困る。
examples.english: I'd accept a small room, but not having an air-conditioner there is not acceptable.

examples.japanese: 著作権のあるものは、個人用のコピーはいいとしても、それを他人に配付することは違法になります。
examples.english: Regarding copyrighted materials, making copies for one's own use may be all right, but distributing them to others is illegal.

examples.japanese: 街頭はいいとしても、電車やレストランなどの公共の場所で声高に携帯電話で話されるのは周りの者にとって極めて迷惑だ。
examples.english: Although it might be all right on the street, talking loudly on your cell phone in public places like trains and restaurants is extremely annoying to the people around you.

examples.japanese: このような結婚式では、結婚する本人たちはいいとしても両親が承知しないだろう。
examples.english: Even if it is all right with the couple getting married, their parents probably won't approve of this kind of wedding ceremony.

examples.japanese: この店は安いから味が少しくらい悪いのはまあいいとしても、古い材料を使うのはやめてもらいたい。
examples.english: Because this restaurant is cheap, it's all right for the food to taste a little off, but they should stop using old ingredients (for cooking).

examples.japanese: 今の社宅は一般の賃貸に比べて格段に安いのであまり文句は言えないのだが、建物が古いのはいいとしても、傷んだところをなかなか補修してもらえないのは問題だ。
examples.english: The rent for the company house (we live in) now is much cheaper than that of ordinary houses, so we can't complain much. And even though we accept the old building, the fact that we can't get repairs done quickly when something is damaged is a problem.

 | 貧乏{な/である/だった/であった}割に(は) | Considering that someone is/was poor |

examples.japanese: この店のサービスランチは値段の割に(は)おいしくボリュームがある。
examples.english: The bargain lunch at this restaurant is tasty and the portions are generous for the price.

examples.japanese: ビルはよく勉強している割に(は)成績が伸びない。
examples.english: For all his hard work, Bill's grades don't seem to improve. / Although Bill studies hard, his grades do not improve.

examples.japanese: このチームは強い割に(は)人気がない。
examples.english: This team is not popular despite its strength.

examples.japanese: 彼は大学で秀才だった割に(は)実社会であまり成功していない。
examples.english: He's not doing very well in the business world considering that he was such a brilliant student at college. / He was a brilliant student at college, but, despite that, he is not doing very well in the business world.

examples.japanese: 彼女はずばらしい研究をしているが、その割に(は)認められていない。
examples.english: She is doing excellent research, but hasn't gained as much recognition as she deserves.

examples.japanese: 清水さんは年の割には若く見える。
examples.english: Ms. Shimizu looks young for her age.

examples.japanese: この辺りはいつも海からの風があるので、強い日射しの割には過ごしやすい。
examples.english: Because there is always a wind coming up off the sea in this area, it is comfortable (to stay here) despite the strong sun.

examples.japanese: このソフトは安い割には機能がよく、使いやすいです。
examples.english: For as cheap as it is, this software is easy to use and has good functionality.

examples.japanese: このビルが完成するのはいつになるのやら。
examples.english: I wonder when this building will be ﬁnished.

examples.japanese: これから先、うちの会社は一体どうなることやら。
examples.english: I wonder what will happen to our company from now on. (I'm quite worried.)

examples.japanese: こんな映画のどこがいいのやらさっぱり分からない。
examples.english: I just don't understand what is good about this movie.

examples.japanese: 学生たちが何やら面白そうな計画をしている。
examples.english: The students are planning something interesting.

examples.japanese: 競技場ははたしてオリンピック開会までに完成するのやら。
examples.english: I really wonder if the stadium will be completed in time for the Olympic Games.

examples.japanese: 一体いつになったら自分の家が持てることやら。
examples.english: I wonder when I'll be able to have my own house. (I feel almost hopeless.)

examples.japanese: さっきまでの元気はどこへ行ったのやら。
examples.english: I wonder where all the energy he had just a little bit ago has gone.

examples.japanese: どこが入り口やら分からずビルの周りを何度も回った。
examples.english: Not being able to ﬁgure out where the entrance was, I walked around the building several times.

examples.japanese: 私は会議やら講習会やらでこのところ出張が続いている。
examples.english: I have been traveling for business a lot these days to conferences, workshops, etc.

examples.japanese: みんなに自分の写真をほめられて嬉しいやら恥ずかしいやら(で)変な気持ちでした。
examples.english: When people praised the picture of me I felt strange, both happy and shy.

meaning_en: Even though ~ try/want to ~; even though ~ be thinking of doing ~; although ~ try/want to ~; although ~ be thinking of doing ~
formation:
Vvolitional | にも(～ない) | | 
 | 話そうにも(～ない) | (not) even though someone tries to talk | 
 | 教えようにも(～ない) | (not) even though someone tries to teach |
explanation: ようにも（～ない） A conjunctive phrase that indicates concession: "even though someone tries to do something, he/she cannot do it for some reason".

examples.japanese: 徹に連絡しようにも電話番号もメールアドレスも知らない。
examples.english: Even though I want to contact Toru, I don't know either her phone number or her e-mail address.

examples.japanese: ひどく頭が痛くて起きようにも起きられない。
examples.english: I have a terrible headache, and I cannot get up even though I want to.

examples.japanese: 記事を書こうにも書く材料がない。
examples.english: Even though I'm thinking of writing an article, I have nothing to write about.

examples.japanese: 寿司を作ろうにも材料が手に入られない。
examples.english: Even though I want to make sushi, I cannot get the ingredients (literally: materials).

examples.japanese: 苦情を言おうにも誰に言っていいか分からなかった。
examples.english: Although I wanted to complain, I didn't know who to complain to.

examples.japanese: 体を動かそうにもあちこち痛くて腕も上げられない。
examples.english: Although I'm trying to move my body, every part aches and I can't even lift my arms.

examples.japanese: 母は僕の日本人のガールフレンドと話しそうにも日本語ができなかった。
examples.english: Even though my mother wanted to talk with my Japanese girlfriend, my mother (couldn't because she) can't speak Japanese.

examples.japanese: 気の毒に彼女は悩み事を相談しようにも相談できる人が近くにいない。
examples.english: It's sad that even though she wants to talk to someone about her troubles, she has no one to talk to near her.

meaning_en: (I heard/It is said/etc.) that
formation:
(i) Nounの | 由 | | 
 | ご入院の由 | I heard of someone’s hospitalisation | 
(ii) {V/Adjectiveい}informal | 由 | | 
 | {行う/行った}由 | I heard that someone will do/did something | 
 | {高い/高かった}由 | I heard that something is/was expensive | 
(iii) {Adjectiveなstem/Noun} | {である/であった}由 | | 
 | 不便{である/であった}由 | I heard that something is/was inconvenient | 
 | 先生{である/であった}由 | I heard that someone is/was a teacher |
explanation: 由・よし A dependent noun that marks the content of what the writer has learned.

examples.japanese: この度は本社営業部長にご栄転の由、誠におめでとう存じます。
examples.english: I heard of your promotion this time to manager of the headquarters' sales department. Please accept my sincere congratulations.

examples.japanese: 地球環境保護の国際会議が来年当市で開催される由(である)。
examples.english: It is said that an international conference on global environmental protection will be held in this city next year.

examples.japanese: 野沢先生は来年一年ドイツにいらっしゃる由、伺っております。
examples.english: I've been informed that next year Professor Nozawa is going to Germany for a year.

examples.japanese: 第一子御出産の由、心からお祝い申し上げます。
examples.english: I heard that you gave birth to your ﬁrst child and I send my heartfelt congratulations.

examples.japanese: 当ホテルでのご滞在が快適でなかった由、誠に申し訳なく存じます。
examples.english: We learned that your stay at our hotel was not a pleasant one. We are very sorry for that.

examples.japanese: 交通事故のこと伺いました。お怪我などなかった由、ほっといたしております。
examples.english: I heard about the trafﬁc accident. I am relieved to hear that you were not hurt.

examples.japanese: 石垣島は運よく台風の通過コースからはずれたため被害が少なかった由。
examples.english: I was informed that there was not much damage on Ishigaki Island because, luckily, the typhoon missed it (literally: swerved away from it).

examples.japanese: 日本消費者連盟は、一部ウイスキーの不正表示に関して、公正取引委員会に申し入れる由である。
examples.english: It is said that the Japan Consumers Union is going to appeal to the Fair Trade Commission regarding the dishonest labels on some whiskies.

meaning_en: Because; because of; due to; therefore
formation:
(i) {Noun(の)/Adjectiveなstem(な)} | 故(に) | | 
 | 天才(の)故(に) | Become someone is a genius | 
 | 便利(な) 故(に) | Because something is convenient | 
(ii)Sinformal(が) | 故(に) | だ after Adjectiveなstem and Noun omitted | 
 | {間違いを/犯す/犯した}(が) 故(に) | Because someone commits/commited an error | 
 | {美しい/美しかった}(が) 故(に) | Because someone/something is/was beautiful | 
 | 便利{である/だった/であった}(が) 故(に) | Because something is/was convenient | 
 | 天才{である/だった/であった}(が) 故(に) | Because someone is/was a genius | 
(iii) Sentence1(それ(が)/その) | 故に、Sentence2。 | | 
 | この議論は前提がおかしい。(それ(が)/その) 故に、結論も間違っている | This argument is based on a wrong premise. Therefore, the conclusion is also wrong |
explanation: 故に・ゆえに A conjunction that presents a reason or a cause.

examples.japanese: 彼女はその美貌(の)故(に)、悩みも多い。
examples.english: Because of her good looks, she also has many things to worry about.

examples.japanese: 結果にこだわりすぎる(が)故(に)、小さなことに心を奪われることになる。
examples.english: Because you want the end result to be perfect, you end up being distracted by little things.

examples.japanese: これは極めてデリケートな問題だ。(それ(が)/その)故に、慎重に取り組む必要がある。
examples.english: This is an extremely delicate problem; therefore, we must handle it very carefully.

examples.japanese: 彼の精神は大病の故に強靭になった。
examples.english: His mind was strengthened because of his serious illness.

examples.japanese: 電子テキストは改変と公開が容易であるが、この特徴故に公開されている電子テキストは元データを追跡することが難しい。
examples.english: Electronic texts are easy to revise and present to the public, but because of these characteristics, it is difﬁcult to trace publicly-displayed electronic texts back to their original data.

examples.japanese: 携帯電話は便利故に、使い方を誤らないようにしなければならない。
examples.english: Because cell phones are convenient, we have to be careful not to use them incorrectly.

examples.japanese: 山は高いが故に尊からず。
examples.english: Mountains are not sacred just because they are tall.

examples.japanese: 日本列島は南北に伸びているが故に、温度差が大きい。
examples.english: Because the Japanese archipelago extends north and south, the temperature difference (within Japan) is great.

meaning_en: Be bound to; definitely; unmistakably; unquestionably; undoubtedly; without fail; without doubt
formation:
Vnegative | ずにはおかない | Exception: する→せずにはおかない | 
 | 働かさずにはおかない | Someone definitely moves something |
explanation: A phrase that expresses the idea that someone/something necessarily or naturally causes something to happen.

examples.japanese: 技術の発達は社会環境の変化をもたらさずにはおかない。
examples.english: Technological advancements are bound to bring about changes to social environments.

examples.japanese: コンピュータの普及とインターネット利用の拡大は大きな教育の変革を促さずにはおかない。
examples.english: The spread of computers and the expansion of Internet use are bound to promote big changes in education.

examples.japanese: この映画は観る者に感動を与えずにはおかない。
examples.english: This movie is bound to move viewers. (literally: This movie does not leave viewers without moving them.)

examples.japanese: この小説は我々に人間とは何かを考えさせずにはおかない。
examples.english: Without fail, this novel makes us think about what it is to be human.

examples.japanese: この事故は日本とアメリカの関係に影響を及ぼさずにはおかないだろう。
examples.english: This accident will undoubtedly affect the relationship between Japan and America.

examples.japanese: 彼女は聴く者を魅了せずにはおかない音楽性とそれを表現する卓越した技術を持っている。
examples.english: She has a musicality that unfailingly captivates her audiences and the superb technique to express it.

examples.japanese: 環境や用途に合わせて動物たちがつくりあげる構造物は、彼らの知恵と工夫がいたるところに見られ、我々の好奇心を惹起せずにはおかない。
examples.english: Structures that animals construct according to their environment and needs exhibit in every aspect their wisdom and ideas, and are bound to arouse our curiosity.

meaning_en: Without ~ing; before (~ing); with no ~; if ~ do not; when ~ do not
formation:
Vnegative | ずして | Exception: する→せずして | 
 | 待たずして | Without waiting | 
 | 練習せずして | Without practicing |
explanation: A phrase meaning "without doing something".

examples.japanese: インカ帝国を知らずして南米大陸を語ることはできない。
examples.english: You cannot talk about the South American continent without some knowledge of the Inca Empire.

examples.japanese: 我々のチームは最終日の最終戦を待たずして優勝が決定した。
examples.english: Our team won the championship before (literally: without waiting for) the ﬁnal game on the ﬁnal day.

examples.japanese: 自分の義務を果たさずして人の責任を問うべきではない。
examples.english: You should not call others to account when you have not performed your own duties.

examples.japanese: 文雄は宝くじが当たって労せずして大金を得た。
examples.english: Fumio won the lottery, receiving a large sum of money with no effort.

examples.japanese: 新しい議長の選出で期せずしてみんなの意見が一致した。
examples.english: In the election for a new chairman, unexpectedly (literally: without expecting), everybody agreed (on who it should be).

examples.japanese: 今勉強せずしていつするのか？
examples.english: If we/you don't study now, when will you study?

examples.japanese: 荒木氏は自分の設計した建物の完成を見ずして亡くなってしまった。
examples.english: Mr. Araki died before (literally: without) seeing the completion of the building he'd designed.

examples.japanese: ウイルスに感染した電子メールを社外の個人、団体に送信してしまい、意図せずして加害者になってしまった。
examples.english: I became an offender without meaning to after sending a virus-infected e-mail to individuals and groups outside my company.

meaning_en: Without ~ing; even if ~ not; if ~ not
formation:
(i) Vnegative | ずとも | Exception: する→せずとも | 
 | 使わずとも | Even if one doesn’t use something; without using something | 
(ii) Nounなら | ずとも | | 
 | 専門家ならずとも | Even if someone is not a specialist |
explanation: A conjunctive phrase that indicates negative concession: "even if ~ not".

examples.japanese: 今年の夏は涼しいので、エアコンを使わずとも過ごせそうだ。
examples.english: It is cool this summer, so it looks like we can get by without using the air-conditioner.

examples.japanese: シカゴには親しい友人が何人かいるので、ホテルに泊まらずともよい。
examples.english: Because I have several close friends in Chicago, I don't have to stay at a hotel.

examples.japanese: こんなに安くヨーロッパへ行けるのなら、旅行好きならずとも行ってみたいと思うだろう。
examples.english: If you can go to Europe this cheaply, even if you don't especially like to travel, you'll probably want to go.

examples.japanese: 東京で会えずとも、大阪では必ず会える。
examples.english: (Even) if we cannot meet up in Tokyo, we will meet in Osaka for sure.

examples.japanese: 彼がどのくらいできるかはテストをせずとも見当がつく。
examples.english: I can guess how much he can do without even giving him a test.

examples.japanese: この程度の故障ならサービスセンター送らずともこの店で修理できます。
examples.english: We can repair this sort of trouble here at the store without sending (the product) to the service centre.

examples.japanese: この携帯電話は音声による操作が可能で、数字キーを押さずとも声だけで電話をかけられる。
examples.english: This cell phone can be voice activated, so you can make a call using just your voice, without having to punch any numbers.

examples.japanese: これからは特別な訓練を受けずとも使えるようなユーザーインターフェースが必要となるだろう。
examples.english: From now on it will be necessary to have a user interface that doesn't require special training.
